- He mentions a third story of humility whose opening is garbled in the transcript, its substance being that Ali said the father of the family is the one most deserving of carrying the flour, and carried the food on his back to his house, seeing no shame in a man returning to his family carrying the food (the start of the story unclear). (needs_source) {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep21 00:41:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep21 00:41:30}
- And his detachment: he relates that Ali, while caliph of the Muslims, recited every night before sleep the verse of the abode of the hereafter granted to those who seek neither exaltedness on earth nor corruption, and that the end is for the God-fearing (the wording of the verse is not written), and attributes to [[person/umar-ibn-abd-al-aziz|Umar ibn Abd al-Aziz]] that the most ascetic on the face of the earth after the prophets is Ali ibn Abi Talib (paraphrased). (needs_source) {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep21 00:42:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep21 00:42:30}
- He relates from a successor who saw him at night without being seen (the transcript writes his name "Zawq ibn Damgha al-Kinani"; a garbled line, not read) that he stood long in prayer swaying like the bitten (bitten by a snake; the speaker explains the Arabs call the bitten man "salim" in hope of his safety), then took hold of his beard and wept, imploring God, then said: O world, deceive another, I have divorced you thrice (paraphrased); the speaker notes that Ali is the narrator of the saying attributed to the Prophet cursing the muhallil (needs_source), and that he heard him say: ah for the paucity of provision, the desolation of the road and the length of the journey (paraphrased; the speaker explains it as the road of the Resurrection and the journey to paradise). (needs_source) {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep21 00:43:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep21 00:43:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep21 00:44:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep21 00:44:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep21 00:45:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep21 00:45:30}
- And his spending: he relates that the verse about those who spend their wealth by night and day, secretly and openly (its wording is not written), came down concerning Ali because he gave in four ways: by night, by day, in secret and in public (the occasion of revelation as the speaker tells it); and that a beggar stood over him while he prayed so he took something out of his hand or pocket and threw it to him so as not to miss the reward of giving (partly garbled lines). (needs_source) {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep21 00:45:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep21 00:46:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep21 00:46:30}
- His courage, he says, took the three past episodes, so he moves to his certainty: he relates that a man came warning him that some people had agreed to send one of them to kill him, and Ali answered in his telling that no person walks the earth without two angels guarding him by God's command (pointing to the verse whose wording is not written), and that the appointed term is well guarded, coming neither early nor late (paraphrased). (needs_source) {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep21 00:47:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep21 00:47:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep21 00:48:00}
- And of his certainty he relates that he had given Fatima six dirhams for flour, and when a beggar asked him he sent al-Hasan to his mother to bring one dirham of them; she reminded him he had given them to her for flour, and he said in his telling that none of them truly believes until his trust in what is in God's hand is greater than his trust in what is in his own hand (paraphrased), so he gave it to the beggar saying he was certain that whoever brings a good deed has ten like it (paraphrased); then he traded in a sale and a purchase (the transcript: a camel for a hundred and forty dirhams bought on credit, then something sold for two hundred leaving him sixty dirhams; the figures and the steps of the trade are garbled), and returned to Fatima with sixty dirhams, and when she asked where he had got it he answered it was from God's saying on the tenfold of the good deed (paraphrased). (needs_source) {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep21 00:48:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep21 00:48:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep21 00:49:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep21 00:49:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep21 00:50:00}
- And his knowledge: he relates the saying attributed to him that there is no verse in the book of God but he knows where it came down and when it came down, by night or day, in plain or mountain (paraphrased). (needs_source) {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep21 00:50:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep21 00:51:00}
- And his judging and sharpness: he relates that while commander of the faithful a pit (a dug well) in Kufa had a lion fall into it, and people crowded around it looking, so four fell in holding to one another and the lion killed them (see [[event/ali-judgment-lion-pit-yemen|Ali's judgment on the four at the lion pit]]; the place of the event is Kufa in the speaker's telling, Yemen in the museum's record); their kin asked for the blood-money, then sixty camels; Ali judged that the first gets fifteen because he held three and so has a quarter, the second twenty because he held two and so has a third, the third thirty because he held one and so has a half, and the fourth the full diyya because he held no one, and that all who crowded the place share in paying it (the speaker's figures and the wording of the ruling paraphrased). (needs_source) {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep21 00:51:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep21 00:51:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep21 00:52:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep21 00:52:30}
- He relates that a woman complained to him that her brother had died leaving six hundred dinars and her mother had given her only one dinar of the inheritance, and he said to her: perhaps your brother left a wife and two daughters and a mother and twelve children (the transcript's "16 and 12 boys and girls"; the figures are garbled), meaning one dinar may be her rightful share (paraphrased); the speaker asks where this knowledge came from, and closes that the next episode continues with Ali. (needs_source) {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep21 00:52:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep21 00:53:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep21 00:53:30}

## Left out of this episode 21

Not written from episode 21: the name of the maid who urged Ali to come forward (not named; 00:01:30); the name of the Azhari scholar in the England story (not named; 00:19:30 to 00:22:00); the name of the successor who narrated the night-prayer vision ("Zawq ibn Damgha al-Kinani", garbled; 00:42:30); the name of the Jewish man in the spitting story, the name of the woman who complained of the inheritance and of her brother (not given); a story one of the women present asked about the fostering of al-Hasan and al-Husayn (00:37:00, garbled, not understood and not told); the second name in the saying on the most hated names attributed to the Prophet ("wa-Naskhar", garbled; 00:11:00); and the description of al-Hasan's first wrap ("a yellow wrap" then "a white wrap"; its image garbled; 00:10:30). Garbled lines read with caution: the name of the raid before which the marriage fell ("ghazwat al-barida/tawhid"; 00:02:30); the figures of the trade after the dirham story (the camel at a hundred and forty, the sale at two hundred, sixty remaining; 00:49:00 to 00:50:00); the shares of the four's blood-money (the speaker's figures; 00:51:30 to 00:52:30); the inheritance figures (six hundred dinars, one dinar, the number of heirs; 00:52:30 to 00:53:00); the place of the lion-pit event (Kufa in the speaker's telling; the museum's record places it in Yemen); the start of the flour-carrying story (00:41:00, garbled); and what exactly was given to the beggar during prayer (00:46:00, garbled). Repetition loops discarded: 00:05:00, 00:08:00, 00:41:00 and 00:50:00 (repeated characters without meaning). The wording of the verses, the Prophet's sayings, Ali's words and the wedding-night supplication is not reproduced but paraphrased and marked as needing a source. The dates, figures and names in this episode are the speaker's, from a machine transcript that has not been listened to.

## Episode 22: Ali with the rightly guided caliphs, as the speaker tells it

:::perspectives
- **Speaker's view (opinion):** His purpose in this episode is that every trace of rancour between Muslims should melt when they see how much the Companions loved one another, and he asks that his listeners share with him the reward of wanting the nation to be one nation joined together. {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep22 00:02:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep22 00:03:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep22 00:03:30}
- **Speaker's view (opinion):** The Muslim wanted is not a naive enthusiast: the Companions were people of clear, explicit thinking and sound judgement, people who understood life and religion together; he makes this comment after an exchange on how to compute the ages of the Companions. {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep22 00:27:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep22 00:28:00}
- **Speaker's view (opinion):** The condition of four witnesses before a hadd is carried out shows that this religion is not thirsty for blood, whatever is claimed against it: to require four upright witnesses to one act of adultery is, in his telling, an almost closing of the door. {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep22 00:32:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep22 00:33:00}
- **Speaker's view (opinion):** A man who has attained standing should still respect the elder: Ali took hold of the halter of Abu Bakr's camel out of courtesy though he was the Prophet's cousin and a grown man, with about twenty-eight years between them. {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep22 00:27:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep22 00:28:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep22 00:28:30}
- **Speaker's view (opinion):** On Ali's advice to Umar to go and receive the keys of Jerusalem himself: the cause of Jerusalem and Palestine should not escape the Muslims, and the believer should feel the worth of that place. {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep22 00:37:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep22 00:38:00}
- **Speaker's view (opinion):** The husband who honours his wife and the wife who minds her husband's pleasure make a house without quarrels, and children raised in such a house come out like al-Hasan and al-Husayn; he draws this lesson from the scene of Ali asking Fatima's leave before Abu Bakr was admitted (the transcript of her answer is partly garbled). {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep22 00:22:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep22 00:23:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep22 00:24:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep22 00:25:00}
:::
- The speaker opens by saying he feels he is nearing the end of the Companions: he repeats the estimate he has quoted before that the Companions numbered about a hundred and twenty thousand (reckoned, in the report he cites, from about a hundred thousand at the Farewell Pilgrimage plus some twenty thousand; he notes the figure is not fixed), and counts that the series has so far run about seventy to eighty episodes and told around three hundred Companions (his figures, unchecked); the series, he says, will go on to the beloved prophets in a later season. (needs_source) {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep22 00:00:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep22 00:00:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep22 00:01:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep22 00:01:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep22 00:02:00}
- He frames the episode: about two episodes remain on [[person/ali-ibn-abi-talib|Ali ibn Abi Talib]], and today's question is how much the caliphs loved one another, how Abu Bakr loved Ali and Ali loved Umar and defended [[person/uthman-ibn-affan|Uthman]], so the listeners may come out saying: these loved one another deeply. {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep22 00:02:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep22 00:02:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep22 00:03:30}
- He begins with Ali and [[person/abu-bakr|Abu Bakr]] and works out the age gap with the audience: Abu Bakr was about thirty-eight when the Prophet was sent and Ali about ten, so about twenty-eight years between them, yet they entered Islam almost at one time (his arithmetic, marked as his). (needs_source) {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep22 00:03:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep22 00:04:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep22 00:04:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep22 00:05:00}
- He relates that the Prophet was seated in a gathering with Abu Bakr on his right and the Companions in a ring when Ali came and found no place, and stood waiting; Abu Bakr, knowing how the Prophet loved Ali, made room on the side of the Prophet rather than on his other side and called "come here, Aba al-Hasan", so Ali sat between Abu Bakr and the Prophet, and the Prophet smiled until the brightness showed on his face (paraphrased). (needs_source) {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep22 00:05:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep22 00:06:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep22 00:06:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep22 00:07:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep22 00:07:30}
- He relates the reverse side: when Ali was caliph of the Muslims and the state had reached its widest sway, he was asked among the Companions who is the bravest of people and answered Abu Bakr, telling how he had seen the Prophet in Mecca among some ten of the unbelievers pulling him, pushing him, insulting him and spitting in his face while they all held back in fear, until Abu Bakr came, pushed [[person/uqba-ibn-abi-muayt|Uqba ibn Abi Muayt]] away, entered to the Prophet and said: will you kill a man for saying my Lord is God (paraphrased); and again that a man asked him who was the best of people after the Messenger of God and he answered Abu Bakr (paraphrased). (needs_source) {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep22 00:07:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep22 00:08:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep22 00:08:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep22 00:09:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep22 00:09:30}
- He describes the moment of the Prophet's death (see [[event/death-of-the-prophet|death of the Prophet]]), when each of the great Companions did what fitted him: Ali, the Prophet's cousin and kin, washed the Prophet and shrouded him; [[person/abu-bakr|Abu Bakr]], [[person/umar-ibn-al-khattab|Umar]] and [[person/abu-ubayda-ibn-al-jarrah|Abu Ubayda ibn al-Jarrah]] went to the Ansar gathered at the portico of the Banu Saida (see [[event/saqifa|the Saqifa gathering]]; the speaker notes its place is still a landmark by the Prophet's mosque) when they heard the Ansar had met unannounced to settle who would rule after the Prophet; and Uthman, the tender and shy, sat unable to move or leave the mosque. (needs_source) {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep22 00:09:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep22 00:10:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep22 00:10:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep22 00:11:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep22 00:11:30}
- He relates that Ali was not present at the Saqifa and pledged a day or two later, and those wishing to attack Islam seized on that day or two; when Abu Bakr asked what had delayed him, Ali answered that only grief had kept them, and when they learned of the gathering they came; then he pledged and went out to the people saying in the speaker's telling that by God he saw no one in the nation more worthy of it than Abu Bakr and that none could equal him, being the companion of the cave and the second of two whom the Prophet had put forward to lead the prayer, adding in the speaker's telling that he himself had been present and well, not absent, and had the Prophet wished to advance him to lead the prayer he would have done so (all paraphrased). (needs_source) {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep22 00:11:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep22 00:12:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep22 00:12:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep22 00:13:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep22 00:13:30}
- In Abu Bakr's caliphate, he relates, Ali sat second in the council of counsel after Umar, and whenever a knot came to Abu Bakr he would say "give us your ruling, Aba al-Hasan" (paraphrased); when the wars of apostasy began (see [[event/ridda-wars|the Ridda wars]]) Abu Bakr posted guards at the entrances of Medina against any enemy and made Ali commander of the guard. (needs_source) {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep22 00:13:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep22 00:14:00}
- He relates that when Abu Bakr rode out to fight the apostates, about a year after the Prophet's death (Abu Bakr then about sixty-two and Ali about thirty-four in his telling), it was Ali holding the halter of Abu Bakr's camel; and when Abu Bakr thought to enter the battle himself, Ali took hold of the halter and reminded him of the Prophet's words to him at [[event/battle-of-uhud|Uhud]]: sheath your sword and do not bereave us of yourself, for if you are killed today Islam will have no order again (paraphrased); and Abu Bakr yielded. (needs_source) {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep22 00:14:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep22 00:15:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep22 00:16:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep22 00:16:30}
- He relates that when Abu Bakr later thought of invading the Persians, the greatest state of the age, he gathered the Companions, those of the ten promised paradise being present, Umar, Uthman, Ali and [[person/talha-ibn-ubaydullah|Talha]] among them, and asked them one by one while they weighed how grave the matter was; when the turn came to Ali he answered: you are victorious, God willing, whether you go yourself or send them (paraphrased); asked whence his certainty, he said he had heard the Prophet say that God had folded the earth for him so that he saw its easts and wests, and that the dominion of his nation would reach what had been folded for him (paraphrased); and Abu Bakr said he saw nothing but good tidings in his words (paraphrased). (needs_source) {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep22 00:16:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep22 00:17:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep22 00:17:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep22 00:18:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep22 00:18:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep22 00:19:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep22 00:19:30}
- He relates that at Abu Bakr's death the Companions stood before his grave and the only one who spoke was Ali, saying in his telling: God have mercy on you, O shaykh of Islam (paraphrased). (needs_source) {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep22 00:19:30}
- He relates that after Ali had become caliph, a man of the people of Kufa (not named in the transcript) said to him: I wonder at the Emigrants and the Helpers that they chose Abu Bakr over you; and Ali answered in his telling that Abu Bakr had preceded him in four things he dared not claim: in faith, in declaring Islam openly while Ali still hid his, in being the Prophet's companion in the cave, and in being put forward by the Prophet to lead the people in prayer before his death (all paraphrased). (needs_source) {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep22 00:19:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep22 00:20:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep22 00:20:30}
- He retells the matter of Fadak between Fatima and Abu Bakr (see [[event/fatima-inheritance-claim-fadak|Fatima's claim of Fadak]]): the Prophet died leaving nothing but the small land of Fadak (the transcript's word is garbled, read as Fadak); Fatima saw it as her right, while Abu Bakr had heard the Prophet say that the prophets are not inherited from and what they leave is charity (paraphrased), a report she had not heard; her anger lasted some months until she fell ill (see [[event/death-of-fatima-bint-muhammad|the death of Fatima]]), and Abu Bakr came to visit her; Ali told her the caliph of the Muslims was at the door asking leave to visit her, she asked what he thought and he said he would like him admitted, and Abu Bakr entered only after her leave (paraphrased); the speaker dwells on the three courtesies of the scene: a man of Medina visiting an ill woman, the caliph waiting at the door, and Ali not ashamed to make the caliph wait while he asked his wife. (needs_source) {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep22 00:20:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep22 00:21:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep22 00:21:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep22 00:22:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep22 00:22:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep22 00:23:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep22 00:23:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep22 00:24:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep22 00:24:30}
- He relates that Fatima died six months after the Prophet, and when she died Ali came to Abu Bakr and said: extend your hand that I may pledge you, and when Abu Bakr said he had already pledged, he answered that he wished to renew the pledge lest anyone think there remained in his heart something of Fatima's anger toward him (paraphrased); and when Abu Bakr asked why he had not pledged while she lived, he said: out of love for her, not wishing her to feel he was taking positions against her (paraphrased). (needs_source) {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep22 00:25:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep22 00:25:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep22 00:26:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep22 00:26:30}
- He passes audience comments before moving to Umar: the merit of clear thinking, a prayer for mercy on Ali, and remarks on the respect of the younger for the elder shown in Ali's holding of the camel's halter (some audience lines are garbled). {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep22 00:26:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep22 00:27:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep22 00:28:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep22 00:28:30}
- With Umar he begins with the saying he attributes to him, that Ali was favoured with three things he himself wished for one of: the banner on the day of [[event/battle-of-khaybar|Khaybar]], when the Prophet said he would give it to one who loves God and His Messenger and whom God and His Messenger love; the Prophet's saying to him, you are to me as Aaron was to Moses; and the Prophet marrying him to his daughter Fatima (all paraphrased). (needs_source) {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep22 00:29:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep22 00:29:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep22 00:30:00}
- He relates that Ali was the judge of the Muslims in Umar's caliphate and that Umar praised his judgement and would say: I seek refuge in God from a hard problem with no Abu al-Hasan for it (paraphrased); he then tells two cases between them. (needs_source) {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep22 00:30:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep22 00:30:30}
- The first: a woman whose husband was away at the war, left alone in Medina, had received men visiting her without a guardian present; Umar had her summoned, and in her fright she miscarried (the lines of the miscarriage are garbled; the speaker first tells a separate anecdote of Umar's awe, of a barber's shears falling at his approach); the Companions told Umar nothing was on him, he was a ruler and a discipliner, but Ali said: if they gave their opinion they erred, and if they wished to flatter you they did not advise you; the woman miscarried from her fear of you, so the blood-money is on you (paraphrased); and Umar said that whatever Abu al-Hasan said, Umar did, and paid the diyya. (needs_source) {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep22 00:30:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep22 00:31:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep22 00:31:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep22 00:32:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep22 00:32:30}
- The second: Umar, walking at night in a lane of Medina, saw with his own eyes and heard with his own ears a man in adultery, and gathered the Companions in the mosque meaning to carry out the hadd; Ali asked him whether he had four witnesses, he said no, and Ali said: by God, if you proceed we will flog you, O commander of the faithful (the eighty lashes of slander, as the speaker tells it); and Umar answered: yes, Abu al-Hasan, you judge and I listen (all paraphrased). (needs_source) {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep22 00:32:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep22 00:33:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep22 00:33:30}
- He relates that Umar went to Ali and asked for his daughter [[person/umm-kulthum-bint-ali|Umm Kulthum]] in marriage; Ali answered she was young; Umar said none would know her worth and honour but himself, and pressed him to send her so he might see, and if pleased would marry her; the speaker explains Umar's eagerness by a saying he attributes to the Prophet, that on the day of Resurrection every tie of kinship and marriage is set aside except the Prophet's own, and Umar wished to add to the ties he already had, his daughter [[person/hafsa|Hafsa]] being the Prophet's wife (paraphrased); and Umar married Umm Kulthum (paraphrased). (needs_source) {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep22 00:34:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep22 00:34:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep22 00:35:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep22 00:35:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep22 00:36:00}
- He adds a sign of that love: among Ali's many sons were three named Abu Bakr, Umar and Uthman, and a man does not name his sons after men he dislikes (the speaker's reading). (needs_source) {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep22 00:36:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep22 00:36:30}
- He relates that when Abu Ubayda ibn al-Jarrah called on Umar to come and receive the surrender of Jerusalem (see [[event/conquest-of-jerusalem|the conquest of Jerusalem]]), Umar gathered the Companions and consulted them; most advised against going, but Ali said: go, commander of the faithful, for if you go the Muslims will be honoured to the day of Resurrection; and the speaker explains that Ali knew the worth of that place, that the keys of Egypt or Iraq were not the same as the keys of Jerusalem (paraphrased). (needs_source) {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep22 00:36:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep22 00:37:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep22 00:37:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep22 00:38:00}
- He relates that Umar used to go to Ali every week or two, and once at night said to him: admonish me, Ali, admonish me, Aba al-Hasan; and among what Ali said: if you wish to catch up with your two companions, the Prophet and Abu Bakr, and they pleased with you, then eat less than fullness, judge justly between the people, and multiply the blessing upon the master of this station (paraphrased; the last phrase partly garbled, read as the blessing upon the Prophet). (needs_source) {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep22 00:38:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep22 00:39:00}
- He relates that a man spoke ill of Abu Bakr and Umar before Ali, and Ali ascended the minbar and said in his telling: by God, none loves Abu Bakr and Umar but a believer and none hates them but a sinner, and whoever follows the way of Abu Bakr and Umar is guided to a straight path (paraphrased). (needs_source) {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep22 00:39:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep22 00:39:30}
- He retells the answer of Muhammad ibn al-Hanafiyya's question (told in episode 21): when his son asked who was best after the Messenger of God he said Abu Bakr, then Umar; and here he adds in his telling that Uthman stood first before him, and of himself he said only: my son, I am but a man of the Muslims (paraphrased). (needs_source) {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep22 00:40:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep22 00:40:30}
- He turns to Ali and Uthman in the days of the siege (see [[event/siege-of-uthman-35|the siege of Uthman]] and [[event/ali-defends-uthman-during-siege|Ali's defence of Uthman]]): when the rebels pressed on Uthman, Ali carried food and water in to him through them day after day, his turban once falling from his head as he pressed through; and when the rebels from Egypt, Syria, Kufa and Basra encamped at two halting-places the transcript names "Dhi al-Marwa" and "Dhi Khushub" and came to Ali offering to pledge him the caliphate while Uthman was still besieged, Ali refused them and said in the speaker's telling that the people of those two places were cursed on the tongue of Muhammad (paraphrased), swearing by God he would never take it from them, and they returned. (needs_source) {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep22 00:40:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep22 00:41:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep22 00:41:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep22 00:42:00}
- He relates that Ali then entered the mosque and was asked to lead the people in prayer and refused, saying he would not lead while the imam was besieged, and prayed alone; and he went in to Uthman and said let us fight for you, while Uthman raised his hands saying: O God, bear witness that I have done my utmost (all paraphrased). (needs_source) {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep22 00:42:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep22 00:42:30}
- He closes with the claim that the Prophet had designated Ali as his successor, and answers it with Ali's own reported answers (flagged for a sourced perspectives pass; the museum makes no judgement): Ali was asked whether the Prophet had singled them out with something apart from the people and said no by God, except one thing, that he called him before his death and enjoined on him kindness to parents, with the saying he attributes to him that cursed is he who curses his father, explaining that a man's cursing another's father leads the other to curse his own father and mother (all paraphrased); and when another asked whether the Prophet had bequeathed him the caliphate he answered: no by God, he bequeathed us nothing; I was the first to believe the Messenger of God and will not be the first to lie upon him; had he bequeathed it to me I would not have let Abu Bakr and Umar ascend the minbar over me even if it cost me my life, and the Prophet in his last days ordered Abu Bakr to lead the people in prayer and did not bequeath to us (all paraphrased). (needs_source) {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep22 00:42:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep22 00:43:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep22 00:43:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep22 00:44:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep22 00:44:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep22 00:45:00}
- He relates that two days before the Prophet's death, [[person/abbas-ibn-abd-al-muttalib|al-Abbas]], the Prophet's uncle, came to Ali and told him to go in and ask the Prophet to make the caliphate his after him; Ali answered: if I go in and ask it of him and he says no, I will never have it after him, so al-Abbas said then do not enter; and Ali smiled at him and said: by God, I would never ask it of him (paraphrased). (needs_source) {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep22 00:45:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep22 00:46:00}
- He closes that the next episode is the hardest of the series: the caliphate, the death and the martyrdom of Ali ibn Abi Talib. {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep22 00:46:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep22 00:46:30}

## Left out of this episode 22

Not written from episode 22: the name of the man of Kufa who questioned Ali's precedence (not named; 00:19:30); the name of the woman whose husband was absent and of her husband (not given; 00:30:30); the name of the barber in the anecdote on Umar's awe (not given; 00:31:30); the exact designation of the men who visited the woman (garbled; 00:31:00); the name of the man who spoke ill of Abu Bakr and Umar before Ali (not given; 00:39:00); the wording of the rebels' offer of the caliphate (paraphrased; 00:41:30); and the names of Ali's sons in full (the speaker names Abu Bakr, Umar and Uthman without their mothers; 00:36:00). Garbled lines read with caution: the number of the Prophet's followers at the Farewell Pilgrimage behind the Companions figure ("a hundred thousand", then "twenty thousand"; the transcript's total reads "two hundred and twenty thousand" against the speaker's stated hundred and twenty; 00:00:00 to 00:00:30); the place of Abu Bakr's battle outing ("mințaqat aṣna", garbled, not read; 00:14:30); the lines of the woman's miscarriage (00:31:30 to 00:32:00); the last clause of Ali's admonition to Umar ("akthir min al-salat ala sahib hadha al-maqam", read as the blessing upon the Prophet; 00:39:00); the spelling of the two rebel halting-places ("Dhi al-Marwa" and "Dhi Khushub"; 00:41:30); and whether the consultation story's dissenting voice was Uthman (garbled; 00:37:00). Repetition loops discarded: 00:24:30 and 00:27:00 (repeated characters without meaning). The wording of the Prophet's sayings (the folded earth, kinship ties on the day of Resurrection, the cursing of parents), of Umar's three distinctions, of Ali's words on the minbar, to Abu Bakr, to Uthman and on the wasiyya, is not reproduced but paraphrased and marked as needing a source. The dates, figures and names in this episode are the speaker's, from a machine transcript that has not been listened to.

## Episode 23: the caliphate and martyrdom of Ali ibn Abi Talib, as the speaker tells it

:::perspectives
- **The speaker's view (opinion):** he chose not to narrate the details of the fitna of Ali's caliphate, after consulting scholars among whom he names "the imam of the Haram of Mecca" (the identification is garbled in the transcript), arguing that the ummah in its present moment needs gathering and mending, that recounting the killing among the Companions reopens wounds fourteen hundred years old, and quoting the scholars' saying about that fitna: God kept our hands clean of it, so let us keep our tongues clean of it (paraphrased). {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep23 00:02:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep23 00:02:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep23 00:03:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep23 00:03:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep23 00:04:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep23 00:04:30}
- **The speaker's view (opinion):** every question in religion on which no action is built should not be entered, giving the joking examples of the sex of Solomon's ant and the father of Abraham's lineage, so what passed among the Companions yields the listener no deed. {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep23 00:07:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep23 00:07:30}
- **The speaker's view (opinion):** the claim that the Companions' fitna was "a fitna of desires" means, to him, that the Prophet did not raise them well, and serves the claim that Islam was sound for only twenty years and then ended in wars; he replies that an ummah about thirteen hundred years old (the figure is garbled in the transcript) cannot be built on desires, and that the greatest nations of the world have not lasted two hundred, so the ummah's foundation must be strong. {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep23 00:24:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep23 00:25:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep23 00:25:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep23 00:26:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep23 00:26:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep23 00:27:00}
- **The speaker's view (opinion):** the fitna itself was a mercy to the ummah, comparing it to the Ridda wars of which he earlier said they were a mercy that taught the ummah, because it taught the lesson of those who blow discord among the Muslims to live off their strife (his didactic reading, not a historical judgement). {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep23 00:27:30}
- **The speaker's view (opinion):** the Jews are people of a heavenly religion to be respected like the Christians, and his talk about Abdullah ibn Saba in the episode concerns a historical account, not the people of that religion; he said this while relating the attribution of the fitna's kindling to Ibn Saba and his group. {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep23 00:23:00}
- **The speaker's view (opinion):** in an attendee's comment he relayed and endorsed: because Aisha saw in Uthman's stand on the fitna a stand that refrained from killing and bloodshed, the events came as a reaction to that phase (an endorsed listener's comment, not written as a confirmed analysis). {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep23 00:40:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep23 00:40:30}
- **The speaker's view (opinion):** he quoted [[person/ibn-taymiyya|Ibn Taymiyya]] on the consensus of the Book, the Sunna and the righteous salaf that the two parties of the fitna were on truth or on good, all of them sincere, with Ali ibn Abi Talib foremost and closest to the truth (paraphrased; the text was not sourced in the episode). {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep23 00:42:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep23 00:42:30} (needs_source)
:::
- The speaker announces the episode closes the rightly-guided-caliphs run and is the last on Ali ibn Abi Talib, and reckons the length of his caliphate with the audience until they settle on four years and nine months (his figures, unchecked). {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep23 00:00:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep23 00:00:30}
- He gives his dates: Ali was pledged the caliphate on Friday 24 Dhu al-Hijja 35 AH, a week after Uthman's death on 18 Dhu al-Hijja, and died on 17 Ramadan 40 AH (elsewhere the transcript reads "year 82 AH", a garbled reading not adopted; and in a third place that the pledge came five days after Uthman's death, so the gap of five days versus a week remains the speaker's own telling), and he describes these years as among the hardest in the ummah's life. (needs_source) {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep23 00:01:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep23 00:01:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep23 00:18:00}
- He describes his dilemma in presenting the fitna on which volumes have been written, between two options: telling it in full detail, or leaving it and keeping only the lessons, and he chose the second, citing the verse on the one ummah and the verse on holding fast together and saying the religion's very name, "the religion of tawhid", requires one God and one ummah upon Him (his didactic frame). {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep23 00:02:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep23 00:05:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep23 00:05:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep23 00:06:00} [[passage/quran-21-92|Surat al-Anbiya, verse 92]] [[passage/quran-3-103|Surat Al Imran, verse 103]] (the speaker's view)
- He presents his other argument: the Quran commended the Companions and declared God pleased with those who gave the pledge, so it is unthinkable after that commendation that they fought over worldly rule; then he lays down the rule he wants carried out of the episode: the Companions are all on good, all sought the truth, whoever strove and was right like Ali, and whoever strove and erred, and their intentions were all sincere (the speaker's didactic rule; the museum makes no judgement on the events of the fitna). {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep23 00:08:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep23 00:08:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep23 00:09:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep23 00:09:30} [[passage/quran-48-18|Surat al-Fath, verse 18]] (needs_source)
- He tells the start of the pledge as he relates it: after the killing of [[person/uthman-ibn-affan|Uthman]] the Muslims rushed to [[person/ali-ibn-abi-talib|Ali]] because he was the most deserving of the caliphate on earth at that time (the speaker's words); Ali had sat in his house weeping for Uthman for a week, saying he was innocent of what befell him; the Muhajirun and the Ansar came and he said: leave me be, I would be a vizier in it and do not want to be its amir, and that he was ready for whomever they chose, warning them of harder days ahead "in which hearts are torn out" (paraphrased). (needs_source) {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep23 00:10:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep23 00:10:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep23 00:11:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep23 00:11:30}
- He relays their answer: by God we find none on earth more deserving of it than you, "who for Islam but you" (paraphrased), and he dwells on the phrase and generalises it as a lesson for the listeners: who for Islam in the building, in the neighbourhood, in the ummah's trials but you — that each one take people's hands through his character, his success and his appearance (his da'wa framing). {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep23 00:11:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep23 00:12:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep23 00:12:30} (the speaker's view)
- He tells Ali's condition: this matter can only be by shura as the caliphs before him came by it; so he stipulates that all the people of Badr be gathered to him, and if they agree on him he is with them, and if they choose another he pledges him with the people; the people of Badr gathered and said they saw none on earth more deserving of it than he (paraphrased). (needs_source) {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep23 00:13:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep23 00:13:30}
- He relates that Ali asked: where are [[person/zubayr-ibn-al-awwam|al-Zubayr]] and [[person/talha-ibn-ubaydullah|Talha]]? and the speaker explains they were the two most important living Companions then, two of the ten promised paradise, whose weight weighs the ummah (his assessment); they came and said we pledge you, and al-Zubayr said: do you ask about us when we asked the people before you asked, and we choose no alternative to Ali (paraphrased). (needs_source) {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep23 00:13:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep23 00:14:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep23 00:14:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep23 00:15:00}
- He relates that Ali stipulated the pledge not be secret but in the mosque openly, in the mosque of the Messenger of God, and that [[person/abdullah-ibn-abbas|Ibn Abbas]] advised otherwise fearing tumult (the lines of the passage are garbled), so the people gathered in the mosque and stood pledging (see [[event/bayat-ali|the pledge to Ali]]). (needs_source) {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep23 00:15:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep23 00:15:30}
- He relates that the first to come forward to pledge was Talha ibn Ubaydullah with his paralysed right hand, and recalls the story of its paralysis: on the day of [[event/battle-of-uhud|Uhud]], when the Muslim army broke and only about twenty remained around the Prophet, Talha among them, he made himself a shield against the arrows, saying in the speaker's telling: my sacrifice before yours, Messenger of God, until an arrow struck his right hand and paralysed it (paraphrased). (needs_source) {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep23 00:15:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep23 00:16:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep23 00:16:30}
- He relates that a newly Muslim man stood and said to himself: the first hand to pledge is a paralysed hand, this matter will not hold; Ali looked at him and said: that is your ignorance — this hand is more blessed than all these hands, a hand that defended the Messenger of God and shielded him from the arrows (paraphrased); then the people pledged Ali and the ummah agreed on him in his telling (see [[event/bayat-ali|the pledge to Ali]]). (needs_source) {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep23 00:16:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep23 00:17:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep23 00:17:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep23 00:18:00}
- The speaker states once more: he will not enter the fitan nor narrate them, pausing on the many books written to shake the Muslims' trust in their religion through those four years, and he affirms the meaning he says ahl al-Sunna wal-Jama'a and the ummah's scholars agreed on: the Companions are all upright and sincere, they sought nothing in the fitna but ijtihad and had no desire for themselves (the speaker's view and declared confessional position). {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep23 00:18:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep23 00:18:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep23 00:19:00}
- He passes over a woman listener's comment drawing from the Companions' lives that Muslims must be one hand in the way of the religion, citing a verse that fingers together grow strong and apart break singly (the verse was not attributed in the transcript). {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep23 00:19:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep23 00:20:00}
- He compresses the fitna with no battle names and no dead: after Uthman's killing the views differed on the timing of taking vengeance for his blood, not on the principle; [[person/muawiya-ibn-abi-sufyan|Muawiya ibn Abi Sufyan]], the governor of al-Sham and Uthman's kinsman-avenger, held his killers must be killed at once, resting in the speaker's telling on the verse granting authority to the heir of one wrongfully killed [[passage/quran-17-33|Surat al-Isra, verse 33]]; Ali held that striking now amid a fitna and dispersal would cause chaos, and that vengeance should come once matters settle and rule stands; al-Zubayr and Talha held to taking it now, and Aisha to gathering armies to be aided (the speaker's summary: the whole matter is ijtihad over timing, and all agreed vengeance for Uthman was due). (needs_source) {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep23 00:20:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep23 00:21:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep23 00:21:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep23 00:22:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep23 00:22:30}
- He relates that [[person/abdullah-ibn-saba|Abdullah ibn Saba]] and his group, who had a hand in Uthman's killing, kept blowing the fitna back into the ummah, and he describes them as Jews, adding his hedge that the Jews are people of a heavenly religion to be respected and that the talk is of a historical account (flagged for a sourced perspectives pass: the attribution of the fitna to Ibn Saba, and his very person, is a matter of scholarly dispute on which the museum makes no judgement). (needs_source) {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep23 00:22:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep23 00:23:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep23 00:23:30}
- He answers what is told of the Companions' enmities: that Muawiya was not seeking the caliphate for himself, that the claim Aisha hated Ali and that al-Zubayr and Talha wanted to wrest it from him is "all untrue" in the speaker's words, that love and affection stood between them even during the wars, and he warns against the "fitna of desires" claim because it means to him the Prophet did not raise them well, and against the claim that Islam is twenty years then ended (all the speaker's didactic position). {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep23 00:23:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep23 00:24:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep23 00:24:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep23 00:25:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep23 00:26:00}
- He relates that during his battles Ali would stand and pray every day: O God set right between us and them, and sow love in our hearts and theirs (paraphrased); and he was asked about his opponents: are they unbelievers? he said they had fled unbelief; hypocrites? he said God forbid, the hypocrites mention God little while these mention God much; so what are they? he said: our brothers who transgressed against us, so it fell on us to fight them until they return to the truth; and the speaker cites the verse on the two fighting groups and the verse on rancour removed from breasts (all paraphrased). (needs_source) {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep23 00:28:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep23 00:29:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep23 00:29:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep23 00:30:00} [[passage/quran-49-9|Surat al-Hujurat, verse 9]] [[passage/quran-15-47|Surat al-Hijr, verse 47]]
- He relates that when the [[event/battle-of-the-camel|battle of the Camel]] stopped, with dead on both sides, Ali said: stand with me and let us pray over them, and he prayed the funeral prayer over the dead of both parties, the dead were buried together, and when the Eid prayer came Ali led both armies together (all in the speaker's telling). (needs_source) {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep23 00:30:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep23 00:30:30}
- He relates that when [[person/ammar-ibn-yasir|Ammar ibn Yasir]], who was in Ali's rank, was killed, and the Prophet had said in a hadith the speaker relays: Ammar will be killed by the transgressing party, half the opposing army joined Ali because the truth had become clear (paraphrased; the hadith's attribution and effect are the speaker's telling). (needs_source) {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep23 00:30:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep23 00:31:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep23 00:31:30}
- He tells of al-Zubayr ibn al-Awwam: at the start of the battle Ali sent to al-Zubayr and they conferred and agreed there would be no war, then a band of Ibn Saba's group went out at night in two halves: one half attacking al-Zubayr and Talha's army killing and saying we are Ali's followers, the other attacking Ali's army saying we are al-Zubayr and Talha's followers, and the war ignited (in the speaker's telling). (needs_source) {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep23 00:31:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep23 00:32:00}
- He relates that before the war caught, Ali called al-Zubayr out man to man and adjured him by God: do you remember the day you and I were on the mountain of Uhud and the Prophet asked you, do you love Ali? you said yes, and he told you: you will fight Ali while wronging him; al-Zubayr said: by God, it is as if I hear it now — I had forgotten it; had I remembered it I would not have come out to you this march, and by God I will never fight you after this (paraphrased; see [[event/testament-of-al-zubayr-on-the-day-of-the-camel|al-Zubayr's testament on the day of the Camel]]). (needs_source) {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep23 00:32:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep23 00:32:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep23 00:33:00}
- He relates that al-Zubayr turned back, and a man followed him until he slept under a tree, at ease that he was no longer fighting Ali, and struck and killed him — the transcript names him "Amr ibn Qurmuz" (the museum reads [[person/amr-ibn-jurmuz|Amr ibn Jurmuz]] in the accounts); and the speaker says none prayed over him but his servant, and he was buried in Wadi al-Siba in a place whose grave is unknown, commenting that the listeners should not grieve since he is in paradise (his comment). (needs_source) {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep23 00:33:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep23 00:33:30}
- He relates that the killer returned with al-Zubayr's sword to Ali to gladden him, and Ali looked at the sword and wept and said: this sword often lifted distress from the face of the Messenger of God, and I heard the Messenger of God say: give the killer of Ibn Safiyya tidings of the Fire (paraphrased); and the speaker adds that the Muslims did not kill the man afterward because he was too slight to kill and his reckoning is on the day of Resurrection (the justifying line is garbled in the transcript: "when he became the Muslims' caliph they left him"). (needs_source) {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep23 00:34:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep23 00:34:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep23 00:35:00}
- He tells of Talha ibn Ubaydullah, that a heavy blow struck him during the battle and he fell, and a man passed him and asked whose man he was, and he said: of the companions of Amir al-Mu'minin Ali ibn Abi Talib, and he stretched out his hand as though pledging him, so Talha pledged him and said: carry it to Ali; the man reached Ali and Ali said: the Messenger of God spoke true — he heard him say in the speaker's telling that Talha would not die except pledging (paraphrased; the speaker counts it among the proofs of prophethood because the Prophet foretold a pledge given at death). (needs_source) {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep23 00:35:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep23 00:35:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep23 00:36:00}
- He relates that Ali found Talha dead in his blood, embraced him, wiped the dust from his face and said: how hard it is on me to see you thus, Abu Muhammad; then he asked God to make him and his brother among those from whose breasts rancour is removed, brothers facing one another, and said: O God I complain to You my bereavement in Talha's death, and by God I had wished I had died twenty years before this day; and al-Hasan ibn Ali came to prop up his weeping father (all paraphrased). (needs_source) {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep23 00:36:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep23 00:36:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep23 00:37:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep23 00:37:30} [[passage/quran-15-47|Surat al-Hijr, verse 47]]
- He tells of the lady [[person/aisha|Aisha]] in the [[event/battle-of-the-camel|battle of the Camel]], so named because she rode a camel while the two armies fought around it, the camel-bearer of her side being [[person/al-qaqa-ibn-amr|al-Qa'qa' ibn Amr]] (the name reads "al-Qa'qa' ibn Amk" in the transcript, the museum's reading); when the fighting raged around the camel Ali ordered the camel hamstrung and the howdah carried away, then he honoured the lady Aisha after the battle and let her choose to return to Mecca or Medina, and she returned; he went out with her to see her off for miles, then walked to greet her, and when told he had gone far he said in the speaker's telling: this is the wife of our Prophet in this world and the next, this is she in whose lap the Prophet died, this is she whose father was the most beloved of the people of earth to the Messenger of God — she is my mother before she is yours (all paraphrased; the line on who accompanied her return is garbled: "her sons returned with her"). (needs_source) {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep23 00:37:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep23 00:38:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep23 00:38:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep23 00:39:00}
- He passes over the attendees' comments: the lesson of the etiquette of disagreement, and that the Companions who preceded us in faith are our brothers to be prayed for only as the verse says (linked to Surat al-Hashr), and a summarised comment on Uthman's stand in the fitna and the reaction of the phase (already in the perspectives). {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep23 00:39:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep23 00:41:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep23 00:41:30} [[passage/quran-59-10|Surat al-Hashr, verse 10]]
- He tells of Ali's justice the famous armour story (see [[event/shurayh-armor-judgment|Shurayh's judgment on the armour]]): he found a Jewish man in the market holding the armour and said it is mine — an armour he had defended the Messenger of God with, in his telling — and they took their case to the judge [[person/shurayh-al-qadi|Shurayh]], who said: sit, Ali ibn Abi Talib, beside your opponent, and did not say Amir al-Mu'minin; he asked: do you have proof? he said I have no proof, so he judged the armour for the man; the man said in his telling: by God this is not the judgment of the people of earth, this is the judgment of God's prophets, and I bear witness there is no god but God and Muhammad is the Messenger of God; and Ali gave him the armour as a gift (all paraphrased). (needs_source) {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep23 00:43:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep23 00:43:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep23 00:44:00}
- He tells of Ali's asceticism while Amir al-Mu'minin ruling the greatest land in his telling: he stood in the market selling his sword, saying: who will buy this sword that used to defend the Messenger of God — were it not that I want the price of a garment I would never sell it; and he rode his donkey letting his legs dangle, saying: I am the one who humbled the world (the phrase is partly garbled in the transcript); and when he bought food for his children from the market and they offered to carry it for him he said: the father of the children has most right to carry it (all paraphrased). (needs_source) {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep23 00:44:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep23 00:44:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep23 00:45:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep23 00:45:30}
- He relates that Ali was the first to found the science of nahw: when those entering Islam grew many and error crept into recitation, he summoned [[person/abu-al-aswad-al-duali|Abu al-Aswad al-Du'ali]] and said he wanted to lay down the foundations of the language, wrote some pages containing the principles of nahw and handed them to him saying: do nahw like this nahw, and from that came the word nahw (paraphrased; see [[concept/ibtida-al-nahw|the beginning of nahw]]). (needs_source) {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep23 00:45:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep23 00:46:00}
- He mentions that Ali's age was sixty-three, the Prophet's own age, but that he had grown very weary: he says the people of al-Sham entered his obedience while the people of Iraq on whom he relied let him down (the line is garbled in the transcript; in the well-known accounts the people of al-Sham opposed him), so he came to pray in the speaker's telling: O God relieve me of them and relieve them of me (paraphrased). (needs_source) {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep23 00:46:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep23 00:46:30}
- He relays the Prophet's sayings to Ali (all paraphrased, no wording): whoever loves you has loved me and whoever hates you has hated me; and you will not die until this is dyed from this, meaning the beard from the blood of the head; and severe hardship will befall you after me — Ali asked: in safety of my religion? he said: in safety of your religion — he said: then I do not care; and his question about the most wretched of people, in his account including the one who hamstrung the she-camel and the one who strikes Ali (garbled lines). (needs_source) {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep23 00:46:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep23 00:47:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep23 00:47:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep23 00:48:00}
- He relates that Ali in Kufa told his companions he would not die of his ailment but when his beard is dyed from his head that would be his death, and he took to repeating a poet's line on preparing for death (the line is garbled, not transcribed); and when a guard came to watch him he asked them: from the people of earth or the people of heaven? they said of earth, and he said nothing befalls on earth but by a command from heaven, and he has two angels guarding him who leave him to his decree when God's decree comes (paraphrased; and he cites the verse of the successive guards). (needs_source) {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep23 00:48:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep23 00:49:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep23 00:49:30} [[passage/quran-13-11|Surat al-Ra'd, verse 11]]
- He relates that three of the Kharijites agreed to kill the three great men of the ummah: Ali, Muawiya and [[person/amr-ibn-al-as|Amr ibn al-As]], on one day, 17 Ramadan, and the speaker comments on the day's sign: the day of [[event/battle-of-badr|Badr]] on which Ali had defended the Prophet (see [[event/kharijite-plot-against-muawiya-and-amr|the Kharijite plot]]). (needs_source) {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep23 00:50:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep23 00:50:30}
- He relates that [[person/abd-al-rahman-ibn-muljam|Abd al-Rahman ibn Muljam]] (the transcript reads "ibn Mawlijim" and "ibn Maljam", garbled) entered Kufa at the start of Ramadan and hid, and named his sword and sharpened it forty nights, and he met a woman who pleased him who was of the Kharijites, and she made her mahr the killing of Ali, so he married her on that condition (all in the speaker's telling). (needs_source) {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep23 00:50:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep23 00:51:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep23 00:51:30}
- He relates that Ali sensed his term was near, so in his last week he broke his fast one day at [[person/hasan-ibn-ali|al-Hasan]]'s, one day at al-Husayn's and one day at Abd Allah ibn Ja'far his nephew's, eating only three mouthfuls, saying: I love to meet God khamis, that is, with an empty stomach, to enjoy meeting his Lord (paraphrased). (needs_source) {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep23 00:51:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep23 00:52:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep23 00:52:30}
- He relates that he rose for the dawn prayer on 17 Ramadan going out to lead the Muslims, and the geese and chickens of the house cried at him, and the women came to shoo them, and he said: leave them, they are mourning me; the speaker comments that even the beasts know the worth of the righteous (paraphrased; his comment). (needs_source) {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep23 00:52:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep23 00:53:00}
- He tells the strike: Ibn Muljam came out at him and struck him hard sword-blows that split his head, his beard filled with blood, and Ali smiled and said: the Messenger of God spoke true; he was carried to his house, and Ibn Muljam was brought bound before him, and Ali asked him: what drove you to this, did I not treat you well? he said: I sharpened this sword of mine forty nights and prayed God to kill the worst of people with it; Ali said: rather it is you who will be killed by it (all paraphrased). (needs_source) {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep23 00:53:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep23 00:53:30}
- He relates his testament to his sons about his killer: be good to him and better his confinement; if I live I am most entitled to him, whether retaliation or pardon; and if I die, kill him but beware mutilating him, and beware killing anyone else with him, for God does not love the transgressors (paraphrased). (needs_source) {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep23 00:53:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep23 00:54:00}
- He relates that the blow fell on Friday and he lived through Saturday until 19 Ramadan, and in his last two days he said nothing but one word: la ilaha illa Allah (the death on 17 Ramadan given in the episode's opening; the transcript reads here "year 82 AH" which is garbled; the date the speaker adopts is 40 AH). (needs_source) {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep23 00:54:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep23 00:54:30}
- He relates that al-Hasan and al-Husayn washed and shrouded him and al-Hasan prayed over him, and he was buried in Kufa in a place whose grave is not certainly known, for fear the Kharijites would exhume it (see [[event/death-of-ali-ibn-abi-talib|the death of Ali ibn Abi Talib]]). (needs_source) {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep23 00:54:30}
- He relates that al-Hasan held the caliphate after him six months then ceded it to Muawiya ibn Abi Sufyan sparing blood, fulfilling in the speaker's telling the Prophet's hadith about al-Hasan as a child: this son of mine is a sayyid through whom God may reconcile two great parties of the Muslims (paraphrased; see [[event/bayat-al-hasan-ibn-ali|the pledge to al-Hasan ibn Ali]]); and the speaker reckons the rightly-guided caliphate ran exactly thirty years to the day, from Rabi' al-Awwal 11 AH when Abu Bakr took office to Rabi' al-Awwal 41 when al-Hasan ceded, fulfilling in his telling the Prophet's word that the caliphate would be thirty years then become kingship (paraphrased). (needs_source) {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep23 00:54:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep23 00:55:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep23 00:55:30}
- He closes recalling Ali defending the Prophet at Badr and Uhud and bearing the banner at [[event/battle-of-khaybar|Khaybar]], and prays that God join the listeners with him and the noble Companions in paradise, closing the series at the end of the rightly guided caliphs (the speaker's words and prayer). {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep23 00:55:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep23 00:56:00} (the speaker's view)

## Left out of this episode 23

Not written from episode 23: the identification of "the imam of the Haram of Mecca" the speaker consulted (garbled; 00:02:30); the names and numbers of the fitna's dead, since the speaker chose not to narrate them at all; the name of the Kharijite woman Ibn Muljam married (not given; 00:51:00); the name of the man who asked Talha whose man he was (not given; 00:35:30); the poet's line Ali kept repeating (garbled; 00:48:30); verification of who accompanied the lady Aisha on her return ("her sons returned with her", garbled; 00:39:00); and the attribution of the verse "the fingers when they gather" (unattributed; 00:20:00). Garbled lines read with caution: "year 82 AH" for Ali's death (a reading not adopted; the opening states 40 AH; 00:54:00); "the people of al-Sham entered his obedience" (garbled and contrary to the well-known order of events; 00:46:30); the variance of five days versus a week between Uthman's death and the pledge (00:01:00 and 00:18:00); "al-Qa'qa' ibn Amk" read as al-Qa'qa' ibn Amr (00:38:30); "Amr ibn Qurmuz" read as Amr ibn Jurmuz (00:34:00); "ibn Mawlijim / ibn Maljam" read as Ibn Muljam (00:50:30); the line justifying that the Muslims left al-Zubayr's killer alone ("when he became the Muslims' caliph they left him"; 00:34:30); transcript repetition loops discarded as non-speech (00:08:00, 00:42:30 and 00:48:00). The wording of all sayings of the Prophet and the Companions is paraphrased, not reproduced, and marked as needing a source; the dates, figures and names are the speaker's, from a machine transcript that has not been listened to. The events of the fitna are left at the speaker's own description — he did not narrate their details — and are flagged for a sourced perspectives pass.

## Episode 24: introduction to the Mothers of the Believers, the Prophet's wives, as the speaker presents them

:::perspectives
- **The speaker's view (opinion):** he presents the episode as an answer to the charge made by "some Orientalists" — his term — that the Prophet's multiple marriages were driven by lust, and he chooses to answer "with reason," not with fervour: the stages of the Prophet's marital life and the circumstances of each marriage are his evidence, and he calls the bearer of the charge "malicious and has seen nothing" (the speaker's apologetic polemic; the museum makes no judgement on the polemic or the reply). {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep24 00:29:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep24 00:30:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep24 00:30:30}
- **The speaker's view (opinion):** he divides the Prophet's marriages into "Muhammad the man," who married once for human need — Khadija — and "Muhammad the Messenger," who married the rest for the message, ethics and mercy, counting even the marriage to Aisha as "for prophethood" (the speaker's didactic framing, not a historical classification). {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep24 00:35:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep24 00:35:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep24 00:36:00}
- **The speaker's view (opinion):** he settles on twelve wives for the Prophet, among them [[person/mariya-dhat-al-qirtayn|Maria the Copt]], while [[person/rayhana-bint-zayd|Rayhana]] "is not among the wives"; the number remaining at the Prophet's death is ten in his count (the number of the wives and whether Maria counts as a wife are known scholarly disagreements; the speaker's words). {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep24 00:14:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep24 00:17:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep24 00:26:00}
- **The speaker's view (opinion):** explaining the Prophet's marriage to the young Aisha he gives two reasons: that she would live many years after him and carry the knowledge, and that a girl in the desert environment reaches maturity earlier than in an icy one, and the custom of that time took account of it (Aisha's age at marriage is a well-known contested question in recent scholarship; the speaker's words as delivered). {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep24 00:42:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep24 00:43:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep24 00:43:30} (needs_source)
- **The speaker's view (opinion):** among the reasons for the marriages he names "the completion of Islamic legislation," giving the example of the abolition of the adoption rule through the Prophet's marriage to Zaynab bint Jahsh (adoption and the marriage of Zaynab are among the interpreted points of the sira; left at the speaker's brevity). {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep24 00:47:30} (needs_source)
- **The speaker's view (opinion):** at the end he gives men an admonition on polygamy: it is a right bound by strict conditions — justice and equal spending and regard for the first wife's feelings — and whoever cannot carry them is "sinful"; he notes the Prophet began his marriages only after the ummah settled in Medina, and states that he is not a mufti (the speaker's exhortation, not a fatwa; the museum gives no ruling). {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep24 00:52:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep24 00:52:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep24 00:53:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep24 00:53:30}
:::

- The speaker announces that he had meant to end "Wa Nal9a al-Aheba" at the close of the men's episodes, but repeated questions on the website — "where are the women?" — moved him to add a whole run on the Prophet's wives and the women Companions; he says delaying the women was deliberate, to gather them in one phase (the episode opens a new phase after the rightly-guided-caliphs run closed). {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep24 00:00:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep24 00:00:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep24 00:01:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep24 00:01:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep24 00:02:00}
- Among his preparation books he names "Usd al-Ghaba" by Ibn al-Athir (read [[person/ibn-al-athir-izz-al-din|Ibn al-Athir al-Jazari]]), saying he found in it a huge volume devoted to the women Companions, which he took as proof of their giving and sacrifice (the transcript reads "Ibn al-Athiq"; the speaker's characterisation, the book itself not consulted). {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep24 00:02:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep24 00:02:30} (needs_source)
- He lists what he calls the women's firsts in Islam: the first to prostrate, believe and carry the call after the Prophet was a woman, the first given glad tidings of paradise in the ummah was a woman, the first martyr in Islam was a woman, and "the first martyr in Europe" (garbled) among the Companion women martyrs was a woman. {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep24 00:03:30} (needs_source)
- He reads the Quran's two examples for the believers as two women: Pharaoh's wife ([[person/asiya|Asiya]]) and Maryam bint Imran ([[person/maryam|Maryam]]), arguing from them for the standing of women (alluding to Surat al-Tahrim, verses 11–12; he does not name the sura in the episode). [[passage/quran-66-11|Surat al-Tahrim, verse 11]] {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep24 00:03:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep24 00:04:00}
- He sets four intentions for the wives' episodes: a role model women can imitate, knowledge of the fine details of the Prophet's home life because his life holds no secrets, learning marital happiness, and feeling the motherhood of the Mothers of the Believers for every believer (the speaker's own declared didactic aims). {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep24 00:05:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep24 00:06:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep24 00:08:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep24 00:11:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep24 00:11:30}
- He grounds the "your mother" call in the Quranic text that the Prophet is closer to the believers than their own selves and his wives are their mothers, and relates that the Companions addressed the Prophet's wives as "O mother," and that Muhammad ibn Abi Bakr would say "O mother" to his sister Aisha (the speaker's account). [[passage/quran-33-6|Surat al-Ahzab, verse 6]] {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep24 00:08:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep24 00:09:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep24 00:21:00} (needs_source)
- He runs a quiz among the audience on the number of the Prophet's wives; answers vary between nine, eleven, twelve and thirteen, then he settles the number at twelve, of whom two died in the Prophet's lifetime: Khadija bint Khuwaylid and Zaynab bint Khuzayma (the speaker's figures; the number of wives is disagreed upon among the scholars). {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep24 00:12:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep24 00:13:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep24 00:14:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep24 00:21:30} (needs_source)
- He gives the names of the twelve wives in order of marriage as displayed on screen: [[person/khadija|Khadija bint Khuwaylid]], then [[person/sawda-bint-zama|Sawda bint Zam'a]], then [[person/aisha|Aisha bint Abi Bakr]], then [[person/hafsa|Hafsa bint Umar ibn al-Khattab]] (the transcript reads "Amr ibn al-Khattab"; read Umar), then [[person/zaynab-bint-khuzayma|Zaynab bint Khuzayma]], then [[person/umm-salama|Umm Salama, Hind bint Abi Umayya]], then [[person/zaynab-bint-jahsh|Zaynab bint Jahsh]], then [[person/juwayriya-bint-al-harith|Juwayriyya bint al-Harith]], then a ninth wife not clearly named (garbled line), then [[person/umm-habiba-bint-abi-sufyan|Umm Habiba, Ramla bint Abi Sufyan]] tenth, then [[person/mariya-dhat-al-qirtayn|Maria]] eleventh, then [[person/maymuna-bint-al-harith|Maymuna]] twelfth (the ordering and count are the speaker's, unchecked). {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep24 00:23:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep24 00:24:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep24 00:28:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep24 00:29:00} (needs_source)
- He remarks on the list: only one was a virgin — Aisha — the rest previously married; all the wives are Arabs from the Peninsula except Maria the Egyptian; Safiyya had been Jewish and Maria Christian, and both embraced Islam before the Prophet married them (the speaker's tally and classification). {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep24 00:25:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep24 00:26:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep24 00:26:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep24 00:27:00} (needs_source)
- He divides the Prophet's marital life into five stages: unmarried to twenty-five; then one wife (Khadija), fifteen years his senior, previously married with children, until fifty; then no marriage from fifty to fifty-two; then multiple marriages to sixty; then the verse forbidding further marriage until his death at sixty-three (alluding to Surat al-Ahzab 52; the speaker's figures). [[passage/quran-33-52|Surat al-Ahzab, verse 52]] {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep24 00:30:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep24 00:31:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep24 00:31:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep24 00:32:00} (needs_source)
