- He argues that "lust" appearing suddenly after fifty-two, when every day held a battle, does not enter reason, and mentions a common saying about a man revisiting his youth between forty and fifty, replying that the time the Prophet spent with his wives was little (the speaker's argument). {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep24 00:32:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep24 00:32:30}
- He relates that Sawda was the first widow in Islam, her husband dying while both were emigrants to Abyssinia with her people in Mecca unbelievers (the speaker's description), and that the Prophet married her out of shelter and honour, staying with her about a year or two before Aisha (the speaker's figures and details, unchecked). {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep24 00:33:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep24 00:34:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep24 00:34:30} (needs_source)
- He notes that prophets before Muhammad practised polygamy: Ibrahim, Ya'qub, Dawud and Sulayman, as in the heavenly books ([[person/ibrahim|Ibrahim]], [[person/yaqub|Ya'qub]], [[person/dawud|Dawud]], [[person/sulayman|Sulayman]]). {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep24 00:36:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep24 00:37:00}
- He recounts a story from the book "al-Mar'a bayn al-Fiqh wa-l-Qanun" by Dr [[person/mustafa-al-sibai|Mustafa al-Siba'i]]: on a visit to Ireland in the fifties, the supervising father of a centre told him plainly they cannot respect a man who married nine women; al-Siba'i answered that Dawud and Sulayman — respected among them — married by the tens near a hundred, and the man apologised (the speaker's telling of the book; the book not consulted). {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep24 00:37:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep24 00:37:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep24 00:38:00} (needs_source)
- He makes the first reason for the marriages the conveying of the religion: the Prophet's house had to receive those who would memorise the details of his life and carry them to the generations, among them Aisha and Hafsa; he says the most prolific narrators from the Prophet were Abu Hurayra then Aisha, calls Aisha "the most learned of the Muslims in the duties and supererogatory acts" (paraphrased, unsourced), and says she died in 52 AH having lived after the Prophet about 22 years (the transcript and figures do not add up; garbled and unchecked). {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep24 00:38:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep24 00:39:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep24 00:40:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep24 00:40:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep24 00:42:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep24 00:42:30} (needs_source)
- He makes the second reason the ummah's cohesion after him: the four rightly-guided caliphs were bound to the Prophet by lineage and marriage — [[person/abu-bakr|Abu Bakr]] father of Aisha and [[person/umar-ibn-al-khattab|Umar]] father of Hafsa, [[person/uthman-ibn-affan|Uthman]] married [[person/ruqayya-bint-muhammad|Ruqayya]] then [[person/umm-kulthum-bint-muhammad|Umm Kulthum]], the Prophet's daughters, and [[person/ali-ibn-abi-talib|Ali]] married [[person/fatima|Fatima]] (the speaker's reading of kinship, not a judgement on history). {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep24 00:43:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep24 00:44:00}
- He makes the third reason mercy toward widows and the unprotected: like Sawda; Umm Salama whose husband died a martyr leaving children; and Umm Habiba bint Abi Sufyan who emigrated with her husband [[person/ubaydullah-ibn-jahsh|Ubaydullah ibn Jahsh]] to Abyssinia where he died (the details of the husband's situation garbled in the transcript), her marriage to the Prophet honouring her in the face of her father [[person/abu-sufyan-ibn-harb|Abu Sufyan]], then the Prophet's first enemy (the speaker's account; Abu Sufyan's words paraphrased, not sourced). {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep24 00:45:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep24 00:45:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep24 00:46:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep24 00:46:30} (needs_source)
- He makes one reason embracing whoever enters Islam from other faiths: so the Prophet married [[person/safiyya-bint-huyayy|Safiyya]] daughter of Huyay ibn Akhtab, the Jewish leader of Banu al-Nadir whom he describes as the head of unbelief in the battle of the Trench (the speaker's characterisation of Huyay ibn Akhtab; [[event/battle-of-the-trench|the battle of the Trench]]), that people might learn whoever enters the religion is accepted, embraced and loved even from a house of enmity (the speaker's reasoning). {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep24 00:47:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep24 00:48:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep24 00:48:30}
- He makes one reason binding a distant land to the Prophet by kinship: so he married Maria the Egyptian Copt, citing the Prophet's saying about the Egyptians that they are the best soldiers of the earth (paraphrased, unsourced), saying the Egyptians take pride until the Day of Judgement that the Prophet's son Ibrahim is from them (the speaker's reading). {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep24 00:48:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep24 00:49:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep24 00:49:30} (needs_source)
- He relates about [[person/juwayriya-bint-al-harith|Juwayriyya bint al-Harith]]: she was taken captive with her tribe in a campaign; when the Prophet married her the Companions said the captives were now the Prophet's in-laws and freed them, so all Banu al-Mustaliq entered Islam, and Aisha is reported to have called her "the greatest blessing of women upon her people" (paraphrased, unsourced; the campaign is [[event/expedition-of-banu-al-mustaliq|the expedition of Banu al-Mustaliq]]). {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep24 00:49:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep24 00:50:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep24 00:50:30} (needs_source)
- He rules that multiple marriage was among the Prophet's special dispensations, not to be imitated, like the special dispensation of continuous fasting (wisal), in which he showed the Companions that he spends the night fed by his Lord and said "I am not like you" (paraphrase of the wisal hadith; the wording unsourced). {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep24 00:50:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep24 00:51:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep24 00:51:30} (needs_source)
- He closes by announcing the next episode is the first of the mothers, [[person/khadija|Khadija bint Khuwaylid]]. {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep24 00:54:00}

## Left out of this episode 24

Not written from episode 24: the identification of the ninth wife in the marriage order (the line between Juwayriyya and Umm Habiba garbled; 00:28:30); the details of the situation of Umm Habiba's husband Ubaydullah ibn Jahsh in Abyssinia ("a problem befell him and he died"; 00:45:30); the line "she refused to be brought a fruit" in Umm Habiba's story (garbled; 00:45:30); the phrase "the first martyr in Europe" (garbled; 00:03:30); the names of footballers and singers in the speaker's examples and the joking "a thousand dollars" prize of the quiz (banter; 00:09:30 and 00:22:00); the attribution "Amr ibn al-Khattab" read as Umar ibn al-Khattab (00:24:30); the reckoning of Aisha's death ("52 AH" with "she lived 22 years after the Prophet" does not add up; 00:40:30); the total of hadith narrated by the wives ("three three hadith" garbled; 00:42:30); Abu Sufyan's words on his daughter's marriage ("that man finds no" garbled; 00:46:00); the description of Sawda's husband ("while emigrating" garbled; read cautiously as dying an emigrant; 00:33:30); and the identification of "the centre" al-Siba'i visited in Ireland (00:37:00). Transcript repetition loops discarded as non-speech: 00:07:30, 00:12:30, 00:13:30, 00:14:00, 00:20:00, 00:25:00, 00:28:30, 00:33:00 and 00:37:00. The wording of all sayings of the Prophet, the Companions and the supplications is paraphrased, not reproduced, and marked as needing a source; the dates, figures, names and ordering are the speaker's, from a machine transcript that has not been listened to. The questions of the charge and reply, polygamy, the number of wives, Maria and Rayhana, Aisha's age and adoption are left at the speaker's own description and flagged for a sourced perspectives pass.

## Episode 25: Khadija bint Khuwaylid, the first of the Mothers of the Believers: lineage, merit, marriage, support and death, as the speaker tells it

:::perspectives
- **The speaker's view (opinion):** he presents the story of the Prophet's marriage to Khadija as "the greatest love story in history," comparing it with Romeo and Juliet and with Qays and Layla, which he describes as love stories that ended before marriage or lived only as tales (the speaker's didactic preference; the museum makes no comparison; the competing stories are literary). {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep25 00:33:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep25 00:34:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep25 00:34:30}
- **The speaker's view (opinion):** he tells that it was Khadija who sought the marriage through her friend Nafisa bint Munya, while the Prophet knew nothing of it (the betrothal story as he gives it; the sira sources differ over who proposed and how, so it is left at his telling). {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep25 00:28:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep25 00:28:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep25 00:30:00} (needs_source)
- **The speaker's view (opinion):** he gives her ages: forty when she married the Prophet, who was twenty-five; fifty-five at the mission; sixty-five at her death, ten years before the Hijra (Khadija's age at marriage and at death is a well-known disagreement in the sources; the speaker's figures as delivered). {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep25 00:18:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep25 00:11:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep25 00:49:00} (needs_source)
- **The speaker's view (opinion):** he says Khadija was the first to steady the Prophet after the revelation, the first of the ummah to prostrate to God and the first to perform the duties, and urges women to feel their worth in Islam (the precedence of belief among Khadija, Ali and Abu Bakr is a well-known scholarly disagreement; the speaker's exhortation). {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep25 00:42:30} (needs_source)
- **The speaker's view (opinion):** he generalises that women's sense of the divine is higher than men's, and that a woman near to God is "better than a hundred men," citing Khadija as the first to sense his prophethood (the speaker's homiletic generalisation, not a museum claim). {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep25 00:29:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep25 00:29:30}
- **The speaker's view (opinion):** he calls on young men and women to choose a spouse for religion rather than looks or money, explains the early divorces of his time by houses not built on faith and purpose, and invokes the hadith "a woman is married for four things" rendered in meaning (the speaker's contemporary counsel; the hadith wording is not fixed). {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep25 00:13:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep25 00:14:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep25 00:15:00} (needs_source)
:::

- He opens with a quick quiz re-fixing the names of the Prophet's wives in marriage order as shown on screen; the audience answers in a varying, overlapping order until the twelve settle (the screen order in this episode places [[person/safiyya-bint-huyayy|Safiyya]] and [[person/juwayriya-bint-al-harith|Juwayriyya]] differently from the list the previous episode displayed; the joking "fifty dollars" prize is banter). {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep25 00:00:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep25 00:01:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep25 00:01:30} (needs_source)
- He lists the references he prepares the mothers' episodes from: Ibn al-Athir's "Usd al-Ghaba" with its volume on the women, a book "Umm al-Mu'minin Khadija bint Khuwaylid, a lady in the heart of the Chosen One" by an author the transcript reads "Dr Muhammad Abd al-Amin," the book "the Prophet's wives in our contemporary reality" by Jasim al-Mutawwa', the cassette series "Immortal Women" of Tariq al-Suwaydan and "Women of the House of Prophethood" of Shaykh Safwat al-Hijazi, a book by Dr Aisha Abd al-Rahman whose title the transcript garbles and the museum reads cautiously as "tarajim sayyidat bayt al-nubuwwa," and "al-Isaba fi tamyiz al-sahaba" (the books as he names them; not consulted; the two garbled titles are museum readings). {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep25 00:02:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep25 00:02:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep25 00:03:00} (needs_source)
- He opens Khadija's story with the theme of God's choosing: God chose Adam, Noah, the house of Ibrahim and the house of Imran above the worlds, then Muhammad's ummah, then the Companions, then the Prophet's household, then his wives who "are not like other women" — on condition of piety, he says — then chose Khadija among them (he alludes to the verses in meaning; Surat al-Ahzab 32). [[passage/quran-3-33|Surat Al Imran, verse 33]] [[passage/quran-33-32|Surat al-Ahzab, verse 32]] {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep25 00:04:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep25 00:04:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep25 00:05:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep25 00:06:00}
- He gives her lineage: Khadija bint Khuwaylid ibn Asad ibn Abd al-Uzza ibn Qusay, meeting the Prophet at the fifth forefather Qusay; her mother Fatima meets him at the seventh, Lu'ayy — making her the Prophet's closest wife in lineage on both sides (the speaker's genealogy as counted; unchecked). {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep25 00:07:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep25 00:07:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep25 00:08:00} (needs_source)
- He says the Prophet named his daughter [[person/fatima|Fatima]] in honour of Khadija's mother, who had died, and sees in that a loyalty God honoured by making all the Prophet's offspring come from Fatima, Khadija's daughter (the speaker's account of the naming; unsourced). {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep25 00:08:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep25 00:09:00} (needs_source)
- He lists her qualities: standing and honour above all Mecca, a mind "weighing tens of men," wisdom, intelligence, tenderness and a rare purity of fitra; he says she never prostrated to an idol and was "on the religion of Ibrahim" before Islam, and that her famous title in Quraysh was "al-Tahira," the Pure, for her chastity (the speaker's description; the title and her pre-Islamic religion unsourced). {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep25 00:09:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep25 00:10:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep25 00:11:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep25 00:12:00} (needs_source)
- He names her two marriages before the Prophet: a man named Atiq al-Makhzumi then Abu Hala al-Tamimi, a son and a daughter from each; she inherited much wealth and grew it many times over in trade; she stayed three years unmarried refusing Quraysh's suitors, with four children whose youngest, [[person/hind-ibn-abi-hala|Hind ibn Abi Hala]], stayed with her (names and order on his telling; "Abu Hala al-Tamimi" and "Hind" read from overlapping lines). {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep25 00:17:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep25 00:17:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep25 00:18:00} (needs_source)
- He tells how she employed men in her trade and after each journey asked them about the man who had gone with them, and how her trusted servant [[person/maysara|Maysara]] was her confidant; [[person/abu-talib|Abu Talib]] came asking her to employ the Prophet in her trade to Syria and Yemen — the Prophet then about twenty-two on the speaker's count — and she answered in meaning that she would do it for his uncle's standing, let alone a noble kinsman (her reply garbled in the transcript and given in meaning; the Prophet's age is the speaker's figure). {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep25 00:20:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep25 00:20:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep25 00:21:00} (needs_source)
- He gives Maysara's three tales from the Syrian journey: a cloud shading the Prophet wherever he went; a tree bowing its branches to shade him as he slept in the sun, until a monk the transcript garbles — read as Nestor — said only a prophet sits beneath it; and a Jewish man in the Syrian market who tested him in buying and, when he refused to swear by other than God, told Maysara "cling to this man, he is the prophet of the end of time" (Maysara's reports on the speaker's telling; unsourced). {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep25 00:22:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep25 00:22:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep25 00:24:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep25 00:24:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep25 00:25:30} (needs_source)
- He says Khadija had stored knowledge from her cousin [[person/waraqa-ibn-nawfal|Waraqa ibn Nawfal]], who used to tell her of a prophet soon to come out of the sanctuary, and he tells a second incident: a Jewish man entered a gathering of Quraysh's women on a feast night announcing the nearness of the last prophet's time, and only Khadija responded among them (the speaker's two anecdotes; unsourced). {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep25 00:26:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep25 00:27:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep25 00:27:30} (needs_source)
- He tells that she began showing signs of interest and asking after the Prophet, until her friend [[person/nafisa-bint-munya|Nafisa bint Munya]] noticed and said "I cannot but wish him to be a husband for you; do you permit me to arrange it?" — she permitted her; Nafisa went to the Prophet describing a beautiful, noble woman of good character, named Khadija bint Khuwaylid when he asked, and he said "and would she accept me?" (the dialogue on his telling, from garbled lines, in meaning). {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep25 00:28:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep25 00:28:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep25 00:30:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep25 00:32:30} (needs_source)
- Of the marriage details he names [[person/abu-talib|Abu Talib]] as the one who made the address, and [[person/hamza|Hamza ibn Abd al-Muttalib]] as the one who "made the wedding feast" on the transcript's reading, and her guardian in the contract the transcript reads as "Waraqa ibn Nawfal her cousin" (garbled lines read with caution; the guardian in the sources is not Waraqa, so the reading is recorded, not the fact). {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep25 00:34:30} (needs_source)
- He says they lived together twenty-five years — fifteen before the mission and ten after, until her death — and gives their children as the sons al-Qasim, Abdullah and al-Tahir, and four daughters: the eldest [[person/zaynab-bint-muhammad|Zaynab]], then [[person/ruqayya-bint-muhammad|Ruqayya]], then [[person/umm-kulthum-bint-muhammad|Umm Kulthum]], then [[person/fatima|Fatima]] (the count, names and order are the speaker's; the sources differ on the Prophet's sons). {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep25 00:34:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep25 00:35:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep25 00:35:30} (needs_source)
- He says she raised in her house beyond her own children: [[person/ali-ibn-abi-talib|Ali ibn Abi Talib]], [[person/zayd-ibn-haritha|Zayd ibn Haritha]] and [[person/zubayr-ibn-al-awwam|al-Zubayr ibn al-Awwam]], "between her and the lady Safiyya" on the transcript's reading (a garbled reading; Safiyya bint Abd al-Muttalib was al-Zubayr's mother; the raising is on the speaker's telling). {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep25 00:36:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep25 00:36:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep25 00:37:00} (needs_source)
- He describes her fifteen years before the mission: the Prophet worshipping in the cave of Hira while she climbed to him with provisions herself in the dark of night, nearing fifty-five on his count, not knowing he would be a prophet and not complaining (the speaker's description of her service before the revelation). {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep25 00:37:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep25 00:38:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep25 00:38:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep25 00:39:30}
- He recounts the night of the revelation on the Prophet's own telling as the speaker relays it: the angel pressing him and saying "read" three times until the first verse descended, and the Prophet returning trembling to Khadija saying "cover me, wrap me" and "I feared for myself" (he alludes to the first verse in meaning; Surat al-Alaq). [[passage/quran-96-1|Surat al-Alaq, verse 1]] {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep25 00:39:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep25 00:40:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep25 00:40:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep25 00:41:30} (needs_source)
- He gives her known answer in meaning: "No, by God, God will never disgrace you," then counts his keeping the kinship bond, honouring the guest, providing for the destitute, carrying the burden and aiding against the strokes of fate, and says "I hope you will be the prophet of this ummah" — then takes him by the hand to her cousin Waraqa ibn Nawfal (the hadith wording not fixed; the meaning is given). {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep25 00:42:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep25 00:42:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep25 00:43:00} (needs_source)
- He tells Waraqa's words: "this is the Namus that was given to Musa and Isa" on the transcript's reading, Waraqa's wish to be "jadha'an," a strong youth, on the day his people would drive him out, and that no man brought what the Prophet brought without being opposed (the speaker's telling; the wording unsourced). {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep25 00:43:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep25 00:44:00} (needs_source)
- He describes her effort after the mission, entering her sixties: by day spreading Islam among the women, using her standing and position to protect the Prophet, by night buying slaves with her money and spending on the Muslims; bearing her daughter Ruqayya's emigration with [[person/uthman-ibn-affan|Uthman]] to Abyssinia, and the divorce of her daughters Ruqayya and Umm Kulthum by the sons of [[person/abu-lahab|Abu Lahab]] to spite the Prophet (her circumstances on his telling; [[event/first-migration-to-abyssinia|the first migration to Abyssinia]]). {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep25 00:44:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep25 00:45:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep25 00:45:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep25 00:46:00} (needs_source)
- He tells her stand in [[event/boycott-of-banu-hashim|the boycott of the ravine of Abu Talib]], about three years, ending three years before the Hijra on his count: Quraysh told her to stay honoured in her house and she answered "by God I will only be where the Muslims are," and went down into the ravine; when her people smuggled food to her she said "by God I shall not eat until the Muslims eat" and gave it to their weak and their children (the words on his telling; unsourced). {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep25 00:47:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep25 00:47:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep25 00:48:00} (needs_source)
- He tells Jibril's descent with the greeting: he tells the Prophet "God conveys His peace to Khadija" and gives her glad tidings of a palace of qasab in paradise with no noise and no toil (rendering of a known hadith; the wording not fixed). {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep25 00:49:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep25 00:49:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep25 00:50:00} (needs_source)
- He says she died at sixty-five and the year was named [[event/year-of-sorrow|the Year of Sorrow]] for the Prophet's grief until the Companions feared for him; the transcript attributes the naming to "Umar ibn Yasir" (a garbled reading, perhaps Ammar ibn Yasir; Khadija died years before the Hijra). {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep25 00:48:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep25 00:50:30} (needs_source)
- He tells the Prophet's loyalty after her death: her sister Hala bint Khuwaylid asking permission and him rejoicing at the likeness of her voice to Khadija's; his distributing the meat of a sacrifice to "Khadija's beloved ones"; and his words to Aisha when she found his remembrance of Khadija too much — "I was granted love of her" in meaning (the anecdotes on his telling; the wording unsourced). {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep25 00:51:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep25 00:51:30} (needs_source)
- He tells the story of Khadija's necklace: her daughter [[person/zaynab-bint-muhammad|Zaynab]] sends from Mecca a necklace that had been Khadija's as ransom for her husband [[person/abu-al-as-ibn-al-rabi|Abu al-As ibn al-Rabi]], captive at [[event/battle-of-badr|Badr]]; the Prophet is moved and asks the Companions to release her captive and return the necklace, and they accept, and he orders him back to Zaynab (the speaker's telling; unsourced; the dialogue in meaning). {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep25 00:52:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep25 00:52:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep25 00:53:00} (needs_source)
- He tells the moment of [[event/conquest-of-mecca|the conquest of Mecca]], about fourteen years after her death: an old woman approaches and he spreads his cloak for her and sits talking with her an hour; Aisha asks and he says "this is a friend of Khadija's — we were remembering the old days of Khadija"; and when Aisha says God gave him better than her, he answers "no, by God, God gave me no better than her," counting her belief when people disbelieved, her trusting him when people called him a liar, her aid with her wealth, and that God granted him children by her (the dialogue on his telling, in the meaning of a known hadith; the wording not fixed). {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep25 00:53:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep25 00:54:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep25 00:54:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep25 00:55:00} (needs_source)
- He closes with two hadiths in meaning: "no women were perfected save four: Maryam bint Imran, Asiya the wife of Pharaoh, Khadija bint Khuwaylid and Fatima bint Muhammad," and "the best women of the worlds" naming the same four, and announces the next episode is a new mother of the believers (the wording not fixed). {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep25 00:55:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep25 00:56:00} (needs_source)

## Left out of this episode 25

Not written from episode 25: the names as the audience called them in the opening quiz, out of the screen's order (overlapping voices; 00:01:30); the name of the author of "Umm al-Mu'minin Khadija" ("Dr Muhammad Abd al-Amin," a garbled reading; 00:02:30); the name of the author of the women-of-the-prophetic-house book ("Mint al-Shatiq," read cautiously as Aisha Abd al-Rahman; 00:03:00); the transcript's "nastur al-rahib" read as Nestor the monk (00:24:00); the details of Maysara's dialogues with the monk and with the Jew in the market (overlapping; 00:24:00 to 00:26:00); the name of Khadija's friend ("Nafisa bint Muniha," read as Nafisa bint Munya; 00:28:30); the identification of Khadija's marriage guardian (the transcript reads Waraqa ibn Nawfal, which the sources contradict; the reading is recorded, not the fact; 00:34:30); the ordering of the three sons al-Qasim, Abdullah and al-Tahir (overlapping lines; 00:35:30); the attribution "between her and the lady Safiyya" in al-Zubayr's upbringing (garbled; 00:36:30); the attribution of the Year of Sorrow's naming to "Umar ibn Yasir" (garbled, perhaps Ammar; 00:50:30); the name of Khadija's daughter who emigrated to Abyssinia read "Sara al-balad" then understood as Ruqayya (00:45:30); and the wording of the Prophet's reply to Aisha in the old-woman story ("no, by God" with "O man in the situation" garbled; 00:54:30). Mechanical repetition loops in the transcript, not speech, discarded: 00:30:30, 00:32:00, 00:33:00 and 00:34:30. The wording of all hadiths, dialogues and supplications is rendered in meaning, not fixed, and marked as needing a source; the dates, ages and names are the speaker's, from a machine transcript that has not been listened to. Khadija's age, the precedence of belief, the betrothal story, the naming of Fatima and the tales told of Maysara, Waraqa and the Jewish man are left at the speaker's own description and flagged for a sourced perspectives pass.

## Episode 26: Sawda bint Zam'a then Zaynab bint Khuzayma Umm al-Masakin: the Prophet's household after Khadija, the counsel of Khawla bint Hakim, and the story of Abu Ubayda ibn al-Harith at Badr, as the speaker tells it

:::perspectives
- **The speaker's view (opinion):** he argues that women in Islam were never on the margin of society, counting firsts he attributes to women: the first to prostrate to God after the Prophet was a woman, the first to worship God after him a woman, the first to spend her wealth Khadija, the first given glad tidings of paradise a woman, the first martyr in Islam [[person/sumayya-bint-khayyat|Sumayya]], the first martyred woman in Cyprus [[person/umm-haram-bint-milhan|Umm Haram]], the Prophet's consulting women in the plan of [[event/battle-of-uhud|Uhud]], and his changing a military decision on the day of the conquest in answer to a woman's intercession, read in the transcript as "Umm Hani" (the speaker's didactic argument; some anecdotes unsourced; "Umm Hani" read as [[person/umm-hani-bint-abi-talib|Umm Hani bint Abi Talib]]). {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep26 00:13:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep26 00:13:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep26 00:14:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep26 00:14:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep26 00:15:00} (needs_source)
- **The speaker's view (opinion):** he makes the episode's proof a didactic-hadith one: that Islam honoured women and that whoever frightened women away from the religion deceived them, and that they are honoured and noble in it (the speaker's preaching and generalisation; not the museum's claim). {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep26 00:15:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep26 00:16:00}
- **Audience comments (from the floor, attributed to their speakers):** three audience members commented after Sawda's story: the first made the sa'y between Safa and Marwa an honouring of the lady [[person/hajar|Hagar]] and a proof that the Muslims' civilisational depth is bound to a woman; the second concluded from the Prophet choosing the previously married woman before the virgin and from Sawda giving up her night to Aisha that the motive is faith and that faith and humanity are inseparable; the third made the Prophet's marriage to an older previously married woman a refutation of the Orientalists' claim that he married many wives, saying it was a sacrifice for his little daughters (the audience's words as the transcript gives them; Sawda's giving up her night is an audience member's statement, not the speaker's; the clause "for her father was a disbeliever" in the third comment is garbled). {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep26 00:20:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep26 00:20:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep26 00:21:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep26 00:21:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep26 00:22:00} (needs_source)
- **The speaker's view (opinion):** he makes the reasons for the Prophet's marriage to Zaynab bint Khuzayma three: honouring Abu Ubayda ibn al-Harith after his martyrdom, honouring her, and a message to Banu Abd al-Muttalib in Mecca that their daughter is safe with him (the speaker's reasoning; unsourced). {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep26 00:29:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep26 00:29:30} (needs_source)
:::

- He opens by saying the program nears its end, that each time they finish one of the Prophet's wives they say most of them are done, and he wishes the meeting with them were in paradise, and he frames the program's idea: that a viewer knows a Companion or a mother and says to them on the Day of Judgement "I knew you, I loved you and I tried to imitate you" (the speaker's didactic frame). {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep26 00:00:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep26 00:00:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep26 00:01:00}
- He restates the episodes' rule: the verse kept before the eyes throughout the talk about the Prophet's wives, and he invokes it in meaning (Surat al-Ahzab). [[passage/quran-33-6|Surat al-Ahzab, verse 6]] {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep26 00:01:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep26 00:02:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep26 00:03:00}
- He repeats the wives' quiz in marriage order on the screen and gives the summary: twelve wives, of whom only Khadija and Zaynab bint Khuzayma died in the Prophet's lifetime, and all are from the Arabian Peninsula except [[person/mariya-dhat-al-qirtayn|Maria]] the Egyptian (the speaker's count and ordering as in the previous episode). {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep26 00:04:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep26 00:05:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep26 00:05:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep26 00:06:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep26 00:06:30}
- He repeats the list of references he works from and advises buying them: Usd al-Ghaba by [[person/ibn-al-athir-izz-al-din|Ibn al-Athir]] with, he says, a volume devoted to women; a book "Sayyida fi Qalb al-Mustafa" attributed in the transcript to "Dr Muhammad Abd al-Amani"; "Azwaj al-Nabi fi Waqi'ina al-Mu'asir" by Ustadh Jasim al-Mutawwa'; the cassettes "Nisa' Khalidat" by Dr [[person/tariq-al-suwaidan|Tariq al-Suwaidan]]; "Tarajim Sayyidat Bayt al-Nubuwwa" by Dr [[person/aisha-abd-al-rahman|Aisha Abd al-Rahman]] (read by the museum from the garbled "Munt al-Shati'"); the cassettes "Nisa' Bayt al-Nubuwwa" by a shaykh the transcript reads "Satfa Hijazi"; "Suwar min Hayat al-Sahabiyyat" whose author's name is garbled; and the series "A'lam al-Muslimin" by a writer read as "Abd al-Hamid Tah Naz" (the garbled author names flagged in place). {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep26 00:07:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep26 00:07:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep26 00:08:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep26 00:08:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep26 00:09:00} (needs_source)
- He describes the Prophet's household after Khadija's death in the tenth year of the mission with the Prophet, on his count, fifty: her three sons al-Qasim, al-Tahir and Abdullah died in her lifetime, and of her four daughters [[person/zaynab-bint-muhammad|Zaynab]] is married to [[person/abu-al-as-ibn-al-rabi|Abu al-As ibn al-Rabi]] in Mecca, [[person/ruqayya-bint-muhammad|Ruqayya]] emigrated with [[person/uthman-ibn-affan|Uthman]] to Abyssinia, [[person/umm-kulthum-bint-muhammad|Umm Kulthum]] is in the house after being divorced by a son of [[person/abu-lahab|Abu Lahab]] (the sons' names in the transcript, "Ud and Utayb," garbled and not fixed), and [[person/fatima|Fatima]] is a little girl of eight or nine (her birth on his telling one or two years after the mission, and he notes the disagreement; all the reckoning is the speaker's). {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep26 00:09:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep26 00:10:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep26 00:10:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep26 00:11:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep26 00:11:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep26 00:12:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep26 00:12:30} (needs_source)
- He relates that [[person/khuwayla-bint-hakim|Khawla bint Hakim]], whom he describes as the wife of a great Companion the transcript reads "Uthman ibn Wad'uhum" (read cautiously as [[person/uthman-ibn-mazun|Uthman ibn Maz'un]]), came to the Prophet in his grief after Khadija and said "Messenger of God, will you not marry?"; he was silent a long while until she saw his tears, then he said in meaning "and after Khadija, who is there?"; she regretted having spoken, then asked him "then who for the house and the little ones, Messenger of God?" (the dialogue on the speaker's telling, in meaning). {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep26 00:16:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep26 00:17:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep26 00:17:30} (needs_source)
- He continues the dialogue: she offered "if you wish a virgin, and if you wish a previously married woman"; he asked about both and she said the virgin is Aisha daughter of "the most beloved of people to you," meaning [[person/aisha|Aisha bint Abi Bakr]], and the previously married one is [[person/sawda-bint-zama|Sawda bint Zam'a ibn Qays]] whose husband "al-Sakran ibn Amr" died and who has no one of her family (the husband's name read by the museum as [[person/al-sakran-ibn-amr|al-Sakran ibn Amr]] from a garbled word close to the transcript's); the Prophet said in meaning "begin with Sawda; go speak to them and mention me to them, that I wish to come forward" (the dialogue in meaning; unsourced). {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep26 00:18:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep26 00:18:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep26 00:19:00} (needs_source)
- It is noted that the episode passes quickly over Sawda's story at this point ("we have finished the lady Sawda") and moves to Zaynab bint Khuzayma because her story is shorter, the order of the wives on his screen being Khadija then Sawda then Aisha then Hafsa then Zaynab bint Khuzayma fifth (what came about Sawda in the episode is what is recorded; no detailed lineage, no account of her Islam and no account of her death is given in this episode). {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep26 00:19:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep26 00:19:30}
- He begins the story of [[person/zaynab-bint-khuzayma|Zaynab bint Khuzayma]]: the Prophet married her in the third year after the Hijra, and she died after eight months on his telling, while some of the reports he mentions say two months and some three, making her the wife who lived with him the shortest time (the figures on his reckoning; the disagreement on the duration is his). {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep26 00:22:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep26 00:34:30} (needs_source)
- He names her two husbands before the Prophet: two of his paternal cousins, of the sons of [[person/al-harith-ibn-abd-al-muttalib|al-Harith ibn Abd al-Muttalib]]; she married a son of al-Harith who died and left her a son named al-Tufayl who died before Islam on the transcript's reading (the sentence garbled in the son's attribution and the death), then she married his brother [[person/ubayda-ibn-al-harith|Abu Ubayda ibn al-Harith]] and they entered Islam together and lived a married story until Badr came (the Prophet's uncles he lists: al-Abbas, Abu Talib, Hamza, Abu Lahab, then al-Harith; the details of the husbands on his telling). {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep26 00:22:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep26 00:23:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep26 00:23:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep26 00:24:00} (needs_source)
- He tells the story of Abu Ubayda at [[event/battle-of-badr|Badr]], the day of the Furqan on his description: three of Quraysh's lords stepped out for the duel, read in the transcript as "Abd ibn Rabi'a, Shayba ibn Rabi'a and al-Walid ibn Abduh" (read as [[person/utba-ibn-rabia|Utba ibn Rabi'a]], his brother Shayba ibn Rabi'a and al-Walid ibn Utba); three of the Ansar went out to them and Quraysh said they wanted their own people of the Muhajirun, so the Prophet sent his uncle [[person/hamza|Hamza]], his cousin [[person/ali-ibn-abi-talib|Ali]] and his other cousin Abu Ubayda ibn al-Harith (the speaker's telling of the duel). {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep26 00:24:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep26 00:25:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep26 00:25:30} (needs_source)
- He continues: Hamza killed Utba quickly and Ali killed al-Walid, while Abu Ubayda and Shayba exchanged blows until Shayba cut off Abu Ubayda's leg and his blood flowed heavily, so Hamza went in, killed Shayba and carried Abu Ubayda to the Prophet, who laid his head on his thigh and began wiping the dust from his face (the duel and the wound on his telling; the sira's accounts of Badr match its broad lines). {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep26 00:25:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep26 00:26:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep26 00:26:30} (needs_source)
- He gives the last dialogue in meaning: Abu Ubayda raised his head asking whether, if he died, he would be in paradise, and the Prophet said in meaning "yes, Abu Ubayda, if you die you are of the people of paradise"; he smiled and asked "are you pleased with me, Messenger of God?"; the Prophet wept until his tears fell on Abu Ubayda's body and raised his hand saying in meaning "O God, I call You to witness that I am pleased with Abu Ubayda ibn al-Harith"; he remained bleeding, alive, until God granted the Muslims victory at Badr, then smiled and died (the dialogue and the supplication on the speaker's telling in meaning; the deathbed scene is the episode's composition). {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep26 00:27:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep26 00:27:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep26 00:28:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep26 00:28:30} (needs_source)
- He says Zaynab died at thirty-five (the transcript once reads thirty; the age is the speaker's), that the Prophet buried her himself, went down into her grave and prayed over her himself, that she was the first of the Mothers of the Believers to be buried in al-Baqi, and that she was titled "Umm al-Masakin" for her great spending on the poor, noting that whoever thinks Umm al-Masakin is another wife — it is Zaynab bint Khuzayma (the title, the burial and the prayer on his telling). {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep26 00:29:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep26 00:30:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep26 00:30:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep26 00:41:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep26 00:42:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep26 00:42:30} (needs_source)
- He closes by announcing that the next episode begins the lady [[person/aisha|Aisha]] in an episode or two (the speaker's announcement). {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep26 00:30:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep26 00:43:00}
- Recording note: the audio broadcasts the Zaynab bint Khuzayma segment and the audience comments twice nearly identically (00:19:00 to 00:31:00, then 00:31:00 to 00:43:00), so the recording itself appears to repeat the episode's second half; the segment is written once and the repetition is recorded.

## Left out of this episode 26

Not written from episode 26: the audience's recitation order of the wives' names in the quiz (overlapping voices; 00:03:30 to 00:05:00); the author of "Sayyida fi Qalb al-Mustafa" ("Dr Muhammad Abd al-Amani / Abd Yamani," garbled readings; 00:07:30); the author of "Suwar min Hayat al-Sahabiyyat" ("Dr Ghufta al-Bashsha," garbled; 00:08:30); the author of the "A'lam al-Muslimin" series ("Abd al-Hamid Tah Naz," garbled; 00:09:00); the name of Khawla bint Hakim's husband ("Uthman ibn Wad'uhum," read cautiously as Uthman ibn Maz'un; 00:16:30); Sawda's husband's name ("al-Sakran ibn Amr," read as al-Sakran ibn Amr; 00:18:30); the names of Abu Lahab's two sons who divorced the Prophet's daughters ("Ud and Utayb," garbled; 00:11:30); the wording of the three audience comments (given in meaning; 00:20:00 to 00:22:30); the phrase "musawwata laha / mu'asata laha" in the audience comment (garbled; 00:21:00); the clause "for her father was a disbeliever, and He willed to bring her back into the fold of Islam" in the third comment (its context garbled, perhaps about Sawda or another story; 00:22:00 and 00:34:00); the name of Zaynab bint Khuzayma's first husband of the sons of al-Harith and the attribution of her son al-Tufayl (the sentence garbled; 00:23:30); the wording of the duel dialogue and Quraysh's reply "we want our own people" (given in meaning; 00:24:30 to 00:26:00); and the wording of the Prophet's answer to Abu Ubayda "if you die you are of the people of paradise" (given in meaning; 00:27:00). Transcript machine repetition loops not counted as speech were discarded: 00:02:30 and 00:04:30 (two long non-speech "fa" and "aah" runs). It is also noted that the recording repeats the episode's second half (00:19:00 to 00:31:00, then 00:31:00 to 00:43:00), which was written once. The wording of all hadiths, dialogues and supplications is paraphrased, not reproduced, and marked as needing a source; the dates, ages and names are the speaker's, from a machine transcript that has not been listened to. The questions of the duration of Zaynab's marriage, her age at death, the details of her two husbands of the sons of al-Harith, the story of the "Umm Hani" intercession and Khawla bint Hakim's account are left at the speaker's description and flagged for a sourced perspectives pass.

## Episode 27: Aisha bint Abi Bakr, part one: the house of Abu Bakr, the Prophet's betrothal after the word to al-Mut'im ibn Adi, and the question of her age and the reasons for the marriage, as the speaker and the audience present them

:::perspectives
- **The speaker's view (opinion):** he derives from the standing verse "and his wives are their mothers" that the Prophet is like a father to the believers, and tells of a young man who reached that meaning by feeling, saying about eighty percent of it is in the books on his word (the speaker's didactic derivation; not the museum's claim). [[passage/quran-33-6|Sura al-Ahzab, verse 6]] {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep27 00:00:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep27 00:01:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep27 00:01:30} (needs_source)
- **The speaker's view (opinion, on ifk material):** he presents the merit of [[person/aisha|Aisha]] by saying God exonerated her with Quran sent down from above seven heavens for a woman, and attributes to her the saying that she had wished only for a dream of his, but Quran came down (the speaker's allusion to the ifk incident and the verses of exoneration; the meaning and the saying are on his telling and unsourced; the museum asserts none of it). {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep27 00:05:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep27 00:05:30} (needs_source)
- **The question of Aisha's age (contested material; the speaker's and audience's words only):** a woman in the audience asks what moved the Prophet to marry Aisha when she was nine years old; the speaker calls it a question thousands ask and promises to answer it in the episode, and he and the audience summarise answers: that women in hot lands mature early and that Aisha at nine was in his description a complete woman; that environment and custom govern and that many families then married daughters at such an age; that she had been betrothed before the Prophet to the son of al-Mut'im ibn Adi on the episode's telling; that ages of girls of that era such as Hafsa and Safiyya fall in the same range on his count; that the doubt appears in no old book and surfaced only some sixty years ago on his word; and that custom changes, the ordinary marriage age in Egypt having been thirteen twenty years earlier (all answers of the speaker and the audience, attributed to their sayers, not established at the museum; the figures, examples and generalisations are their own). {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep27 00:21:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep27 00:24:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep27 00:25:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep27 00:29:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep27 00:33:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep27 00:35:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep27 00:36:00} (needs_source)
- **The speaker's own caution (opinion):** after all that, the speaker warns that a girl today should not imitate that age nor take it as a precedent, saying the environment governs, custom binds so long as it does not contradict a clear text, and age-compatibility is an important matter to be observed in today's societies, where a nine-year-old girl has in his view not matured (the speaker's caution and his balance between the story and today's custom; his word, not the museum's). {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep27 00:38:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep27 00:39:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep27 00:39:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep27 00:40:00} (needs_source)
- **The speaker's view (opinion):** he distinguishes "Muhammad the man" from "Muhammad the messenger," saying the Prophet married as Muhammad the man only once, Khadija, and every marriage after her was on his description a marriage of Muhammad the messenger, and he argues the marriage to Aisha was by God's command with the dream hadith he attributes to Sahih al-Bukhari: that Jibril brought him her image on a cloth of silk three nights saying "this is your wife in this world and the next" (the speaker's distinction and the hadith he attributes to al-Bukhari, in meaning on his telling; the wording not fixed). {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep27 00:49:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep27 00:50:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep27 00:50:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep27 00:51:00} (needs_source)
- **The speaker's view (opinion):** he makes the Prophet's instructions to armies on his telling an example of moral consistency toward Muslim, disbeliever and enemy alike: kill no child, woman or old man, burn no crop, tear down no house, cut no palm, destroy no temple, harm no monks in their cells, and do not attack by night lest women and children be terrified (the instructions on the speaker's telling in meaning, inside an ethics lesson; unsourced). {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep27 00:16:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep27 00:17:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep27 00:17:30} (needs_source)
:::

- He opens by recapping what passed: they took Khadija, then Sawda bint Zam'a last episode, and with her Zaynab bint Khuzayma; he repeats the series' standing verse and tells of a young man who told him the verse struck him until he concluded from "his wives are their mothers" that the Prophet is as it were our father (the anecdote on the speaker's telling). [[passage/quran-33-6|Sura al-Ahzab, verse 6]] {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep27 00:00:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep27 00:00:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep27 00:01:00}
- He repeats the wives' ordering quiz on the screen with their twelve names, then repeats the usual list of references and adds a book by Dr Muhammad Said Ramadan al-Bouti on the lady Aisha, calling it a valuable book ([[person/ramadan-al-buti-muhammad-said|al-Bouti]] read this time; the other authors' names remain garbled in the transcript as in previous episodes). {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep27 00:02:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep27 00:03:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep27 00:03:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep27 00:04:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep27 00:04:30} (needs_source)
- He introduces the lady [[person/aisha|Aisha]]: the Prophet's wife and beloved, the only virgin he married on his word, daughter of [[person/abu-bakr|Abu Bakr al-Siddiq]]; he recalls the anecdote of the Prophet "no wealth availed me as Abu Bakr's wealth did" and Abu Bakr's reply "I and my wealth are yours, messenger of God" in meaning, that she is on his word the one who narrated the most hadiths from the Prophet, and among the most learned of the Companions and the most knowledgeable of women on his praise (hadiths and titles on the speaker's telling in meaning). {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep27 00:04:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep27 00:05:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep27 00:06:00} (needs_source)
- He describes Abu Bakr's house: he had two wives before Islam, Qutayla mother of [[person/asma-bint-abi-bakr|Asma]] and [[person/abdullah-ibn-abi-bakr|Abdullah]], and [[person/umm-ruman|Umm Ruman]] his second wife, mother of Aisha and Abd al-Rahman; so Asma and Aisha are sisters of one father, not full sisters (the lineage on the speaker's telling). {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep27 00:06:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep27 00:07:00} (needs_source)
- He says Umm Ruman accepted Islam and emigrated to Medina and died there after the ifk incident on his word, that the Prophet prayed over her, descended into her grave and laid her in it, supplicating for her in meaning "O God, You know what Umm Ruman met in Your path and in the path of Your messenger" (the death, burial and supplication on the speaker's telling in meaning; unsourced). {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep27 00:07:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep27 00:07:30} (needs_source)
- He notes that her full brother [[person/abd-al-rahman-ibn-abi-bakr|Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Bakr]] came late to Islam, fighting against the Muslims on his word at [[event/battle-of-badr|Badr]] and [[event/battle-of-uhud|Uhud]] and not accepting Islam until just before the [[event/conquest-of-mecca|conquest of Mecca]], and he cites the wonder that a man does not guide whom he loves: Qutayla, Asma's mother, refused Islam and Abu Bakr divorced her on his telling (the stances on the speaker's telling; unsourced). {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep27 00:07:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep27 00:08:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep27 00:08:30} (needs_source)
- He puts the episode's numbers on the screen: she was born in year five of the mission when the Prophet was forty-five on his count, betrothed at seven, married at nine, and the Prophet died when she was eighteen (the transcript reads fourteen and eleven in two overlapping places; the intended figure is eighteen), she lived after him about forty-seven years (the transcript reads forty-eight elsewhere), and died aged sixty-six on 17 Ramadan of year 57 AH, the same day as the death of [[person/ali-ibn-abi-talib|Ali ibn Abi Talib]] on his matching (all figures the speaker's count from a machine transcript that contradicts itself at points; all flagged). {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep27 00:08:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep27 00:09:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep27 00:10:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep27 00:10:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep27 00:11:00} (needs_source)
- He retells Khawla bint Hakim's story in the brevity of the last episode and continues it at Abu Bakr's house: she entered and did not find Abu Bakr, so she said to [[person/umm-ruman|Umm Ruman]] in meaning "rejoice at a good such as your mother has not borne since she bore you," and Umm Ruman deferred the answer until Abu Bakr should know; when he came and she told him, he said in meaning he could not answer before looking into a matter (the dialogue entirely on the speaker's telling in meaning). {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep27 00:11:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep27 00:12:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep27 00:13:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep27 00:13:30} (needs_source)
- He explains Abu Bakr's hesitation on his telling: [[person/mutim-ibn-adi|al-Mut'im ibn Adi]], a disbeliever in his account, had spoken to him about his son [[person/jubayr-ibn-mutim|Jubayr ibn al-Mut'im]] marrying Aisha, and Abu Bakr had answered there was no objection, so he could not accept for the Prophet before asking leave and settling the Jubayr matter (the man's name in the transcript "Mut'im ibn Ali / ibn Adi" and the son's "Jubayl / Jubayw ibn al-Mut'im"; the museum reads al-Mut'im ibn Adi and Jubayr ibn al-Mut'im cautiously; the story on the episode's telling). {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep27 00:13:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep27 00:14:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep27 00:18:00} (needs_source)
- From the story he draws a lesson on keeping one's word and contracts, asking about suitors who sign promises then look for clauses by which to escape, and about the man who says in the contract "I marry you on the book of God and the sunna of His messenger" while intending otherwise, and he makes cheating in exams the first training in faithlessness (the speaker's sermon and its educational extension). {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep27 00:14:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep27 00:15:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep27 00:15:30}
- He digresses to Abu Bakr's steady character toward Muslim and non-Muslim: al-Mut'im was a disbeliever and yet Abu Bakr kept faith with him; he notes that the marriage of a Muslim to a disbelieving woman had not yet been forbidden at that time on his word, and recalls from the morals of armies in his telling the Prophet's instructions in meaning (the note on prohibition on the speaker's word; the instructions in meaning). {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep27 00:16:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep27 00:16:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep27 00:17:30} (needs_source)
- After the break he completes it: Abu Bakr enters al-Mut'im's house and al-Mut'im's wife speaks first, in meaning "do you want to take our son and make him enter your religion, Abu Bakr, and make him a sabi'?", so Abu Bakr looks to al-Mut'im and asks him, and al-Mut'im says he says what she said; Abu Bakr is released from his word, returns to Khawla and tells her to send to the messenger of God, and the Prophet comes and betroths Aisha (the dialogue entirely on the episode's telling in meaning; the word "sabi'" is al-Mut'im's wife's wording in the speaker's story). {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep27 00:21:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep27 00:22:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep27 00:22:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep27 00:23:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep27 00:24:00} (needs_source)
- He relays an audience comment before the age question: a member commented on the Prophet's praying over Umm Ruman and descending into her grave, making the mother-in-law relationship in the Companions' history one of affection and honour, the opposite of what media has spread on his word; the speaker agrees and adds that the mother-in-law is the children's grandmother, that honour is the norm, and that selfishness sometimes disturbs the relation (the audience member's and the speaker's words attributed to their sayers). {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep27 00:19:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep27 00:19:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep27 00:20:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep27 00:20:30}
- Then a woman in the audience asks the episode's question: what moved the Prophet to marry Aisha when she was a virgin of nine years; the speaker thanks her and says thousands ask it and the episode will not end before answering (the question in the asker's own formulation; the speaker's promise of an answer). {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep27 00:21:00}
- He begins his answer on the age by stating that women in hot lands mature early and in cold lands late by the nature of the climate, making Aisha at nine a complete woman on his description; and the audience comments: that the variety of the Prophet's wives in age and temperament served the call; that his acts are legislation, which the speaker corrects as specific to him; that a young girl was better able to memorise his hadiths; that people of that era had earlier mental maturity than today; that she was mature in body and mind, one member asking whether an early-maturing girl may marry rather than a fixed age that pushes her into error; that the Prophet knew she would outlive him to carry the religion; and another drew the example of environment governing from children in Palestine who he said fight better than grown men (all statements of speaker and audience, attributed; the museum asserts none of them). {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep27 00:25:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep27 00:26:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep27 00:26:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep27 00:27:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep27 00:28:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep27 00:29:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep27 00:29:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep27 00:30:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep27 00:30:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep27 00:31:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep27 00:31:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep27 00:32:00} (needs_source)
- The speaker adds on his side that a girl is measured by her maturity not her years on his word, that she was Abu Bakr's daughter in upbringing and character, and he argues the matter was ordinary since she had been betrothed to Jubayr ibn al-Mut'im before the Prophet, counting examples of early marriage in that era: [[person/hafsa|Hafsa]] on his word (her age in the transcript contradictory, nineteen then twelve), [[person/abd-al-muttalib|Abd al-Muttalib]] marrying a woman the age of [[person/amina-bint-wahb|Amina bint Wahb]] on a garbled reading, and [[person/safiyya-bint-huyayy|Safiyya bint Huyayy]] first married at fifteen, ten in some reports (the examples and ages all on the speaker's count and the garbled transcript). {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep27 00:32:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep27 00:33:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep27 00:34:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep27 00:34:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep27 00:35:00} (needs_source)
- He says the doubt about the age appeared only some sixty years ago and was never mentioned in an old book or by an Arab on his word, and he cites an English Orientalist quoted in a book by a Dr the transcript reads "Fahmat al-Shati" (read cautiously as [[person/aisha-abd-al-rahman|Aisha Abd al-Rahman]] Bint al-Shati as in previous episodes): that Arab women's growth is rapid, that such a marriage "was and remains an Asiatic custom" still found in Eastern Europe, natural until recently in Spain and Portugal, and found in remote mountain regions of the United States (the Orientalist's name is not given in the transcript; the quotation is attributed to the book the speaker names; not the museum's claim). {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep27 00:35:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep27 00:36:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep27 00:36:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep27 00:37:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep27 00:38:00} (needs_source)
- He turns to "and why did he marry her": an audience member makes the marriage in year two AH the start of the era of legislation, the Prophet needing someone inside his house to transmit his private life and acts, and cites a hadith in meaning "take from her hadiths" whose chain he himself says is weak while its meaning is sound (the audience member's words in meaning; the hadith weak-chained on his own word). {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep27 00:40:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep27 00:41:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep27 00:41:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep27 00:42:00} (needs_source)
- The speaker spells out the meaning: a young, sharp, questioning woman who lives long after the Prophet to transmit the details of his house to the umma; he counts among her transmissions on his telling the laylat al-qadr supplication she asked him for and he taught her, her question on the meaning of the verse "their hearts fearful" which he answered in meaning, her question about istihadha, her question whether a day will come when no one remembers his family, and the story of her guiding him to the spot of her lips on the cup in her days of menstruation (all on the speaker's telling in meaning; wordings unsourced). {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep27 00:42:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep27 00:43:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep27 00:43:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep27 00:44:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep27 00:44:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep27 00:45:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep27 00:46:00} (needs_source)
- He makes the preservation of the Reminder spoken of in the Quranic verse in meaning God preparing means, men and women, to preserve the religion, Aisha being among those means on his reading; that she bore no children so her life could be given to transmission on his word; and that she lived after the Prophet narrating what happened from age nine to eighteen as she grew older (the speaker's interpretation of the verse and of the reason she bore no children; his word). {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep27 00:46:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep27 00:47:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep27 00:47:30} (needs_source)
- An audience member comments that the four caliphs were bound to the Prophet by mutual marriage ties: he married Aisha daughter of Abu Bakr and [[person/hafsa|Hafsa]] daughter of [[person/umar-ibn-al-khattab|Umar]], and [[person/uthman-ibn-affan|Uthman]] and [[person/ali-ibn-abi-talib|Ali]] married his daughters, which he makes a cause of the umma's cohesion for its first thirty years; the speaker agrees and adds the marriage to Aisha was in this way a matter of calling for Islam (the audience member's and the speaker's count). {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep27 00:48:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep27 00:49:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep27 00:49:30} (needs_source)
- He closes by noting Aisha's story cannot finish in one episode and may need two or three, announces the next episode continues her in the hijra and the wedding night, and presents Aisha on his word as a model for a girl of twenty who loves life and loves Islam together (the speaker's announcement and his address aimed at young women). {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep27 00:51:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep27 00:52:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep27 00:52:30}

## Left out of this episode 27

Not written from episode 27: the audience's recitation order of the wives' names in the quiz and the transcript's garbled renderings of some of them ("Zaynab bint Jahsh," "Juwya Juwya bint al-Harith," "Safiyya bint Harith ibn Akhtar," "Maryam huna bint al-Harith al-Hilaliyya"; read cautiously as Zaynab bint Jahsh, Juwayriyya bint al-Harith, Safiyya bint Huyayy and Maymuna bint al-Harith; 00:02:30 to 00:03:30); the reference-list authors' names ("Muhammad Abdu Yamen," "Khalil Suwaidan," "Dift al-Basha," "Abd al-Hamid Taha Naz," as in previous episodes; 00:03:30 to 00:04:30); the name of Abu Bakr's first wife ("Qutayla," no lineage; 00:06:30); the names of al-Mut'im and his son ("Mut'im ibn Ali / ibn Adi" and "Jubayl / Jubayw ibn al-Mut'im," read cautiously as [[person/mutim-ibn-adi|al-Mut'im ibn Adi]] and [[person/jubayr-ibn-mutim|Jubayr ibn al-Mut'im]]; 00:13:30 and 00:21:30); the name of the English Orientalist quoted and the book's title (the transcript gives neither; "Dr Fahmat al-Shati" read cautiously as Aisha Abd al-Rahman; 00:36:30 to 00:38:00); Hafsa's age at her first marriage (nineteen then twelve, contradictory; 00:34:00); the name of Abd al-Muttalib's wife in his example ("Hala bint ammihi," a garbled reading; 00:34:30); the attribution and wording of the hadith "take from her hadiths" (the audience member himself called its chain weak; 00:41:00); and the wording of every dialogue, supplication, hadith and instruction, rendered in meaning, not fixed, and flagged. Mechanical repetition loops in the transcript, not speech, discarded: 00:02:00, 00:14:00, 00:25:00, 00:28:00, 00:37:00 and 00:48:00 (long non-speech runs of "ya," "da," "fa," "ba" and "ta"). Aisha's ages at betrothal and marriage, the Jubayr ibn al-Mut'im story, the ages of Hafsa, Safiyya and Amina, her birth and death dates and the 17 Ramadan 57 AH date, and every answer to the age question are statements of the speaker and the audience, attributed, placed under opinions not established facts, and flagged for checking against sources.

## Episode 28: Aisha bint Abi Bakr, part two: the two families' late departure in the hijra, the wedding night in Shawwal, the simplicity of the house, and the love and the treatment, as the speaker and the audience tell them

:::perspectives
- **The question of Aisha's age again (contested material; the speaker's own recap of last episode's answers):** he opens by restating the summary of his answer to marrying Aisha at nine and betrothing her at seven on his word: that it was ordinary among the Arabs and the Jews on his claim and that the doubt is recent, some sixty or seventy years old; that Khawla bint Hakim was the one who proposed her to the Prophet and that Abu Bakr hesitated over his earlier word to al-Mut'im's son; that Abd al-Muttalib married a woman related to [[person/amina-bint-wahb|Amina bint Wahb]] on a garbled reading; that [[person/safiyya-bint-huyayy|Safiyya bint Huyayy]] first married at ten and [[person/hafsa|Hafsa]] at eleven on his new count; that maturity follows the hot environment and comes late in the cold, citing Siberia; that the Meccans never faulted the Prophet for this marriage while they charged him with everything else; that the ordinary marriage age in Egypt thirty or forty years ago was sixteen to eighteen on his contradictory count; and he repeats the audience member's example of the child in Palestine standing before a tank (all of it a recap of the speaker's and audience's attributed statements from the last episode, not established at the museum; the figures on the garbled transcript). {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep28 00:07:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep28 00:08:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep28 00:09:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep28 00:09:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep28 00:10:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep28 00:10:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep28 00:11:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep28 00:12:30} (needs_source)
- **The speaker's caution again (opinion):** he renews his warning that no one today should take Aisha's age as a measure, saying in meaning that a nine-year-old girl today goes off to play and read, and that environment is the difference between maturing then and maturing now (the speaker's own caution as in the last episode; his word, not the museum's). {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep28 00:11:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep28 00:11:30} (needs_source)
- **The speaker's view (opinion, an address aimed at girls):** he announces the episode is his gift to girls from sixteen to their thirties and to those who fear that religion cannot combine with love and a successful life; he presents [[person/aisha|Aisha]] as the example of a religious woman who lived a great lawful love and a light spirit, and he argues for his point from her playing on a swing with her friends on her wedding day, which he reads as a normal life, not childhood (the speaker's address and his argument; the museum does not establish it). {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep28 00:21:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep28 00:22:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep28 00:23:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep28 00:24:00}
- **The speaker's view (opinion):** he qualifies [[person/anas-ibn-malik|Anas ibn Malik]]'s saying on his telling "the first love in Islam was the Prophet's love for Aisha" by noting Anas was young and never saw Khadija, and that the Prophet's love for Khadija was the greater in the speaker's estimation (the saying on his telling in meaning; the correction is the speaker's own view). {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep28 00:30:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep28 00:30:30}
- **The question of fairness among the wives (contested material; an audience question and the speaker's answer):** an audience member asked about the ruling on equality given the Prophet's greater love for Aisha; the speaker separated the fairness owed in provision, spending, time and the outward showing of feelings from what is in the heart, which no one controls, and related the Prophet's supplication in meaning "O God, this is my division in what I control" (the speaker's answer and the supplication on his telling in meaning). {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep28 00:45:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep28 00:45:30} (needs_source)
- **The speaker's view (opinion):** he makes the secret of lasting love that a house is built on obedience to God and worship and raising the children on it so the family enters paradise, not on a fading admiration on his description (the speaker's closing sermon; his word). {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep28 00:56:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep28 00:56:30}
:::

- He opens with the series plan and a recap, making [[person/aisha|Aisha]] three episodes in all, and repeats the standing rule "the Prophet is closer to the believers than their own selves, and his wives are their mothers", calling for the feeling of motherhood toward the mothers of the believers and for naming daughters after them rather than after foreign names on his word. [[passage/quran-33-6|Sura al-Ahzab, verse 6]] {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep28 00:00:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep28 00:01:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep28 00:02:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep28 00:02:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep28 00:03:00}
- He displays the list of the Prophet's wives on screen directly, no quiz this episode for the length of the Aisha material, in the order he reads: [[person/khadija|Khadija]], [[person/sawda-bint-zama|Sawda]], Aisha, [[person/hafsa|Hafsa]], [[person/zaynab-bint-khuzayma|Zaynab bint Khuzayma]], [[person/umm-salama|Umm Salama]] Hind bint Abi Umayya, [[person/zaynab-bint-jahsh|Zaynab bint Jahsh]], [[person/juwayriya-bint-al-harith|Juwayriyya bint al-Harith]], [[person/safiyya-bint-huyayy|Safiyya bint Huyayy]], [[person/umm-habiba-bint-abi-sufyan|Umm Habiba]] Ramla bint Abi Sufyan, [[person/maria-al-qibtiyya|Mariya]] bint Sham'un the Egyptian, and [[person/maymuna-bint-al-harith|Maymuna bint al-Harith]] (the transcript's renderings of several names garbled; the order on the speaker's count). {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep28 00:03:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep28 00:04:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep28 00:04:30}
- He explains why the Prophet's wives' rooms at the mosque were nine while the list is twelve: Khadija had died and was buried at al-Ma'la in Mecca, [[person/zaynab-bint-khuzayma|Zaynab bint Khuzayma]] lived with him only some thirty months on the garbled transcript's count, and [[person/maria-al-qibtiyya|Mariya]] used to stay in al-Awali where the green countryside resembled her homeland on his word (the speaker's and the transcript's count). {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep28 00:04:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep28 00:05:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep28 00:05:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep28 00:06:00} (needs_source)
- He repeats the reference list on screen and adds "Asad al-Ghaba" and a book by a doctor the transcript reads "Muhammad Abd al-Amani" and another by a doctor it reads "Jasim al-Mutawwa'", recommending households own and read them (the names on the garbled transcript's readings). {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep28 00:06:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep28 00:07:00}
