- He turns to the order of the hijra departure: the families of [[person/abu-bakr|Abu Bakr]] and of the Prophet were the last to leave Mecca, since the departure of women and children would have exposed the hijra; he counts those who remained of Abu Bakr's house as [[person/asma-bint-abi-bakr|Asma]], Aisha, [[person/abdullah-ibn-abi-bakr|Abdullah]] and [[person/umm-ruman|Umm Ruman]], and of the Prophet's house [[person/ali-ibn-abi-talib|Ali ibn Abi Talib]], [[person/fatima|Fatima]], [[person/umm-kulthum-bint-muhammad|Umm Kulthum]] and Sawda; the Prophet sent [[person/zayd-ibn-haritha|Zayd ibn Haritha]] and Abu Bakr sent his son Abdullah, so the two families set out at the end of the night with Aisha eight years old on his count (the story on the speaker's telling; "the sayyida Salta" a garbled reading, read cautiously as Sawda). {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep28 00:13:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep28 00:14:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep28 00:14:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep28 00:15:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep28 00:15:30} (needs_source)
- He dates the wedding night: he places [[event/battle-of-badr|Badr]] on 17 Ramadan of year two AH and says the Prophet consummated the marriage with Aisha in Shawwal; he comments on its lawful name "the night of building" praising the choice of word, and relays Aisha's pride on his telling that she was betrothed, married and wed in Shawwal against the Arabs' custom of ill-omening marriage in Shawwal (the timing and the reports on the speaker's telling in meaning; the Shawwal superstition his word). {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep28 00:16:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep28 00:16:30} (needs_source)
- He tells a joke meant as a warning: a man understood "he wed her in shawwal" as a dance and went in to his wife doing the shawwal; from it he draws the rule that no one should take from religion what he does not understand and should ask the scholars before imitating (the joke and the lesson on the speaker's word). {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep28 00:17:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep28 00:17:30}
- He retells the wedding day in Aisha's voice on his telling in meaning: she was light in weight so her mother fed her much; while she was playing on a swing with her friends her mother called her, and she was brought into a house of the Ansar whose women adorned her, her breath nearly breaking on the transcript's expression, and a woman the transcript reads "Asma bint Zayd" was fixing her hair (the story entirely in meaning on the episode's telling; the woman's name garbled). {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep28 00:23:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep28 00:23:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep28 00:24:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep28 00:25:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep28 00:25:30} (needs_source)
- He relates the walima in meaning: the Prophet offered the people milk and some food and was giving the little girls with his own hand, and when they were shy and said we do not want it he said in meaning do not combine hunger and lying, so they took; then he sat beside Aisha and handed her a cup and she drank a little and left it (the walima and the dialogue on the episode's telling in meaning). {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep28 00:25:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep28 00:26:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep28 00:26:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep28 00:27:00} (needs_source)
- He describes the house's simplicity on his telling: a cushion stuffed with fibre, a water skin and a mat; he attributes to [[person/al-hasan-al-basri|al-Hasan]] that he used to enter the Prophet's wives' houses and gesture at their smallness with his hand, and to [[person/said-ibn-al-musayyab|Sa'id ibn al-Musayyab]] a saying in meaning "would that you had seen the houses of the Prophet's wives, to learn how he was content with little of this world"; from it he draws a sermon to fathers and mothers against exaggerating marriage costs while households wait (the descriptions and sayings attributed on the speaker's telling in meaning). {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep28 00:27:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep28 00:28:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep28 00:28:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep28 00:29:00} (needs_source)
- He relays proofs of the love from the sayings of the Followers and Companions on his telling: [[person/masruq-ibn-al-ajda|Masruq]] never related from her except "the beloved of the beloved of God, the one exonerated from heaven, told me"; [[person/ammar-ibn-yasir|Ammar ibn Yasir]] scolding a man who spoke ill of her; and [[person/amr-ibn-al-as|Amr ibn al-As]] returning from Dhat al-Salasil asking "who is dearest to you?" and being answered Aisha, then her father, then Umar, then Uthman, then Ali, then [[person/talha-ibn-ubaydullah|Talha]], then [[person/zubayr-ibn-al-awwam|al-Zubayr]], and counting some twenty names (the sayings all on the episode's telling in meaning). {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep28 00:29:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep28 00:30:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep28 00:31:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep28 00:31:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep28 00:32:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep28 00:32:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep28 00:33:00} (needs_source)
- He relates her question "how is your love for me?" and his answer in meaning "like the knot in the rope", and that she used to ask again how the knot was and he would say it was as it was; he comments that love is a message governing the relation, not standards of money on his word (the hadith in meaning on the speaker's telling; the comment his sermon). {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep28 00:33:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep28 00:34:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep28 00:34:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep28 00:35:00} (needs_source)
- He relates the story of the gifts in meaning: his love for her became known among the Muslims so people sent their gifts on her day; the wives sent [[person/umm-salama|Umm Salama]] to ask that he order the people to divide the gifts over the days, and he answered her in meaning do not hurt me regarding Aisha, for the revelation never came to him under the cover of any wife but hers, and her house was called the landing place of the revelation on his telling; then they sent [[person/fatima|Fatima]], and he said to her in meaning do you love me, she said yes, he said then love whom I love, and Fatima swore never again to speak against Aisha; and he relays that Fatima later confided to Aisha the secret of Jibril reviewing the Quran with him twice that year and that she would be the first of his family to follow him (the story and dialogues entirely on the episode's telling in meaning; unsourced). {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep28 00:35:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep28 00:36:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep28 00:36:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep28 00:37:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep28 00:37:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep28 00:38:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep28 00:38:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep28 00:40:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep28 00:40:30} (needs_source)
- He relays two audience comments after the break: a member made the wisdom of the age gap that she lived transmitting from him some fifty years, calling her like a computer on his expression; and a member asked about the ruling of equality alongside his preferring her in love (the audience's words attributed to their sayers). {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep28 00:44:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep28 00:45:00}
- He moves to the treatment inside the house and relates in meaning their outings: the Abyssinians playing with spears in the mosque on a feast day, the Prophet standing to shield her at the door of the room, her chin on his shoulder and her cheek against his cheek, and he asks her in meaning have you had enough and she says no, until she bored and says she wanted to know her standing with him (the story and dialogue on the episode's telling in meaning). {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep28 00:46:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep28 00:46:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep28 00:47:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep28 00:47:30} (needs_source)
- He relates the two races in meaning: he raced her and she won while she was light, then years later he raced her and won and said in meaning this for that; and that he used to call her "O A'ish" endearingly on his telling (in meaning on the speaker's telling). {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep28 00:48:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep28 00:48:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep28 00:49:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep28 00:49:30} (needs_source)
- He relates his tenderness with her in her days of menstruation in meaning: she relates he used to take the vessel and turn it until he placed his mouth on the spot of her lips to drink; and he comments that this is in times of joy, while for the mistake there is the story of the dish (in meaning on the episode's telling). {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep28 00:49:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep28 00:50:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep28 00:50:30} (needs_source)
- He relates the dish story in meaning, calling it a hadith in al-Bukhari and Muslim on his word: [[person/hafsa|Hafsa]] made food in an earthenware dish, which pleased the Prophet and he gathered the Companions to it; Aisha grew jealous and broke the dish or tipped it on a garbled reading, and the Prophet knelt gathering the dish and collecting the food with his hands, saying in meaning your mother was jealous, then told her in meaning you have ruined Hafsa's dish, so return to her a dish for her dish; and he contrasts with it those who divorce over a shirt or over a reason they can no longer remember (the story on his telling in meaning; its attribution to the two Sahihs on his word). {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep28 00:50:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep28 00:51:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep28 00:51:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep28 00:52:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep28 00:52:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep28 00:53:30} (needs_source)
- He relates the arbitration story in meaning: Aisha disagreed with him and he asked her who should judge between them; she named [[person/abu-ubayda-ibn-al-jarrah|Abu Ubayda ibn al-Jarrah]] on the transcript's reading "ibn al-Zarakh", then her father; when she said to the Prophet you speak and say nothing but truth, Abu Bakr moved his hand to strike her "O daughter of Umm Ruman" and she hid behind the Prophet, so the Prophet stood between them saying in meaning we did not come for this, then said to her in meaning did you see how I judged between you and your father, and she laughed; Abu Bakr heard her laugh and returned saying in meaning include me in your peace as you included me in your war (the story and dialogue on the episode's telling in meaning; ibn al-Zarakh read cautiously as Abu Ubayda ibn al-Jarrah). {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep28 00:53:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep28 00:54:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep28 00:54:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep28 00:55:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep28 00:55:30} (needs_source)
- He relates the oath story in meaning: he told her I know when you are pleased with me and when you are angry: when pleased you swear no, by the Lord of Muhammad, and when angry no, by the Lord of Ibrahim; she answered in meaning I abandon only your name, and he comments she left the name without the love on his telling (in meaning on his telling). {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep28 00:55:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep28 00:56:00} (needs_source)
- He closes by announcing the next episode is the last of Aisha's and completes the love and the story (the speaker's announcement). {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep28 00:56:30}

## Left out of this episode 28

Not written from episode 28: the transcript's renderings of the wives' names in the displayed list ("Ghaliya bint Khuwayni," "Zayna bint Khuzayma," "Juway'iya bint al-Haris," "Safiyya bint Habibna Akhtuha," "Umm Habiba Ghamla bint Abi Sufyan"; read cautiously as Khadija bint Khuwaylid, Zaynab bint Khuzayma, Juwayriyya bint al-Harith, Safiyya bint Huyayy and Umm Habiba Ramla bint Abi Sufyan; 00:03:30 to 00:04:30); the name of the Prophet's wife who stayed in Mecca with his daughters ("the sayyida Salta," read cautiously as Sawda bint Zam'a; 00:14:30); the duration of Zaynab bint Khuzayma's companionship ("thirty or eighty months, dusar"; garbled; 00:05:00); the name of the woman fixing Aisha's hair ("Asma bint Zayd"; 00:26:30); the speaker's figures for the marriage age in Egypt (sixteen, seventeen, eighteen then twenty-six, twenty-seven, contradictory; 00:10:30 to 00:11:00); the name of Abd al-Muttalib's wife ("Hala," a garbled reading as in the last episode; 00:08:30); and the name of Abu Ubayda ("ibn al-Zarakh," read cautiously as ibn al-Jarrah; 00:54:00); and the wording of every hadith, dialogue, supplication and saying of the Followers, rendered in meaning, not fixed, and flagged, among them the supplication of the division, the knot hadith, the revelation-under-the-cover hadith, the oath hadith, the dish story, and the sayings of Masruq, Anas, Ammar, al-Hasan and Sa'id ibn al-Musayyab. Mechanical repetition loops in the transcript discarded, not counted as speech: 00:05:30, 00:14:00, 00:19:30, 00:29:00, 00:50:00 and 00:53:00 (long non-speech runs of "wa," "ah," "ba," "fa," "da" and "ta"); a mechanical repeat of the greeting sentence at 00:20:00; and commercial breaks with no transcribed speech (00:18:30 to 00:19:00, and between 00:41:30 and 00:44:00). Aisha's ages at betrothal and marriage, the repeated answers to the age question and the ages of Safiyya and Hafsa, the repeated Jubayr story, and the timing of the wedding night in Shawwal of year two are all statements of the speaker and the audience, attributed, placed under opinions not established facts, and flagged for checking against sources.

## Episode 29: Aisha bint Abi Bakr, part three: the last days and the death of the Prophet in her house, her knowledge, worship and giving, and her own last days, as the speaker and the audience tell them

:::perspectives
- **The speaker's argument for the young bride (contested material; his view):** he argues that a young bride was needed so that a girl could learn all this knowledge from the Prophet and then live on after him, forty-seven years on his count, to pass it to the community, whose practice, he says, rests on what she did in those years; without this, he says, much of the knowledge we have would not have reached us (the argument is the speaker's own; the museum does not establish it). {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep29 00:34:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep29 00:35:00}
- **The speaker's ranking of Aisha among narrators (opinion):** he lists those who narrated most from the Prophet as [[person/abu-hurayra|Abu Hurayra]] first, [[person/abdullah-ibn-umar|Abdullah ibn Umar]] second and [[person/anas-ibn-malik|Anas ibn Malik]] third, then Aisha or [[person/abdullah-ibn-abbas|Abdullah ibn Abbas]] fourth on differing views, and argues that she should be counted first because she took her reports, which he puts at 250, straight from the Prophet, many from the hours they were alone at home, whereas other Companions often reported from one another (the order and the figure are his and unchecked; the argument is his). {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep29 00:26:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep29 00:26:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep29 00:27:00}
- **The practical sunna through Aisha (opinion; the speaker's report of views):** he says that on some views about ninety percent of the practical sunna reached the community through her, because few Companions saw the Prophet perform ablution, and he describes her standing before her nephew (the transcript reads "Umar ibn al-Zubayr"; not linked) and showing the ablution step by step (the percentage is credited by him to unnamed views and is unchecked; the demonstration is on his telling). {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep29 00:28:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep29 00:29:00} (needs_source)
- **The question of what interrupts prayer (contested material; the speaker's relay of Aisha's objection):** he says that Aisha, hearing after the Prophet's death that a dog, a donkey and a woman interrupt prayer, was very angry and answered that they were being likened to dogs and donkeys, and he relays in meaning that she lay between the Prophet and the qibla while he prayed, and that when he wanted to prostrate he pressed her foot and she drew it in (his relay in meaning; the museum rules on nothing here). {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep29 00:05:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep29 00:05:30} (needs_source)
- **Studio participants on the woman's place (opinions of the participants):** a male participant says he counts woman not as half of society but as three quarters, since a sound woman makes a sound house, and speaks of his own marriage in a line the transcript renders garbled; the speaker thanks him for his frankness; another participant says that behind every great woman stands a man who is ready to help her, teach her and love her faithfully, though not necessarily like the Prophet (the participants' words, unnamed in the transcript, attributed to them). {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep29 00:46:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep29 00:46:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep29 00:48:30}
- **The speaker's address to girls (opinion):** he contrasts a girl who spends her days on her looks and her own future with Aisha (the transcript gives the figure eighteen in a garbled line; nothing more is written from it), and asks girls to put strong religion and tenderness together; later, when he relates her modesty before Umar's grave, he calls on girls who uncover most of the body to hear what she said (his address and exhortation; the museum prescribes nothing). {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep29 00:30:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep29 00:31:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep29 00:52:30}
- **The speaker's view (opinion): love that becomes a mission:** he says Aisha did not sit on the memory of her love and weep until she died but turned it into a message; that love fades and ends when it is only love, while love that is a mission and a blessing from God lasts; and he urges spouses to choose a shared mission and raise their children for it (his sermon; his word; the example he gives of a contemporary cause is left out under the exclusions). {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep29 00:40:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep29 00:41:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep29 00:41:30}
- **What Aisha's scholarship shows, as the speaker presents it (opinion):** he says that without her many hadiths, much knowledge, much interpretation of verses and much jurisprudence known today would not have reached us, says he could name the episode a tribute to women in Islam, and argues from it against a claim that this religion hides, neglects or hates women (his argument, aimed at an unnamed claim; the museum does not adjudicate it). {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep29 00:25:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep29 00:25:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep29 00:33:30}
:::

- He opens with the greeting and says this is again the Mother of the Believers [[person/aisha|Aisha]], repeating the standing rule that the Prophet is closer to the believers than their own selves and that his wives are their mothers, and saying that more remains to be said about the love between her and the Prophet. [[passage/quran-33-6|Sura al-Ahzab, verse 6]] {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep29 00:00:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep29 00:00:30}
- He dedicates the episode to every girl who wants to live with love and every young man who wants a love story with religion and marriage, saying love is purer and longer-lasting in the frame God gives it; he says the trouble is that people seek love wrongly outside marriage, including, as he puts it, relationships formed at work between married people, and that houses then break because they were not founded on piety; he points to the verse about a building founded on piety against one founded on a crumbling bank, and advises choosing a spouse for character and religion so that love can grow. [[passage/quran-9-109|Sura al-Tawba, verse 109]] {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep29 00:01:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep29 00:01:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep29 00:02:00}
- Recapping the last episode, he mentions the weekly outings into the open desert, the races, the endearing form of her name, the Abyssinians playing in the mosque with her chin on the Prophet's shoulder and her cheek against his, his asking whether she had had enough and her answering no, and his tenderness with the drinking vessel in her days of menstruation (a recap in meaning of what episode 28 told). {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep29 00:02:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep29 00:03:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep29 00:03:30}
- He turns to the night prayer: on her night the Prophet would say in meaning, O Aisha, let me rise to my Lord for an hour; and she would answer in meaning that she loved to have him near but that his pleasure was dearer to her than her own; he comments on love of worship inside tenderness (the dialogue on his telling in meaning). {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep29 00:04:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep29 00:04:30} (needs_source)
- He says the private life of a ruler or any great man with his wife is not known, but that the Prophet's household life is known in the finest detail because his wives were meant to relate it so that people could hear and imitate; as an example he gives her saying in meaning that she and the Prophet bathed from one vessel, each telling the other to leave some water, and he contrasts that closeness with homes today where spouses cannot speak to each other (the account in meaning and the comparison are his). {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep29 00:06:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep29 00:06:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep29 00:07:00} (needs_source)
- He says she used to talk to the Prophet through the night while he listened, and relates the long hadith of the women who each described her husband, which the transcript renders "hadith of eleven" in a garbled form; he praises her eloquence in it and says reading it takes four hours on the transcript's figure (the figure is his and unchecked). As the transcript carries the story, Abu Zar' loved Umm Zar' and they lived well, then he changed and divorced her; the Prophet answered in meaning that he was to her as Abu Zar' was to Umm Zar', with a last clause the transcript renders garbled (not written as fact; the museum reads it cautiously as "except that I do not divorce"). {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep29 00:07:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep29 00:08:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep29 00:08:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep29 00:09:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep29 00:09:30} (needs_source)
- He repeats the knot-in-the-rope exchange (her asking how his love was, his answer in meaning that it was like the knot in the rope, and his saying, when she asked how the knot was, that it was as it was), then asks whether that love came only from their living at ease; he answers that love is not lost to the hardships of life but when faith leaves the heart, that God alone places love in hearts, and that love is kept by obedience to God and by giving, not by outings, adding that her life with the Prophet was struggle, expeditions and worship (the hadith in meaning; the answer is his). {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep29 00:09:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep29 00:10:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep29 00:10:30} (needs_source)
- On the household's means he relays her saying in meaning that month followed month without a fire lit in the Prophet's house; asked by her nephew (the transcript reads "Uqba ibn al-Zubayr"; not linked) what they lived on, she answered dates and water, with milk sometimes brought by Ansar neighbours who kept animals (the transcript names a second source in a garbled phrase, not written); he adds that the Prophet was not poor, since he had a fifth of the spoils, but spent it and left his family little, calls that a distinction of the Prophet, and notes that many Companions, such as [[person/abd-al-rahman-ibn-awf|Abd al-Rahman ibn Awf]] and [[person/uthman-ibn-affan|Uthman ibn Affan]], lived in comfort and wealth (the report in meaning; the comment his). {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep29 00:11:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep29 00:11:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep29 00:12:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep29 00:12:30} (needs_source)
- He places the choice after the spoils grew, when, on his telling, the Persians drew near and the wives asked for more maintenance and pressed the Prophet so hard that he withdrew from them until the verses of the choice came down (the order of events is his and unchecked). The verses say that whoever wants this world and its adornment will be provided for and released with grace, and whoever wants God, his messenger and the next abode has a great reward; he went to them one by one and began with Aisha, told her he had a matter to put to her and that she should not hasten until she consulted her parents, and she answered in meaning, about you should I consult my parents? I choose God and his messenger and the abode of the hereafter, and he was glad; the speaker says young people should learn from her. [[passage/quran-33-28|Sura al-Ahzab, verse 28]] [[passage/quran-33-29|Sura al-Ahzab, verse 29]] {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep29 00:12:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep29 00:13:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep29 00:13:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep29 00:14:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep29 00:14:30} (needs_source)
- He says Aisha lived the finest love with the Prophet and was at the same time obedient to God and attached to him, so that religion and great love go together; he gives her ages as nine when she married the Prophet and eighteen when he died, so that her time with him was nine years (his figures, restating what earlier episodes gave; see the left-out section). {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep29 00:14:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep29 00:15:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep29 00:15:30}
- For the last days he relays that several days before his death the Prophet kept asking whose night it was, since he was bound to fairness in all that shows while the heart is not in anyone's control; the night turned out, in a line the transcript renders garbled, to be that of [[person/maymuna-bint-al-harith|Maymuna]]; he asked his wives' leave to be nursed in Aisha's house and they agreed; he tried to rise and could not, so men the transcript names only in garbled forms ("Ali ibn Abi", "al-Khalid", "al-Fadl min al-Abbas"; not linked) carried him to her house (the account in meaning on his telling). [[event/death-of-the-prophet|the death of the Prophet]] {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep29 00:15:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep29 00:16:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep29 00:16:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep29 00:17:00} (needs_source)
- He relays her account of the Prophet's agony in meaning: he raised his hands and said there is no god but God and that death has its agonies; she took his hand and wiped his face with it, saying his hand was more blessed than hers; near the end her brother [[person/abd-al-rahman-ibn-abi-bakr|Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Bakr]] came with a [[practice/miswak|siwak]], the Prophet could not speak and looked at it, she understood that he wanted to clean his mouth before meeting his Lord, took it, chewed it to soften it and gave it to him, and says the last thing that entered his body was her saliva (the account in meaning on his telling). {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep29 00:17:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep29 00:17:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep29 00:18:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep29 00:18:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep29 00:19:00} (needs_source)
- He comments that the Prophet did not die prostrating, nor reciting the Qur'an, nor in a third setting the transcript renders garbled, but with his head on his wife's breast, and asks whether there can be a greater honouring in a line whose end is garbled; in her account, as he relays it in meaning, the Prophet laid his head against her, between her throat and her chest, raised his hand and said "the highest companion" three times, and she understood he was choosing. He adds the report in which [[person/jibril|Jibril]] came and said that the angel of death asked leave to enter, which he had not asked of anyone before nor would after, and the Prophet said let him in; the angel said God had sent him and given him the choice between staying in this world and meeting God, and the Prophet said "the highest companion"; the angel stood by his head and called the good soul of Muhammad ibn Abdullah to come out to the pleasure and satisfaction of a Lord who is not angry; then, as she says, his hand fell and his head grew heavy on her chest (the story on his telling in meaning). {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep29 00:19:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep29 00:20:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep29 00:20:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep29 00:21:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep29 00:21:30} (needs_source)
- He says Aisha went to the opening onto the mosque (the transcript reads "khurja"), where the Companions had gathered to learn how the Prophet was, and called out loudly that the Messenger of God had died, so that the mosque broke into weeping; he says [[person/umar-ibn-al-khattab|Umar]] spoke at that moment (his words garbled in the transcript) and that her father was the one who stood firm; [[person/abu-bakr|Abu Bakr]] entered, saw that he had died, said in meaning that God would not give him two deaths, embraced him, kissed him between the eyes and said good in life and good in death; the speaker points to the honour that the last moments were with her (the account in meaning on his telling). {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep29 00:22:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep29 00:22:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep29 00:23:00} (needs_source)
- After the break he returns to what the death meant for her: she was eighteen at the Prophet's death and, on his count, lived until sixty-six, so that forty-seven years remained (his arithmetic; eighteen and sixty-six give forty-eight), which he calls the years of the work of Islam and of knowledge; he repeats that [[person/masruq-ibn-al-ajda|Masruq]] never related from her without saying that the beloved of God's beloved had told him. He says she opened the first school in Islam for teaching what the transcript reads as 'falak' (astronomy; not checked) and hadith and that about a hundred and one took from her; among those he names, in a passage the transcript renders unevenly, are [[person/said-ibn-al-musayyab|Sa'id ibn al-Musayyab]] and [[person/al-hasan-al-basri|al-Hasan al-Basri]], the lines on her Companion students and on al-Hasan's mother being garbled and not written (the account, the count and the names are his, on a machine transcript, unchecked). {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep29 00:24:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep29 00:24:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep29 00:25:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep29 00:27:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep29 00:28:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep29 00:28:30} (needs_source)
- He credits her with the occasion of the verses of tayammum: on a journey with the Prophet and the Companions they were delayed, had no water and could not pray, and the verses came down; he relays a remark of praise for the family of Abu Bakr that he attributes to a man the transcript reads "Usayd ibn al-Khattab" (garbled; not written), and says she corrected the Companions in matters filling several whole books (his claim; unchecked). {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep29 00:29:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep29 00:30:00} (needs_source)
- He says [[person/abu-musa-al-ashari|Abu Musa al-Ashari]] said that when the Companions were unsure of a matter they found knowledge of it with Aisha, and that the senior Companions went to her when they disagreed; he relays her nephew (the transcript reads "Umar ibn al-Zubayr"; not linked) telling her in meaning that he was not amazed at her knowledge of genealogy, as the daughter of Abu Bakr, nor of religion, as the wife of the Prophet, nor of poetry, but of medicine, and asking where it came from; she answered that the Prophet fell ill often at the end of his life and Arab delegations came with remedies that she learned (the dialogue on his telling in meaning). {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep29 00:31:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep29 00:31:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep29 00:32:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep29 00:32:30} (needs_source)
- He attributes her learning to a sharp mind, a strong memory, concentration and the many questions she put to the Prophet, and relays that the Companions said they knew none more learned in the lawful and the forbidden, the obligations and the voluntary acts; he calls her the teacher of the men and says women should be proud of it. He adds that [[person/muawiya-ibn-abi-sufyan|Muawiya ibn Abi Sufyan]] said the most eloquent of the Arabs was Aisha (the line reads "asahh"; the museum reads "afsah") and that a son of Abu Musa said he had seen the caliphs speak, from Abu Bakr and Umar and Uthman and Ali to Muawiya, and had seen none more eloquent in speech than Aisha (the word before it is garbled) (the sayings on his telling in meaning). {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep29 00:33:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep29 00:33:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep29 00:34:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep29 00:34:30} (needs_source)
- On her worship he says she prayed and fasted much, and relays from her nephew, whom the transcript first reads "Umar ibn al-Zubayr" and later "Urwa" ([[person/urwa-ibn-al-zubayr|Urwa ibn al-Zubayr]] is the museum's reading), that he found her praying at night and repeating a verse about God's favour and protection from the torment of the scorching wind, weeping and asking for it; he left to put a question to her, came back after an hour and found her at the same verse, and he wept at her weeping; the speaker adds that nine years with the Prophet shaped her for the rest of her life (the account in meaning). [[passage/quran-52-27|Sura al-Tur, verse 27]] {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep29 00:35:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep29 00:36:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep29 00:36:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep29 00:37:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep29 00:37:30} (needs_source)
- He relays that when she was old, nearing sixty-five on his count, she was fasting the day of Arafa and so weak that water was poured over her face; her nephew (the transcript reads "Umar ibn al-Zubayr"; not linked) told her to break the fast, and she answered in meaning that she would never break it on a day on which God forgives the sins of a year past and a year to come; he asks his listeners who fasts Mondays and Thursdays and includes himself in the reproach (the account in meaning on his telling). {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep29 00:38:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep29 00:38:30} (needs_source)
- On her spending he says money came to her and she gave all of it away; he tells that on a day of fasting she gave away all the food in the house and a person in her household (the word is garbled) asked what she would break her fast on, to which she answered in a line the transcript renders garbled; he adds that she used to put the coins (the word is read "al-ḍarāʾim"; read cautiously as dirhams) into white musk and perfume them before giving, saying in meaning that it falls into God's hand before the hand of the poor, and asks listeners when they last gave in God's way (the account in meaning on his telling). {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep29 00:39:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep29 00:39:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep29 00:40:00} (needs_source)
- After the break the studio participants comment: one reads a verse about the good for the good, which the transcript renders in garbled form, and says the good seek the good; another says that when a young man chooses his wife by religion and she chooses by religion the house starts on obedience to God and the marriage will last; a young woman says her goal is a righteous husband who helps her obey God and a family raised on love of God, and hopes to raise children strong in their religion (her phrase echoes a Qur'anic description, given in meaning only); the speaker welcomes the remarks (the participants' words, unnamed, attributed to them). [[passage/quran-24-26|Sura al-Nur, verse 26]] {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep29 00:42:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep29 00:43:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep29 00:43:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep29 00:44:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep29 00:44:30}
- Another participant says marriage matters to young girls but that marriages now take place without knowledge, languages or culture, and that a community cannot advance without educated people; the speaker agrees that spouses must have awareness and understanding and restates it in his own words; further participants thank him, one saying the episode showed what the Muslim woman can do and her role in society, and one that after nine years in the Prophet's school she spent forty-seven years teaching and striving until she joined the Prophet; one adds that her gifts came from the Prophet's upbringing and that the husband's role is to help his wife develop all of them (the participants' words, unnamed, attributed to them). {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep29 00:45:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep29 00:45:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep29 00:47:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep29 00:47:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep29 00:48:00}
- Before the break he announces a section on Aisha and striving, and near the end says he had forgotten to mention that she took part at [[event/battle-of-uhud|Uhud]], giving water to the wounded and moving among the people, and at [[event/battle-of-the-trench|the battle of the Trench]] (on his telling; the rest of the passage, with an exchange about her that the transcript renders garbled, is not written). {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep29 00:41:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep29 00:42:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep29 00:49:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep29 00:50:00} (needs_source)
- On her preferring others to herself he relays that [[person/umar-ibn-al-khattab|Umar]], as his death drew near, asked her leave to be buried beside 'my companion', as the transcript reads it in the singular (not checked), and that she, who had thought only one place remained in the room, answered in meaning that she had wanted it for herself but would prefer Umar today over herself; he holds her up to wives who want everything for themselves, and says that afterwards it appeared that room remained for one more, yet when her own death came she declined to be buried there, asking to be buried with the other wives of the Messenger so that she would not be singled out and so that people would not speak well of her beyond what she deserved (the second part is garbled and read cautiously); he also relays her saying that after Umar was buried in the room she never entered it without drawing her clothes tight out of modesty before him (all in meaning on his telling). {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep29 00:50:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep29 00:51:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep29 00:51:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep29 00:52:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep29 00:52:30} (needs_source)
- Her death as he gives it: she was sixty-six, in the year 57 AH, on a Tuesday, 17 Ramadan, after the people had prayed tarawih; as the end drew near [[person/abdullah-ibn-abbas|Abdullah ibn Abbas]] asked leave to visit her and, though she refused visitors, insisted that he had something to say; he told her to rejoice, since nothing lay between her and meeting the Prophet but the spirit leaving the body, that she was his beloved, that her innocence came down from heaven in the affair of the ifk and that he loved her; she answered in meaning that she wished she were something utterly forgotten, and that if he wanted to give her glad tidings it was that the Messenger of God had died between her throat and her chest. He adds that she was carried at night, all of Medina bearing her, that [[person/abu-hurayra|Abu Hurayra]] prayed over her, that she was buried beside the Prophet's wives and that [[person/abdullah-ibn-al-zubayr|Abdullah ibn al-Zubayr]] went down into the grave, and in garbled lines that people cried that the beloved of the Messenger of God had died; he closes by saying he has finished Aisha's story except the affair of the ifk, which he will keep for a separate episode, and announces the next episode on a new Mother of the Believers, [[person/hafsa|Hafsa bint Umar]]. {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep29 00:52:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep29 00:53:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep29 00:53:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep29 00:54:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep29 00:54:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep29 00:55:00} (needs_source)

## Left out of this episode 29

Not written from episode 29: the transcript's readings of names that are not clear: the nephew of Aisha whom the transcript first reads "Uqba ibn al-Zubayr" (00:11:30) and then "Umar ibn al-Zubayr" (00:28:30, 00:29:00, 00:31:30, 00:35:30 and 00:38:00) and at 00:36:30 "Urwa" (the museum reads Urwa ibn al-Zubayr, linked only at 00:36:30 where the name is legible); the men who carried the Prophet to Aisha's house ("Ali ibn Abi", "al-Khalid" and "al-Fadl min al-Abbas"; 00:16:30 to 00:17:00); the night of the wife the transcript reads "Maymuna" in a garbled line (00:16:00); the readings "Usayd ibn al-Khattab" (00:29:30), "Umar ibn al-Khattab" among her students (00:27:30) and al-Hasan al-Basri's mother (00:28:00); the Abu Zar' and Umm Zar' story's last clause of the Prophet's reply ("aṭbīquk"; 00:09:30), the "hadith of eleven" words (00:08:00) and the figure of four hours to read it (00:07:30); Umar's words at the Prophet's death ("qaṭʿ ṭarāfa"; 00:23:00); the word the transcript reads "khurja" (00:22:00); the speaker's remark that the Prophet did not die "in a field" (00:19:30); the objects of her gifts in the line "law rakaltini" (00:39:00 to 00:39:30) and the word "al-ḍarāʾim" for the coins (00:40:00); the participant's "thirty years" of marriage (00:46:00) and "forty years together" (00:48:00); the Trench passage and the exchange about her (00:49:30 to 00:50:00); the burial and 'who walked first' lines (00:54:30 to 00:55:00); and her age at marriage of nine and at the Prophet's death of eighteen, her total life of sixty-six and 'forty-seven years' remaining (18 and 66 give forty-eight), the year 57 AH with Tuesday 17 Ramadan for her death, the figure of 250 hadiths, the 'one hundred and one' students, the ranking of narrators, the ninety percent figure and the age 'nearly sixty-five' at the Arafa fast, and the figure '27' for her years of study (00:33:00; garbled), are all the speaker's or the transcript's, attributed, unchecked and marked needs_source or placed under perspectives. The wording of every hadith, dialogue, supplication and saying is rendered in meaning, not fixed; the verses he reads (the verse of the foundation, the choice verses, the good-for-the-good verse and the verse of the torment) are given only as passage links and never typed; the Qur'anic phrase in a participant's wish and a reproach beginning 'she wished to be forgotten' are in meaning only. Left out as contemporary political asides, for the founder's decision: the speaker's example of a mission a couple might share with their children, which names a contemporary public cause and a historical commander (00:41:00 to 00:41:30). Mechanical repetition loops in the transcript discarded, not counted as speech: 00:19:00, 00:21:30 and 00:49:00 (long runs of "eh", "hadha" and "fi al"); commercial breaks with no transcribed speech between 00:23:30 and 00:24:00, and between 00:42:00 and 00:42:30. The statements about what a ruler or a prophet's household did, and the comparisons with homes today, are the speaker's own and are not established by the museum.


## Episode 30: the slander affair (hadith al-ifk) as the speaker and the audience tell it: the return from Bani al-Mustaliq, the lost necklace, the rumour, the consultations, the revelation and the lessons

:::perspectives
- **The speaker's account of who spread the rumour (his identification; not established by the museum):** he names the hypocrites led by [[person/abdullah-ibn-ubayy|Abdullah ibn Ubayy]] as the first source, then some simple believers and some who spoke without thought; he names [[person/hassan-ibn-thabit|Hassan ibn Thabit]] as a poet who spoke and erred, and [[person/hamna-bint-jahsh|Hamna bint Jahsh]] as the one who spread the most. {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep30 00:03:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep30 00:11:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep30 00:12:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep30 00:27:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep30 00:28:00} (needs_source)
- **The speaker's argument that the Prophet consulted and did not doubt (contested; his view):** he argues that the Prophet asked Ali, Usama and the servant only because the matter touched his household, and that consulting was not a sign of doubt; the museum does not settle the question of the Prophet's inner state. {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep30 00:39:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep30 00:40:00} (needs_source)
- **The speaker's proof of prophethood from the story (his apologetic argument):** he says the Prophet gave no answer of his own and waited for revelation, and that this shows the Prophet did not compose the text, answering those he says claim otherwise; the argument is his and the museum does not adjudicate it. {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep30 00:41:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep30 00:41:30} (needs_source)
- **The speaker's counsel to husbands and listeners on haste and hearsay (his advice):** he urges patience before judging, not repeating a rumour, and not wounding a wife's honour with a harsh word; the museum prescribes nothing and records the advice as his. {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep30 00:37:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep30 00:43:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep30 00:44:00}
- **Studio participants on the Prophet as the reference in household trouble (participants' opinions):** a participant says that many marriage problems come from taking other people as the reference, and that the Prophet's conduct in the story is the first point to learn from; another says God chose Aisha by the lot, knowing she could bear the test (his words are attributed to the participants). {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep30 00:46:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep30 00:46:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep30 00:50:00}
- **The speaker on gossip about women today (opinion):** he says the verses on the slander warn against speaking of what one does not know, and that women are too often accused without proof in his time; the statement is his. {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep30 00:30:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep30 00:38:30}
:::

- He opens with the greeting and says that the three earlier episodes on Aisha covered her marriage at that age, the love between her and the Prophet, and her knowledge, worship and conduct; he gives the slander affair its own episode because it is a large subject in itself. {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep30 00:00:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep30 00:00:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep30 00:01:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep30 00:01:30}
- He sets the scene in the fifth year, in the month of Sha'ban (his date), when the Prophet went out on the expedition against [[event/expedition-of-banu-al-mustaliq|Bani al-Mustaliq]]; the Prophet cast lots among his wives for who would go, the lot fell to Aisha, and she travelled with the army, which won and set out for home. {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep30 00:02:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep30 00:02:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep30 00:03:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep30 00:05:30} (needs_source)
- On the way back there was a quarrel between a servant of Umar and a man of the Ansar; each called out for his own side, and [[person/abdullah-ibn-ubayy|Abdullah ibn Ubayy]] spoke against the Muhajirun and said that the mighty would drive out the weak from Medina. The speaker says the Prophet would not have Abdullah killed, lest people say that Muhammad kills his companions. The words Abdullah is said to have spoken are those the Qur'an records in [[passage/quran-63-8|Sura al-Munafiqun, verse 8]] (a museum cross-reference, not a reading from the recording). {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep30 00:04:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep30 00:04:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep30 00:05:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep30 00:05:30}
- At a halt near Medina Aisha went out of the litter to relieve herself, then found that her necklace had gone and went back to search for it; the caravan moved on, and the men who lifted her litter did not notice she was missing, since she was light then. {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep30 00:06:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep30 00:06:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep30 00:07:00}
- She waited where the army had left her and fell asleep against a rock. The speaker says a man had been sent behind the army to deal with what it left, and that [[person/safwan-ibn-al-muattal|Safwan ibn al-Mu'attal]], who had seen her before the veil, found her asleep, recognised her, said the words of return and made his camel kneel. {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep30 00:07:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep30 00:08:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep30 00:09:00}
- Safwan led her camel back to Medina, and she spoke no word to him on the way beyond the one phrase of return. On her arrival the Prophet asked where she had been; she told him what had happened, and the speaker has the Prophet answer that she had said it and he believed her; the museum keeps this reading as the speaker's (the wording of the answer is partly garbled in the transcript). {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep30 00:10:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep30 00:11:00}
- The speaker says that Abdullah ibn Ubayy seized on the sight of her returning with Safwan, and that the hypocrites and some believers spread the matter until the whole city talked of it and no house in Medina had not heard it; he describes the Prophet as being in the midst of it, and the Prophet's household and his honour as at stake. {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep30 00:11:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep30 00:12:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep30 00:13:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep30 00:14:00}
- He says that the revelation came in parts, that no revelation concerning her came for about a month, and that Aisha fell ill for some days without knowing what was being said; during the illness the Prophet asked only how she was, and she missed the tenderness she had known from him in her good days. {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep30 00:15:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep30 00:16:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep30 00:17:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep30 00:17:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep30 00:18:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep30 00:18:30}
- After she recovered she went out with Umm Mistah to the open ground used for relieving oneself; Umm Mistah, a cousin of hers, spoke ill of her son [[person/mistah-ibn-uthatha|Mistah ibn Uthatha]], and when Aisha asked why, Umm Mistah told her what was being said. Aisha asked leave to go to her parents' house, and her mother [[person/umm-ruman|Umm Ruman]] told her, in the speaker's words, that every beloved wife has rivals. {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep30 00:19:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep30 00:19:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep30 00:20:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep30 00:20:30}
- She wept without pause through that day and night, and the speaker relays that her parents feared for her health. {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep30 00:21:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep30 00:21:30}
- The Prophet asked [[person/ali-ibn-abi-talib|Ali ibn Abi Talib]] and [[person/usama-ibn-zayd|Usama ibn Zayd]] for their view. In the speaker's account Usama said he knew nothing but good of her, and Ali advised asking the servant girl; the servant, whom the transcript reads as Buraida (the museum reads Barira; not linked), said she knew nothing but good of Aisha beyond her youth, the dough she left to rise and her sleep while the goat came in. {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep30 00:22:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep30 00:22:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep30 00:23:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep30 00:23:30}
- On the pulpit the Prophet asked who would help him against the man who harmed him in his family. [[person/sad-ibn-muadh|Sa'd ibn Mu'adh]] offered to deal with the man if he was of the Aws; [[person/sad-ibn-ubada|Sa'd ibn Ubada]] of the Khazraj objected angrily; [[person/usayd-ibn-hudayr|Usayd ibn Hudayr]] of the Aws, as the transcript has it in a garbled line, rebuked Sa'd ibn Ubada; the two groups were close to fighting until the Prophet came among them and calmed them, calling the tribal zeal rotten. {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep30 00:24:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep30 00:24:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep30 00:25:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep30 00:25:30}
- The speaker relays a scene in the house of [[person/abu-ayyub-al-ansari|Abu Ayyub al-Ansari]] and his wife: he asked her whether she had heard what people said and whether she would have done such a thing; she said no, and he said Aisha was better than her; she answered that Safwan was better than him. {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep30 00:26:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep30 00:26:30} (needs_source)
- The Prophet asked [[person/zaynab-bint-jahsh|Zaynab bint Jahsh]], who said she guards her hearing and sight and knows only good of Aisha; the speaker says [[person/hamna-bint-jahsh|Hamna bint Jahsh]] was the one who took up the rumour most. {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep30 00:27:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep30 00:28:00}
- Aisha wept in her parents' house; an Ansari woman sat weeping with her; the Prophet came in and said that if she was innocent God would clear her, and if she had sinned she should ask forgiveness, since a believer who confesses and repents is forgiven. {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep30 00:28:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep30 00:29:00}
- She asked her father and her mother to answer for her; neither knew what to say. She then said that if she told the truth they would not believe her, and if she confessed to what she had not done they would believe her, and that she could only answer as the father of Yusuf answers in the Qur'an, by patience and by seeking God's help; the verse is not quoted here. {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep30 00:29:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep30 00:30:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep30 00:31:00} (the Yusuf reference is the speaker's; not linked)
- The speaker says that Gabriel then came down and the Prophet laughed and told her that God had cleared her. Aisha is said to have answered that she had hoped only for a dream from the Prophet, and never imagined that Qur'an would be revealed about her to remain until the Day of Resurrection. {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep30 00:31:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep30 00:32:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep30 00:32:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep30 00:33:00}
- The speaker recites and explains the verses on the slander in [[passage/quran-24-11|Sura al-Nur, verse 11]], [[passage/quran-24-12|verse 12]] (believers should think well of one another), [[passage/quran-24-15|verse 15]] (people repeat with their tongues what they have no knowledge of), [[passage/quran-24-16|verse 16]], [[passage/quran-24-17|verse 17]] (a warning never to return to the like of it) and [[passage/quran-24-19|verse 19]] (those who love that indecency should be spread among believers). The verses are not typed here; he reads them on the screen as paraphrased in this summary. {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep30 00:33:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep30 00:34:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep30 00:35:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep30 00:36:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep30 00:37:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep30 00:37:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep30 00:38:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep30 00:38:30}
- He notes that the Prophet told the believers to teach the Surat al-Nur to their women, and that Aisha, when her mother urged her to stand up and thank the Prophet, answered that she would stand up to praise God alone, who had cleared her. {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep30 00:36:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep30 00:36:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep30 00:54:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep30 00:55:00}
- The speaker draws his lessons: patience first, no haste, and no word that wounds a wife's feelings; from the Prophet's gentle question during the illness he takes that mercy and restraint should go together with the search for the truth. {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep30 00:43:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep30 00:44:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep30 00:44:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep30 00:45:30}
- He lists the Prophet's trials as the speaker presents them: the death of his sons, the death of his beloved wife Khadija, the death of his uncle Hamza, and the hardships of Mecca; he urges listeners to be patient in their own trials. {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep30 00:47:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep30 00:48:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep30 00:48:30}
- A participant reads the affair as a lesson in patience and mercy towards wives, and in Aisha's trust in God; the speaker says the story ends with the verses that clear her and that the Qur'an speaks of a great calumny. {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep30 00:49:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep30 00:49:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep30 00:37:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep30 00:37:30}
- The speaker closes by saying that the love of the Prophet is beyond description, but that worship belongs to God, who alone holds the favour in this matter. {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep30 00:55:00}

## Left out of this episode 30

Not written from episode 30: the transcript's readings of names that are not clear: the name the transcript gives to the expedition at its first mention (00:03:00; the museum reads the expedition from the later passage at 00:05:30, linked as Bani al-Mustaliq); the name of Safwan ibn al-Mu'attal, which the transcript reads in garbled forms at 00:09:30 and 00:12:00 (the museum reads Safwan ibn al-Mu'attal, linked); the poet the transcript reads as "Hasan ibn Sabit" at 00:27:00 (the museum reads Hassan ibn Thabit, linked as the museum's reading); the servant the transcript reads as "Buraida" at 00:23:00 and 00:23:30 (the museum reads Barira; not linked, no record); the name of the speaker's Ansari companion in the quarrel on the way home, which the transcript does not give clearly (00:04:00 to 00:04:30); the name the transcript gives in a garbled line at 00:35:30 as the one who first raised the matter; the word for the Yusuf story's father, read as "Abu Yusuf" (00:31:00; not linked); and the words the transcript gives Umm Mistah at 00:19:00, which are summarised only as what she told Aisha.

Transcript machine repetition loops at 00:08:00 and 00:47:00, and the final segment at 00:55:30 (repetition and very short), were discarded as non-speech; the Qur'anic verses read on screen are not typed; the participants' personal anecdotes about marriage (00:45:30 to 00:46:00) are summarised only as their opinions; the speaker's remarks on present-day marriages are not written beyond the advice recorded above.


## Episode 31: Hafsa bint Umar, as the speaker and the audience tell it: her family and first marriage, her widowhood, Umar's search for a husband for her, the Prophet's marriage to her, the honey episode, the withdrawal from the wives, the copy of the Qur'an and her death

:::perspectives
- **The speaker's view on fathers, early marriage and choosing a husband (his opinion):** he says Umar's search for a husband for his daughter shows that a father should look for a good man for his daughter and should not delay her marriage for the sake of appearances; he relays a saying he attributes to the Prophet, that he saw no way for two who love each other but marriage (the speaker's wording; needs_source). {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep31 00:14:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep31 00:17:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep31 00:20:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep31 00:20:30} (needs_source)
- **The speaker's argument that the marriage bound the future Rightly Guided Caliphs to the Prophet's household (contested; his interpretation):** he says the Prophet married his daughters to two of the men who would later be caliphs, Uthman and Ali, and took as wives Hafsa, the daughter of Umar, and Aisha, the daughter of Abu Bakr, so that the community would be held together after his death; the museum records this as his reading of the marriages, not as a settled account of their motives. {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep31 00:28:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep31 00:29:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep31 00:29:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep31 00:30:00} (needs_source)
- **The speaker on the honey episode and the law (his opinion):** he argues that the honey episode should not be turned into a ruling against what God made lawful, and that the verse on the Prophet forbidding what God made lawful to please his wives is a lesson about his conduct, not about the rules of eating. {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep31 00:38:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep31 00:39:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep31 00:39:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep31 00:40:00}
- **Studio participants on fathers, daughters and the freedom women had with the Prophet (participants' opinions):** a participant says the bond between fathers and daughters was strong in that time and is weaker now; another says the Prophet gave his wives room to speak, and that people today have forgotten his example and look to distant models (the words are the participants', attributed to them). {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep31 00:45:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep31 00:46:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep31 00:47:00}
- **The speaker's reading of the withdrawal from the wives (his reading):** he praises the Prophet's balance between mercy and firmness and says the withdrawal was meant to show his displeasure and not to end the marriages; the museum rests on the record for the account of the withdrawal and does not add a ruling. {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep31 00:48:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep31 00:49:00} (needs_source)
:::

- The speaker presents the Prophet's wives in the order of their marriages, with the audience reciting the names, and says the series treats them as mothers of the believers, so that the reader should hear each as a mother. {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep31 00:00:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep31 00:00:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep31 00:01:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep31 00:02:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep31 00:02:30}
- He takes as the principle of the series the verse that the Prophet is closer to believers than their own selves and that his wives are their mothers, [[passage/quran-33-6|Sura al-Ahzab, verse 6]]. {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep31 00:03:00}
- Hafsa's mother is Zaynab bint Maz'un, [[person/zaynab-bint-mazun|Zaynab bint Maz'un]], and her maternal uncle is [[person/uthman-ibn-mazun|Uthman ibn Maz'un]], one of the early Companions, of whom the series gives no separate episode because he died young. {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep31 00:03:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep31 00:04:00}
- The speaker tells how a Meccan notable, whom the transcript reads as al-Mughira (the museum reads [[person/al-walid-ibn-al-mughira|al-Walid ibn al-Mughira]]; not confirmed by the transcript), offered Uthman ibn Maz'un his protection, and Uthman refused, preferring God's protection. {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep31 00:04:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep31 00:04:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep31 00:05:00}
- He tells the story of Uthman's exchange with a poet, [[person/labid-ibn-rabia|Labid ibn Rabi'a]]: Uthman said he had spoken truly when Labid said that all but God is vain, then said he had lied when Labid went on to say that all bliss must perish, since the bliss of Paradise does not perish; the Meccans beat Uthman until he lost the sight of one eye, and he said his healthy eye longed for the other in God's cause. {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep31 00:05:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep31 00:06:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep31 00:06:30}
- Hafsa's full brother is [[person/abdullah-ibn-umar|Abdullah ibn Umar]]; the speaker names him as the one who held the Sunna firmly. {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep31 00:07:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep31 00:07:30}
- The speaker says Hafsa was born five years before the call, that she was about thirty-five years younger than the Prophet on his count, and that she was first married at about twelve, in the seventh year (his figures; the museum has not checked them and marks them as needing a source). {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep31 00:07:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep31 00:08:00} (needs_source)
- He says that early marriages at that age were common among the Arabs and also among Jews of that time, and that people then matured younger than they do now. {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep31 00:08:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep31 00:09:00}
- Her first husband was Khunays ibn Hudhafa al-Sahmi (clear in the transcript; not linked), who had made both migrations, to Abyssinia and then to Medina; the speaker says his brother [[person/abdullah-ibn-hudhafa-al-sahmi|Abdullah ibn Hudhafa al-Sahmi]] carried the Prophet's letters to the rulers of Rome and Persia. {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep31 00:09:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep31 00:09:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep31 00:10:00}
- The speaker says the couple had no children, and counts their married life as six years in Mecca and three in Medina, nine years in all (his count; needs_source). {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep31 00:10:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep31 00:10:30} (needs_source)
- Khunays was struck by an arrow at the battle of [[event/battle-of-uhud|Uhud]] and died of the wound, the speaker says. {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep31 00:12:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep31 00:13:00}
- After his death Hafsa grieved deeply; the speaker gives her age then as twenty-one, and says that for seven or eight months no one came to propose to her, which he explains by the custom of the time that women married soon after widowhood. {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep31 00:13:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep31 00:13:30} (needs_source)
- Umar, seeing his daughter grieve and no suitor come, decided to offer her to a husband himself, and the speaker tells of his search through the Companions. {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep31 00:14:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep31 00:14:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep31 00:21:00}
- Umar first went to [[person/abu-bakr|Abu Bakr]], offered him Hafsa, and Abu Bakr said nothing; Umar was angry. {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep31 00:21:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep31 00:22:00}
- He then went to [[person/uthman-ibn-affan|Uthman ibn Affan]], whose wife, the Prophet's daughter [[person/ruqayya-bint-muhammad|Ruqayya]] (the transcript's name is garbled; the museum reads Ruqayya), had died, and whom he says had since married the Prophet's other daughter, [[person/umm-kulthum-bint-muhammad|Umm Kulthum]]; Uthman said he did not wish to marry at that time, and Umar was angry. {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep31 00:22:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep31 00:22:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep31 00:23:00}
- Umar went to the Prophet, who smiled and told him that Hafsa should marry one better than Uthman and Uthman one better than Hafsa; Umar understood that the Prophet had already spoken of Hafsa to Abu Bakr and Uthman, who therefore had said nothing. {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep31 00:23:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep31 00:24:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep31 00:24:30}
- The speaker relays that the Prophet then told Umar that he himself was asking for Hafsa and that Uthman would marry Umm Kulthum. Abu Bakr, meeting Umar, understood that the matter was settled, and explained that the Prophet had mentioned Hafsa to him and he would not reveal the Prophet's secret. {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep31 00:25:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep31 00:25:30}
- The speaker draws from this the lesson of keeping a secret entrusted to one, and quotes the saying that among the worst sins before God is a man telling his wife a secret and her spreading it. {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep31 00:26:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep31 00:26:30} (needs_source)
- The speaker explains that the Prophet's marriage to Hafsa served, in his view, the mission: that the Rightly Guided Caliphs, Abu Bakr, Umar, Uthman and Ali, should be bound to the Prophet's household so that they would be heard after his death; in that frame the Prophet married his daughters Umm Kulthum to Uthman and Fatima to Ali, and took Aisha and Hafsa, the daughters of Abu Bakr and Umar, as wives. {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep31 00:29:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep31 00:30:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep31 00:30:30} (needs_source)
- He says Hafsa was known for worship, with much fasting and night prayer, and for jealousy, which he calls a natural trait of women that was stronger in her and was known of her before her second marriage. {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep31 00:31:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep31 00:31:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep31 00:32:00}
- Umar, the speaker relays, warned his daughter not to be proud because of the Prophet's love for Aisha, since Aisha had a place in the Prophet's heart that Hafsa should not compete with, and that her father was not like Aisha's. {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep31 00:31:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep31 00:32:00} (needs_source)
- Hafsa and Aisha became close and allied with each other. The speaker says that the Prophet's love for Khadija was the deepest of all: when Aisha said that God had given him a wife better than her, the Prophet answered that God had given him none better than Khadija. {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep31 00:32:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep31 00:33:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep31 00:33:30} (needs_source)
- After Khadija, the speaker says, Zaynab bint Jahsh was nearest to Aisha in the Prophet's affection, and Zaynab kept honey, which the Prophet liked to take in her house. {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep31 00:34:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep31 00:34:30}
- The honey episode as told: Aisha and Hafsa agreed that when the Prophet came to one of them, she would say that she smelled mughafir on his breath, and he would answer that he had not eaten it, and she would suggest that he had perhaps eaten honey from a bee that had fed on such a plant; the speaker says the plan was to reduce the Prophet's visits to Zaynab. {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep31 00:34:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep31 00:35:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep31 00:36:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep31 00:36:30}
- The speaker describes mughafir as a plant of Arabia with a strong smell that people dislike, and says the Prophet loved fragrance; he adds that Anas praised the Prophet's scent. {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep31 00:35:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep31 00:35:30} (needs_source)
- He says the Prophet went to Hafsa and then to Aisha, and each told him the same thing; the Prophet smiled at Aisha, and then said that he would not eat honey again. {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep31 00:37:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep31 00:37:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep31 00:38:00}
- The speaker recites the opening verse of [[passage/quran-66-1|Sura al-Tahrim]], which asks why the Prophet should forbid what God has made lawful to him to seek his wives' pleasure. {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep31 00:38:30}
- Hafsa's question on the people of the tree of Hudaybiyya is told as follows: the Prophet said that the people of the tree, who had pledged allegiance at [[event/treaty-of-hudaybiyya|Hudaybiyya]], would not enter the Fire, and Hafsa asked about the verse that there is none of you but will come to it, to which he recited the verse that God saves those who feared Him, [[passage/quran-19-71|Sura Maryam, verse 71]] and [[passage/quran-19-72|verse 72]]. {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep31 00:42:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep31 00:42:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep31 00:43:00} (needs_source)
- The speaker relays that the wives used to question the Prophet on matters and that Umar scolded Hafsa for it, reminding her of Aisha's standing; he attributes to Umar the words that she should not be deceived. {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep31 00:43:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep31 00:44:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep31 00:45:00} (needs_source)
- He says the wives asked the Prophet for more maintenance after the conquests, including Khaybar, and that they pressed him until he withdrew from them for a time, showing his displeasure (the length of the withdrawal is not given as a number in this passage). {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep31 00:48:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep31 00:48:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep31 00:49:00}
