- The speaker relays the rumour in Medina that the Prophet had divorced his wives, and tells of Umar, who lived in the outskirts of Medina and took turns with a neighbour to visit the Prophet. {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep31 00:49:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep31 00:50:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep31 00:50:30}
- Umar heard the rumour from his neighbour, went to Hafsa, who was weeping, and then to the mosque, where the Companions were weeping by the pulpit; he asked for leave to see the Prophet through the servant Rabah, was refused twice, and was let in on the third request. {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep31 00:50:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep31 00:51:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep31 00:51:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep31 00:52:00}
- Inside, the Prophet was on a mat that had marked his side, and Umar said that Kisra and Caesar were in their luxury; the Prophet answered that the others were pleased with this world and they with the next. {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep31 00:52:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep31 00:52:30}
- Umar then asked whether the Prophet had divorced his wives, and the Prophet said no; the speaker says Umar then went out and gave the takbir in the mosque. {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep31 00:53:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep31 00:53:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep31 00:54:00}
- The speaker says that Hafsa kept the one copy of the Qur'an written under Abu Bakr, which Uthman later used to make copies sent to the regions; she kept it until her death. {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep31 00:54:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep31 00:54:30} (needs_source)
- Her death, as the speaker gives it: she died in the time of Muawiya in the year 55 AH (his date; needs_source), was prayed over by [[person/marwan-ibn-al-hakam|Marwan ibn al-Hakam]] and buried in al-Baqi'; Aisha walked among the first mourners, weeping and calling her the daughter of her father; her brother [[person/abdullah-ibn-umar|Abdullah ibn Umar]] asked her for a prayer. {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep31 00:55:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep31 00:55:30} (needs_source)
- The speaker ends with the lesson of Hafsa as a mother of the believers and says that the next episode will treat three further wives of the Prophet. {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep31 00:56:00}

## Left out of this episode 31

Not written from episode 31: the names the audience recites in the opening segments (00:00:30 to 00:02:30), where the transcript is garbled and the names are given only in the order the speaker states; the exchange at 00:07:30 about Abdullah ibn Umar and the mother, which the transcript renders garbled and which is not written; the Egyptian proverb about marrying a daughter while one's parents live, at 00:14:30 (the speaker's words, summarised as his view of fathers); the speaker's remark at 00:19:00 that a man kept from marriage who falls into sin shares the sin, which he attributes to a report he heard and which is summarised only as his view; the Ruqayya name where the transcript's form is garbled (00:22:00; the museum reading is linked); the speaker's arithmetic on Hafsa's age beyond the figures given above; and the verses on the story of Shu'ayb and Musa, which the speaker recites in paraphrase and which are not linked, since the verse text is not typed here.

Transcript machine repetition loops at 00:19:30 and 00:44:00 were discarded as non-speech; the final segment at 00:56:30 is non-Arabic repetition and was discarded; the participants' remarks on the Hajj and on the present-day forgetting of the Prophet's example are summarised in one line, and the rest of their comments in that passage is not written where the transcript is garbled.

## Episode 33: Zaynab bint Jahsh: her lineage and family, her brothers, her marriage to Zayd ibn Harithah, the verses on abolishing adoption, and Juwayriya bint al-Harith and the Banu al-Mustaliq, as the speaker and the audience tell it

:::perspectives
- **The speaker's view on social equality in marriage (his opinion):** he holds that equality between spouses, especially in social standing and lineage, matters for a marriage to last, and that he means the closeness of the two families, not money. {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep33 00:20:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep33 00:20:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep33 00:21:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep33 00:45:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep33 00:46:00}
- **The speaker's reply to a narration that says the Prophet hid a love for Zaynab (his reply to the narration):** he answers a report that the Prophet concealed affection for Zaynab, calls it weak and without basis, and holds that the verse itself explains the episode. {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep33 00:22:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep33 00:22:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep33 00:23:00}
- **The verses as proof of prophethood (his argument):** he argues that if the Prophet had composed the Qur'an himself he would not have included a revelation that rebukes him and exposes what he kept hidden in his heart, and so the revelation is from God. {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep33 00:24:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep33 00:25:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep33 00:25:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep33 00:26:00}
- **The speaker on Juwayriya and the conversion of her people (his opinion):** he holds that Juwayriya's sincerity and the strength of a woman's feeling when it turns to God were the reason her people became Muslims, and that this shows the social effect women can have. {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep33 00:42:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep33 00:43:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep33 00:44:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep33 00:44:30}
- **Studio participants on the "ethics of war" (participants' opinions):** one participant says the army that came to fight the Prophet became Muslim after it was taken prisoner, and another says the phrase "ethics of war" was not known among nations before Islam; the speaker sets this out without settling it by a source. {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep33 00:46:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep33 00:47:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep33 00:47:30} (needs_source)
:::

- The speaker opens by saying the series takes up the Mothers of the Believers one after another in the order of the Prophet's marriages to them, and that the previous episodes ended with Umm Salama. {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep33 00:00:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep33 00:01:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep33 00:01:30}
- The speaker asks the listener to treat each wife as a mother, and cites the verse that the Prophet is nearer to the believers than they are to themselves and that his wives are their mothers, and notes that the series follows the order of the marriages. {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep33 00:02:00} [[passage/quran-33-6|Surat al-Ahzab, verse 6]]
- He begins with Zaynab bint Jahsh. He says her mother was Umayma bint Abd al-Muttalib, the Prophet's aunt, and that her family was among the most prominent of Quraysh and among the most present in the history of the Companions. {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep33 00:02:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep33 00:03:00}
- He names her brother Abdullah ibn Jahsh, whom he describes as one of the people most devoted to God. He tells of Abdullah's prayer on the day of Uhud that he would meet a fierce enemy, be killed and mutilated, and say to God that it was for Him; the speaker says God confirmed it. {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep33 00:03:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep33 00:04:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep33 00:04:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep33 00:05:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep33 00:05:30}
- He names her sister Hamna bint Jahsh, the wife of Mus'ab ibn Umayr. He describes Mus'ab as the most handsome youth of Quraysh, the first man the Prophet sent to Medina to teach its people Islam, and says he was killed at Uhud. {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep33 00:06:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep33 00:06:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep33 00:07:00} (needs_source)
- He counts the relatives Zaynab lost at Uhud: her brother, her sister's husband and her uncle. He says the rumour that the Prophet had been killed reached Hamna before the news of her brother did, and that when a Companion asked her about her brother she said he was well as long as the Prophet was well. {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep33 00:07:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep33 00:08:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep33 00:08:30}
- He gives Hamna's words to the Prophet when she met him: every calamity is light after you, O Messenger of God. He says the scene shows how the Companions regarded the Prophet. {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep33 00:09:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep33 00:09:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep33 00:10:00}
- He says Zaynab had reached marriageable age, and that the Prophet wished to marry her to Zayd ibn Harithah, whom the Prophet had adopted and loved very much. {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep33 00:10:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep33 00:10:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep33 00:11:00}
- He tells Zayd's story: Khadija gave him to the Prophet; later his father and uncle came to ask for him back for a ransom; the Prophet let Zayd choose, and Zayd chose to stay; the Prophet then declared him his son before the people, and he was called Zayd ibn Muhammad. {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep33 00:11:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep33 00:11:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep33 00:12:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep33 00:12:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep33 00:13:00}
- He says Aisha said that had Zayd lived the Prophet would have made him his successor, and offers this as evidence of the Prophet's love for him; he describes the Prophet embracing Zayd when Zayd knocked at his door. {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep33 00:13:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep33 00:13:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep33 00:14:00}
- He says that when the verse abolishing adoption came down, each adopted son was once again to be called after his own father, so Zayd became Zayd ibn Harithah again, and that he is the only Companion whose name appears in the Qur'an, a claim the speaker gives in his own words. {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep33 00:14:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep33 00:14:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep33 00:15:00} (needs_source)
- He says the [[passage/quran-33-4|verses on adoption]] directed that sons be called after their fathers, to keep lineages intact and so that no one's right is taken through adoption. {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep33 00:14:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep33 00:26:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep33 00:27:00}
- He says the Prophet wished to honour Zayd by marrying him to Zaynab, but Zaynab was reluctant because Zayd had been a freed slave; she said she did not want him. A verse then came that makes the command of God and his Messenger binding on a believing man or woman, and the speaker takes it as the ground for accepting the marriage. {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep33 00:15:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep33 00:16:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep33 00:16:30} [[passage/quran-33-36|Surat al-Ahzab, verse 36]]
- He says the Prophet did sometimes intercede for believers in marriage, but this was a special case, and gives the example of Barira and her husband Mughith: the Prophet let her choose and she chose separation, while Mughith wept behind her on the road. The name Barira is read from a garbled transcript line. {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep33 00:16:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep33 00:17:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep33 00:17:30} (needs_source)
- He cites a saying he attributes to the Prophet: "I do not see for two who love each other anything but marriage". He gives it in his own words and offers no chain of narrators in the episode. {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep33 00:18:30} (needs_source)
- He says the marriage of Zaynab to Zayd did not last, and that the gap in social standing was at the root of the complaints: Zayd complained to the Prophet and asked for a divorce, and the Prophet told him to keep his wife and fear God. {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep33 00:21:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep33 00:22:00}
- He says the Prophet knew from God that Zaynab would become his wife and hid this in himself out of fear of what people would say, and he counts this as one of the signs of prophethood. {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep33 00:24:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep33 00:25:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep33 00:25:30}
- He says the verse put an end to adoption, that what people had held about it was removed, and that Muslims came to fear doubts about their faith and to hesitate to repeat what the verse contained. {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep33 00:26:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep33 00:27:00}
- He says Zaynab married the Prophet after the Battle of the Trench in the fifth year after the Hijra (his date, which needs a source), that she was the most generous of the wives in charity, and that she worked with her own hands and gave away what she earned. {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep33 00:27:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep33 00:28:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep33 00:28:30} (needs_source)
- He says that after the Prophet's death the wives measured their arms to see which of them would follow him first; Sawda was the tallest, and Zaynab, who died first among them, was first to follow him, which he attributes to her great charity. {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep33 00:28:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep33 00:28:30} (needs_source)
- He says Zaynab's gifts were large. He tells that when a large sum reached her she gave it all away in one day to those in need, that Umar advised her to keep some of it, and that she prayed God not to send her such a sum again. {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep33 00:29:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep33 00:29:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep33 00:30:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep33 00:30:30} (needs_source)
- He says Zaynab died in the twentieth year after the Hijra (his date, which needs a source), that she was the first of the Mothers of the Believers to follow the Prophet after him, that Umar led the funeral prayer over her, and that she was buried in al-Baqi'. {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep33 00:31:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep33 00:32:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep33 00:32:30} (needs_source)
- He moves on to Juwayriya bint al-Harith. He says her earlier name is garbled in the transcript and is not written here, that the Prophet changed it to Juwayriya, that she was from the Banu al-Mustaliq, and that her father al-Harith was the chief of his people and was gathering an army against the Prophet. {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep33 00:33:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep33 00:33:30} (needs_source)
- He says the Prophet got ahead of the Banu al-Mustaliq army to their water, at the place known as al-Muraysi' (the transcript's reading is unsure), defeated them, took a whole household prisoner, and the spoils were divided among the Muslims. {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep33 00:33:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep33 00:34:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep33 00:34:30} [[event/expedition-of-banu-al-mustaliq|The expedition of the Banu al-Mustaliq]] (needs_source)
- He says Juwayriya fell to the share of Thabit ibn Qays, who agreed to a manumission contract for a sum, and that she went to the Prophet to ask for help in paying it. {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep33 00:35:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep33 00:35:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep33 00:36:00}
- He says the Prophet offered her marriage and help with the manumission, she accepted, the Prophet married her, and the Companions then freed the prisoners of the Banu al-Mustaliq out of respect for her; he says this led to the conversion of the whole tribe. {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep33 00:36:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep33 00:37:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep33 00:37:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep33 00:38:00} (needs_source)
- He says Juwayriya's father came with camels to ransom his daughter, and when he arrived he learned that the tribe had become Muslim and had been freed, and so he too became Muslim; the number of camels is given in a garbled phrase in the transcript. {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep33 00:38:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep33 00:39:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep33 00:39:30} (needs_source)
- He says that Juwayriya's standing came through her sincerity and not through wealth, and that God honoured her. {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep33 00:40:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep33 00:41:00}
- He gives the audience's comments on Juwayriya: one says her sincerity showed before she announced her Islam, another that a sincere feeling moves a woman to influence her people; the speaker says this meaning returns in every age. {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep33 00:42:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep33 00:43:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep33 00:44:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep33 00:44:30}
- He gives a comment on mercy in Islam: the Companions treated prisoners with kindness, the phrase "ethics of war" was not known before Islam, and kindness to prisoners came from the religion. {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep33 00:45:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep33 00:47:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep33 00:47:30} (needs_source)
- He introduces Safiyya bint Huyayy for the next episode and closes with a prayer for the Mothers of the Believers. {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep33 00:48:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep33 00:50:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep33 00:50:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep33 00:51:00}

## Left out of this episode 33

Not written from episode 33: the audience's recitation of the wives' names at the start (00:01:30 to 00:04:00), where the transcript is garbled, so only the order the speaker states is kept. The segment at 00:23:30 is a machine repetition loop and was discarded, and so were 00:41:30 and 00:42:30, which are repetition without clear speech. The speaker's remarks on the Jewish tribes, including Banu Qaynuqa and Banu al-Nadir, are left for the Safiyya episode. The scattered comments of the audience between 00:40:00 and 00:45:00 are summarised in their general sense, without names, because the sound is unclear. The speaker's remarks on the names of the sons of Abdullah ibn Jahsh and other names are not written, because they cannot be checked from the transcript.

## Episode 34: Safiyya bint Huyayy: the Jews of Medina, the dream, Khaybar, and her marriage to the Prophet; then Umm Habiba Ramla bint Abi Sufyan: the migration to Abyssinia, the proposal by proxy, and the distance from her father, as the speaker and the audience tell it

:::perspectives
- **The speaker on mercy and tolerance (his view):** he separates mercy from tolerance, and holds that the Prophet's marriage to Safiyya is an application of mercy and not only of tolerance, and that Islam keeps family ties even when the family is Jewish. {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep34 00:24:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep34 00:24:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep34 00:25:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep34 00:26:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep34 00:26:30}
- **A comment on marriage as a way to end captivity (a comment from the audience):** a participant says the Prophet's marriage to the daughter of a tribal chief led the Companions to be shy about taking women as captives, and that the wisdom lay in ending the idea of slavery; the speaker presents this comment without judging it. {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep34 00:20:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep34 00:20:30} (needs_source)
- **Marriage at an early age (his view; the figures need a source):** he says marriage at that age was common in the desert environment and among Jews, and holds this to be part of the custom of the time; he gives figures for Safiyya's age in this passage, so only what the museum can tie to a source is written. {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep34 00:15:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep34 00:15:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep34 00:16:00} (needs_source)
- **The speaker's lesson on speech and backbiting (his lesson):** he draws from the episode of the wives and Safiyya a lesson against speaking ill of others, warns against backbiting, slander and words that anger God, and makes this general for fathers, teachers, mothers and young people. {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep34 00:30:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep34 00:31:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep34 00:31:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep34 00:32:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep34 00:32:30}
- **Participants on Islam as mercy to the worlds (participants' opinions):** a participant holds that Safiyya's marriage shows the religion is one of mercy, and that the Companions learned from the Prophet to love someone who had been an enemy once he became a Muslim; the speaker presents this as a lesson in tolerance. {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep34 00:21:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep34 00:22:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep34 00:25:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep34 00:26:30} (needs_source)
- **The speaker's telling of the story of Abu Ayyub al-Ansari (his telling; needs a source):** he tells it as it is told, including what is said about his guarding the tent, the Prophet's prayer for him, and his wish to be buried near the walls of Constantinople; all of it comes from the speaker without a chain of narrators in the episode. {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep34 00:28:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep34 00:28:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep34 00:29:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep34 00:29:30} (needs_source)
:::

- The speaker lists the wives' names in the order of their marriages, and says the earlier episodes covered eight of them and this and the next will cover the rest. {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep34 00:02:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep34 00:02:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep34 00:03:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep34 00:04:00}
- The speaker goes through the names on screen in order, and says memorising them matters because the wives are mothers of the believers. {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep34 00:04:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep34 00:05:00}
- He begins with Safiyya bint Huyayy, and says her father was the chief of the Banu al-Nadir, that the Jews of Medina were three large tribes, the Banu Qaynuqa, the Banu al-Nadir and the Banu Qurayza, and that the Prophet had first made a covenant with them. {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep34 00:05:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep34 00:05:30} [[group/banu-nadir|Banu al-Nadir]] [[group/banu-qaynuqa|Banu Qaynuqa]] [[group/banu-qurayza|Banu Qurayza]]
- He says the Banu Qaynuqa broke the covenant after an incident in the gold market, when a Jewish man exposed a Muslim woman, and a Muslim killed him, and that the Prophet then expelled them from Medina. {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep34 00:06:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep34 00:06:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep34 00:07:00} (needs_source)
- He says the Banu al-Nadir tried to kill the Prophet by dropping a rock on him from the top of a house, and that Gabriel told him to return to Medina; the Prophet then expelled them. {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep34 00:07:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep34 00:08:00} (needs_source)
- He says Huyayy ibn Akhtab, Safiyya's father, was the first of the Banu al-Nadir to be expelled, went to Khaybar, and gathered the Arab tribes to besiege Medina in the Battle of the Trench. {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep34 00:08:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep34 00:08:30} [[event/battle-of-the-trench|Battle of the Trench]]
- He says the Jews knew the Prophet's description from their scriptures, that Safiyya was the object of her father's and uncle's close attention, and that her qualities seemed to them to match those of the wife of the last prophet. {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep34 00:09:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep34 00:09:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep34 00:10:00} (needs_source)
- He says the Jews spread in Medina that the last prophet would come from among them, and when the Prophet came from the Arabs they denied him; he says her father and uncle, who knew his description best, went out to meet him to test him. {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep34 00:10:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep34 00:11:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep34 00:11:30} (needs_source)
- He tells that Huyayy questioned the Prophet about his father, grandfather and sheep, then saw the seal of prophethood on his back and said he found it in their books; he says her uncle Yasir told Huyayy that this was the one, and Huyayy said he would stay hostile to him as long as he lived. {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep34 00:12:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep34 00:12:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep34 00:13:00} (needs_source)
- He says Safiyya was eleven years old when she had a dream that the matter had come down from heaven and settled in her lap; when she told her father, he struck her and said she wanted to marry the Prophet of the Arabs. {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep34 00:13:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep34 00:14:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep34 00:14:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep34 00:15:00} (needs_source)
- He says her father married her to a Jewish man (the name in the transcript is garbled; the museum reads it as Salam ibn Mishkam), and that she stayed with him for a period. He gives her age at that marriage as eleven and says she stayed with him until seventeen; these figures need a source. {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep34 00:15:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep34 00:16:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep34 00:17:00} (needs_source)
- He says Safiyya went with her husband and her father to Khaybar after the Banu al-Nadir were expelled, and that they settled there. {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep34 00:16:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep34 00:16:30} [[place/khaybar|Khaybar]]
- He tells of the Battle of Khaybar: the Muslims numbered about 1,400, the Jews about ten thousand in seven fortresses, the Muslims won, and Huyayy ibn Akhtab and Salam ibn Mishkam were killed (the figures are his and need a source). {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep34 00:16:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep34 00:17:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep34 00:17:30} [[event/battle-of-khaybar|Battle of Khaybar]] (needs_source)
- He says Safiyya was taken captive and brought to the Prophet; she greeted him, he asked whether she knew he was the Messenger of God, and then offered to marry her in place of captivity, and she accepted. {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep34 00:18:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep34 00:18:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep34 00:19:00} (needs_source)
- He gives an audience comment that the Prophet wanted to protect the captives from enslavement, and that when he married the daughter of a chief the Companions were shy about taking women; the speaker presents this as wisdom. {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep34 00:20:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep34 00:20:30} (needs_source)
- He presents audience comments on mercy in religion: mercy in Islam includes the one who was an enemy, and the Prophet's faith was founded on mercy to the worlds. {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep34 00:21:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep34 00:21:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep34 00:22:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep34 00:22:30} [[passage/quran-21-107|Surat al-Anbiya, verse 107]]
- He tells of a man who was fiercely hostile to the Muslims and then became one; he says Umar said that the man was dearer to him than some of his own children, and draws the lesson that Islam turns hearts. The man's name in the transcript is garbled and the museum reads it as Umayr ibn Wahb. {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep34 00:25:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep34 00:26:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep34 00:26:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep34 00:27:00} (needs_source)
- He says the Prophet went in to Safiyya after the army returned, having waited because she feared for him from the Jews of Khaybar, and that this explains the delay. {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep34 00:27:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep34 00:28:00} (needs_source)
- He says Abu Ayyub al-Ansari guarded the Prophet's tent that night with a sword; when the Prophet asked him, he said he feared for him from this woman, and the Prophet prayed that God would protect him as he had protected the Prophet. He says this became well known. {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep34 00:28:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep34 00:29:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep34 00:29:30} (needs_source)
- He adds that Abu Ayyub kept guarding and going on campaigns until he was close to ninety, and that he asked to be buried near the walls of Constantinople (his telling, which needs a source). {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep34 00:30:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep34 00:30:30} [[person/abu-ayyub-al-ansari|Abu Ayyub al-Ansari]] (needs_source)
- He tells of a moment between Aisha and Safiyya, in which Aisha said something about Safiyya's height; the Prophet told her that she had said a word that, if it were mixed into the water of the sea, would change it, and the speaker draws a warning against backbiting from this (his telling, which needs a source). {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep34 00:30:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep34 00:31:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep34 00:31:30} (needs_source)
- He tells of an exchange among the wives and Safiyya in the Prophet's last days, and draws from it that speaking ill of others is a sin; the transcript is garbled at this point, so only the general sense is given (the speaker's reading; the transcript is garbled). {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep34 00:33:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep34 00:33:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep34 00:34:00} (needs_source)
- He says that when Safiyya spoke in a way that angered the wives she wept, and the Prophet told her to say that her father was Aaron, her uncle was Moses and her husband was Muhammad, so that she had joined three prophets. {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep34 00:34:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep34 00:35:00} (needs_source)
- He says Safiyya stayed with the Prophet until his death, that in the caliphate of Uthman she sent food and water to him while he was besieged, and that she was buried in al-Baqi'. {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep34 00:35:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep34 00:36:00} [[person/uthman-ibn-affan|Uthman ibn Affan]] (needs_source)
- He tells of an incident in Umar's caliphate, in which a servant of Safiyya told Umar that Safiyya loved Saturday; Umar asked her, and she answered that God had given her Friday in place of it and that Islam enjoined keeping ties of kinship. {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep34 00:36:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep34 00:36:30} [[person/umar-ibn-al-khattab|Umar ibn al-Khattab]] (needs_source)
- He moves to Umm Habiba, named Ramla bint Abi Sufyan, and says the Prophet married her after she returned from Abyssinia, and that her father Abu Sufyan was among the Prophet's fiercest enemies. {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep34 00:37:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep34 00:37:30} [[person/umm-habiba-bint-abi-sufyan|Umm Habiba bint Abi Sufyan]] [[person/abu-sufyan-ibn-harb|Abu Sufyan ibn Harb]]
- He says her husband Ubaydullah ibn Jahsh migrated with her to Abyssinia, then left Islam, became Christian, and died after drinking heavily (his account, which needs a source), so that Umm Habiba was left alone with her daughter Habiba. {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep34 00:42:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep34 00:42:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep34 00:43:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep34 00:44:00} [[person/ubaydullah-ibn-jahsh|Ubaydullah ibn Jahsh]] (needs_source)
- He says Umm Habiba had no home to return to in Mecca, because she feared her father's revenge, and she stayed in Abyssinia under the protection of the Negus, whom he says embraced Islam in secret. {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep34 00:44:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep34 00:45:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep34 00:45:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep34 00:46:00} [[person/najashi-al-harithi|The Negus]] (needs_source)
- He tells that the Prophet sent to the Negus asking him to propose Umm Habiba on his behalf; the Negus sent a servant woman to her with the good news, she did not believe it at first and did not open the door, and then she did. {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep34 00:46:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep34 00:47:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep34 00:47:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep34 00:48:00} (needs_source)
- He says Umm Habiba was so glad at the news that she gave the servant all that was in her hands of money and jewellery, and he says patience after hardship brings its reward. {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep34 00:48:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep34 00:49:00} (needs_source)
- He says the Negus appointed Khalid ibn Sa'id to conclude the marriage on the Prophet's behalf, that the Negus gave the Prophet a dowry of four hundred (the figure in the transcript; it needs a source), and held a feast for the Muslims. {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep34 00:50:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep34 00:50:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep34 00:51:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep34 00:51:30} [[person/khalid-ibn-said-ibn-al-as|Khalid ibn Sa'id]] (needs_source)
- He says the Negus gave Umm Habiba gifts of perfume, whose scent stayed in her house until she died, and he gives her death as the year 51 AH (his date, which needs a source). {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep34 00:52:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep34 00:52:30} (needs_source)
- He says that when Abu Sufyan came to Medina he asked to visit his daughter, went into her house and tried to sit on the Prophet's bedding, and Umm Habiba folded it away and told him he was a polytheist and unclean. {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep34 00:53:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep34 00:54:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep34 00:54:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep34 00:55:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep34 00:55:30}
- He says Umm Habiba thereby stood with Islam and the Prophet against her father, and that the Prophet approved of her. {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep34 00:55:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep34 00:56:00}
- He tells that before her death Umm Habiba asked Aisha to forgive her, Aisha forgave her, and Umm Habiba said she wished to meet the Prophet with nothing between her and any of his wives; she died and was buried in al-Baqi'. {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep34 00:56:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep34 00:57:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep34 00:57:30} [[person/aisha|Aisha]]
- He closes with a lesson for every woman who has suffered: patience and steadfastness in obedience to God are repaid, and Umm Habiba is an example; he says the next episode will take up three more wives. {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep34 00:58:00}

## Left out of this episode 34

Not written from episode 34: the repeated talk about names at the start, the segment at 00:03:00, which is a machine repetition loop, the segment at 00:19:30, also a loop, and the segment at 00:56:30, which is non-Arabic. The segments at 00:07:00 and 00:38:00 consist of sounds that cannot be transcribed and were left out, and 00:49:30 is repeated laughter with no speech. The audience's remarks on the migration to Abyssinia and on names and degrees of kinship at the edges of the episode are summarised, not quoted, because the transcript is garbled. The speaker's remarks on other wives belong to later episodes and are not written here.

## Episode 35: Maria the Copt and her family in Egypt, Hatib ibn Abi Balta'a's mission to al-Muqawqis, Ibrahim the son of the Prophet and his death, and Maymuna bint al-Harith, the last of the Prophet's wives, as the speaker and the audience tell it

:::perspectives
- **The speaker on Egypt's bond with the Prophet (his view; needs a source):** he holds that the people of Egypt have a kinship and a marriage tie with the Prophet through Hagar and Maria, cites a saying on being kind to the people of Egypt, and gives this in his own words. {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep35 00:20:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep35 00:20:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep35 00:21:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep35 00:21:30} (needs_source)
- **The speaker on a wife's standard of living (his general guidance):** he holds that a husband should, as far as he can, take account of the living conditions his wife grew up in, that this does not mean requiring the same standard, and that marriage is better than leaving it unmade. {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep35 00:22:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep35 00:23:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep35 00:23:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep35 00:24:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep35 00:24:30}
- **The speaker on patience at the death of a child (his view):** he holds that grief for a child does not contradict contentment with God's decree, cites the Prophet's conduct at Ibrahim's death, and gives a saying on the children of Muslims that he uses to console parents (his words; needs a source). {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep35 00:33:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep35 00:33:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep35 00:34:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep35 00:34:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep35 00:35:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep35 00:35:30} (needs_source)
- **Audience comments on the Mothers of the Believers (participants' opinions):** one participant says the Mothers of the Believers came from different origins and that Islam honours good lineage; another remarks that God called the Prophet's wives mothers without calling the Prophet a father; the speaker presents both. {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep35 00:40:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep35 00:40:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep35 00:41:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep35 00:41:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep35 00:42:00}
- **Audience comments on time and on the bond between prophets and Muslims (participants' opinions):** one participant holds that time among Muslims draws so close that a person feels with the prophets, another says the hope of young people in this is great; the speaker presents this without judging it. {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep35 00:43:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep35 00:43:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep35 00:44:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep35 00:44:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep35 00:45:00}
:::

- The episode opens by saying two wives remain, Maria the Copt and Maymuna bint al-Harith, and the speaker shows the names of the wives in order on screen. {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep35 00:00:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep35 00:00:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep35 00:01:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep35 00:01:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep35 00:02:00}
- He says Maria the Copt was from Egypt and was the only wife who was not from the Arabian Peninsula (his claim, which needs a source), and he sees this as an honour for Egypt. {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep35 00:02:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep35 00:03:00} [[person/maria-al-qibtiyya|Maria al-Qibtiyya]] (needs_source)
- He says the Prophet dealt with peoples through his words as he dealt with individuals, and gives sayings about the people of Syria, Yemen and Egypt, holding that the Prophet addressed whole peoples as he addressed persons. {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep35 00:02:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep35 00:03:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep35 00:03:30} (needs_source)
- He says Maria was from Upper Egypt, that her father was a Copt and her mother a Roman Christian, that she had a sister named Sirin, and that the two served in al-Muqawqis's palace (his account; needs a source). {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep35 00:04:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep35 00:04:30} (needs_source)
- He says that in the seventh year the Prophet sent letters to the rulers of the world, and that he sent fourteen messengers on one day, one of them to al-Muqawqis, the great man of the Copts (his count; needs a source). {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep35 00:04:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep35 00:05:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep35 00:05:30} (needs_source)
- He says the Prophet chose messengers who knew languages and dealt well with people, and that the Companions combined worldly skill and learning, and that religion does not prevent work or excellence. {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep35 00:05:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep35 00:06:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep35 00:06:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep35 00:07:00} (needs_source)
- He tells that Hatib ibn Abi Balta'a carried the letter to al-Muqawqis, and reads the text of the letter as he gives it: from Muhammad son of Abdullah to al-Muqawqis, great man of the Copts, peace be on whoever follows the guidance. {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep35 00:07:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep35 00:08:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep35 00:08:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep35 00:09:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep35 00:09:30} [[person/hatib-ibn-abi-baltaa|Hatib ibn Abi Balta'a]]
- He says the letter called the People of the Book to a common word, and that the text shows the Prophet's character; he tells that al-Muqawqis read it and said he knew a prophet had appeared, that he had expected him to come from Syria, that he believed him, but feared for his kingdom. {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep35 00:09:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep35 00:10:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep35 00:10:30} (needs_source)
- He says al-Muqawqis sent gifts with Hatib: two slave girls, Maria and her sister Sirin, honey, woven cloth and a mule, and a reply to the Prophet that was respectful (the list of gifts needs a source). {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep35 00:11:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep35 00:11:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep35 00:12:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep35 00:12:30} (needs_source)
- He says Hatib told the two girls on the road about Hagar, mother of Ishmael, who was an Egyptian slave girl who later was with a prophet, to comfort them. {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep35 00:13:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep35 00:13:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep35 00:14:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep35 00:14:30} [[person/hajar|Hajar]]
- He draws a comparison between Hagar and Maria: both were slave girls from Egypt, and each bore a child to a prophet; he sees this as God's design (his reading; needs a source). {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep35 00:14:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep35 00:15:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep35 00:15:30} (needs_source)
- He says Hatib told the girls about Zamzam and the building of the Ka'ba, and about Hagar, whom Abraham left in the desert with her son by God's command; she said that God would not let them be lost. {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep35 00:15:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep35 00:16:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep35 00:16:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep35 00:17:00} (needs_source)
- He says Hagar spoke her well-known words of patience and trust, and remarks that the people of Egypt are known for patience with hunger rather than with what is forbidden; he then says Hatib offered Islam to Maria and she accepted. {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep35 00:16:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep35 00:17:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep35 00:17:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep35 00:18:00} (needs_source)
- He says Maria reached Medina and went in to the Prophet, and Hatib told him what had happened; the Prophet then gave gifts, and a mule named Duldul is mentioned, which he says had many stories of its own. {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep35 00:18:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep35 00:18:30} (needs_source)
- He says the Prophet married Maria so as to honour the Egyptians, and cites a saying to the effect of being kind to the people of Egypt, because they have kinship and a marriage tie (his words; needs a source). {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep35 00:19:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep35 00:20:00} (needs_source)
- He says Maria's sister Sirin married Hassan ibn Thabit, and that they had a son Abd al-Rahman (his account; needs a source). {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep35 00:21:30} [[person/hassan-ibn-thabit|Hassan ibn Thabit]] (needs_source)
- He says the Prophet lodged Maria in al-Awali, a rural area near Medina with crops and water, because it was closer to her earlier life, and says the house of Umm Ibrahim still stands there (his words; needs a source). {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep35 00:21:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep35 00:22:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep35 00:22:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep35 00:23:00} (needs_source)
- He says a garden at al-Awali became the Prophet's after a Jewish man who embraced Islam on the day of Uhud left him his property, and the Prophet then gave the garden to Maria (the name of the man in the transcript is garbled; the museum reads it as Mukhayriq, with no record linked). {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep35 00:24:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep35 00:25:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep35 00:25:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep35 00:26:00} (needs_source)
- He says Aisha was jealous at the Prophet's frequent visits to Maria, that the Prophet liked to sit with her for the sweetness of her speech, and that Aisha described this (his telling; needs a source). {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep35 00:26:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep35 00:27:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep35 00:27:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep35 00:28:00} (needs_source)
- He says Maria became pregnant in the eighth year after the Hijra and gave birth to Ibrahim in the ninth, and that this was God's mercy (his dates; needs a source). {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep35 00:28:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep35 00:29:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep35 00:29:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep35 00:30:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep35 00:30:30} (needs_source)
- He says Ibrahim died as an infant about a year and a couple of months after his birth, that the Prophet grieved, and that the Prophet said to Ibrahim that they could not avail him anything against God (his dates; needs a source). {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep35 00:31:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep35 00:32:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep35 00:32:30} (needs_source)
- He says the Prophet wept at Ibrahim's death and said that the eye sheds tears and the heart grieves, and that he said only what pleases God; he says the Prophet took the infant on his lap and that Ibrahim died in the Prophet's lap. {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep35 00:33:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep35 00:34:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep35 00:34:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep35 00:35:00} (needs_source)
- He tells a saying on the children of Muslims who die before puberty: that they enter Paradise and take their parents with them (his words; needs a source), and a sacred hadith in which God asks his angels whether they took the son of His servant. {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep35 00:35:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep35 00:35:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep35 00:36:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep35 00:36:30} (needs_source)
- He says the Prophet told Umm Ibrahim that if Ibrahim was her son he was also the Prophet's son, that God would complete his suckling in Paradise, and that the Prophet consoled Maria with this (his words; needs a source). {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep35 00:37:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep35 00:37:30} (needs_source)
- He says Fadl ibn al-Abbas washed Ibrahim's body while the Prophet sat in a corner and watched, that Ibrahim was buried in al-Baqi', and that his tomb is well known. {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep35 00:39:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep35 00:39:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep35 00:40:00} (needs_source)
- He says Maria died about six years after the Prophet's death, in the sixteenth year after the Hijra (his date; needs a source), and was buried in al-Baqi'. {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep35 00:37:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep35 00:38:00} (needs_source)
- He says the Prophet married Maymuna bint al-Harith late, in the seventh year, that she was a widow in Mecca who was weak and could not migrate, and that the Prophet married her to take care of her and to end her loneliness. {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep35 00:46:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep35 00:47:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep35 00:47:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep35 00:48:00} [[person/maymuna-bint-al-harith|Maymuna bint al-Harith]]
- He says Maymuna's mother was Hind bint Awf, that her six daughters were all married to notable men, and that the Prophet called them the believing sisters (his genealogy; needs a source). {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep35 00:48:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep35 00:49:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep35 00:49:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep35 00:50:00} (needs_source)
- He tells that Maymuna waited until the Prophet came for the Umra of the Making Up, that she asked Umm al-Fadl to arrange her marriage, and that the Prophet proposed to her through al-Abbas (the details of the proposal need a source). {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep35 00:50:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep35 00:50:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep35 00:51:00} (needs_source)
- He says the Prophet married Maymuna in Mecca during the Umra, then left with her; he says Quraysh had given him three days, and when he wished to hold a feast they said they had no need of his food, so that he wanted to draw nearer to Quraysh by staying (his account; needs a source). {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep35 00:51:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep35 00:51:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep35 00:52:00} (needs_source)
- He says the Prophet consummated the marriage with Maymuna at Sarif on the road between Mecca and Medina, that she was about thirty-five years old (his figure; needs a source), and that she was the last of the Prophet's wives. {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep35 00:52:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep35 00:52:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep35 00:53:00} (needs_source)
- He says Maymuna was a skilled cook whom the Prophet liked to eat from, that each of the wives had a distinctive skill, that Ibn Abbas narrated from her, and that she was the maternal aunt of Ibn Abbas (his kinship account; needs a source). {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep35 00:53:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep35 00:53:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep35 00:54:00} [[person/abdullah-ibn-abbas|Abdullah ibn Abbas]] (needs_source)
- He tells that after the Prophet's death Maymuna answered a rumour that a husband may not come near his wife during her menses; she said the Prophet slept with her while she was menstruating, and the speaker counts this among her services to the community. {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep35 00:54:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep35 00:54:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep35 00:55:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep35 00:55:30}
- He says Maymuna died in the sixty-first year after the Hijra (his date; needs a source), after performing the pilgrimage, that she gave much in charity and borrowed in order to give, and that she died at the place where the Prophet had married her. {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep35 00:55:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep35 00:56:00} (needs_source)
- He closes by saying the next episode will take up the daughters of the Prophet, after which the series moves on to a new programme. {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep35 00:56:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep35 00:57:00}

## Left out of this episode 35

Not written from episode 35: the segment at 00:19:30, which is a machine repetition loop with unclear speech, the segment at 00:38:30, which is non-Arabic and was removed, and the segment at 00:45:30, a repetition loop that was removed. The scattered audience comments at 00:43:00 and 00:45:00 are summarised in their general sense. A remark by one participant about al-Shafi'i at 00:28:00 is not written, because the sentence in the transcript is garbled and cannot be attributed with confidence. The names of the sons that the audience recites were not written, because the transcript is garbled there.

## Episode 36: Abu Ayyub al-Ansari: the Pledge of Aqaba, the Prophet's seven months in his house, the manners of visiting and asking permission, and his last campaign at Constantinople, as the speaker and the audience tell it

:::perspectives
- **The speaker's view on the place of the Ansar after the Prophet (his opinion):** he holds that the Ansar had little share in rule after the Prophet's death, lists the caliphates and dynasties that followed, and explains this by saying the Ansar sought what is with God and not the world. This is his own phrasing; no source is named in the episode. {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep36 00:07:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep36 00:07:30}
- **The speaker on loving the Prophet above everyone (his opinion):** he holds that love for the Prophet must rank above love for family, children and companions, cites the people of Medina on the road to him, and sets against them those who love their companions more than the Prophet. {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep36 00:14:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep36 00:15:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep36 00:15:30}
- **The speaker on garlic, onion and smoking (his opinion, no ruling):** he says the angels are harmed by the smell as people are, judges that this alone is reason enough to stop smoking, and states that he is not speaking on what is lawful or forbidden. This is the speaker's view, not a ruling of the museum. {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep36 00:35:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep36 00:36:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep36 00:36:30}
- **The speaker on relationships before marriage (his opinion; needs a source to be quoted as more than his view):** he says relationships before marriage make the comparison with the spouse unfair afterwards, advises young people to approach families by the front door, and to make religion the basis of getting to know someone. {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep36 00:43:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep36 00:44:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep36 00:44:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep36 00:45:00}
:::

- The speaker opens by saying that the Beloved are the Companions of the Prophet, and that the aim of the programme is to bring young people back to them as models. He quotes, in his own words and without a chain in the episode, a saying about the best generation and a saying that a group of his community will remain upon the truth. {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep36 00:00:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep36 00:00:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep36 00:01:00} (needs_source)
- He introduces Abu Ayyub al-Ansari: his kunya is Abu Ayyub, his nisba al-Ansari; he is a Khazraji, of the Banu al-Najjar. The speaker says he witnessed Badr and was one of the seventy-three who attended the Greater Pledge of Aqaba, and gives his real name as Khalid ibn Zayd. {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep36 00:01:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep36 00:02:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep36 00:02:30} (needs_source) [[person/abu-ayyub-al-ansari|Abu Ayyub al-Ansari]]
- He describes the Pledge of Aqaba. Abu Ayyub did not attend the first pledge; the second was a pledge to support the religion, to fight, to protect the Prophet and to emigrate. By the speaker's count those present were seventy-three men and two women. {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep36 00:03:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep36 00:03:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep36 00:04:00} (needs_source) [[event/second-pledge-of-aqaba|The second Pledge of Aqaba]]
- He describes a dark night in the days of Tashriq near the place of the stoning of the pillars. He says the Prophet asked those present to worship God alone, to spend, to hear and obey in hardship and in ease, and to protect him as they protect their own families; the reward he named was Paradise. The transcript is partly garbled at 00:04:30 to 00:05:00, and the claim that Muhajirun guarded the approach needs a source. {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep36 00:04:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep36 00:05:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep36 00:05:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep36 00:06:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep36 00:06:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep36 00:07:00} (needs_source)
- He says the emigration to Medina began after the pledge, and that each emigrant lodged with an Ansari. Abu Ayyub took in [[person/musab-ibn-umayr|Mus'ab ibn Umayr]], who had brought Islam to Medina, and the people of Medina went out each day to wait for the Prophet. {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep36 00:08:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep36 00:08:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep36 00:09:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep36 00:11:00}
- He says the Prophet first stayed at Quba and prayed there, and that the mosque of Quba was the first mosque built in Islam. He cites the verse about a mosque founded on piety. {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep36 00:10:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep36 00:10:30} [[place/quba|Quba]] [[passage/quran-9-108|Surat al-Tawba, verse 108]] (needs_source for the claim of the first mosque)
- He describes the welcome in Medina. A Jewish man on a palm tree called out to the Banu Qayla when he saw the Prophet and Abu Bakr coming, the people came out, and they crowded round the Prophet's she-camel, each asking him to stay at his house. {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep36 00:12:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep36 00:13:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep36 00:13:30} (the Jewish man's words need a source)
- He says the Prophet told them to leave the camel, that she was commanded, and she walked until she knelt at the house of Abu Ayyub. He says the Prophet's mosque was later built on that open space, and that the Prophet stayed seven months in Abu Ayyub's house until the mosque and the dwellings were built. {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep36 00:14:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep36 00:16:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep36 00:16:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep36 00:17:00} [[event/prophets-mosque-built|The Prophet's mosque]] (the seven months and the place of the kneeling need a source)
- Abu Ayyub offered the Prophet the upper floor, with himself and his wife below. The Prophet refused and chose the lower floor. Abu Ayyub did not sleep that night for fear of walking over the Prophet, and proposed that the Prophet go up; the Prophet agreed after seeing how careful they were. {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep36 00:17:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep36 00:18:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep36 00:18:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep36 00:19:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep36 00:19:30}
- On a cold night a water jar spilled on the upper floor. Abu Ayyub and his wife came down with coverings to soak up the water so that none would fall on the Prophet, and the Prophet then went up. The transcript is garbled at this point, and the account here is only what is clear. {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep36 00:21:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep36 00:21:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep36 00:22:00}
- The speaker turns to the manners of visiting: the visitor gives his name, asks permission three times with a pause between each, stands to the right or left of the door and not in front of it, and goes back if he is told to go back. He cites the verses on asking permission to enter houses. {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep36 00:22:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep36 00:23:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep36 00:23:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep36 00:24:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep36 00:24:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep36 00:25:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep36 00:30:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep36 00:30:30} [[passage/quran-24-27|Surat al-Nur, verse 27]] [[passage/quran-24-28|Surat al-Nur, verse 28]]
- He adds further manners: greet on entering, keep the visit short, do not look into the house, and keep to yourself what you hear inside a house. {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep36 00:26:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep36 00:30:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep36 00:31:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep36 00:31:30}
- He says Jews told the Companions that Muhammad had taught them everything, even the manners of the lavatory, and presents this as evidence that Islam covers all the manners of life. {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep36 00:32:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep36 00:32:30} (needs_source)
- He tells of young girls of the Banu al-Najjar who came to the Prophet and sang verses of welcome; the Prophet said that God knows his heart loves them. {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep36 00:33:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep36 00:33:30} (needs_source)
- He says Abu Ayyub and his wife would send food to the Prophet and then eat from the place his fingers had touched. One day food with garlic and onion was brought, and the Prophet sent it back, saying that he speaks with his Lord and receives revelation, and that anyone who goes to the mosque should not eat garlic or onion, because of the harm to the angels. {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep36 00:34:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep36 00:34:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep36 00:35:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep36 00:35:30}
- He tells that the Prophet, Abu Bakr and Umar went out at midday driven by hunger, and met Abu Ayyub, who slaughtered sheep for them, cooked part and roasted part. The Prophet ate, asked that a share be sent to Fatima because she had not eaten for days, and then quoted the verse on being asked about the bounties on the Day of Judgement, and wept. The cooking details are the speaker's telling. {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep36 00:37:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep36 00:37:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep36 00:38:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep36 00:38:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep36 00:39:00} [[passage/quran-102-8|Surat al-Takathur, verse 8]] (cooking details need a source)
- He tells the story of the slander affair. Abu Ayyub told his wife that what was said of Aisha was a lie; he asked her what she would have done in Aisha's place, and she said she would not have, and then he asked the same about Safwan ibn al-Mu'attal; she said Safwan was better than him and Aisha better than her. The speaker ties this to the verse on the believers who should have thought well when they heard the slander. {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep36 00:40:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep36 00:40:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep36 00:41:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep36 00:41:30} [[event/incident-of-the-slander|The slander affair]] [[passage/quran-24-12|Surat al-Nur, verse 12]] (needs_source)
- He says Umar wanted to apply the punishment on a man he had seen, and that Ali told him to bring four witnesses or be flogged himself, and that the Companions were scrupulous about the honour of others. {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep36 00:42:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep36 00:42:30} (needs_source) [[person/umar-ibn-al-khattab|Umar ibn al-Khattab]] [[person/ali-ibn-abi-talib|Ali ibn Abi Talib]]
- The speaker says Abu Ayyub took part in the campaigns after the age of eighty, and went out with an army against Constantinople in the time of Yazid ibn Mu'awiya (the speaker's words; needs a source). He says Abu Ayyub asked to be carried on his horse and buried in enemy land, and that he was buried under the walls of Constantinople. {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep36 00:49:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep36 00:50:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep36 00:50:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep36 00:51:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep36 00:51:30} [[place/constantinople|Constantinople]] [[passage/quran-9-41|Surat al-Tawba, verse 41]] [[passage/quran-9-38|Surat al-Tawba, verse 38]] (needs_source)
- The speaker gives the last hadith Abu Ayyub narrated, that whoever dies without associating anything with God enters Paradise, in his own words, with no chain in the episode. He gives the year of death as 52 AH (needs_source). {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep36 00:52:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep36 00:52:30} (needs_source)

## Left out of this episode 36

Not written from episode 36: the speaker's comparison of the Companions' emigration with other migrations and his generalisations about named peoples and nations, because they carry no source in the episode. The first word of the episode is rendered by the machine as a word meaning "press" in the transcript; it is read here as the Companions ("al-sahaba"), and the reading is the drafter's. The remark on telephone calls and the excuses children make (about 00:30:00) is not written because the transcript is garbled there. A repetition loop at 00:12:30 and passages at 00:34:30 and 00:43:00 that do not parse were discarded. The number of hadiths Abu Ayyub narrated, given near 00:52:30, is unclear in the transcript and is not written. The audience's scattered remarks around 00:45:00 are summarised in their general sense, without names.

## Episode 37: Abu Hurayra: his name and kunya, his conversion and his companionship with the Prophet, the People of the Suffa, his memory of hadith as the speaker presents it, his mother, his worship and his death, as the speaker and the audience tell it

:::perspectives
- **The speaker's answer to critics of Abu Hurayra's many narrations (his opinion):** he holds that critics use the large number of Abu Hurayra's narrations and the short time he spent with the Prophet as a pretext to deny the Sunnah, and answers that the memory was a miracle of the Prophet, confirmed by a test. He sets out the critics' argument in brief and gives his own reply. {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep37 00:11:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep37 00:11:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep37 00:14:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep37 00:14:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep37 00:15:00}
- **The speaker on staying close to the Prophet after his death (his opinion):** he holds that sending blessings on the Prophet, reading his biography and walking in his footsteps in Medina bring a sense of his nearness, and he invites the audience to add to this. {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep37 00:22:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep37 00:22:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep37 00:24:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep37 00:25:00}
- **The speaker on worship alongside work (his opinion; his hours of sleep are not checked):** he holds that the Companions combined worship with work and trade, gives Uthman's funding of an army as an example, and warns that time is lost to late nights. The sleep arithmetic he gives is not verified here. {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep37 00:49:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep37 00:50:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep37 00:50:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep37 00:51:00}
:::

- The episode opens with the name of the programme, which the speaker takes from Bilal's words at his death: tomorrow we meet the beloved, Muhammad and his Companions. The speaker says the programme aims to bring young people back to the Companions as models. {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep37 00:00:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep37 00:00:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep37 00:01:00} (needs_source for the words attributed to Bilal)
- He says that loving a Companion one has not seen is a sign of faith, and introduces Abu Hurayra. He gives his real name as Abd al-Rahman ibn Sakhr, says his name before Islam was Abd al-Shams, and that the Prophet changed it to Abd al-Rahman. {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep37 00:01:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep37 00:01:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep37 00:02:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep37 00:02:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep37 00:03:00} [[person/abu-hurayra|Abu Hurayra]] (names and kunya need a source; the kunya is written in garbled forms in many places of the transcript)
- The speaker says Abu Hurayra cared for a small cat, carrying it in his sleeve and giving it milk, and that the kunya that stuck came from this and from the Prophet's address to him. He says the Prophet called him by the kunya, which he loved to hear. {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep37 00:03:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep37 00:04:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep37 00:04:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep37 00:05:00} (needs_source)
- He says Abu Hurayra came from the tribe of Daws in Yemen, and that he converted through [[person/tufayl-ibn-amr-al-dawsi|al-Tufayl ibn Amr al-Dawsi]], who converted in Mecca and then returned to his people. Another report, the speaker says, puts Abu Hurayra's conversion at Khaybar. {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep37 00:05:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep37 00:06:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep37 00:06:30} (needs_source)
- He says Abu Hurayra was with the Prophet for about three years only, that he was poor and an orphan, and that he was among the [[concept/ahl-al-suffa|People of the Suffa]]. {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep37 00:06:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep37 00:07:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep37 00:07:30} (the length of companionship and the orphanhood need a source)
- He places the People of the Suffa in dwellings behind the Prophet's house at the mosque, and says the Prophet did not eat until he had fed them, Abu Hurayra among them. {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep37 00:08:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep37 00:08:30} (the location needs a source)
- He gives a figure for the hadiths Abu Hurayra narrated: 30,574 (speaker's figure, needs a source), says he is the most prolific of the Companions, and says more than two thousand Companions and two thousand Followers narrated from him (figures need a source). He says al-Shafi'i said Abu Hurayra was the most retentive of those who narrated from the Prophet, a saying given without a chain. {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep37 00:09:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep37 00:09:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep37 00:10:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep37 00:10:30} [[person/al-shafii|al-Shafi'i]] (needs_source)
- He says the Prophet prayed for Abu Hurayra that he would not forget what he heard, that he became a memory of this kind, and that whoever doubts Abu Hurayra's memory doubts the Prophet's miracle. {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep37 00:11:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep37 00:12:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep37 00:12:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep37 00:13:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep37 00:13:30} (needs a source)
- He tells of the test by [[person/marwan-ibn-al-hakam|Marwan ibn al-Hakam]]: Marwan had a scribe write down everything Abu Hurayra said, then recited it to him a year later, and Abu Hurayra repeated it word for word. The episode gives no chain for the story. {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep37 00:14:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep37 00:14:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep37 00:15:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep37 00:15:30} (needs_source)
- He cites the verse on those who conceal what God has sent down, and says Abu Hurayra feared being counted among the concealers if he did not transmit what he heard. [[passage/quran-2-159|Surat al-Baqara, verse 159]] {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep37 00:16:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep37 00:17:00}
- He reports Abu Hurayra's words that the emigrants were busy with trade and the Ansar with their farms, that he kept to the Prophet to learn what they did not, and that this was his particular position. He reports that when Aisha asked him why he narrated so much he said he had put the world aside. {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep37 00:17:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep37 00:18:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep37 00:18:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep37 00:19:00} (needs a source)
