- He reports from Talha ibn Ubayd Allah that the Ansar and the Muhajirun went to the Prophet at the two ends of the day, while Abu Hurayra was with him all day, and so learned what they did not learn. {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep37 00:19:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep37 00:20:00} (needs a source)
- He asks the audience what is the least one can do to be close to the Prophet. He answers with sending blessings on him, and tells, in his own words, a saying that whoever sends blessings on the Prophet, God returns his soul to him until he returns the greeting. {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep37 00:21:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep37 00:22:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep37 00:23:00} (needs a source)
- He says Abu Hurayra's own story of his mother: she did not accept Islam, he called her to it, she answered him harshly, and he went to the Prophet weeping. The Prophet prayed that God guide her, and she accepted Islam at her son's return. Abu Hurayra then asked that God make him and his mother beloved to the believers. {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep37 00:26:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep37 00:27:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep37 00:27:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep37 00:28:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep37 00:28:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep37 00:29:00} (told in the speaker's words; needs a source)
- He tells that Abu Hurayra was hungry and recited verses on giving to passers-by, then went to Abu Bakr and Umar and found no food with them. The Prophet took him home and asked for milk, which he gave Abu Hurayra to drink, then to the People of the Suffa, and Abu Hurayra drank until he was full. {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep37 00:31:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep37 00:31:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep37 00:32:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep37 00:32:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep37 00:33:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep37 00:33:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep37 00:34:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep37 00:34:30} (needs a source)
- He recounts a supplication Abu Hurayra reported the Prophet taught him for the opening of prayer, asking God to set one's sins as far from one as east is from west. The wording is not reproduced here. {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep37 00:35:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep37 00:35:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep37 00:36:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep37 00:36:30} (needs a source)
- He reports a saying that the person most blessed by the Prophet's intercession is whoever says there is no god but God sincerely from the heart, and notes that sincerity is the condition. {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep37 00:37:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep37 00:37:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep37 00:38:00} (needs a source)
- He says Abu Hurayra divided the night into three parts with his wife and daughter, that he glorified God twelve thousand times a day (the speaker's figure, needs a source), and he invites the audience to two rak'as at night with a spouse. {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep37 00:38:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep37 00:39:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep37 00:39:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep37 00:40:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep37 00:40:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep37 00:42:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep37 00:43:00} [[concept/tasbih-glorification|Glorification of God]]
- He says that the people of the Fire in Saqar will say they were not among those who prayed, and sets this against Abu Hurayra's prayer. [[passage/quran-74-42|Surat al-Muddaththir, verse 42]] [[passage/quran-74-43|Surat al-Muddaththir, verse 43]] {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep37 00:42:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep37 00:42:30}
- He tells that Abu Hurayra said the Prophet's inheritance was being divided in the mosque, that the traders went and found only people remembering God, and that he said this was the Prophet's inheritance. {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep37 00:43:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep37 00:44:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep37 00:44:30} (needs a source)
- He tells that Umar and his Ansari companion took turns to attend the Prophet, because they had a farm to work, and offers this as a sign that the Companions combined worship with work. [[person/umar-ibn-al-khattab|Umar ibn al-Khattab]] {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep37 00:48:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep37 00:49:00} (needs a source)
- He says Uthman ibn Affan equipped an army from his own wealth. [[person/uthman-ibn-affan|Uthman ibn Affan]] {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep37 00:50:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep37 00:51:00} (needs a source)
- He says Abu Hurayra died aged seventy-eight, in 57 AH, and was buried in [[place/al-baqi|al-Baqi']]; in his last hours he wept and said that he loved to meet God, and cited a saying to that effect. {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep37 00:45:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep37 00:45:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep37 00:46:00} (age, year and burial place need a source)
- He concludes that the lesson of Abu Hurayra is precedence in worship and sincerity in it, invites the audience to comment, and notes that many Companions kept night prayers. {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep37 00:46:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep37 00:47:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep37 00:48:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep37 00:48:30}

## Left out of this episode 37

Not written from episode 37: the speaker's arithmetic on how much life is gained by delaying sleep, because it is not checked. The remark about blood-money in the passage on glorification is garbled and is not written. The transcript writes Abu Hurayra's name and kunya in garbled forms in many places; the familiar name is used here. Repetition loops at 00:23:30 and passages at 00:29:30 and 00:52:00 that do not parse were discarded. The passage from 00:43:00 to 00:44:00 tells a story that cannot be followed in the transcript and is not written. Scattered audience remarks on personal matters are not written.

## Episode 38: Bilal ibn Rabah: his lineage, conversion, torture and purchase, his call to prayer and the dream of Abdullah ibn Zayd, Badr and the conquest of Mecca, and his death in Damascus, as the speaker and the audience tell it

:::perspectives
- **The speaker on a Companion without lineage or wealth (his opinion):** he holds that what remains in history is reform and faith, not demolition or wealth, cites Bilal, and says the world is not kept for one who does not work for the hereafter. {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep38 00:02:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep38 00:03:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep38 00:03:30}
- **The speaker on shame and religion (his opinion):** he holds that a person who is ashamed of his religion does not feel love for it, and calls for the heart to be full of love for Islam. {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep38 00:08:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep38 00:09:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep38 00:09:30}
- **The speaker on visiting Medina and its effect (his opinion; some sayings are given in meaning):** he holds that a visit to Medina strengthens faith, cites a saying that faith returns to Medina as a snake returns to its hole, and holds that a useful journey is one that does not take a person away from obedience. {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep38 00:41:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep38 00:42:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep38 00:42:30}
:::

- The speaker says the programme introduces young people to the Companions, and that Bilal ibn Rabah is known to every Muslim child as the Prophet's first muezzin. He describes Bilal as a Black slave, thin and poor, and sets him against people history forgets. {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep38 00:00:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep38 00:01:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep38 00:01:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep38 00:02:00} [[person/bilal-ibn-rabah|Bilal ibn Rabah]]
- He says Bilal embraced Islam at about thirty years of age, and gives the age difference with the Prophet as ten years at one point and twelve at another; the episode does not settle the difference. He says Bilal's conversion was in the first year of the mission. (needs a source) {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep38 00:04:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep38 00:05:00}
- He says Bilal was the third person to declare Islam openly in Mecca, and that the first seven to do so included the Prophet, Abu Bakr and Bilal. (needs a source) {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep38 00:06:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep38 00:06:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep38 00:07:00}
- He describes the torture of Bilal by his master [[person/umayya-ibn-khalaf|Umayya ibn Khalaf]]: Bilal was laid in the midday heat with a heavy stone on his chest, and kept repeating a word of God's oneness. The name of the master is garbled in the transcript and read here as Umayya. (needs a source) {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep38 00:10:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep38 00:10:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep38 00:11:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep38 00:11:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep38 00:12:00}
- He says [[person/abu-bakr|Abu Bakr]] bought Bilal, and that his master first asked for nine uqiyya; Abu Bakr said he would buy him even for a hundred. The metal in which the uqiyya were counted is garbled in the transcript and is not given. (needs a source) {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep38 00:14:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep38 00:14:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep38 00:15:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep38 00:15:30}
- He says Abu Bakr freed Bilal, and that Bilal stayed with the Prophet until the emigration. (needs a source) {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep38 00:16:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep38 00:16:30}
- He tells how the Muslims settled the call to prayer after the emigration. The bell was not accepted, nor a banner. Abdullah ibn Zayd saw in a dream a man carrying a bell and was taught the words of the call; he told the Prophet, who said it was a true vision and ordered Bilal to call with it, because his voice was more resonant. {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep38 00:16:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep38 00:17:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep38 00:17:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep38 00:18:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep38 00:18:30} [[person/abd-allah-ibn-zayd-al-ansari|Abdullah ibn Zayd al-Ansari]] (needs a source)
- He says Bilal then called to prayer as the first muezzin of the Prophet, and that he did not miss an expedition with the Prophet until Badr. (needs a source) {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep38 00:19:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep38 00:19:30}
- He says Bilal met Umayya ibn Khalaf at Badr and raised his voice, and that God gives victory to the wronged, invoking the supplication of the wronged in the speaker's own words. The episode does not clearly state the outcome of the meeting, so none is written here. [[event/battle-of-badr|Badr]] (needs a source) {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep38 00:19:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep38 00:20:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep38 00:20:30}
- He says the Prophet entered Mecca with ten thousand, that Bilal climbed onto the Kaaba and called to prayer, and that the Prophet asked where Bilal was. He says Bilal was the only one who prayed inside the Kaaba with the Prophet. (needs a source) [[event/conquest-of-mecca|The conquest of Mecca]] {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep38 00:20:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep38 00:21:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep38 00:21:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep38 00:22:00}
- He says the Prophet asked Bilal about his most excellent deed. Bilal said he never broke his wudu without performing two rak'as afterwards, and the Prophet said he had heard the sound of Bilal's sandals in Paradise. (needs a source) {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep38 00:23:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep38 00:23:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep38 00:24:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep38 00:24:30}
- He says [[person/umar-ibn-al-khattab|Umar ibn al-Khattab]] addressed Bilal with the honorific sayyid (master); the passage is partly garbled. (needs a source) {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep38 00:22:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep38 00:23:00}
- He says the Prophet died on a Monday, that Bilal was among those most grieved, that the Prophet died with his head on Aisha's chest, and that Medina wept. [[event/death-of-the-prophet|The death of the Prophet]] (needs a source) {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep38 00:25:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep38 00:25:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep38 00:26:00}
- He quotes Anas ibn Malik that Medina was lit up on the day the Prophet entered and darkened on the day he died, and he recalls Fatima's words to Anas about the dust. He says the mosque wept when Bilal first called to prayer after the death. (needs a source) {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep38 00:26:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep38 00:27:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep38 00:27:30}
- He says Bilal could not finish the call at the words that Muhammad is the Messenger of God, tried again three days later and could not, and went to Abu Bakr to ask to be released from calling to prayer, and then said he wanted to leave Medina. (needs a source) {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep38 00:28:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep38 00:28:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep38 00:29:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep38 00:29:30}
- He says Abu Bakr allowed Bilal to leave, that Bilal went to Syria with the army, and that Umar took him to Palestine and to Jerusalem. (needs a source) {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep38 00:30:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep38 00:30:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep38 00:31:00} [[event/conquest-of-jerusalem|The conquest of Jerusalem]] [[place/jerusalem|Jerusalem]]
- He says Umar asked Bilal to call to prayer at a gathering of the Companions on the plateau the speaker names as the Golan (the place needs a source); Bilal called and the whole army wept. {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep38 00:31:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep38 00:32:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep38 00:32:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep38 00:33:00}
- He tells a dream of Bilal in Damascus, in which the Prophet rebuked him for not visiting; Bilal went to Medina, greeted the Prophet at his grave, met al-Hasan and al-Husayn, who asked him to call to prayer, and he did, and the people of Medina came out weeping. The dream and the greeting are given in the speaker's words. (needs a source) {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep38 00:33:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep38 00:34:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep38 00:34:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep38 00:35:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep38 00:35:30}
- He says Bilal died in Damascus in 17 AH, aged about sixty, and that his last words were that tomorrow we meet the beloved Muhammad and his Companions; when his wife cried out woe, he told her to say joy. [[place/damascus|Damascus]] (needs a source) {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep38 00:36:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep38 00:36:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep38 00:37:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep38 00:37:30}
- He summarises the basic facts: first muezzin of the Prophet, converted at about thirty, freed by Abu Bakr, called to prayer for the Prophet about ten years, the only one who prayed with the Prophet inside the Kaaba by his account, and died in Damascus. (needs a source) {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep38 00:37:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep38 00:37:30}
- He imagines himself in the place of Abu Dujana, who shielded the Prophet from the arrows, and says that whoever is sincere in obedience to God may hope for reward (the speaker's reflection). [[person/abu-dujana|Abu Dujana]] {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep38 00:39:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep38 00:40:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep38 00:40:30}
- He says the Companions included the rich, and that Abd al-Rahman ibn Awf died leaving eighty million dirhams (the figure needs a source), and calls for the world to be in the hand and not in the heart. [[person/abd-al-rahman-ibn-awf|Abd al-Rahman ibn Awf]] {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep38 00:42:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep38 00:43:00} (needs a source)

## Left out of this episode 38

Not written from episode 38: a garbled exchange at 00:43:30 to 00:44:30 about Bilal's pronunciation of a letter and what is attributed to Ali and to the Prophet, because the sentence cannot be attributed with confidence. The story of a young girl at Khaybar and a necklace (00:44:30 to 00:46:00) is not written because the transcript is garbled in most of it. A passage at 00:41:00 in which audience remarks repeat without clear sense was discarded. The speaker's remarks on young people and travel are written only in their general sense, in the third perspective. Audience comments on personal matters, names and ages are not written.

## Episode 39: Hudhayfa ibn al-Yaman: the Prophet's trusted companion, his name and his choice of the Ansar, Badr and Uhud and his father, the Trench and the night mission to Abu Sufyan's camp, the names of the hypocrites, and his governorship and death, as the speaker and the audience tell it

:::perspectives
- **The speaker on anger and its control (his view):** he holds that the Prophet's advice "do not get angry" can be trained, that restraining anger is a sign of strength, and that the strong man is the one who controls himself, not the one who wrestles. This is his view, not a ruling of the museum. {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep39 00:17:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep39 00:26:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep39 00:27:00}
- **An audience member on whether anger can change (a contested claim, not checked):** a listener says that behavioural psychology teaches that behaviour is learned and can be changed, and the speaker accepts this as a general point. The claim is recorded as the listener's, with no check against the literature. {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep39 00:24:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep39 00:25:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep39 00:25:30}
- **The speaker on the rules of war (his view):** he sets the Prophet's instructions to his armies against the conduct of modern armies, and says the Muslim army was distinguished by its ethics. The list he gives is his own telling and is not sourced in the episode. {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep39 00:10:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep39 00:11:00}

- The speaker opens by saying that the Companion trusted with the Prophet's greatest secrets is the subject of the episode, and that the purpose of the programme is to bring the Companions back into the heart. People know footballers and singers, he says, but not Hudhayfa ibn al-Yaman. {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep39 00:00:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep39 00:00:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep39 00:01:00} [[person/hudhayfa-ibn-al-yaman|Hudhayfa ibn al-Yaman]]
- The speaker gives his real name as Hudhayfa ibn Husayl, and says his father Husayl had shed blood in the Jahiliyya, fled his own land, and made an alliance with Banu Abd al-Ashhal of the Aws in Medina. The Ansar, he says, called people of Yemeni origin "Yemenis", which is how the name "ibn al-Yaman" is explained. The account is the speaker's and the origin of the name is not checked. {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep39 00:01:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep39 00:02:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep39 00:02:30} (needs_source) [[group/banu-abd-al-ashhal|Banu Abd al-Ashhal]] [[group/al-aws|the Aws]]
- He says that before the Hijra, Hudhayfa and his father left Medina for Mecca to be near the Prophet, and then came back to Medina. The speaker presents this as proof of how deep their love was. {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep39 00:03:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep39 00:04:00} (needs_source) [[place/mecca|Mecca]] [[place/medina|Medina]]
- The Prophet, the speaker says, offered Hudhayfa a choice between being of the Muhajirun or of the Ansar. Hudhayfa chose the Ansar, saying he loved his own city, and the Prophet agreed. {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep39 00:07:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep39 00:07:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep39 00:08:00} (needs_source)
- Before Badr, the speaker says, Quraysh seized Hudhayfa and his father near the field, asked whether they meant to fight with Muhammad, and let them go when they swore they would not fight. The Prophet told them to keep their word and to seek God's help against the enemy, and the two did not take part in the battle. The transcript is partly garbled at this point. {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep39 00:08:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep39 00:08:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep39 00:09:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep39 00:09:30} (needs_source) [[event/battle-of-badr|Badr]]
- At Uhud, the speaker says, Hudhayfa's father was a very old man and was excused from the fight, but he and another old man chose to go out, saying they would not stay behind and would die with the Messenger of God. {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep39 00:12:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep39 00:12:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep39 00:13:00} (needs_source) [[event/battle-of-uhud|Uhud]]
- In the battle, the speaker says, the father was masked, and some Companions did not know him and struck at him, taking him for one of Quraysh. Hudhayfa, from a distance, called out "servants of God, my father, my father", but the father had already fallen. {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep39 00:13:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep39 00:14:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep39 00:14:30} (needs_source; garbled in places)
- When the Companions said they had not known who he was, Hudhayfa prayed for their forgiveness and mercy. The speaker reports that the Prophet ordered the blood-money gathered for Hudhayfa, that the Prophet said most Muslims were in need of it, and that Hudhayfa gave the money to the Muslims as charity. {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep39 00:15:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep39 00:15:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep39 00:16:00} (needs_source)
- The speaker tells of a man who asked the Prophet for advice three times and was told each time, "do not get angry". He asks whether Hudhayfa had heard this saying or had the disposition by nature, and he presents the saying as a principle that can be learned. The report is given without its chain in the episode. {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep39 00:17:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep39 00:17:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep39 00:18:00} (needs_source)
- The speaker cites the verse that praises those who restrain their anger and pardon people, and says it shows the rank of such people. The verse is referenced here by its link only: [[passage/quran-3-134|Surat Al Imran, verse 134]]. {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep39 00:19:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep39 00:19:30}
- He tells of an enslaved girl who spilled a pot of boiling water on an infant of the household, who died. The master was angry, and the girl recited the verses on restraint and pardon, and he pardoned her, then set her free. The speaker names the master as Zayn al-Abidin; the name is garbled in the transcript, and the story is not checked. {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep39 00:19:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep39 00:20:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep39 00:20:30} (needs_source)
- Applying the lesson to daily life, the speaker says that two drivers can quarrel for three hours where one word of apology would end it, and he calls forgiveness the first step to a better life. This is his advice. {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep39 00:21:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep39 00:21:30}
- The speaker says that Ali ibn Abi Talib, in a fight with a Jewish man, threw him down and was about to strike when the man spat in his face; Ali then stopped and let him go, because he had struck out of anger and would not kill for his own sake. The transcript is partly garbled at this point, and the words are not checked. {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep39 00:26:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep39 00:26:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep39 00:27:00} (needs_source; garbled) [[person/ali-ibn-abi-talib|Ali ibn Abi Talib]]
- The speaker turns to the Trench. A young man of a later generation asks Hudhayfa what the Companions did when they sat with the Prophet, and Hudhayfa answers that the young man has not seen what they saw at the Trench. {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep39 00:28:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep39 00:28:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep39 00:29:00} [[event/battle-of-the-trench|The Battle of the Trench]]
- The speaker gives the number of the enemy at the Trench as ten thousand (his figure, not checked), and says a Jewish group broke its covenant with the Muslims and agreed with Quraysh to attack from inside Medina. He describes the fear among the Muslims and cites the verse about hearts rising to the throats. {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep39 00:29:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep39 00:29:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep39 00:30:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep39 00:30:30} [[passage/quran-33-10|Surat al-Ahzab, verse 10]] (needs_source for the figure)
- On a cold, windy night the Prophet asks for a volunteer to go to the enemy camp and bring back news, promising that he will return safely and be a companion in Paradise. No one answers at first; the speaker says the Prophet then called on Hudhayfa by name, and Hudhayfa went. {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep39 00:31:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep39 00:31:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep39 00:32:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep39 00:32:30} (needs_source)
- In the camp, the speaker says, Hudhayfa saw Abu Sufyan on his horse, drew an arrow to shoot him, and then remembered the Prophet's command not to act against them, and held back. {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep39 00:33:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep39 00:34:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep39 00:34:30} [[person/abu-sufyan-ibn-harb|Abu Sufyan ibn Harb]] (needs_source)
- Abu Sufyan, the speaker says, called his leaders together and told each man to check the man beside him. Hudhayfa took the hand of his neighbour and asked who he was; the speaker names the two men as Amr ibn al-As and Ikrima ibn Abi Jahl. {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep39 00:35:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep39 00:35:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep39 00:36:00} [[person/amr-ibn-al-as|Amr ibn al-As]] [[person/ikrima-ibn-abi-jahl|Ikrima ibn Abi Jahl]] (needs_source)
- The speaker says Abu Sufyan then declared that the cold and wind had made the camp untenable, and the army left. Hudhayfa returned to the Prophet, who was praying, and the Prophet, the speaker says, drew him into his cloak during the prayer. {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep39 00:37:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep39 00:37:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep39 00:38:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep39 00:38:30} (needs_source)
- The speaker says the Prophet entrusted Hudhayfa with the names of the hypocrites and that Hudhayfa alone knew them. The Prophet did not make them public, and the speaker gives the reason as the command not to pray over them. {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep39 00:39:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep39 00:39:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep39 00:40:00} (needs_source)
- He says that Umar ibn al-Khattab, when someone died in Medina, would first ask whether Hudhayfa had attended the funeral. If he had, Umar attended; if not, Umar did not. {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep39 00:40:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep39 00:40:30} (needs_source) [[person/umar-ibn-al-khattab|Umar ibn al-Khattab]]
- The speaker quotes Hudhayfa's answer to a man who asked him what hypocrisy is: speaking Islam without acting on it. {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep39 00:43:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep39 00:43:30} (needs_source)
- The speaker tells that Umar asked Hudhayfa about the trials to come. Hudhayfa said there is a closed door between Umar and the trials. Umar asked whether the door would be opened or broken, and was told it would be broken; Umar then said that it would then never close again. The speaker reads this as Umar's protection of the community. {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep39 00:44:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep39 00:45:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep39 00:45:30} (needs_source)
- During the Persian campaign, the speaker says, Umar named Nu'man ibn Muqarrin as commander with Hudhayfa to succeed him. Nu'man was killed and Hudhayfa led the army. The speaker gives the Persian strength as 150,000 against 30,000 Muslims (his figures, not checked). {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep39 00:48:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep39 00:48:30} (needs_source)
- The speaker says Hudhayfa then became governor of al-Mada'in, the former capital of Kisra. He entered on a mule with a loaf in his hand and asked the people only for their daily food and the use of his mule. The speaker says he remained governor until his death. The main record of Hudhayfa on the museum gives other posts, and the difference is recorded for review. {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep39 00:49:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep39 00:49:30} (needs_source) [[place/al-madain|al-Mada'in]]
- The speaker says Hudhayfa stayed in al-Mada'in under Uthman and that he died a short time after Uthman was killed. He asked for simple shrouds and said that if he was good God would give him better, and if he was bad God would take them. {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep39 00:50:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep39 00:50:30} (needs_source; the figure for the days is garbled) [[person/uthman-ibn-affan|Uthman ibn Affan]]
- In his last hour, the speaker says, Hudhayfa asked the time and was told it was just before dawn. He wept and sought refuge from a night in this world that ends in a morning in the Fire. He said he wept not for longing for the world but because he did not know whether his Lord was pleased with him, and then said "welcome, death, a beloved who comes after absence". {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep39 00:51:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep39 00:51:30} (needs_source)

## Left out of this episode 39

Not written from episode 39: the exchange at about 00:41:00 to 00:42:30 in which the speaker says Umar asked Hudhayfa under oath about his name among the hypocrites, because the transcript is garbled and the answer cannot be read. The speaker's remarks on mobile phones and gossip (about 00:41:00) and the audience's personal remarks (about 00:21:30 and 00:24:00) are not written. The audience's psychology argument is recorded only in the perspective above, as a listener's claim. Repetition loops at 00:22:00, 00:23:30, 00:24:00 and 00:46:00 that do not parse were discarded.

## Episode 40: Sa'd ibn Mu'adh: the shaking of the Throne at his death, his conversion through Mus'ab ibn Umayr, Badr and the Trench, the judgement on Banu Qurayza, and his death, as the speaker and the audience tell it

:::perspectives
- **The speaker on calling people by character (his advice):** he holds that good conduct, competence and visible sincerity are the first form of calling people to God, that people trust a man of character before they hear him, and that a believer should not hold back from speaking to friends and family. This is his advice, not a ruling of the museum. {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep40 00:16:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep40 00:21:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep40 00:22:00}
- **The speaker on the judgement of Banu Qurayza (his view):** he presents Sa'd's sentence as a just judgement, and says it was God's judgement given through him. The sentence and its details are the speaker's telling and are not sourced in the episode. The museum records them as his account, not as a settled verdict, and the academic reading of the event is left to the sources in the record of the event. {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep40 00:48:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep40 00:48:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep40 00:49:00}

- The speaker opens by saying that the Throne of the Merciful shook at Sa'd ibn Mu'adh's death, a sign of his rank, and compares it with Uhud shaking when the Prophet stood on it. He presents Sa'd as a figure honoured by the heavens. {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep40 00:00:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep40 00:00:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep40 00:01:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep40 00:01:30} (needs_source) [[person/sad-ibn-muadh|Sa'd ibn Mu'adh]]
- The speaker says Gabriel came to the Prophet after Sa'd's death and asked whether anyone had died in the house, because the gates of heaven had opened for a soul. The Prophet then rose and found Sa'd there. {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep40 00:02:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep40 00:03:00} (needs_source)
- At the funeral, the speaker says, the Companions were surprised that the bier was light, though Sa'd was tall and heavy. The Prophet told them the angels had carried it with them. He adds that the grave was made wide and that the angels filled it. {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep40 00:03:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep40 00:03:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep40 00:04:00} (needs_source)
- The speaker says Sa'd's mother wept, and the Prophet told her to dry her tears because God laughs for her son now. He reports a saying that every lamenter lies except the lamenter for Sa'd. {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep40 00:04:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep40 00:04:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep40 00:05:00} (needs_source)
- Sa'd was the chief of Banu Abd al-Ashhal. The speaker says Mus'ab ibn Umayr, sent to Medina to teach Islam, spread the message there; he was hosted by As'ad ibn Zurara, and households across Medina came to Islam through him. {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep40 00:06:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep40 00:07:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep40 00:07:30} [[person/musab-ibn-umayr|Mus'ab ibn Umayr]] [[group/banu-abd-al-ashhal|Banu Abd al-Ashhal]]
- Sa'd sent Usayd ibn Hudayr to stop Mus'ab, the speaker says, and Usayd came back changed. Sa'd then went himself with his spear and confronted Mus'ab and As'ad ibn Zurara. {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep40 00:08:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep40 00:08:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep40 00:09:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep40 00:09:30} [[person/usayd-ibn-hudayr|Usayd ibn Hudayr]]
- Mus'ab asked Sa'd to sit and listen; he offered to recite and to leave if Sa'd disliked what he heard. The speaker says Mus'ab recited the Qur'an and Sa'd was moved by it. {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep40 00:10:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep40 00:10:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep40 00:11:00} [[person/musab-ibn-umayr|Mus'ab ibn Umayr]]
- Sa'd asked what he should do to enter the religion. He was told to wash, to testify that there is no god but God and that Muhammad is the Messenger of God, and to pray two cycles. The speaker presents this as Sa'd's first act in Islam. {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep40 00:11:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep40 00:12:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep40 00:12:30} (needs_source)
- Sa'd went back to his tribe and told them that he would not speak to their men or their women until they believed in God alone. The speaker says the whole tribe embraced Islam the same day. {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep40 00:13:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep40 00:13:30} (needs_source)
- The speaker gives Sa'd's years in Islam as seven, his age at conversion as about thirty, and his age on the day of the Trench as thirty-seven. The figures are not reconciled in the episode and are not checked. {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep40 00:02:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep40 00:06:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep40 00:07:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep40 00:42:00} (needs_source)
- The speaker tells of his own approach to a group of young men who were quarrelling in a street at four in the morning, and of one of them whom he took aside to talk to. He calls it the method of Sa'd: a word of character before a word of rebuke. The story is his telling; the people are not named. {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep40 00:28:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep40 00:29:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep40 00:30:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep40 00:31:00}
- Before the Trench, the speaker says, the Prophet asked Sa'd whether to give a third of Medina's dates to Ghatafan to lift the siege. Sa'd said that in the Jahiliyya the people of Medina did not give up their dates, and the Prophet accepted his view. {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep40 00:40:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep40 00:40:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep40 00:41:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep40 00:41:30} [[group/ghatafan|Ghatafan]] (needs_source)
- The speaker places a council before Badr. Abu Bakr and Umar speak, then Miqdad, and then Sa'd, who says the Muslims have given their pledge and would cross the sea with the Prophet. The speaker gives the numbers as 300 men against 1,000, and one horse against 300 horses; these figures are not checked. {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep40 00:35:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep40 00:35:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep40 00:36:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep40 00:37:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep40 00:38:00} [[event/battle-of-badr|Badr]] (needs_source for the figures)
- At Uhud, the speaker says, the Prophet's face was bloodied and he said "O God, guide my people, for they do not know." The speaker uses this as a lesson on patience with people. {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep40 00:17:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep40 00:18:00} (speaker's telling; needs_source) [[place/uhud|Uhud]]
- At the Trench, the speaker says, Sa'd was struck by an arrow in the shoulder. He prayed that if God had kept any battle with Quraysh for him he should live for it, and if the war was over he should die as a martyr. The Prophet had him placed in a tent in the mosque, and a woman who treated the wounded, read by the transcript as Rufayda, tended him. {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep40 00:42:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep40 00:43:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep40 00:43:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep40 00:44:00} [[event/battle-of-the-trench|The Battle of the Trench]] [[person/rufayda-al-aslamiyya|Rufayda al-Aslamiyya]] (the name is read from a garbled line and needs a source)
- The speaker says Banu Qurayza broke their pact during the Trench, and that the Prophet besieged them. They asked for arbitration, the speaker says, and named Sa'd because he had been their ally in the Jahiliyya. {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep40 00:46:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep40 00:47:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep40 00:47:30} (needs_source) [[group/banu-qurayza|Banu Qurayza]] [[event/siege-of-banu-qurayza|The siege of Banu Qurayza]]
- Sa'd's judgement, as the speaker gives it: the men to be killed, the property taken, the dwellings divided among the Muhajirun only, and the women and children taken captive. The garbled word for the last clause is read here as captivity. The Prophet, the speaker says, told Sa'd that he had judged by God's judgement from above the seven heavens. {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep40 00:48:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep40 00:48:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep40 00:49:00} (needs_source; see perspectives)
- The speaker says Sa'd prayed that his wound would stay open until he had seen the end of Banu Qurayza, and that the wound then burst and he died as a martyr. He says the Throne shook at his death and that seventy thousand angels attended the funeral. {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep40 00:49:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep40 00:49:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep40 00:50:00} (needs_source)
- The speaker tells that the Companions admired an embroidered robe brought from a Roman commander, and the Prophet said that the handkerchiefs of Sa'd in Paradise are better than it. The anecdote is the speaker's telling and is not checked. {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep40 00:50:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep40 00:50:30} (needs_source)
- The speaker closes by lamenting that young people do not know figures like Sa'd, and hopes that listeners will take him as a model. {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep40 00:50:30}

## Left out of this episode 40

Not written from episode 40: the programme announcements at about 00:14:00 and 00:27:00, the speaker's remarks on young women and the summer hijab (about 00:14:30 to 00:15:00), and an anecdote about a man who stopped a car and an audience remark on answered prayer (about 00:24:30 to 00:25:30), because the transcript is garbled there and the people are not named. Repetition loops at 00:08:00 and 00:45:30 were discarded. The speaker's list of reasons why prayers are not answered is not written in full.

## Episode 41: Suhayl ibn Amr: the Quraysh orator who opposed the Prophet, his son Abd Allah, Badr, Hudaybiyya and the treaty clauses, the Conquest of Mecca, his conversion and death, as the speaker and the audience tell it

:::perspectives
- **The speaker on the Prophet's way with opponents (his view):** he holds that the Prophet did not seek to break or humiliate Quraysh's leaders but to bring them to Islam, and that a believer should not humiliate others for their errors. This is his view. {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep41 00:08:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep41 00:09:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep41 00:09:30}
- **The speaker on calm and the spread of Islam (his view, with a figure that is not checked):** he holds that Islam is received better in a calm atmosphere than in conflict, and says that the two years after Hudaybiyya brought in more people than the nineteen years before it. The figure is his claim and is not checked. {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep41 00:24:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep41 00:24:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep41 00:25:00}
- **The speaker on the Prophet's unlettered state (his belief):** he presents the Prophet's inability to read and write as a sign, shown when the Prophet dictated the treaty. This is the speaker's belief, recorded as his. {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep41 00:27:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep41 00:28:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep41 00:28:30}

- The speaker introduces Suhayl ibn Amr as a companion whose story is strange: he was a fierce opponent of the Prophet for about twenty years, by the speaker's count, and later became one of the beloved. {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep41 00:00:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep41 00:00:30} (needs_source for the count) [[person/suhayl-ibn-amr|Suhayl ibn Amr]]
- The speaker describes Suhayl as a leader of Quraysh, one of its richest men, and an orator whose speech could move the people. He says Suhayl was past forty at the time of the mission, though the exact age is not known. {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep41 00:01:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep41 00:01:30} (needs_source) [[group/quraysh|Quraysh]]
- The speaker says that Suhayl's son Abd Allah and his daughter embraced Islam and went in the first emigration to Abyssinia. Suhayl punished his son harshly when he returned after a rumour, and Abd Allah hid his faith under torture. {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep41 00:02:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep41 00:02:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep41 00:03:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep41 00:03:30} [[place/abyssinia|Abyssinia]] [[person/abdullah-ibn-suhayl|Abd Allah ibn Suhayl]] (needs_source)
- Before Badr, the speaker says, Abd Allah went out with his father's army and then, at the start of the battle, left it and joined the Prophet's side. {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep41 00:04:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep41 00:05:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep41 00:05:30} [[event/battle-of-badr|Badr]] (needs_source)
- After Badr, the speaker says, Suhayl was among the captives. He gives the numbers as seventy dead and seventy captured (his figures, not checked). Umar asked to pull out Suhayl's two front teeth so he could not speak again; the Prophet refused, and said that perhaps God would make Suhayl a source of pleasure to you on the Day of Judgement. {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep41 00:06:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep41 00:06:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep41 00:07:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep41 00:07:30} [[person/umar-ibn-al-khattab|Umar ibn al-Khattab]]
- The speaker notes that the Prophet did not aim to humiliate the leaders of Quraysh. He says that three commanders at Uhud, Abu Sufyan, Ikrima and Khalid, later became Muslims and served Islam, and that Ikrima was martyred, Khalid was known as the sword of God, and Abu Sufyan lost his eyes in jihad. These details are the speaker's and are not checked. {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep41 00:07:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep41 00:08:00} (needs_source) [[person/abu-sufyan-ibn-harb|Abu Sufyan ibn Harb]] [[person/ikrima-ibn-abi-jahl|Ikrima ibn Abi Jahl]] [[person/khalid-ibn-al-walid|Khalid ibn al-Walid]]
- The speaker says the Prophet wanted people to enter Paradise, not to be humiliated. He tells believers not to humiliate those who sin, and not to give up on them after one failure. {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep41 00:08:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep41 00:09:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep41 00:09:30}
- The speaker says the Prophet saw in a vision that he entered the Sacred Mosque, and set out for the umra with about 1,400 men who carried animals for sacrifice and wanted the House, not war. Quraysh refused them entry at Hudaybiyya. {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep41 00:11:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep41 00:12:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep41 00:12:30} (needs_source for the figure) [[place/hudaybiyya|Hudaybiyya]] [[event/treaty-of-hudaybiyya|The Treaty of Hudaybiyya]]
- Quraysh sent a series of envoys, and the speaker says the Prophet dealt with each according to his character. The first, Budayl ibn Warqa, was a wise chief whose tribe the transcript names as Quza'a (a name read from the transcript and needing a check). The Prophet told him that the Muslims had come to visit the House, that Quraysh had been worn down by war, and that he would accept a truce for a period; if they chose war, he would fight until his neck was cut. {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep41 00:13:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep41 00:13:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep41 00:14:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep41 00:14:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep41 00:15:00} [[person/budayl-ibn-warqa|Budayl ibn Warqa]]
- The speaker describes the next envoys, Mikraz ibn Hafs and Hulays ibn Alqama. The Prophet called Mikraz treacherous, and was given the sign of a sacred offering by Hulays, who respected the rites. {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep41 00:15:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep41 00:16:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep41 00:16:30} (needs_source)
- Urwa ibn Mas'ud spoke roughly and pulled at the Prophet's beard, the speaker says, and al-Mughira ibn Shu'ba struck his hand with the sheath of his sword. Urwa then reported to Quraysh that the Companions competed for the water of the Prophet's ablution. {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep41 00:17:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep41 00:17:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep41 00:18:00} (needs_source) [[person/urwa-ibn-masud|Urwa ibn Mas'ud]] [[person/al-mughira-ibn-shuba|al-Mughira ibn Shu'ba]]
- The speaker says the Prophet saw Suhayl ibn Amr coming from afar and said that Suhayl had come, and that the matter was made easy for them. {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep41 00:18:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep41 00:19:00} (needs_source)
- Suhayl asked for the terms, the speaker says: a peace of ten years, and the Muslims to go back that year without entering Mecca and return the next year. Umar objected to the Prophet, and then went to Abu Bakr to ask whether they were not on the truth. Abu Bakr answered that the Prophet is the Messenger of God and will not neglect him. {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep41 00:19:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep41 00:20:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep41 00:20:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep41 00:21:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep41 00:25:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep41 00:26:00} [[person/umar-ibn-al-khattab|Umar ibn al-Khattab]] [[person/abu-bakr|Abu Bakr]] (needs_source)
- The speaker states the clause on people who come over from either side, which the Companions found hard to accept. The Prophet accepted it, and the speaker says the reason was to give room for the message among the Arabs and beyond. The transcript is garbled on the direction of the clause, so the direction is not written. {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep41 00:21:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep41 00:22:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep41 00:22:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep41 00:23:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep41 00:23:30} (needs_source; garbled)
- When the treaty was to be written, Suhayl objected to the opening formula, and asked that it be written in the name of God rather than the Merciful and the Compassionate. The speaker says Ali was told to write, and Suhayl objected to "Messenger of God" and asked for the name and father's name of the Prophet instead. The Prophet, the speaker says, told Ali to erase the phrase, Ali refused, and the Prophet himself erased it. {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep41 00:26:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep41 00:26:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep41 00:27:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep41 00:27:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep41 00:28:00} [[person/ali-ibn-abi-talib|Ali ibn Abi Talib]] (needs_source)
- Abu Jandal ibn Suhayl came in chains and declared his Islam. Suhayl struck him in the face and demanded that he be returned. The Prophet asked Suhayl to leave him, Suhayl refused, and the Prophet told Abu Jandal to be patient, saying that God would give him a way out. {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep41 00:29:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep41 00:29:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep41 00:30:00} [[person/abu-jandal-ibn-suhayl|Abu Jandal ibn Suhayl]] (needs_source)
- The speaker says Umar said that a man does not kill his father for God. Abu Jandal asked why Umar did not kill him, and Umar said he could not disobey the Messenger. The transcript is partly garbled here. {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep41 00:30:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep41 00:31:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep41 00:31:30} (needs_source; garbled) [[person/umar-ibn-al-khattab|Umar ibn al-Khattab]]
- Abu Basir, the speaker says, escaped and led a band of men who intercepted the caravans of Quraysh; the speaker gives their number as three hundred. Quraysh asked the Prophet to take back those who came to him, and the Prophet said he was bound by the covenant. {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep41 00:32:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep41 00:32:30} (needs_source) [[person/abu-basir|Abu Basir]]
- At the Conquest of Mecca, the speaker says, the Prophet gathered Quraysh and asked what they expected of him. They answered with good words, and he quoted Joseph's words to his brothers: [[passage/quran-12-92|Surat Yusuf, verse 92]]. {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep41 00:33:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep41 00:33:30} [[event/conquest-of-mecca|The Conquest of Mecca]]
- The speaker says Suhayl became a Muslim after Hunayn, about two years before the Prophet's death. His arithmetic of the years of opposition is not consistent in the transcript and is not written. He gives 18 AH as the year of death. These dates need a source. {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep41 00:33:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep41 00:34:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep41 00:34:30} (needs_source) [[event/battle-of-hunayn|Hunayn]]
- The speaker describes Suhayl's change after his conversion: he prayed much at night, fasted until he was thin, and wept when he recited the Qur'an. These are the speaker's descriptions. {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep41 00:34:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep41 00:35:00} (needs_source)
- The speaker says Suhayl learned the Qur'an from Mu'adh ibn Jabal, a younger Khazraji companion, and sat before him as a pupil. He tells older listeners that it is never too late to learn. The young age of Mu'adh needs a source. {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep41 00:35:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep41 00:36:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep41 00:36:30} (needs_source) [[person/muadh-ibn-jabal|Mu'adh ibn Jabal]]
- The speaker reports Suhayl's pledge: whatever he had spent to block the way of God he would now spend twice over, and whatever he had opposed the Messenger in he would now defend. {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep41 00:37:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep41 00:37:30} (needs_source)
- In Medina, the speaker says, Abu Sufyan, Safwan ibn Umayya and Suhayl came to Umar, who let Bilal and Suhayb enter first. Suhayl told the Quraysh men that the Prophet had called them and that they should answer quickly, and said that God does not treat alike those who hasten to Him and those who delay. {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep41 00:39:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep41 00:40:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep41 00:40:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep41 00:41:00} [[person/bilal-ibn-rabah|Bilal ibn Rabah]] [[person/suhayb-ibn-sinan|Suhayb ibn Sinan]] [[person/safwan-ibn-umayya|Safwan ibn Umayya]] [[person/abu-sufyan-ibn-harb|Abu Sufyan ibn Harb]] (needs_source)
- The speaker says Suhayl fought in Syria, and died there. He says the plague of Amwas is named as the cause, though he thinks it more likely that Suhayl fell at Yarmuk. The sources are not checked. {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep41 00:42:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep41 00:44:00} (needs_source) [[place/amwas|Amwas]] [[event/battle-of-yarmuk|The Battle of Yarmuk]]
- The speaker says Abd Allah prayed for his father for years, and that his father became a Muslim after that. He says that a martyr intercedes for seventy of his family, and the saying is his. {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep41 00:42:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep41 00:43:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep41 00:43:30} (needs_source) [[person/abdullah-ibn-suhayl|Abd Allah ibn Suhayl]]
- The speaker reports Suhayl's words at his death: he grieved only for his objection to the Prophet at Hudaybiyya, and asked God to forgive him that and to give him martyrdom. {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep41 00:44:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep41 00:44:30} (needs_source)
- The speaker draws the lesson that God is patient and forgiving, and that a man who opposed the Prophet for years can be pardoned. He calls on listeners to pray for parents, children and spouses who are far from God. This is his advice. {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep41 00:45:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep41 00:46:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep41 00:46:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep41 00:47:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep41 00:47:30}

## Left out of this episode 41

Not written from episode 41: the audience's personal remarks from about 00:48:00 to 00:49:30, which are private and not named. The speech after the Prophet's death, at about 00:38:00, is delivered by a speaker the transcript does not name; the attribution of its words is not checked, so the speech is not attributed to anyone here, and the founder should decide how it is to be recorded. The speaker's remark at 00:39:00 that Umar wept and gave thanks that he had not broken Suhayl's tooth is left out for the same reason, since the transcript places it after that speech. The Qur'anic phrase in the garbled line at about 00:41:30 is not typed. Repetition loops at 00:10:00, 00:26:30, 00:41:30, 00:48:30 and 00:49:30 were discarded.

## Episode 42: Abbas ibn Abd al-Muttalib: the Prophet's uncle, the Aqaba pledge, Badr and the captives, the Conquest of Mecca, his prayer and death, as the speaker and the audience tell it

:::perspectives
- **The speaker on the Ansar and the caliphate (his view):** he holds that the Ansar gave without seeking posts, and that none of the Rightly Guided Caliphs was from the Ansar. This is his view, and the episode does not check it against the sources. The episode sets out no other view on this question. {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep42 00:13:00}
- **The speaker on talents (his view):** he holds that a loud voice, drawing, writing, storytelling and other gifts should be directed to serving Islam. This is his view in the closing exhortation. {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep42 00:39:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep42 00:40:00}
:::

- The speaker opens with a quiz on the Prophet's uncles and aunts. By his count the Prophet had nine uncles and six aunts; he names Abbas ibn Abd al-Muttalib as the subject of the episode. These counts are the speaker's own (needs_source: the counts of uncles and aunts). {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep42 00:00:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep42 00:00:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep42 00:01:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep42 00:03:00} [[person/abbas-ibn-abd-al-muttalib|Abbas ibn Abd al-Muttalib]]
- The speaker says Abbas was the only one of the uncles who lived to see the Prophet's death, and he reports that the Prophet, seeing him, said that only this one remained of his forefathers. {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep42 00:03:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep42 00:04:00}
- The speaker describes Abbas as fair, handsome, very tall and large, with a voice that carried across Mecca: when a leader of Quraysh wanted his opinion he sent a messenger, but Abbas would stand on a hill and call out, and be heard. This is the speaker's description (needs_source: the description and the voice, as the speaker tells them). {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep42 00:04:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep42 00:05:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep42 00:05:30}
- The speaker says Abbas defended the Prophet as Abu Talib did, and that his own conversion came late. Among the narrations he prefers a later date for it (needs_source: the date of his Islam). [[person/abu-talib|Abu Talib]] {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep42 00:06:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep42 00:07:00}
- The speaker places Abbas at the second pledge of al-Aqaba, a night meeting in the Days of Tashriq at the Great Jamra, and says that the attendees were seventy-three men and two women (needs_source: the number). [[event/second-pledge-of-aqaba|Second pledge of al-Aqaba]] {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep42 00:07:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep42 00:08:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep42 00:08:30}
- The speaker says Abbas spoke first, calling on the Khazraj to protect the Prophet as they would protect their own families. The Ansar then asked what they would gain, and the Prophet answered that it was Paradise. [[group/ansar|the Ansar]] {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep42 00:11:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep42 00:12:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep42 00:12:30}
- The speaker tells of a dream seen by Atika bint Abd al-Muttalib, an aunt of the Prophet, three days before the campaign of Badr: a man standing on Mount Qubays warned Quraysh of a disaster within three days. She told Abbas, who told a friend on condition of secrecy, and the dream was known across Mecca within about twenty-four hours (needs_source: the dream as the speaker tells it). [[person/atika-bint-abd-al-muttalib|Atika bint Abd al-Muttalib]] {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep42 00:13:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep42 00:14:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep42 00:14:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep42 00:15:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep42 00:15:30}
- The speaker reports that Abu Jahl threatened that, unless the dream showed a sign, he would hang a writing on the Kaaba calling the Banu Abd al-Muttalib the greatest liars of the Arabs. The wording is garbled in the transcript, so the meaning is taken from the summary, not the words. [[person/abu-jahl|Abu Jahl]] {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep42 00:16:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep42 00:16:30}
- The speaker says Abbas sent the Prophet reports of Quraysh's preparations, and that the Prophet kept Abbas's part secret from the Companions, for fear that hypocrites in Medina would carry the news to Mecca (needs_source). {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep42 00:16:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep42 00:17:00}
- At Badr the speaker says Abu Jahl insisted that Abbas march with Quraysh, and that he went out unwillingly; the Prophet, the speaker says, had ordered before the fighting that whoever met Abbas should not kill him, because he had come out under compulsion. [[event/battle-of-badr|Badr]] {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep42 00:17:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep42 00:18:00}
- The speaker says Abu Hudhayfa ibn Utba, whose father had been killed in the battle, said that he would kill Abbas if he met him; Umar offered to kill him, and the Prophet refused. The speaker adds that Abu Hudhayfa later died a martyr; the name of the battle is garbled in the transcript and is not written. [[person/abu-hudhayfa-ibn-utba|Abu Hudhayfa ibn Utba]] [[person/umar-ibn-al-khattab|Umar ibn al-Khattab]] {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep42 00:18:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep42 00:19:00}
- The speaker says Ibn Mas'ud took Abbas prisoner; Abbas said that a man held his hand so that he could not move, and the Prophet said that an angel had taken him captive. The speaker reports that some scholars hold that God so arranged it that Abbas would not be killed (needs_source: the angel account and its reading). [[person/abdullah-ibn-masud|Abdullah ibn Masud]] {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep42 00:19:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep42 00:20:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep42 00:20:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep42 00:21:00}
- The speaker says the Prophet could not sleep that night because he heard Abbas moaning in his bonds. A man loosened Abbas's bonds, and the Prophet asked whether he had done the same for the other captives; the reply is garbled in the transcript and is not written. {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep42 00:22:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep42 00:22:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep42 00:23:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep42 00:23:30}
- The speaker says Abbas left Mecca before the Prophet's army arrived and declared his Islam and his testimony. He gives the army as ten thousand (needs_source: the number). [[event/conquest-of-mecca|Conquest of Mecca]] {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep42 00:24:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep42 00:24:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep42 00:25:00}
- The speaker calls Abbas the last of the emigrants, and says the Prophet said something to him in a sentence garbled in the transcript and not written (needs_source: the wording is garbled). {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep42 00:25:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep42 00:26:00}
- The speaker says Abbas rode the Prophet's mule to Mecca to call its people to Islam and met Abu Sufyan on the way, then brought him into the Muslim camp. [[person/abu-sufyan-ibn-harb|Abu Sufyan ibn Harb]] {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep42 00:26:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep42 00:27:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep42 00:27:30}
- The speaker says Abu Sufyan spoke words like those of Joseph's brothers, and that the Prophet answered that there is no reproach on them today. The verse the speaker has in mind is not written here; it is given by reference only. [[passage/quran-12-91|Qur'an 12:91]] [[passage/quran-12-92|Qur'an 12:92]] {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep42 00:28:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep42 00:28:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep42 00:30:30}
- The speaker says Umar wanted to kill Abu Sufyan; Abbas said that he had given him protection, and that Umar would not act so if Abu Sufyan were of the Banu Adi. Umar wept and said that Abbas's Islam pleased the Prophet more than his own father al-Khattab's would have. [[person/umar-ibn-al-khattab|Umar ibn al-Khattab]] {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep42 00:29:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep42 00:29:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep42 00:30:00}
- The speaker says Abu Sufyan declared the first testimony, hesitated over the second and then made it, and asked to return to Quraysh. The Prophet, the speaker says, asked that he be held with Abbas until morning so that he could see the army (needs_source). {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep42 00:31:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep42 00:31:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep42 00:32:00}
- The speaker describes the battalions passing before Abu Sufyan. He asked about the green battalion, and Abbas told him it was the Prophet among the Muhajirun and the Ansar. {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep42 00:33:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep42 00:34:00}
- The speaker says that Abbas, who was in charge of the water supply, asked that the key of the Kaaba be added to his office. The Prophet refused, returned the key to its keepers, and said that no one would take it from them except a wrongdoer. The speaker says the key belongs to the Banu Abd al-Dar, its keepers (needs_source). [[building/kaaba|the Kaaba]] {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep42 00:34:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep42 00:35:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep42 00:35:30}
- At Hunayn the speaker says Abbas stood holding the Prophet's mount when the ranks broke, and called out in a voice that the Prophet had him use to call on the people of the pledge of al-Aqaba, of Badr and of al-Ridwan; they answered his call. [[event/battle-of-hunayn|Hunayn]] [[event/bayat-al-ridwan|the pledge of al-Ridwan]] {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep42 00:36:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep42 00:36:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep42 00:37:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep42 00:38:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep42 00:38:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep42 00:39:00}
- The speaker reports that the Prophet taught Abbas a prayer: to ask God for pardon and well-being. Abbas asked again, and the Prophet said it was among the prayers he most enjoined (needs_source: the narration). {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep42 00:40:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep42 00:41:00}
- The speaker's account: in the last days before the Prophet's death Abbas told Ali ibn Abi Talib to ask the Prophet to give them the succession after him. Ali is described as declining to make that request; the speaker's reading of the reply is not written because the transcript is garbled (needs_source: the account is not checked against the historical sources). This is the speaker's narration alone; no other narration of it is set out here, so it is held for review. [[person/ali-ibn-abi-talib|Ali ibn Abi Talib]] {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep42 00:41:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep42 00:42:00}
- The speaker says the Prophet was pleased with Abbas and said, "Abbas is from me and I am from him," and that Abbas was among those who washed the Prophet's body. The speaker names five who did so: Abbas, two of his sons (the names are garbled in the transcript), Ali ibn Abi Talib and Usama ibn Zayd (needs_source). [[person/usama-ibn-zayd|Usama ibn Zayd]] {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep42 00:42:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep42 00:43:00}
- The speaker says that in the year of famine in Umar's caliphate, Umar asked for rain through Abbas, saying that they used to ask through their Prophet and now ask through the Prophet's uncle; rain fell, and Abbas came to be called the giver of water to the two sanctuaries. The year's name is garbled in the transcript and is not written. [[person/umar-ibn-al-khattab|Umar ibn al-Khattab]] {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep42 00:43:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep42 00:44:00}
- The speaker says Abbas lost his sight late in life and died at the age of eighty-eight (needs_source: the age). He was buried in al-Baqi, and Uthman ibn Affan led the prayer over him; the speaker quotes Abu Hurayra on the crowd at his funeral. [[place/al-baqi|al-Baqi]] [[person/uthman-ibn-affan|Uthman ibn Affan]] [[person/abu-hurayra|Abu Hurayra]] {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep42 00:44:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep42 00:45:00}
- The speaker closes with a call to keep the ties of kinship. He says family bonds break over inheritance and quarrels, and he holds up the Prophet's care for his captive uncle as a model. This is the speaker's advice. {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep42 00:46:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep42 00:46:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep42 00:47:00}
- The speaker says Abbas cared that his old friend Abu Sufyan should taste the sweetness of faith. This is the speaker's reading of the story. {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep42 00:48:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep42 00:49:00}

## Left out of this episode 42

Not written from episode 42: the discussion of the people of Palestine and the present ordeal at about 00:50:00 to 00:52:00, which is outside the subject of the biography and connects to a present-day dispute; it is held for review in the track register. The audience's personal remarks are not written, and the garbled sentence about names at 00:06:00 (repeated and cut off) is not written, nor the non-Arabic fragments at the end (00:53:00 onward). Verses the speaker recited without a clear link to the text are not written.

## Episode 43: Ja'far ibn Abi Talib: the first emigration to Abyssinia, his account before the Negus, the recitation of Surat Maryam, his return from Abyssinia, Mu'ta and his martyrdom, as the speaker and the audience tell it

:::perspectives
- **The speaker on presenting Islam briefly (his view):** he holds that someone presenting Islam in a short time needs to order the points into a few themes, and that Ja'far is a model of this. This is his view. {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep43 00:15:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep43 00:15:30}
- **The speaker on this world and Paradise (his view, citing a saying he attributes to a scholar):** he holds that people prefer the passing world to the lasting Paradise, and he reports the Prophet's saying that a bow's length in Paradise is better than this world and what is in it. This is his view and his wording. {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep43 00:44:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep43 00:44:30}
:::

- The speaker introduces Ja'far ibn Abi Talib as the thirty-second to accept Islam, after about thirty-one men (needs_source: the order), and says the Prophet told him that he resembled him in form and in character, and that at that time Ja'far was the one who most resembled the Prophet. [[person/jafar-ibn-abi-talib|Ja'far ibn Abi Talib]] {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep43 00:00:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep43 00:00:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep43 00:01:00}
- The speaker says persecution of the weaker Muslims grew, and the Prophet told the Companions to go to the land of Abyssinia, where the king would not wrong anyone; about eighty Companions left, by the speaker's figure (needs_source: the number). [[event/first-migration-to-abyssinia|the first migration to Abyssinia]] [[place/abyssinia|Abyssinia]] {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep43 00:01:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep43 00:02:00}
- The speaker notes that women emigrated with their husbands: Uthman with Ruqayya, Ja'far with Asma bint Umays, and Ubaydullah ibn Jahsh with Umm Habiba. [[person/uthman-ibn-affan|Uthman ibn Affan]] [[person/ruqayya-bint-muhammad|Ruqayya bint Muhammad]] [[person/asma-bint-umays|Asma bint Umays]] [[person/ubaydullah-ibn-jahsh|Ubaydullah ibn Jahsh]] {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep43 00:02:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep43 00:03:00}
- The speaker holds that the emigrants were not only the weak: Uthman, Umm Habiba daughter of Abu Sufyan and Ja'far, the Prophet's cousin, were among them. He reads the Prophet's message to the Negus as meant to reach notables as well as the weak (the speaker's reading of the Prophet's message). {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep43 00:03:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep43 00:04:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep43 00:04:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep43 00:05:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep43 00:05:30}
- The speaker says Quraysh sent Amr ibn al-As and Abdullah ibn Abi Rabi'a with gifts to the Negus. He describes Amr as the cleverest and most eloquent of them, and says the plan was to win over the courtiers first and then the king before the Muslims were heard. [[person/amr-ibn-al-as|Amr ibn al-As]] [[group/quraysh|Quraysh]] {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep43 00:06:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep43 00:07:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep43 00:07:30}
- The speaker reports that Amr told the Negus the Muslims were foolish youths who had left their fathers' religion without joining his. The Negus said he would not hand them over until he had heard them. [[person/negus-of-aksum|the Negus]] {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep43 00:08:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep43 00:08:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep43 00:09:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep43 00:09:30}
