- The speaker describes the Negus's court and says the Muslims chose Ja'far as their spokesman. He asks the audience to imagine being asked to present Islam in two minutes, a challenge the episode sets for its listeners. {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep43 00:10:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep43 00:10:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep43 00:11:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep43 00:11:30}
- The speaker sets out Ja'far's speech in five points, as he reconstructs it: first, the ignorance of the past, with idols, carrion, the breaking of kinship and the strong devouring the weak; second, the Prophet known for truthfulness, trust and lineage; third, the teachings of Islam, such as truthfulness, returning trusts, kinship and refraining from indecency; fourth, the wrongs the Muslims suffered; fifth, praise of the Negus without flattery. {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep43 00:15:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep43 00:16:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep43 00:16:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep43 00:17:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep43 00:17:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep43 00:18:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep43 00:18:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep43 00:19:00}
- The speaker says Ja'far recited the opening verses of Surat Maryam to the Negus, who wept until his beard was wet, and said that what he had brought and what Jesus brought came from one niche. The verses are given by reference only. [[passage/quran-19-2|Qur'an 19:2]] [[passage/quran-19-3|Qur'an 19:3]] [[passage/quran-19-4|Qur'an 19:4]] {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep43 00:21:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep43 00:22:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep43 00:22:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep43 00:23:00}
- The speaker says Amr asked the Negus to put a question to the Muslims about Jesus. Ja'far's answer, as the speaker gives it, implies that Jesus is God's servant and messenger; this is the speaker's rendering and is not a quotation or a link to the Qur'an wording. The Negus took a twig from the ground and said the difference between them was no more than that twig, and then he returned the gifts to Amr. [[person/isa-ibn-maryam|Jesus ibn Maryam]] {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep43 00:23:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep43 00:24:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep43 00:24:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep43 00:25:00}
- The speaker says the Negus became a Muslim by Ja'far's hand (needs_source). He also says that a son was born to Asma bint Umays in Abyssinia, whom Ja'far named Abdullah, and that the Negus said he would name his own son the same; the sentence is garbled in the transcript and is held for review. {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep43 00:25:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep43 00:25:30}
- The speaker says the Companions stayed in Abyssinia about ten years (needs_source: the duration), until after Khaybar. The Prophet, when they asked to return, told them to wait; the speaker reads this as a plan to keep a second base for Islam outside Medina (the speaker's reading). [[event/battle-of-khaybar|Khaybar]] {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep43 00:26:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep43 00:27:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep43 00:27:30}
- The speaker says Ja'far returned with the emigrants in three ships; the number of ships and of those returning is not clear in the transcript (needs_source: the number of ships and of returnees. Another item on the site, on the return of the emigrants, says two ships, and the difference is held for review). [[event/return-of-abyssinian-emigrants|the return of the emigrants from Abyssinia]] {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep43 00:28:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep43 00:28:30}
- The speaker says the Prophet embraced Ja'far on his return and kissed him between the eyes, and said that he did not know which to rejoice at: the conquest of Khaybar or Ja'far's return. {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep43 00:29:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep43 00:29:30}
- The speaker says Umar told Asma bint Umays that the men of Medina had preceded her in emigration, and she wept; the Prophet, the speaker says, told the people in general that there was one emigration, but that the people of Abyssinia had two (the speaker's narration). [[person/umar-ibn-al-khattab|Umar ibn al-Khattab]] {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep43 00:30:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep43 00:31:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep43 00:31:30}
- The speaker says Ja'far fed the poor and needy in Medina, and that the Prophet gave him the title Abu al-Masakin, the father of the poor, within about the seventh and eighth years after the Hijra (needs_source: the dating). He relates Abu Hurayra's account of hunger, and of Ja'far taking him home. [[person/abu-hurayra|Abu Hurayra]] {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep43 00:32:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep43 00:32:30}
- The speaker gives the battle of Mu'ta with figures: about three thousand Muslims against two hundred thousand Romans (needs_source: both figures and the number of horses). He says the Prophet named three commanders in order: Zayd ibn Haritha, then Ja'far, then Abdullah ibn Rawaha. [[event/battle-of-mutah|Mu'ta]] [[person/zayd-ibn-haritha|Zayd ibn Haritha]] {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep43 00:33:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep43 00:34:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep43 00:34:30}
- The speaker's account: Zayd fell first, and Ja'far took up the banner; he dismounted and hamstrung his horse, carried the banner in his right hand until it was cut off, then in his left until that too was cut, then held it between his arms until he was killed. The account is the speaker's narration, and some phrases are garbled. [[event/mutah-martyrdom-of-jafar|the martyrdom of Ja'far at Mu'ta]] {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep43 00:35:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep43 00:36:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep43 00:36:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep43 00:37:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep43 00:38:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep43 00:38:30}
- The speaker quotes Abdullah ibn Umar as having found more than forty blows and wounds on Ja'far's body, and none on his back (the speaker's narration of Ibn Umar; needs_source: the number). [[person/abdullah-ibn-umar|Abdullah ibn Umar]] {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep43 00:39:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep43 00:39:30}
- The speaker reports that the Prophet told Asma that Ja'far flies in Paradise with two wings in place of his hands, and that the Prophet asked for the children of Ja'far, embraced them, and asked the Companions who would take charge of them (needs_source: the narrations). {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep43 00:38:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep43 00:40:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep43 00:40:30}
- The speaker recounts several narrations about Ja'far's place in Paradise, including one about Hamza and one about Ja'far flying with Gabriel and Michael. The wording is not written (needs_source: the wording of the narrations). {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep43 00:41:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep43 00:41:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep43 00:42:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep43 00:42:30}
- The speaker says Asma bint Umays married Abu Bakr after Ja'far and bore him Muhammad, then married Ali after Abu Bakr, and that Abu Bakr had asked that Asma wash his body. [[person/asma-bint-umays|Asma bint Umays]] [[person/abu-bakr|Abu Bakr]] [[person/ali-ibn-abi-talib|Ali ibn Abi Talib]] {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep43 00:45:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep43 00:45:30}
- The speaker says her sons, Muhammad ibn Abi Bakr and Abdullah ibn Ja'far, quarrelled, each saying his father was better than the other's; Asma answered each of them in a way that pleased him, and Ali praised her answer. [[person/abdullah-ibn-jafar|Abdullah ibn Ja'far]] {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep43 00:46:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep43 00:46:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep43 00:47:00}
- The speaker says Asma had nine sisters, several of whom were connected by marriage to the Prophet's family, among them Maymuna, the Prophet's wife (needs_source: the names and the connections). [[person/maymuna-bint-al-harith|Maymuna bint al-Harith]] {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep43 00:47:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep43 00:47:30}

## Left out of this episode 43

Not written from episode 43: the two repeated passages at 00:33:00 and 00:37:00, where the transcript is cut off, and the garbled sentences naming people without context. The call to the audience to give to a cause, and the speaker's remarks on the present situation of listeners, are not written. The wording of the narrations given in mixed language is not written.

## Episode 44: Asma bint Abi Bakr: the Hijra and carrying provisions, Abu Jahl's visit, Dhat al-Nitaqayn, her charity, her son Abdullah ibn al-Zubayr and her death, as the speaker and the audience tell it

:::perspectives
- **The speaker on women's capacities (his view):** he holds that women bear more patience and endurance than men, can manage more than one task at a time, and that men focus on one thing. This is his generalisation, and no evidence is given in the episode (needs_source). {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep44 00:35:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep44 00:35:30}
- **A participant on balancing home and work (a participant's view):** one audience member holds that the general environment today does not help women as it helped Asma, and the speaker holds that the way begins with awareness and small steps. These are the views of a participant and of the speaker. {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep44 00:15:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep44 00:16:00}
:::

- The speaker opens by saying the episode is about a woman, after many episodes on Companions, and recalls Umm Umara and Sumayya. He says Sumayya was the first martyr in Islam, and that Khadija was, by the scholars' consensus, the first to prostrate to God after the Prophet (needs_source: the order). [[person/sumayya-bint-khayyat|Sumayya bint Khayyat]] [[person/khadija|Khadija]] {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep44 00:00:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep44 00:00:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep44 00:01:00}
- The speaker presents Asma bint Abi Bakr as a woman in whose family four generations of Companions met: her grandfather Abu Quhafa, her father Abu Bakr, her son Abdullah ibn al-Zubayr, and her husband al-Zubayr ibn al-Awwam, with her mother-in-law Safiyya bint Abd al-Muttalib and her sister Aisha. [[person/asma-bint-abi-bakr|Asma bint Abi Bakr]] [[person/abu-quhafa|Abu Quhafa]] [[person/abu-bakr|Abu Bakr]] [[person/abdullah-ibn-al-zubayr|Abdullah ibn al-Zubayr]] [[person/zubayr-ibn-al-awwam|al-Zubayr ibn al-Awwam]] [[person/safiyya-bint-abd-al-muttalib|Safiyya bint Abd al-Muttalib]] [[person/aisha|Aisha]] {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep44 00:02:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep44 00:02:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep44 00:03:00}
- The speaker says Asma was the sister of Aisha through their father, not their mother, and that their mother had not accepted Islam. He gives the age gap as about fifteen years, and at another point as twenty; the two figures are not reconciled in the transcript (needs_source). {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep44 00:03:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep44 00:04:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep44 00:04:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep44 00:05:30}
- The speaker says Asma was among the first seventeen or eighteen to accept Islam (needs_source: the order), and that she was about twenty-five at the Hijra (needs_source: the age; the transcript also gives twenty at one point). {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep44 00:04:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep44 00:05:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep44 00:05:30}
- The speaker describes the Hijra: the Prophet took a route away from Medina towards the south; he had Quraysh believe he was going elsewhere for three days; he left at midday with his face covered, and asked Ali to sleep in his bed (the speaker's narration). [[event/hijra|the Hijra]] {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep44 00:05:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep44 00:06:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep44 00:06:30}
- The speaker asks where the Prophet was from night until the following noon, and says he found no answer in the books of biography. This is the speaker's question. {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep44 00:07:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep44 00:07:30}
- In Asma's account, as the speaker gives it, Abu Bakr came at an hour when he had never come before, covered his face, and asked those in the house to leave. The Prophet said that Asma and Aisha were his household; Abu Bakr asked for the companionship and wept with joy. {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep44 00:08:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep44 00:08:30}
- The speaker says the journey needed food, news from Mecca and a guide. Abdullah ibn Abi Bakr went around Mecca gathering news by day, and Asma carried the food (the division of tasks as the speaker tells it). {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep44 00:09:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep44 00:09:30}
- The speaker says the distance from Mecca to Mount Thawr was about three miles, and that Asma was in her seventh month of pregnancy and carried food every day (needs_source: the distance and the pregnancy; the transcript also says she gave birth two months after the Hijra). [[place/jabal-thawr-madina|Mount Thawr]] {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep44 00:10:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep44 00:10:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep44 00:11:30}
- The speaker says Abu Jahl came to the house of Abu Bakr; Asma opened the door, and he asked where her father was. She said she did not know, and he struck her. The transcript's description of the blow is garbled, and its details are not written. [[person/abu-jahl|Abu Jahl]] {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep44 00:12:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep44 00:12:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep44 00:13:00}
- The speaker says Asma received the title Dhat al-Nitaqayn, the one with two belts, and ties it to an act in her life; the act is not described, because the transcript is garbled at this point (needs_source). {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep44 00:13:30}
- The speaker says that one night of sincerity can change a person's life, and points to Asma's conduct as an example. This is the speaker's exhortation. {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep44 00:14:00}
- The speaker recalls a saying of the Prophet that a worker in a certain time will earn the reward of seventy of the earlier generation; when the Companions asked whether it was them or the others, the Prophet said it was them. The speaker holds that Asma and her like have great reward, and that hardship does not prevent obedience (needs_source: the wording of the saying). {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep44 00:17:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep44 00:17:30}
- The speaker says Asma lived about a hundred years, and that she narrated fifty-eight hadiths from the Prophet, and that many men narrated from her (needs_source: her age and the number of hadiths). {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep44 00:21:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep44 00:21:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep44 00:22:00}
- The speaker relays al-Zubayr's account: he came into his house and found Asma praying and repeating two verses of Surat al-Tur that speak of God's mercy in protecting from the scorching wind and of God being the Good, the Merciful. She wept and kept repeating them, and this was still so when he came back later. [[passage/quran-52-27|Qur'an 52:27]] [[passage/quran-52-28|Qur'an 52:28]] [[person/zubayr-ibn-al-awwam|al-Zubayr ibn al-Awwam]] {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep44 00:22:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep44 00:23:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep44 00:23:30}
- The speaker contrasts the generosity of Asma and Aisha: Aisha gathered dirhams one by one and then gave a large sum, while Asma kept nothing in her house and spent all she had. This is the speaker's comparison. [[person/aisha|Aisha]] {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep44 00:24:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep44 00:25:00}
- Asma, as the speaker quotes her, looked after al-Zubayr's horse, kneaded bread, and carried date stones from al-Zubayr's land to the house, while running her household (the speaker's narration of her words). {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep44 00:25:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep44 00:25:30}
- The speaker asks the audience whether a woman can combine home and work, and some participants say it is hard in their time (the audience's discussion). {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep44 00:26:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep44 00:26:30}
- The speaker holds that idle women are more exposed to going astray, and calls young women to learn and to do useful work (the speaker's view). {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep44 00:27:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep44 00:28:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep44 00:29:30}
- The speaker describes Asma's giving in secret and the hadiths he links to charity: a dirham given in God's way is multiplied until its owner meets God with it weighing more than a mountain; God causes usury to vanish and makes charities grow; and a person who gives in secret is shaded by God on the Day of Resurrection (needs_source: the wording of the sayings; the speaker urges secret giving). {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep44 00:37:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep44 00:37:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep44 00:38:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep44 00:38:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep44 00:39:30}
- A participant recounts a personal experience of trusting God when money was short, and the speaker recalls the story of Abu al-Dahdah, who gave his garden to God; his wife and child were asked to leave it. [[person/abu-al-dahdah|Abu al-Dahdah]] {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep44 00:40:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep44 00:41:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep44 00:41:30}
- The speaker says Asma's mother, who had not accepted Islam, came to visit her in Medina. Asma asked the Prophet whether she should keep ties with her, and he said: keep ties with your mother. The speaker holds that this shows that kindness to parents is not cut off by a difference of faith. [[person/asma-bint-abi-bakr|Asma bint Abi Bakr]] {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep44 00:43:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep44 00:43:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep44 00:44:00}
- The speaker warns against disobedience to parents, even when they are angry, and urges that a person should not die while a parent is angry with him (the speaker's exhortation). {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep44 00:44:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep44 00:45:00}
- The speaker says Asma lived to about a hundred. Her son Abdullah ibn al-Zubayr sought the caliphate, and an army from Syria under al-Hajjaj ibn Yusuf, sent on the orders of Abd al-Malik ibn Marwan, besieged Mecca. Abdullah went to his mother, saying he feared his body would be mutilated after he was killed, and she told him to go out in the way of God (the speaker's narration). [[person/abdullah-ibn-al-zubayr|Abdullah ibn al-Zubayr]] [[person/al-hajjaj-ibn-yusuf|al-Hajjaj ibn Yusuf]] [[person/abd-al-malik-ibn-marwan|Abd al-Malik ibn Marwan]] {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep44 00:45:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep44 00:46:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep44 00:46:30}
- The speaker says al-Hajjaj reproached Asma for what he had done to her son, and she answered him: you have spoiled his worldly life, and he has spoiled your hereafter. He says Hajjaj killed her son and left his body hanging for seven days, and that Asma lost her sight late in life (the speaker's narration; needs_source: the seven days). {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep44 00:47:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep44 00:47:30}
- The speaker says Asma died at about a hundred years of age and was buried in Medina, in al-Baqi (needs_source: the age and the place). [[place/al-baqi|al-Baqi]] {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep44 00:48:00}

## Left out of this episode 44

Not written from episode 44: the segment at 00:50:00 on the people of Palestine and the appeals connected with them, which is outside the subject of the biography and connects to a present-day dispute; it is held for review in the track register. The participants' personal experiences beyond those noted, and the passages that cannot be read clearly in the machine transcript, are not written, including the repeated passage at 00:31:30. The participants' personal details are not written, and no description of the family life of the speaker or of participants is given.

## Episode 45: Jabir ibn Abdullah: the second pledge of al-Aqaba, the lot for Uhud, his father's debts and death, the flood that uncovered the grave, the army fed from a handful of barley, the camel sold to the Prophet, and the speaker's questions on burdens and trials, as the speaker and the audience tell it

:::perspectives
- **The speaker on the pressures of work and money (his view):** he holds that career and money must not crowd out worship, family duties and service to God, and he puts the question to married people and to young people (his exhortation; no evidence is given beyond the story). {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep45 00:40:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep45 00:41:00}
- **Why the righteous are tested (the speaker and an audience member):** the audience member gives the saying that God tests the one He loves so that his sins are wiped away; the speaker restates a second reason given by the audience, that a servant who has no sins is tested to raise his rank. These are views of those who voice them, presented as sayings they quote; the episode does not settle them (needs_source for both sayings). {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep45 00:49:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep45 00:50:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep45 00:50:30}
:::

- The speaker introduces [[person/jabir-ibn-abdullah|Jabir ibn Abdullah]], son of [[person/abdullah-ibn-amr-ibn-haram|Abdullah ibn Amr ibn Haram]] of the Khazraj, a Companion who witnessed [[event/second-pledge-of-aqaba|the second pledge of al-Aqaba]], and says that pledge was the basis on which the Prophet and the Companions later emigrated to Medina. {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep45 00:00:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep45 00:00:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep45 00:03:00}
- The speaker gives the number at the pledge as seventy-three men and, in a figure the transcript garbles, some women. He says it took place at night, with some Companions, among them Abu Bakr and Umar, posted on the mountain passes, and that the Companions pledged to protect the Prophet with their lives, their children and their wealth (needs_source: the number of women is garbled). {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep45 00:01:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep45 00:01:30}
- The speaker says Abdullah ibn Haram had lost his wife and was left with nine daughters and a son, Jabir, and with debts. When the army set out for Uhud he did not let his family's burden keep him back. Jabir asked to go with him and was refused for being still too young, as he had been too young for Badr; the speaker gives Jabir's age at Uhud as about twenty (needs_source: the age is not confirmed in the transcript). {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep45 00:03:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep45 00:03:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep45 00:04:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep45 00:04:30}
- They drew lots over who would go and who would stay with the daughters, and the lot allowed the father to go. Jabir wept. The father told him that if it were anything but Paradise he would have chosen him for it. Then the father said that he had been shown, in what the speaker calls a vision, that he would be the first martyr that day. {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep45 00:05:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep45 00:05:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep45 00:06:00}
- The father told Jabir that after God's Messenger no one was dearer to him, and charged him with the debts and the sisters: pay what I owe, and look after your sisters well (the speaker's narration of the father's words). {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep45 00:06:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep45 00:07:00}
- Abdullah ibn Haram was killed at [[event/battle-of-uhud|the Battle of Uhud]], which the speaker presents as the first martyrdom of that day, and the news reached Jabir in Medina. {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep45 00:07:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep45 00:08:00}
- When Jabir came to see the body, the Companions held him back, because the enemy had mutilated it; the Prophet told them to let him look. He told Jabir that whether he wept or not, the angels kept shading his father with their wings (the speaker's narration of the Prophet's words). {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep45 00:08:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep45 00:09:00}
- The Prophet told Jabir that God had spoken to no one except from behind a veil, but had spoken to his father face to face, without a veil, and asked him what he wished (the speaker's narration). {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep45 00:09:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep45 00:10:00}
- The father asked to be sent back to the world to fight and be killed again; God answered that it had already been decreed that they would not return. The father then asked that his brothers be told of the happiness he was in. {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep45 00:10:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep45 00:11:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep45 00:11:30}
- The speaker cites the verses at this point and places them at the centre of the account. [[passage/quran-3-169|Surat Al 'Imran, verse 169]] [[passage/quran-3-170|Surat Al 'Imran, verse 170]] {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep45 00:12:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep45 00:12:30}
- The speaker tells Jabir's later account: some twenty years after the death, a torrent struck Medina, the ruler called on families to move their dead, and Jabir found his father's grave and the body as it had been left. When Jabir moved the hand, the wound bled, and the account ends with a scent of musk (needs_source: the twenty years and the detail of the wound). {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep45 00:12:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep45 00:13:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep45 00:13:30}
- Jabir did not attend Badr, being young, nor Uhud with his father, and from then on, the speaker says, he took part in all seventeen expeditions with the Prophet. The speaker gives two figures for the hadiths Jabir reported from the Prophet, 1,520 at 00:14:30 and 1,540 near the end; the two conflict in the transcript and are not reconciled (needs_source). {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep45 00:14:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep45 00:14:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep45 00:52:30}
- The speaker turns to a second moment with the Prophet: the [[event/battle-of-the-trench|Battle of the Trench (al-Ahzab)]]. He says the trench was three kilometres long and two hundred metres deep, dug in rock in fifteen days (needs_source: the speaker's figures, not checked against the sources). {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep45 00:16:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep45 00:16:30}
- In the hunger of the Trench, the speaker says, the Companions asked the Prophet to show them the bellies they had tied stones to; he lifted his garment and showed two stones tied on his own belly. {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep45 00:17:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep45 00:18:00}
- Jabir went home to ask his wife what food there was. She said there was little, and then, the speaker says, a handful of barley and a hen. The speaker's word for the hen is partly garbled in the transcript; the handful of barley and the hen are the items the account names. {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep45 00:18:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep45 00:19:30}
- The Prophet asked whether Jabir was asking only for himself, and said it was not for him to eat alone. He asked what the food was; Jabir named the barley and the hen, and the Prophet said that was enough (the speaker's narration). {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep45 00:20:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep45 00:20:30}
- The Prophet called out to the Muhajirun and the Ansar that Jabir was their host that day, and told Jabir to go ahead to the house to tell his household that the Prophet and the army were coming. The speaker's account of the wife's reply in the transcript is garbled and left out. {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep45 00:21:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep45 00:21:30}
- The Prophet had the army enter ten at a time; the speaker gives the army as one thousand five hundred (needs_source) and says that all of them ate. He calls the handful of barley and the hen a miracle of the Prophet, which he says is an authentic report, and says the food was still as it had been when the whole army had eaten. {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep45 00:22:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep45 00:23:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep45 00:23:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep45 00:24:00}
- The speaker draws the lesson of giving from what one has: many people with means, he says, do not give to the needy who are near them, and Jabir's giving is the model he holds up (his exhortation). {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep45 00:24:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep45 00:25:00}
- On a long raid, the speaker says, the army walked far with worn-out feet, and they bound their feet with patches, which gave the expedition its name; the name is garbled in the transcript and is not written. He gives the distance as 200 to 700 kilometres (needs_source). {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep45 00:25:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep45 00:26:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep45 00:26:30}
- Jabir's old, weak camel fell behind the army, and the Prophet, who was at the centre of the army, noticed that Jabir was behind and turned back to him. The Prophet asked what was wrong, asked for a stick, struck the camel, and it began to race ahead of the Prophet's own camel (the speaker's narration). {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep45 00:27:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep45 00:27:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep45 00:28:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep45 00:28:30}
- The Prophet asked Jabir whether he had married, and whether the bride was a young unmarried woman; Jabir said he had married a woman older than a girl, because he had nine daughters and needed someone who could look after them. The Prophet said he had done well (the speaker's narration). {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep45 00:29:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep45 00:30:00}
- The Prophet told Jabir not to enter Medina until his wife knew of his return, so that she could prepare; the army waited outside the city for a while (the speaker's account; the word the speaker uses for the preparation is garbled). Jabir said they had no means to prepare, and the Prophet told him that it would come right, and to act wisely when he returned. {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep45 00:30:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep45 00:31:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep45 00:33:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep45 00:33:30}
- The Prophet wanted to give Jabir money without embarrassing him, and so asked to buy his camel; Jabir offered it as a gift, and the Prophet insisted on paying. The speaker gives the price as seven hundred dirhams; the earlier offers in the bargaining are garbled and left out. The Prophet told Jabir to keep riding the camel to Medina. {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep45 00:34:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep45 00:34:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep45 00:36:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep45 00:36:30}
- The speaker says the Prophet asked God's forgiveness for Jabir twenty-five times (needs_source for the count as given). On arrival, Jabir brought the camel to the door of the Prophet's house; the Prophet asked for [[person/bilal-ibn-rabah|Bilal]] and told him to give Jabir the seven hundred dirhams and that the money and the camel were his (the speaker's narration). {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep45 00:37:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep45 00:37:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep45 00:38:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep45 00:38:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep45 00:48:30}
- The speaker says the Prophet died pleased with Jabir, and that Jabir taught hadith in the circle of the Prophet's mosque. He says Jabir died at ninety-four, and gives the year as 74 or 75 AH in one sentence (the two dates are not reconciled); he was buried in [[place/al-baqi|Al-Baqi']]. He calls Jabir the last to die of the seventy-three men and women of the second pledge, and the youngest of the Companions (needs_source: the age at death and the claim that he was the youngest). {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep45 00:39:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep45 00:39:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep45 00:40:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep45 00:53:00}
- The speaker puts a question to married people and to young people: do the burdens of life take a person away from his religion, and how can a person keep his worship safe from them? He asks for comments from the audience, and says he himself feared that marriage would draw him away from the Qur'an. {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep45 00:40:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep45 00:41:00}
- An audience member cites the saying that a woman is married for three things, her wealth, her beauty and her religion, and that the one who is religious should be chosen; the audience member presents it as a reason to choose a spouse for religion. {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep45 00:43:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep45 00:43:30}
- Looking back over Jabir's life, the speaker lists his trials: the deaths of his father and mother, nine daughters, debts, the responsibility for his daughters, and the hard end of his life. He asks why the trials of the righteous are so heavy, and puts the question to the audience. {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep45 00:48:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep45 00:49:00}

## Left out of this episode 45

Not written from episode 45: the segment at 00:29:00 (very short and unreadable) and the repeated segment at 00:31:30; the name of the expedition at 00:26:00, which is garbled in the machine transcript (the story itself is written); the audience members' personal accounts of work and family at 00:44:30 to 00:48:00, which are personal experiences beyond the subject; and the closing thanks and invocations.

## Episode 46: Sumayya, Yasir and Ammar ibn Yasir: the first family to embrace Islam openly, Sumayya as the first martyr, Ammar's torment and the Prophet's words to him, Badr, and Umm Umara Nusayba bint Ka'b at Uhud and in the war against Musaylima, as the speaker and the audience tell it

:::perspectives
- **The speaker on family standing (his view):** he holds that worldly names and fame count for little before God, and that a family's worth lies in obedience shared at home: praying together at night, reading the Qur'an together and giving to the poor together. This is his exhortation; the episode gives no evidence beyond the story (needs_source). {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep46 00:01:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep46 00:02:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep46 00:03:00}
- **The end of Ammar and the rebel group (the speaker's account of a contested war):** the speaker says the fighting stopped when Ammar was killed, because the Prophet had said that a rebel group would kill him, and that this showed who the rebel group was. The war between Ali's army and Mu'awiya's is contested in the sources. The episode gives only the speaker's account; other accounts are not set out here and are to be added from sources (needs_source). {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep46 00:32:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep46 00:32:30}
:::

- The speaker presents Sumayya and Yasir as poor people with nothing, Yasir a man of modest means and Sumayya over sixty and very thin. He says their master was [[person/abu-jahl|Abu Jahl]] (needs_source: the speaker's word; the ownership is not checked). He says that by worldly measure the family counted for nothing, and that by God's measure it counted for a great deal. {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep46 00:00:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep46 00:00:30}
- The speaker says this was the first family to accept Islam together, in a single day: [[person/yasir-ibn-amir|Yasir ibn Amir]], [[person/sumayya-bint-khayyat|Sumayya bint Khayyat]] and their son [[person/ammar-ibn-yasir|Ammar ibn Yasir]], the father, the mother and the son. {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep46 00:06:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep46 00:07:00}
- The speaker says that only seven people had openly embraced Islam in Mecca when this family did, among them the Prophet, Abu Bakr and [[person/bilal-ibn-rabah|Bilal]]; the names of the others are garbled in the transcript. He places the family as the thirtieth to accept Islam, after twenty-nine others (needs_source: the order and the count). {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep46 00:07:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep46 00:08:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep46 00:08:30}
- The speaker says this was the first family to be martyred together, and gives what he calls the scholars' definition: a family that lived in Islam and did everything in obedience to God, whom God joined together as martyrs, as they had lived for Him. {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep46 00:09:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep46 00:09:30}
- The speaker says [[person/sumayya-bint-khayyat|Sumayya]] was the first martyr in Islam, and that she was a woman. He says this was not an arrangement of rank: a woman was first so that women learn that they had light from the first day, and so that men are shamed by it (the speaker's view). {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep46 00:10:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep46 00:13:30}
- The speaker says Abu Jahl pressed Sumayya to deny Muhammad, and that she refused; he then struck her with a weapon whose name is garbled in the transcript, while she was bound, and she died. The speaker describes the blow in detail; the detail is not written here, only the outcome. {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep46 00:14:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep46 00:14:30}
- Sumayya died between her husband and her son, and the speaker says the Prophet told the family to be patient and promised them Paradise (the speaker's narration). {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep46 00:15:00}
- The speaker reads the Qur'an passage on the one who turns away from the remembrance of God and has a narrow life, and takes the remembrance to mean reading and living by the Qur'an and the Sunna at home. [[passage/quran-20-124|Surat Ta-Ha, verse 124]] {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep46 00:15:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep46 00:16:00}
- The speaker says that Islam gave women their rights fourteen hundred years ago, and that women are not confined but are mistresses of their homes and active outside them (the speaker's assertion; no source is given for the general claim). {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep46 00:17:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep46 00:17:30}
- The speaker says that [[person/yasir-ibn-amir|Yasir]] died not long after Sumayya, under torment (needs_source: the days and the manner of his death). {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep46 00:20:30}
- The speaker says [[person/ammar-ibn-yasir|Ammar]] gave in under severe torment and spoke words his tormentors demanded (the speaker does not write them out here). He came to the Prophet weeping, and the Prophet asked him how he found his heart; he answered that it was at peace with faith. {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep46 00:21:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep46 00:21:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep46 00:22:00}
- The speaker reads the Qur'an passage on those who worship God at the edge, and says the Prophet told Ammar that if they returned to torment him he should do the same as before (the speaker's narration of the Prophet's words). [[passage/quran-22-11|Surat al-Hajj, verse 11]] {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep46 00:22:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep46 00:23:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep46 00:23:30}
- The speaker says the Prophet loved Ammar greatly, called him near, and said he wished to pray for Ammar's parents and family. He then prayed: O God, forgive the family of Yasir; the speaker says this was answered (the speaker's narration). {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep46 00:24:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep46 00:24:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep46 00:25:00}
- At [[event/battle-of-badr|the Battle of Badr]], the speaker says, news reached the Prophet in the fighting that Abu Jahl had been killed; the first thing he asked was where Ammar was, and he told Ammar that God had avenged his father and mother. The speaker gives the time since Sumayya's death as twelve to fourteen years (needs_source: the figure is the speaker's and is not checked). {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep46 00:25:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep46 00:26:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep46 00:26:30}
- The speaker says Paradise longs for three people, and names Ammar among them; the other names are garbled in the transcript and are not written. {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep46 00:27:00}
- The speaker tells of a quarrel between [[person/khalid-ibn-al-walid|Khalid ibn al-Walid]] and Ammar, in which Khalid spoke harshly to him. The Prophet came out, saw Ammar weeping, and said that whoever opposes Ammar has opposed God; the speaker says the Prophet's face reddened (the speaker's narration). {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep46 00:27:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep46 00:28:00}
- The speaker says Ammar was killed at about ninety-four years of age (needs_source: the age is the speaker's; the name of the battle is not his), in the war between the army of [[person/ali-ibn-abi-talib|Ali ibn Abi Talib]] and the army of Mu'awiya, at the [[event/battle-of-siffin|Battle of Siffin]], and that Ammar was on Ali's side. The speaker tells the sequence of the death in the terms of the battle, as told below. {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep46 00:31:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep46 00:32:00}
- The speaker turns to Nusayba bint Ka'b, Umm Umara, and quotes the Prophet on [[event/battle-of-uhud|Uhud]]: he did not turn right or left without seeing her defending him. The speaker says she went out with the army to treat the wounded. {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep46 00:35:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep46 00:36:00}
- The speaker says that when the Prophet was left exposed in the fighting, she took up a sword and stood before him. She was struck on the shoulder by an attacker whose name is garbled in the transcript, and her son [[person/habib-ibn-zayd|Habib ibn Zayd]] described the wound, which he said was deep enough for a fist to go into (the speaker's narration). {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep46 00:36:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep46 00:37:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep46 00:38:00}
- The speaker says the Prophet told Umm Umara that she, her husband and her children were his companions in Paradise (the speaker's narration). {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep46 00:40:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep46 00:40:30}
- The Prophet sent [[person/habib-ibn-zayd|Habib ibn Zayd]] with a letter to [[person/musaylima|Musaylima]], whom the speaker calls 'the liar'. Musaylima asked Habib whether he testified that Muhammad was God's messenger, and then whether he testified to Musaylima's own messengership. Habib refused the second question, saying he was deaf; the speaker says Musaylima had him cut limb by limb, and that he gave the same answer each time. {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep46 00:41:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep46 00:41:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep46 00:42:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep46 00:42:30}
- The speaker says that when the news of her son's martyrdom reached Umm Umara, she was glad, and that she went out in the Muslim army against [[person/musaylima|Musaylima]] (the speaker does not name the place of the battle). {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep46 00:44:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep46 00:44:30}
- The speaker says that in that battle a spear struck Musaylima, which he attributes to the man who had killed Hamza at Uhud (named by him as Wahshi; the name is partly garbled), and that Umm Umara struck him with a sword. He presents this as an act of revenge. {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep46 00:44:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep46 00:45:00}
- An audience member gives the purpose of life as raising a child who enters Paradise and entering it with him, and says that is the main aim (the audience member's view). {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep46 00:46:00}
- The speaker closes by saying that the account of Ammar, Yasir and Sumayya teaches that whoever holds fast to faith will be helped by God to bear what comes, and he asks God to keep the audience steadfast (his closing exhortation). {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep46 00:46:30}

## Left out of this episode 46

Not written from episode 46: the segment at 00:05:30 (repetition) and the segment at 00:10:00 (repetition and very short); the speaker's comparison of Islamic and Western civilisation at 00:29:00 to 00:30:30, which is an unsourced comparison; an audience member's personal anecdote about an English Muslim woman and the name she gave her daughter, at 00:34:30 to 00:35:00; and the closing segment at 00:48:00 to 00:50:00, which is a present-day framing held for review in the track register.

## Episode 47: Sa'd ibn Mu'adh: his conversion at the hand of Mus'ab ibn Umayr, the conversion of Banu Abd al-Ashhal, his stand at Badr and at the Trench, his wound, his judgment on Banu Qurayza, and his death at which the Throne of the Merciful shook, as the speaker and the audience tell it

:::perspectives
- **The judgment on Banu Qurayza (the speaker's account of a contested event):** the speaker tells that Banu Qurayza asked for arbitration and chose Sa'd, once their ally in the days before Islam, expecting leniency; that Sa'd ruled that their men be killed, their property taken, their homes divided among the Emigrants and their women taken captive; and that the Prophet said he had judged with God's judgment above the seven heavens. The fate of Banu Qurayza is contested in the sources and in modern scholarship. The episode gives only the speaker's account, which is the classical Sunni telling; the academic views are not set out here and are to be added from sources (needs_source). {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep47 00:44:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep47 00:47:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep47 00:48:30}
:::

- The speaker opens with the death before the life: if any man deserved that the Throne of the Merciful should shake at his death, it was [[person/sad-ibn-muadh|Sa'd ibn Mu'adh]]. He presents the Throne as a creature of God that was given feeling, and compares it with Mount Uhud, which trembled under the Prophet until he set his hand on it and told it to be firm, for upon it were a prophet, a truthful man and martyrs (the speaker's narration of the Prophet's words; the wording is not reproduced, needs_source). {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep47 00:00:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep47 00:00:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep47 00:01:00}
- The speaker reports what he calls the scholars' explanation: the Throne shook from the joy of the angels who carry it as the soul of Sa'd ascended, citing the Qur'anic mention of those who bear the Throne (the verse is not typed; the speaker does not name it). {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep47 00:01:30}
- The speaker says Sa'd had been a Muslim only about seven years when he died, and that Gabriel came to the Prophet saying that the doors of heaven had opened for a soul that had ascended and the Throne of the Merciful had shaken; the Prophet rose and found Sa'd had died (the speaker's narration). {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep47 00:02:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep47 00:02:30}
- Sa'd was tall, large-built, handsome and fair. As the Companions carried his bier they found it strangely light and told the Prophet; he answered that they had not carried it alone, for the angels had carried it with them (the speaker's narration). {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep47 00:03:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep47 00:03:30}
- The speaker says that as the Prophet entered to pray over him he kept raising his garment, explaining that the place was crowded with angels (the line is partly garbled in the transcript; the detail is given in outline only). {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep47 00:04:00}
- Sa'd's mother came weeping and began recounting his virtues; the Prophet said that every wailer lies except the wailer over Sa'd ibn Mu'adh, then told her to dry her tears and ease her grief, for God was pleased with her son (the speaker's narration of the exchange). {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep47 00:04:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep47 00:04:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep47 00:05:00}
- The speaker's first lesson: Sa'd reached this rank in about seven years, because what counts is not how early one comes but how truthful one is with God; he asks the audience not to listen for a tale but to take Sa'd as a model and imitate him (his exhortation). {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep47 00:05:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep47 00:06:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep47 00:06:30}
- Sa'd was the master of Banu Abd al-Ashhal, a clan of the Aws, and so one of the Ansar; though only about thirty he had nobility, standing and honour in Medina. The Prophet had sent [[person/musab-ibn-umayr|Mus'ab ibn Umayr]] to Medina to teach, and Mus'ab's fame spread until there was hardly a house without a Muslim; he was the guest of [[person/asad-ibn-zurara|As'ad ibn Zurara]], Sa'd's cousin. {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep47 00:06:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep47 00:07:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep47 00:07:30}
- When news of Mus'ab reached Sa'd he was angered and sent [[person/usayd-ibn-hudayr|Usayd ibn Hudayr]] to drive the stranger out; Usayd returned having himself embraced Islam, though he told Sa'd only that the man's talk was beyond them. Sa'd saw that he had come back with a different face, took his spear and went himself to expel Mus'ab (the speaker's narration). {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep47 00:08:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep47 00:08:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep47 00:09:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep47 00:09:30}
- Sa'd came in raging, accusing Mus'ab of dividing families and corrupting the town. Mus'ab answered calmly: sit and hear; if what I say pleases you, take it, and if not, I leave it be. Sa'd called that fair, planted his spear and sat; Mus'ab recited the Qur'an to him and his face changed as Islam entered him (the speaker's narration; the recitation is not typed). {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep47 00:09:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep47 00:10:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep47 00:10:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep47 00:11:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep47 00:11:30}
- Sa'd asked what a man does who wishes to enter this religion; told to wash, testify and pray two rak'as, he did so. The speaker remarks that history knows no one else at whose death the Throne of the Merciful shook (his assertion). {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep47 00:11:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep47 00:12:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep47 00:12:30}
- His first act as a Muslim: he gathered Banu Abd al-Ashhal and asked what he was to them; they answered, our master and our best. He declared that the words of their men and women were forbidden to him until they believed in God alone; the whole clan entered Islam (the speaker's narration). {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep47 00:12:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep47 00:13:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep47 00:13:30}
- The speaker draws the lesson he wants the audience to keep: Sa'd preached on the first day of his Islam with almost no knowledge, unashamed, because his standing, his success and his character carried his word; he asks what stops the audience from taking their friends and families by the hand (his exhortation, with audience exchanges about fear of answering wrongly and about preaching by example). {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep47 00:14:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep47 00:16:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep47 00:21:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep47 00:22:00}
- The speaker tells two of his own experiences as witness to that lesson: stopping his car before a coffee house to deliver a one-line message to a man he heard cursing religion, and addressing a crowd of youths gathered in a street before dawn to tell them that what they did was wrong, which ended with him speaking alone to the one among them who was a keeper of the Qur'an (the speaker's personal testimony). {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep47 00:25:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep47 00:26:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep47 00:28:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep47 00:30:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep47 00:31:00}
- An audience member answers that what matters is the strength of a person's bond with God, for that is what lets the word pass from one heart to another; a caller recalls the Prophet's question to Mu'adh on how he would judge. The speaker thanks them and returns to the story. {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep47 00:31:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep47 00:34:00}
- At [[event/battle-of-badr|Badr]], the speaker reminds that the Ansar's pledge bound them inside Medina, while the battle came outside it: some three hundred Muslims against a thousand, one horse against three hundred (the figures are the speaker's, needs_source). The Prophet asked the people's counsel; Abu Bakr and Umar answered, then [[person/al-miqdad-ibn-amr|al-Miqdad ibn Amr]] said they would not repeat what Israel said to Moses but would fight beside him. The Prophet asked again, and it was Sa'd who understood whom he was waiting for. {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep47 00:34:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep47 00:35:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep47 00:35:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep47 00:36:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep47 00:36:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep47 00:37:00}
- Sa'd stood and answered: is it us you mean, Messenger of God? We have given you our pledges to hear and obey; go forward to whatever you were ordered and we are with you; by Him who sent you with the truth, if you lead us into the sea we will plunge with you, and perhaps God will show you of us what will please your eye. The Prophet then gave the people the good news of one of the two promised outcomes (the speaker's narration of the exchange). {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep47 00:37:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep47 00:38:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep47 00:38:30}
- The speaker comments that Sa'd made perhaps five stands in his life and each was worth ten years of another man's, because he loved Islam with all his being (his assessment). {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep47 00:41:30}
- At the [[event/battle-of-the-trench|Trench]], ten thousand besieged Medina and fear reached the hearts, as the Qur'an describes (the verse is not typed). The Prophet considered winning the tribe of Ghatafan away with a third of Medina's harvest to break the confederacy, and consulted Sa'd, who asked whether this was God's command or something done for them; told it was for them, he answered that in the days of ignorance those tribes never hoped for a single fruit of Medina, and that now that God had honoured them with Islam the tribes would not take a third of its fruit without price — they would be given the sword only. The Prophet accepted his counsel (the speaker's narration). {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep47 00:39:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep47 00:40:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep47 00:40:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep47 00:41:00}
- Sa'd, then about thirty-seven, prayed during the siege that if God had left any war with Quraysh He would keep him for it, since no people were dearer to him to fight than those who had wronged, denied and driven out the Prophet, and that if war had ended between them He would take him a martyr. Soon after, an arrow struck him in the shoulder and the wound began to bleed (the speaker's narration; the place of the wound is given as the transcript has it). {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep47 00:42:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep47 00:42:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep47 00:43:00}
- The Prophet had him carried to a tent in the mosque so that he would be nursed nearby, and [[person/rufayda-al-aslamiyya|Rufayda al-Aslamiyya]], whom the speaker calls the first woman doctor of Medina, tended him in her tent pitched in the Prophet's mosque; the speaker adds that Hassan ibn Thabit composed verse about her, though the line is garbled (the speaker's narration; needs_source for the verse). {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep47 00:43:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep47 00:44:00}
- When Banu Qurayza broke their pact and sided with the confederates, Sa'd added to his prayer that God should not let him die until his eyes were cooled of them; when his wound burst open he prayed again, and the wound dried (the speaker's narration). {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep47 00:44:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep47 00:45:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep47 00:46:00}
- The Prophet besieged [[event/siege-of-banu-qurayza|Banu Qurayza]]; the speaker tells that Ali ibn Abi Talib stood at their fortress and declared he would not come down until their castles fell or he met Hamza's fate. They asked for arbitration and named Sa'd, their ally of old, not knowing of his prayer. He came on a donkey, and his tribesmen urged him to be good to his allies; he asked only that his word bind, and when they and the Prophet agreed, he gave his judgment as told above. {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep47 00:46:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep47 00:47:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep47 00:47:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep47 00:48:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep47 00:48:30}
- After the judgment Sa'd prayed: O God, the war with Quraysh is ended and I have seen my satisfaction of Banu Qurayza, so let the wound burst — and it burst, and he fell, a martyr (the speaker's narration). {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep47 00:49:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep47 00:49:30}
- The speaker gathers the Prophet's reported words over his death: that the Throne of the Merciful shook for it, that seventy thousand angels walked in his funeral, that the grave's first squeeze spared no one but Sa'd, and to his mother that God was pleased with her son (the speaker's narration; needs_source). {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep47 00:49:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep47 00:50:00}
- The speaker ends with the Prophet's word over a gold-embroidered cloak taken years later from a Roman commander: the kerchiefs of Sa'd ibn Mu'adh in Paradise are better than it; and with his closing appeal that the listeners attach themselves to Sa'd, whose mark was an all-consuming love and zeal for Islam. {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep47 00:50:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep47 00:50:30}

## Left out of this episode 47

Not written from episode 47: the programme promo at 00:14:00 and 00:26:30 to 00:27:30; the Qur'an verses the speaker recites or quotes at 00:01:30, 00:34:00 and 00:39:30 (Qur'an text is not typed, and the verses are not named); the hadith wordings on the Throne, on Uhud the mountain, on the angels carrying the bier and on the Prophet's prayer at Uhud at 00:00:30 to 00:02:30 and 00:17:30, which are paraphrased only; repetition loops at 00:08:00 and 00:45:30; the garbled opening line at 00:00:00; audience exchanges and personal anecdotes in outline only at 00:15:00 to 00:20:30, 00:23:00 to 00:25:00 and 00:32:30 to 00:33:30; and the speaker's comment on the Prophet's words about Umar at Uhud at 00:30:00, which is partly garbled.

## Episode 48: Abu Dharr al-Ghifari: his search for the truth, his conversion through Ali's care, his open declaration and beatings in Mecca, the conversion of Ghifar, his walking alone at Tabuk, his truthfulness and zuhd, and his death at al-Rabadha as the Prophet had foretold, as the speaker and the audience tell it

:::perspectives
- **Abu Dharr's leaving for al-Rabadha (the speaker's view of a contested point):** the speaker insists that Abu Dharr left for al-Rabadha of his own will and that whoever says Uthman expelled him lies. The manner of his leaving Medina is told differently in the sources; the episode gives the speaker's position only, and the differing accounts are to be added from sources (needs_source). {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep48 00:47:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep48 00:48:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep48 00:48:30}
:::

- The speaker begins, in answer to listeners who asked, by naming the books the series is built on: [[work/usd-al-ghaba|Usd al-Ghaba]] of Ibn al-Athir, [[work/al-isaba-fi-tamyiz-al-sahaba|al-Isaba]] of Ibn Hajar and [[work/siyar-alam-nubala|Siyar A'lam al-Nubala]] of al-Dhahabi as the three classical sources; for easier reading he names picture-books of the Companions' lives, a life of the Companions in four parts, an encyclopaedia of sacrifice in Islam, a book on the Prophet's Companions and Ali Tantawi's essays on historical figures, besides the sira books of Ibn Hisham, the sealed nectar and Said Ramadan al-Bouti's fiqh of the sira (the titles and authors are read from the machine transcript and are marked needs_source where they are garbled). {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep48 00:01:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep48 00:02:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep48 00:02:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep48 00:03:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep48 00:03:30}
- [[person/abu-dharr-al-ghifari|Abu Dharr]] is Jundab ibn Junada of Ghifar, a tribe known among the Arabs for highway robbery; the speaker asks what kind of man such a soil could yield (needs_source for the brother's name, which the transcript gives in two garbled forms). {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep48 00:04:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep48 00:04:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep48 00:05:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep48 00:05:30}
- Hearing that a man in Mecca claimed prophecy, Abu Dharr sent his brother to bring him news; the brother reported a man who preached noble morals and whom his people accused of poetry and madness. Not satisfied, Abu Dharr took a water-skin and provisions and walked to Mecca himself to know the truth (the speaker's narration). {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep48 00:06:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep48 00:07:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep48 00:07:30}
- The speaker pauses for an exhortation on prayer and on keeping company with the righteous, quoting from the Qur'anic passage on Saqar without typing it, and warning against joining those who follow every crowd; the verses are not named (his exhortation). {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep48 00:08:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep48 00:09:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep48 00:10:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep48 00:11:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep48 00:11:30}
- In Mecca, warned by his brother that Quraysh watched whoever asked after Muhammad, Abu Dharr waited three days by the Kaaba on Zamzam water, while the Prophet was meeting the Muslims secretly in the house of al-Arqam, teaching them the Qur'an and how to call people (the speaker's narration). {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep48 00:12:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep48 00:12:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep48 00:13:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep48 00:13:30}
- The task of approaching strangers fell to the boy [[person/ali-ibn-abi-talib|Ali ibn Abi Talib]], thirteen to fifteen years old, whom no one suspected. Ali found the stranger lying by the Kaaba and hosted him two nights without asking his business; on the third night he asked, and Abu Dharr answered that he had left his land to hear the man who claimed prophecy. Ali told him he had found the truth and that he was the Prophet's cousin (the speaker's narration). {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep48 00:14:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep48 00:15:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep48 00:17:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep48 00:18:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep48 00:18:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep48 00:19:00}
- The next day Ali walked ahead and Abu Dharr followed at a distance until they reached the house of al-Arqam. The Prophet asked who he was; on hearing 'from Ghifar' he touched his forehead, and the speaker says Abu Dharr felt he had been disliked for his tribe. The Prophet offered him Islam, he testified, and the Prophet rejoiced, then told him to return to his people and call them until news came that the Prophet had emerged (the speaker's narration). {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep48 00:21:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep48 00:21:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep48 00:22:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep48 00:22:30}
- Abu Dharr answered that by Him who sent the Prophet with truth he would cry it aloud in Mecca. He stood near the Kaaba and proclaimed the testimony; the crowd beat him until he fainted. [[person/abbas-ibn-abd-al-muttalib|Al-Abbas]], then not yet a Muslim, threw himself over him, warning that they would kill a Ghifari through whose land their trade road to Syria ran, and pulled him free (the speaker's narration). {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep48 00:22:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep48 00:23:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep48 00:23:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep48 00:24:00}
- The next day, covered in wounds, he proclaimed it again and was beaten worse until al-Abbas rescued him a second time; the Prophet then told him to go back to his people, call them, and not return until the Prophet had emerged victorious (the speaker's narration). {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep48 00:24:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep48 00:25:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep48 00:25:30}
- Back in Ghifar he first converted his brother, then called the tribe one by one until half of them entered Islam; the rest said they would follow when the Prophet emerged. After the Hijra the delegations of [[group/banu-ghifar|Ghifar]] and Aslam came to Medina, and the Prophet, rejoicing, said: Ghifar — may God forgive her; Aslam — may God keep her safe. The speaker remarks how the Prophet honoured people with a sentence, turning a tribe once called the worst of the Arabs into one God had forgiven (his comment). {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep48 00:26:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep48 00:26:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep48 00:27:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep48 00:27:30}
- The speaker then turns to the audience with his standing question — what have we done for Islam? — and reports [[person/al-hasan-al-basri|al-Hasan al-Basri]]'s image of Islam passing over the faces of people until it takes [[person/umar-ibn-al-khattab|Umar]] by the hand, saying: O Lord, I was a stranger until this man embraced Islam (the speaker's narration of a saying he attributes to al-Hasan; needs_source). {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep48 00:28:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep48 00:29:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep48 00:30:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep48 00:30:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep48 00:31:00}
- Audience members offer their answers: to learn the Qur'an's recitation and teach it, to give money for the religion, to excel in one's work so as to honour Islam before others, for a mother to hold a small teaching circle for her children each day, and for everyone to study and speak to those around him (the audience's own words, in outline). {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep48 00:31:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep48 00:32:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep48 00:33:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep48 00:34:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep48 00:35:00}
- A caller named Yaqub, speaking from Switzerland in English, says that where he lives his whole conduct is his call to Islam: people see that he does not drink or do what they do, ask him why, and he explains; the speaker translates his words and tells the audience that this is what believers abroad do (the caller's testimony, summarised). {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep48 00:35:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep48 00:36:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep48 00:36:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep48 00:37:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep48 00:37:30}
- Returning to Abu Dharr's qualities, the speaker names his extreme zuhd, his humility and his truthfulness, quoting the Prophet's words that neither the green shade nor the dusty earth has carried one truer of tongue than Abu Dharr, and that whoever wishes to see the zuhd of Jesus son of Mary should look at Abu Dharr (the speaker's narration; wording not reproduced, needs_source). {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep48 00:39:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep48 00:40:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep48 00:40:30}
- At the [[event/expedition-to-tabuk|expedition to Tabuk]], thirty thousand in terrible heat over a march the speaker gives as a thousand kilometres, the weak began to drop behind; the Prophet answered each report of a laggard that if there was good in him God would bring him to join them. Abu Dharr's camel gave out; he shifted his load onto his own back and walked after the army. The Companions sighted a lone figure in the desert, the Prophet said 'be it Abu Dharr', and when it was he, the Prophet said: may God have mercy on Abu Dharr — he walks alone, he dies alone, and he will be raised alone on the Day of Resurrection (the speaker's narration). {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep48 00:40:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep48 00:41:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep48 00:42:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep48 00:43:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep48 00:44:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep48 00:45:00}
- Under Abu Bakr and Umar he was among the muftis of the Companions and took part in the conquest of Jerusalem. In Uthman's reign, living in Syria under [[person/muawiya-ibn-abi-sufyan|Mu'awiya]], he kept rebuking people and the rich so sharply that Mu'awiya wrote to Uthman; summoned, he debated with Uthman and left smiling, saying he hears and obeys — had Uthman ordered him to walk to San'a he would have gone, for the Prophet had told him to hear and obey even if an Abyssinian slave ruled over him (the speaker's narration; needs_source for Ali's reported praise that no one remained whom blame did not touch in God but Abu Dharr). {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep48 00:45:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep48 00:46:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep48 00:46:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep48 00:47:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep48 00:47:30}
- Finding he could no longer live among people, Abu Dharr asked Uthman's leave to withdraw and chose the desert place called [[place/al-rabadha|al-Rabadha]]; the speaker insists this was his own choice and rejects the charge that Uthman expelled him, as set out in the perspectives block above. {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep48 00:47:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep48 00:48:00}
- At his death there was only his wife and small daughters with him. When she wept that she could not wash and shroud him, he recalled the Prophet's words that one of them would die in a tract of land and a company of believers would attend him, and told her a party of riders would come; and riders came through the emptiness, among them the Companion [[person/abdullah-ibn-masud|Abdullah ibn Mas'ud]], who wept and bore witness that he had heard the Prophet say Abu Dharr would walk alone, die alone and be raised alone (the speaker's narration). {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep48 00:48:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep48 00:49:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep48 00:49:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep48 00:50:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep48 00:50:30}
- The speaker gives Abu Dharr's dying counsel to those who buried him: fast a day of burning heat for the day of the fiercest thirst, undertake a pilgrimage for the grave matters, and pray two rak'as in the darkness of night for the loneliness of the grave (the speaker's narration of his words). {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep48 00:51:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep48 00:51:30}
- He died at al-Rabadha, which the speaker places in 32 AH, was buried there, and Uthman joined his daughter to his own dependents; the speaker gives the number of hadith Abu Dharr transmitted from the Prophet as 281 (the figure is the speaker's, needs_source). The speaker closes that the point is not whether a man dies a martyr but whether he dies obedient to God. {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep48 00:51:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep48 00:52:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep48 00:52:00}

## Left out of this episode 48

Not written from episode 48: the programme's opening remarks on the season and its purpose at 00:00:00 to 00:01:30 in outline only; repetition loops at 00:06:00 to 00:06:30, 00:12:30, 00:14:00, 00:21:30, 00:27:30 and 00:44:00; Qur'an verses quoted on Saqar and on keeping company with wrongdoers at 00:09:30 to 00:10:30 (not typed, and not named); the speaker's exhortation on hijab, work and appearance at 00:14:30 to 00:17:00 and on women and sport at 00:38:00 to 00:39:00 in outline only; and garbled names and figures at 00:04:30 to 00:05:30 (the brother's name), 00:23:30 and 00:26:00.
