## Episode 49: Tufayl ibn Amr al-Dawsi: his conversion on hearing a passage of the Qur'an, the light between his eyes, the conversion of his people Daws, the Prophet's prayer for them, and his death as a martyr at Yamama, as the speaker tells it

:::perspectives
- **The speaker on the lesson of Tufayl (his view):** he holds that Tufayl reached Islam through love of the religion and zeal for it rather than through much learning, and that a caller begins with his own family and people. This is his exhortation; the episode gives no evidence beyond the story (needs_source). {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep49 00:31:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep49 00:31:30}
- **The speaker on companionship and family (his view):** he says a Muslim should take his companion by the hand towards God, and that belonging to the religion passes through a whole family when it starts with those closest. {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep49 00:19:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep49 00:20:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep49 00:18:00}
:::

- The speaker opens by asking the audience for the sweetest words they have ever heard. He says Tufayl embraced Islam on hearing a passage of the Qur'an and cites the first verse of [[passage/quran-112-1|Surat al-Ikhlas, verse 1]]. His own commentary on the verse is not written here. {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep49 00:00:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep49 00:00:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep49 00:01:00}
- The speaker describes Tufayl as over forty, one of the chiefs of Daws and a man of distinction. He says the first thing Tufayl said to the Prophet after embracing Islam was a request; the word itself is garbled in the transcript and is not written here. {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep49 00:02:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep49 00:02:30}
- The speaker asks why many people are slow to answer the call, and says that custom overcame teaching for many of them. He sets Tufayl's quick answer against that (the speaker's view). {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep49 00:03:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep49 00:04:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep49 00:04:30}
- The speaker counts pride and self-respect among the reasons for delay. He says Tufayl, a lord of his people, became obedient to the Prophet's command within five minutes (the speaker's words). {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep49 00:06:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep49 00:06:30}
- Among other reasons the speaker names troubled homes and family conflicts, says that religion brings comfort, and calls it a mistake to put off the answer on the grounds that life is long (the speaker's words). {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep49 00:08:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep49 00:09:30}
- The speaker tells that the Prophet said to Tufayl: go back to your people and call them. Tufayl asked for a sign, and the Prophet prayed: O Allah, give him a sign. A light appeared between Tufayl's eyes. He asked that it not appear on his face, so that his people would not think it a blemish, and the light moved to a place the transcript does not make clear. {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep49 00:15:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep49 00:15:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep49 00:16:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep49 00:16:30}
- The speaker says Tufayl came to his people at night with his light shining like a candle. His mother embraced Islam first, then his father, then his wife; each said, in substance, "your religion is my religion" (the speaker's account). He wishes that families would again gather for a meal on Friday as they once did. {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep49 00:17:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep49 00:17:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep49 00:18:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep49 00:18:30}
- The speaker says that Tufayl came back to the Prophet with [[person/abu-hurayra|Abu Hurayra]]; the place they went to is unclear in the transcript. He claims that every hadith Abu Hurayra narrated counts "in Tufayl's scale" (the speaker's claim; needs_source). He says that Daws refused Islam at that time. {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep49 00:19:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep49 00:19:30}
- The speaker tells that Tufayl asked the Prophet to pray against Daws. Tufayl expected a curse and put his hand on his head; the Prophet raised his hands and prayed: O Allah, guide Daws. He then told Tufayl to go back to his people and call them. {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep49 00:24:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep49 00:24:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep49 00:25:00}
- The speaker says Tufayl came back to the Prophet from time to time, and that Badr, Uhud, the Trench and Hudaybiyya fell in that period. He says the time between the truce and Khaybar was "seven years" (needs_source: the figure should be checked against the Hudaybiyya and Khaybar dates in the record). {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep49 00:25:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep49 00:25:30}
- After Khaybar, the speaker says a thick dust came over Medina. The Prophet asked what it was, and was told that it was Daws, brought by Tufayl, and that all of Daws embraced Islam. He says the matter is feeling and love for the religion rather than knowledge alone, and that Daws asked to be the right wing of the Muslims in battles. {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep49 00:25:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep49 00:26:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep49 00:26:30}
- The speaker says the Prophet sent Tufayl to destroy an idol in Yemen. The idol's name is garbled; the speaker addresses it as the one "of the two palms" (name garbled). Tufayl burned it. The speaker says Tufayl recited verses to it, which are not written here. {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep49 00:26:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep49 00:27:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep49 00:27:30}
- The speaker says the Prophet died pleased with Tufayl, and that Tufayl longed for martyrdom until the battle of Yamama against [[person/musaylima|Musaylima]]. He recounts a dream Tufayl had and gives its interpretation: the shaved head is the neck cut in God's cause, the bird from the mouth is the soul, the woman is the earth in which the body is laid, and his son will follow him as a martyr (the speaker's interpretation). {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep49 00:27:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep49 00:28:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep49 00:28:30}
- The speaker says Tufayl was martyred at Yamama, and that his son [[person/ibn-tufayl|Ibn Tufayl]] longed for martyrdom until his hand was cut off. He withdrew from people, thinking himself no longer able to act. The speaker names [[person/umar-ibn-al-khattab|Umar ibn al-Khattab]] as the one who called for him (the name is partly garbled: "uncle ibn al-Khattab"). The speaker says the caller told him that the hand had gone before him to Paradise and swore that he would not eat until the hand shared his food (the wording of the oath is garbled). {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep49 00:29:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep49 00:29:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep49 00:30:00}
- The speaker says that Tufayl, though (in his own words) of little learning, took the hand of a whole tribe and then of a whole town towards faith and towards God. {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep49 00:30:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep49 00:31:00}
- The speaker contrasts nobles who raised a banner of evil, around which people gathered, with the good who were ashamed to raise a banner of good. He calls on each person to take the hand of those around him. {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep49 00:31:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep49 00:32:00}
- In a digression on the Prophet's orders that people neglect, the speaker mentions a saying that a believer loves for his brother what he loves for himself, and a number of voluntary daily prayers with their reward. He does not name the source of these sayings in the episode (needs_source). {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep49 00:12:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep49 00:12:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep49 00:13:00}

## Left out of this episode 49

Not written from episode 49: the passages at 00:07:00 and 00:08:00 (repetition); the audience questions from 00:10:00 to 00:11:30 on family life, the veil and a wedding, which are personal accounts with no source; a garbled account, at 00:22:00 to 00:23:30, of a member of a delegation whom the Prophet asked about a deed of the day before and who then pledged allegiance, not written; a friend's story from 00:32:30 to 00:33:30 about a film and a young man's debts, personal with no source; and the speaker's closing from 00:34:30 to 00:35:00, which announces the next episode.

## Episode 50: Khalid ibn al-Walid, part one: the Pakistani general's journey after Khalid, the boyhood wrestling with Umar, the house of Makhzum, al-Walid's ransom and conversion at Badr, and Khalid's cavalry at Uhud, as the speaker tells it

- After the Ramadan break the speaker resumes the series and opens its phase on the famous Companions with [[person/khalid-ibn-al-walid|Khalid ibn al-Walid]], a sword of the swords of God and of His messenger, whose kunya he gives as Abu Sulayman. {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep50 00:00:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep50 00:02:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep50 00:02:30}
- The speaker prefaces the story with two examples of devotion to the Prophet's heritage: [[person/abu-ayyub-al-ansari|Abu Ayyub al-Ansari]], who in old age rode from Medina to Egypt only to confirm a single hadith with Uqba ibn Amir and rode back once satisfied (the speaker's narration; the hadith itself is not given); and a Pakistani general, a teacher in his country's war college, whom he does not name. {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep50 00:03:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep50 00:03:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep50 00:04:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep50 00:04:30}
- The speaker retells, from the preface of that general's book on Khalid, how the man met Khalid in a military-history course, grew to love him, learned Arabic for three years to read the sources of the first Hijri centuries, worked through the British Museum's maps and manuscripts, then took leave and spent two years walking every land where Khalid had campaigned — Lebanon, Syria, Jordan, Arabia, Kuwait and Iraq — counting more than ten thousand miles, until he wrote the book the speaker now uses; the author and title are not given in the episode (needs_source). {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep50 00:04:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep50 00:05:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep50 00:06:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep50 00:06:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep50 00:07:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep50 00:07:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep50 00:08:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep50 00:08:30}
- The lesson he draws is attachment: a man loved the Companions enough to learn a language and cross deserts for them, while believers will not knock on a neighbour's door to speak of the religion (his exhortation). {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep50 00:09:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep50 00:09:30}
- The story begins with two boys whose wrestling stopped all Mecca, the strongest pair of youths in Arabia: Khalid ibn al-Walid and Umar ibn al-Khattab. In their famous match the younger Khalid threw Umar and broke his leg, then tended him; the speaker remarks that the two would one day lead the world together (the speaker's narration of the anecdote; needs_source). {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep50 00:10:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep50 00:10:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep50 00:11:00}
- He is Khalid ibn al-Walid ibn al-Mughira of [[group/banu-makhzum|Banu Makhzum]]. The speaker lays out the offices of the Quraysh clans as the episode's screen shows them: Banu Hashim the pilgrims' water, Banu Umayya the Kaaba's covering, Banu Nawfal the relief of the pilgrims, Banu Abd al-Dar the custody of the sanctuary, Banu Asad the counsel, Banu Taym the blood-moneys, Banu Adi the delegations, and Banu Makhzum the army's horses and command; of the three great powers he names Hashim the spiritual, Umayya the political and Makhzum the military (needs_source: the list is the speaker's as read from the transcript). {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep50 00:11:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep50 00:12:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep50 00:12:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep50 00:13:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep50 00:13:30}
- Of Makhzum's standing he gives two marks: alone of the clans they rebuilt the quarter of the Kaaba between the Black Stone and the Yemeni corner when Quraysh rebuilt it before the Prophet's mission, and alone they could field thirty riders (the speaker's figures, needs_source). {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep50 00:13:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep50 00:14:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep50 00:14:30}
- His father was [[person/al-walid-ibn-al-mughira|al-Walid ibn al-Mughira]], master of Makhzum and of such wealth that he alone clothed the Kaaba one year in two, and no pilgrim's fire was lit on the Hajj road but his, the speaker says (needs_source). Khalid grew in this house of riches and rank. {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep50 00:14:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep50 00:15:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep50 00:15:30}
- The speaker notes that Abu Jahl was Khalid's cousin and that both were among the fiercest enemies of the Prophet. He tells of Abu Jahl confessing to the Prophet that he knew him truthful but could not follow him, because Banu Abd Manaf had rivalled his own clan in feeding and giving until the clans were neck and neck, and then they said a prophet had risen among them; the speaker adds that al-Walid ibn al-Mughira thought in the same way, and that the Qur'an came down speaking of him (the verse is not typed or named). {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep50 00:16:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep50 00:16:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep50 00:17:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep50 00:17:30}
- From boyhood Khalid rode so that by sixteen to eighteen he had become the finest horseman in Arabia; his father carried him on long journeys and trained him in every weapon until he could throw the spear at full gallop without a miss — with which, the speaker says, he later killed three Muslims at Uhud (the speaker's narration). {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep50 00:18:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep50 00:18:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep50 00:20:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep50 00:20:30}
- The speaker turns this into his appeal: a father grew his son's gift though he was an enemy of the Prophet, and he calls on parents to seek out and grow their children's gifts and on the young not to waste themselves, for gifts not grown die (his exhortation). {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep50 00:18:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep50 00:19:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep50 00:20:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep50 00:21:00}
- Khalid did not fight at [[event/battle-of-badr|Badr]] — the transcript's reason is garbled — but his brother al-Walid was captured among the seventy prisoners of Quraysh. His ransom was set at the highest band, four thousand dirhams, and Khalid came with [[person/ikrima-ibn-abi-jahl|Ikrima ibn Abi Jahl]] to negotiate the ransoms (the figures are the speaker's, needs_source). {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep50 00:22:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep50 00:23:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep50 00:23:30}
- On the way back, the speaker says, al-Walid slipped away by night, returned to the Muslims and testified before the Prophet — for in captivity he had seen their mercy, recalling the Qur'anic line about food given for love of God to the poor, the orphan and the captive (the verse is not typed; the speaker does not name it). The speaker remarks that al-Walid converted only after he had seen what the Muslims did to him, and draws the lesson that hearts are won by mercy, not by harshness (his comment). {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep50 00:23:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep50 00:24:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep50 00:24:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep50 00:25:00}
- At [[event/battle-of-uhud|Uhud]], the speaker gives Abu Sufyan's plan as encirclement: [[person/ikrima-ibn-abi-jahl|Ikrima]] with about seven hundred horse around Mount Uhud from the right, Khalid with two hundred horse around the north, and Abu Sufyan himself with two thousand from the front, having learned that the Muslims could not be met head-on (the numbers are the speaker's, needs_source). {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep50 00:25:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep50 00:26:00}
- The Prophet countered by posting the archers on the hill so that Ikrima could not flank, with his standing order that they must not leave it whether the Muslims were being plucked by birds or collecting the spoils. Khalid stood waiting with his squadron; when the archers broke the order, he seized the moment, took the hill with the few who remained, wheeled behind the army and struck — crying 'take it from me, I am Abu Sulayman' — and the speaker says his severity at Uhud was great (the speaker's narration). {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep50 00:26:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep50 00:27:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep50 00:28:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep50 00:28:30}
- The episode ends here, before Khalid's conversion; the speaker promises the next episode will take up his Islam and what the Prophet made of this gift. {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep50 00:28:30}

## Left out of this episode 50

Not written from episode 50: the opening greetings and Ramadan recap at 00:00:00 to 00:02:00 in outline only; the Qur'an verse quoted on feeding captives at 00:24:30 (not typed or named); repetition loops at 00:14:00, 00:21:30 and 00:27:30; garbled names and lines at 00:03:00 to 00:04:30 (partly used), 00:08:00, 00:21:30 to 00:22:00 and 00:27:00 to 00:27:30; the screen display of the Quraysh clans, which the transcript cannot reproduce; the speaker's exhortation on gifts and on children at 00:19:00 to 00:20:00 in outline only; and the closing formula from 00:28:30.

## Episode 51: Khalid ibn al-Walid, part two: his conversion on the road to Medina, the letter from his brother al-Walid, the prayer of fear as Khalid saw it, the conversion of three men, and Mu'tah and the withdrawal of the army, as the speaker and the audience tell it

:::perspectives
- **The speaker on companionship (his view):** good companionship pushes a person forward and bad companionship drags him back; he offers Abu Jahl and Khalid as two examples. This is his exhortation; the episode gives no evidence beyond the story (needs_source). {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep51 00:31:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep51 00:32:00}
- **The speaker on the question "where do I go?" (his view):** each person should ask himself the question that Khalid asked: where am I going? {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep51 00:33:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep51 00:34:00}
:::

- The speaker says this is the second part of the story of [[person/khalid-ibn-al-walid|Khalid ibn al-Walid]] and that the series will take four episodes (this conflicts with episode 52, which says five; to be reviewed). He says that Khalid tells the story of his conversion in his own words. {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep51 00:00:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep51 00:00:30}
- The speaker recounts what Khalid says of his opposition to the Prophet at Uhud, at the Trench and at Hudaybiyya, and says that God placed the love of Islam in his heart (as the speaker relates it). {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep51 00:01:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep51 00:01:30}
- The speaker says Khalid said he never stood before Muhammad without coming out of the encounter with nothing, and that he thought Muhammad would prevail. The speaker counts this among the best things Khalid said. {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep51 00:02:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep51 00:02:30}
- The speaker says the organisation and manners of the Muslims affected Khalid more than their military strength, and that one act of good character outweighs many words (the speaker's view). {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep51 00:03:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep51 00:04:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep51 00:04:30}
- At Hudaybiyya, the speaker says Khalid meant to attack the Muslims while they prayed. He watched them pray at noon and then at asr, and concluded that nothing was dearer to them than this prayer, so he did not attack (as the speaker relates it). {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep51 00:05:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep51 00:06:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep51 00:06:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep51 00:07:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep51 00:07:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep51 00:08:00}
- The speaker describes the prayer of fear, in which the army is divided, one part praying while the other keeps watch, and says Khalid was moved by it. The transcript places this description at Hudaybiyya, and the place needs checking (needs_source: the place of the event). {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep51 00:06:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep51 00:07:00}
- After the truce, the speaker says Khalid considered going to Abyssinia, to the Byzantine ruler or to the Persians, and then saw no way out but to go to the Prophet (as the speaker tells it). {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep51 00:10:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep51 00:10:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep51 00:11:00}
- The speaker says that when the Muslims entered Mecca for the umra in the following year, Khalid hid in the mountains. He also gives a figure of four hundred thousand Companions, which needs a source. {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep51 00:11:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep51 00:12:00}
- Khalid's brother al-Walid searched for him and wrote to him. The speaker reads the letter, which asks how Khalid's mind can be closed to Islam, and says that al-Walid reports the Prophet asked about Khalid and said that a man like Khalid could not be ignorant of Islam. {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep51 00:12:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep51 00:13:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep51 00:14:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep51 00:14:30}
- The speaker says that al-Walid also reports the Prophet saying that had Khalid given his strength to Islam it would have been better for him. The speaker says that rank before God is not gained by wealth or position. Khalid read the letter and smiled. {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep51 00:14:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep51 00:15:00}
- The speaker says Khalid saw a dream of a narrow land, and then of a wide, bright land. He went to [[person/abu-bakr|Abu Bakr]], who interpreted it: the narrow land was his former path and the wide land was Islam (as the speaker relates it). {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep51 00:16:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep51 00:17:00}
- Khalid asked who would go with him to the Prophet. The speaker cites the verse [[passage/quran-39-73|Surat al-Zumar, verse 73]] and reads it as meaning that those who loved one another in this world enter Paradise together (the speaker's reading). {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep51 00:17:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep51 00:18:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep51 00:18:30}
- The speaker says [[person/safwan-ibn-umayya|Safwan ibn Umayya]] refused and said he would not convert even if no one else were left; [[person/ikrima-ibn-abi-jahl|Ikrima ibn Abi Jahl]] refused likewise; [[person/uthman-ibn-talha|Uthman ibn Talha]] accepted and went with Khalid; and [[person/amr-ibn-al-as|Amr ibn al-As]] met them on the road, asked where they were going, and said he wanted what they wanted (as the speaker relates it). {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep51 00:19:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep51 00:20:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep51 00:20:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep51 00:21:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep51 00:21:30}
- The speaker says the Prophet said that these three would later open the lands. This is the speaker's report, and no source is named (needs_source). {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep51 00:22:00}
- The three reached Medina. Khalid wore his best clothes and entered the mosque; he greeted the Prophet, who answered him, and he bore witness. The speaker gives Khalid's age at that time as forty-one (elsewhere in the transcript, forty-two; the figures need checking). Khalid asked whether his past could be forgiven, and the speaker says the Prophet told him that Islam wipes out what came before it (needs_source: the saying attributed to the Prophet). {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep51 00:23:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep51 00:23:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep51 00:24:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep51 00:24:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep51 00:25:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep51 00:25:30}
- The speaker reports the Prophet's prayer for Khalid: O Allah, forgive Khalid. He says the Prophet praised the three as the choicest of Quraysh's young men (the speaker's report). The speaker says Khalid became one of the Companions closest to the Prophet (the speaker's account). When Amr ibn al-As asked who was most beloved to the Prophet, the answer is given as a list of names, which the transcript garbles after the seventh. {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep51 00:26:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep51 00:27:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep51 00:27:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep51 00:28:00}
- The Mu'tah story begins: the speaker says that the Prophet's envoy to the Ghassanids was killed, and that the Prophet sent an army of three thousand, with Khalid among them, a Muslim of two months (the speaker's words). {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep51 00:34:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep51 00:34:30}
- The speaker says the Prophet named three commanders in order: [[person/zayd-ibn-haritha|Zayd ibn Haritha]], then [[person/jafar-ibn-abi-talib|Ja'far ibn Abi Talib]], then [[person/abd-allah-ibn-rawaha|Abd Allah ibn Rawaha]]; and that if all three fell, the army should choose whom it wished. He says Zayd had been a freed slave whom the Prophet freed (as the speaker relates it). {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep51 00:35:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep51 00:36:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep51 00:36:30}
- The speaker says the Ghassanids and the Byzantines numbered two hundred thousand, with fifty thousand horsemen, and that this figure is "in the Islamic sources" (the speaker's claim; needs_source: the figures differ between sources). {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep51 00:38:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep51 00:38:30}
- The speaker says the Muslims took refuge in a village at Mu'tah, that the fighting lasted six days, and that the Muslims had the upper hand in the first days (the speaker's account). {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep51 00:39:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep51 00:39:30}
- The speaker tells Khalid's plan for the withdrawal: the positions of the right and left wings, the vanguard and the rear were exchanged, the colours of the banners were changed, and new words were written on them. He says this plan is taught in military academies in Europe and America (the speaker's claim; needs_source). {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep51 00:42:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep51 00:43:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep51 00:43:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep51 00:44:00}
- The speaker says Khalid sent three hundred horsemen to raise dust behind the army, so that the enemy would think reinforcements had come, and that this restored the army's morale. The Muslims then withdrew without the enemy following (as the speaker relates it). {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep51 00:45:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep51 00:45:30}
- The speaker says that a new army came to the Byzantines the next day, and that Abu Hurayra describes the battle (the passage is garbled at this point; needs_source). He says Khalid withdrew the whole army without great loss, and that a thousand Byzantines died (the speaker's figure; needs_source). {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep51 00:46:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep51 00:47:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep51 00:47:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep51 00:48:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep51 00:49:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep51 00:49:30}
- The speaker says that when Khalid returned he feared that the Prophet would be angry at the withdrawal, and said: I seek refuge in God from the anger of God and of His Messenger. The Prophet answered that he had angered neither God nor His Messenger, and that he was "a sword among the swords of God" (as the speaker relates it). {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep51 00:51:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep51 00:51:30}

## Left out of this episode 51

Not written from episode 51: the passage at 00:09:30 (repetition and very short); the speaker's personal digression on phones and sin from 00:26:00 to 00:26:30, which is a personal remark with no source; the speaker's personal anecdote with unsourced figures, from 00:29:00 to 00:31:00, which lies outside the subject of the episode; the audience's remarks on Ramadan and the Qur'an from 00:32:00 to 00:33:00, which are personal comments; and the passage from 00:50:00 to 00:50:30, which is garbled and repeats the Prophet's account of the battle in Medina (written in episode 52 from 00:16:30).

## Episode 52: Khalid ibn al-Walid, part three: Mu'tah and the withdrawal of the army, the conquest of Mecca and the destruction of al-Uzza, Banu Jadhima, Hunayn, Tabuk and Dumat al-Jandal, and Banu al-Harith, as the speaker and the audience tell it

:::perspectives
- **The speaker on blood and religion (his view):** he says that religion does not thirst for blood, that its purpose is to guide people and not to kill them, and that the error at Banu Jadhima was a hasty mistake by Khalid. This is his exhortation; the incident itself is told by the speaker and no other evidence is set out here (needs_source). {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep52 00:29:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep52 00:29:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep52 00:30:00}
- **Sincerity and self-respect (the speaker's view):** he holds that the Prophet trained Khalid in sincerity when he was a young soldier, and that the line between pride and self-respect is fine. {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep52 00:44:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep52 00:45:00}
:::

- The speaker says the aim is that people should take pride in Khalid as a model. He says the Khalid series will take five episodes, and that this is the third, which covers his events with the Prophet (this conflicts with episode 51, which says four; to be reviewed). {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep52 00:00:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep52 00:01:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep52 00:01:30}
- The speaker gives Khalid's ages at a sequence of points: twenty-four at the Prophet's mission, thirty-four at the Hijra, thirty-seven at the raid when he fought the Muslims, forty-one at his conversion, twenty-two at the conquest of Mecca, and fifty-six at his death. These figures do not agree with one another as transcribed and need checking (needs_source: conflicting figures). {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep52 00:03:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep52 00:03:30}
- The speaker counts seven prominent positions out of twenty-two missions that the Prophet gave Khalid: Mu'tah, the conquest of Mecca, the destruction of al-Uzza, the expedition against Banu Jadhima, Hunayn, Tabuk and Dumat al-Jandal, and the conversion of Banu al-Harith ibn Ka'b at his hands. {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep52 00:04:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep52 00:04:30}
- At Mu'tah the speaker says Khalid had been a Muslim for only "four months, or three" (the transcript gives both). He says the Prophet appointed three commanders so that Khalid would learn to be a soldier under them before he led (the speaker's reading). {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep52 00:05:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep52 00:06:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep52 00:06:30}
- The speaker says the Ghassanids and the Byzantines numbered two hundred thousand against three thousand Muslims, and that the Muslims took refuge in a small village. He says that twelve Muslims were killed, citing Ibn Hisham and al-Raheeq al-Makhtum without quoting them (needs_source). {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep52 00:07:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep52 00:07:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep52 00:08:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep52 00:08:30}
- The speaker says that the three commanders were killed one after another and that [[person/thabit-ibn-aqram|Thabit ibn Aqram]] took the flag and called on Khalid to take it. Khalid said Thabit had the better claim, and Thabit replied that he had taken it only to give it to Khalid. The speaker says that nine swords broke in Khalid's hand that day (the speaker's claim; needs_source). {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep52 00:09:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep52 00:09:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep52 00:10:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep52 00:10:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep51 00:40:30}
- The speaker tells the withdrawal plan: Khalid judged that an immediate retreat would destroy the army, so he changed the positions of the army and the colours of the banners, sent three hundred horsemen to raise dust behind the army so that the enemy would think reinforcements had come, and the army then returned without pursuit (the speaker's account; the numbers given for the units are garbled). {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep52 00:10:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep52 00:11:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep52 00:12:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep52 00:12:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep52 00:13:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep52 00:13:30}
- The speaker says the Prophet described the battle to his companions in Medina: Zayd, Ja'far and Ibn Rawaha were killed, and he saw them in Paradise. He said that a "sword of the swords of God" took the flag, and then told Khalid that he was a sword of the swords of God (as the speaker relates it). {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep52 00:16:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep52 00:17:00}
- The speaker says that at the conquest of Mecca the Prophet sent Khalid at the head of the vanguard with a thousand horsemen of Banu Sulaym; that al-Zubayr led the right wing, Abu Ubayda the left, and Sa'd ibn Ubada led the Ansar (the speaker's account). {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep52 00:17:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep52 00:18:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep52 00:18:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep52 00:19:00}
- The speaker says that al-Abbas held [[person/abu-sufyan-ibn-harb|Abu Sufyan]] back so that he could watch the army pass, and that when Khalid passed, Abu Sufyan asked who he was (as the speaker relates it). {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep52 00:19:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep52 00:20:00}
- The speaker says the Prophet sent Khalid to destroy [[event/demolition-of-al-uzza-and-idols|al-Uzza]], the most important idol of Quraysh. He addressed it with words of scorn and then destroyed it. The speaker says this was the third of the seven missions (the speaker's account; what Khalid said is not written here). {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep52 00:25:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep52 00:26:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep52 00:26:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep52 00:27:00}
- The speaker says that the Prophet sent Khalid to Banu Jadhima after learning that they were preparing to rebel. They said "we have converted", but the word used in the transcript is "we changed religion" (the wording is garbled). Khalid killed some of them. The Prophet raised his hands and said that he was innocent before God of what Khalid had done, and the Companions disagreed (the speaker's account; needs_source). {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep52 00:27:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep52 00:28:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep52 00:28:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep52 00:29:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep52 00:29:30}
- The speaker says that some Companions said Khalid had acted to avenge his uncle, and that the Prophet sent [[person/ali-ibn-abi-talib|Ali]] with blood money to them. The speaker says the Prophet judged that Khalid had acted in haste and had not meant it, and kept him in his army afterwards (the reason for the revenge is garbled in the transcript). {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep52 00:30:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep52 00:30:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep52 00:31:30}
- The speaker says that the Prophet went out to [[event/battle-of-hunayn|Hunayn]] with about twelve thousand Muslims, and that Hawazin came with twenty thousand. He names the Hawazin commander as Awf ibn Malik (the name as the speaker gives it; there is no matching commander of Hawazin on record, and this needs checking). {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep52 00:32:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep52 00:32:30}
- The speaker says the army entered the valley where the enemy lay in ambush, that the ranks broke and were scattered, and that Khalid was in the first group to go down and was wounded many times (the speaker's account). {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep52 00:32:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep52 00:33:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep52 00:33:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep52 00:34:00}
- The speaker says the Prophet called on the Muslims with a small number beside him, and that al-Abbas called the companions of the pledge (the name is given as the speaker has it; "the pledge of Aqaba" is the name in the transcript, and the second name is garbled). The army came back. The speaker gives conflicting figures for those who came back and those present (twelve thousand, and eighteen thousand) (needs_source: conflicting figures). {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep52 00:34:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep52 00:35:00}
- The speaker says Khalid was found unconscious and covered in wounds, and that the Prophet wiped his wounds and he rose. The speaker says the Prophet said that whoever is wounded in God's cause will come on the Day of Judgement with the scent of musk, and that Khalid's whole body was wounded (a saying the speaker cites; needs_source). {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep52 00:35:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep52 00:36:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep52 00:36:30}
- The speaker says the Prophet sent Khalid in [[event/expedition-to-tabuk|the expedition to Tabuk]] with four hundred horsemen to the fortress of [[place/dumat-al-jandal|Dumat al-Jandal]], to bring back its lord, whom the speaker calls [[person/ukaydir-ibn-abd-al-malik|Ukaydir]] (the name is garbled in the transcript and needs checking). The Prophet told him he would find the lord hunting cattle, and that is what happened when Khalid caught him (the speaker's account). {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep52 00:38:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep52 00:38:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep52 00:39:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep52 00:40:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep52 00:40:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep52 00:41:00}
- The speaker says that the Prophet sent Khalid to Banu al-Harith ibn Ka'b four months before the Prophet died, to invite them for three days and then to fight them if they refused. They accepted, and Khalid taught them prayer, the Qur'an and the Sunna. He wrote to the Prophet to tell him so and to ask that he order him back (the speaker's account; needs_source: the length of the months). {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep52 00:41:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep52 00:42:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep52 00:42:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep52 00:43:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep52 00:43:30}
- The speaker says the Prophet replied that Khalid should come back, and that the Prophet died two or three days later (the speaker's account; needs_source). {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep52 00:43:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep52 00:43:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep52 00:48:00}
- The speaker reads out, in substance, Khalid's letter to the Prophet: that Banu al-Harith had accepted Islam, that he had stayed among them for three days inviting them, and that he asks leave to return. The text of the letter is not written here (the sense is given in own words). {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep52 00:46:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep52 00:47:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep52 00:47:30}

## Left out of this episode 52

Not written from episode 52: the passage at 00:26:00 (repetition and very short); the speaker's remarks on Western civilisation and modern weapons from 00:31:00 to 00:31:30, which are a present-day frame left out and referred to review; a present-day frame about how outsiders view Muslims, which appears in the Banu Jadhima passage at 00:28:00 to 00:28:30; that frame was dropped and the incident is told without it; the closing prayer from 00:50:30 to 00:51:00, which carries a present-day political frame; and the letters and comments of the audience from 00:45:30 to 00:50:00.

## Episode 53: the Ridda wars and the eleven armies: Tulayha ibn Khuwaylid, Uyayna ibn Hisn and his repentance, Malik ibn Nuwayra and Khalid, as the speaker and the audience tell it

:::perspectives
- **The speaker on why the tribes followed the claimants (the speaker's view):** he holds that they followed out of tribal loyalty, not after checking their claims, and that the reluctance to admit the truth and turn back from error is one of the causes of loss among people. {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep53 00:06:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep53 00:07:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep53 00:09:00}
- **The speaker on the wisdom of the trial (the speaker's view):** he sees good in what the Muslims suffered in the apostasy: it trained the army, united the ranks and turned them from grief, which he takes as part of God's wisdom in the trial of the community. {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep53 00:13:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep53 00:14:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep53 00:16:00}
:::

- The speaker says the series on [[person/khalid-ibn-al-walid|Khalid ibn al-Walid]] continues here, and that the missions the Prophet gave Khalid in about three years of his company number, by his count, twenty-two or twenty-three. This is his estimate and has not been checked against a source (needs source). {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep53 00:00:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep53 00:01:00}
- The speaker says the Prophet died in the tenth year after the Hijra, that his mission lasted twenty-three years, thirteen in [[place/mecca|Mecca]] and ten in [[place/medina|Medina]], and that he was sixty-three at his death. These are the speaker's figures and his arithmetic (needs source). {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep53 00:04:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep53 00:04:30}
- The speaker says [[person/abu-bakr|Abu Bakr]] was chosen as caliph after the Prophet's death, and that Arabia was shaken in a way the Muslims had not expected: the Arab tribes apostatised and only [[place/medina|Medina]], [[place/mecca|Mecca]] and [[place/taif|Taif]] remained, as he describes it (the speaker's account; the transcript garbles the word for the apostasy, so its known name is used). {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep53 00:05:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep53 00:05:30}
- The speaker describes the forms the apostasy took: some stopped paying zakat, some kept the prayer but withheld part of their duties, and some moved to attack Medina. He names three who claimed prophecy: [[person/tulayha-ibn-khuwaylid|Tulayha ibn Khuwaylid]] at [[event/battle-of-buzakha|Buzakha]], [[person/sajah|Sajah]], and [[person/musaylima|Musaylima]], and says their tribes followed them out of tribal loyalty and not because they had checked the claims (the speaker's view; the transcript gives Tulayha's nisba as al-Azdi in one place and al-Asadi in another, which is not settled here). {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep53 00:05:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep53 00:06:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep53 00:06:30}
- The speaker says the causes of the apostasy were more than one and counts five or six. The first was resentment of [[group/quraysh|Quraysh]] and each clan's wish to lead, and he says the Muslims in Medina were like a small believing island among unbelieving tribes (the speaker's view). {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep53 00:07:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep53 00:07:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep53 00:08:00}
- The speaker tells of a man who said to [[person/tulayha-ibn-khuwaylid|Tulayha ibn Khuwaylid]] that he testified he was a liar, and then said that a liar of Rabi'a was dearer to them than a truthful man who opposed them. The speaker reads this as a sign that loyalty to one's own overrides the truth for many, and calls his listeners not to resist the truth out of fear that yielding would look weak. This is his counsel, and the anecdote is not sourced in the episode (needs source). {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep53 00:08:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep53 00:08:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep53 00:09:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep53 00:09:30}
- The speaker names two more causes: meanness with money and dislike of paying zakat, and the fact that faith had not taken root in the hearts of those who entered Islam in the last two years before the Prophet's death. He cites verses of [[passage/quran-110-1|Surat al-Nasr, verse 1]] and [[passage/quran-110-2|Surat al-Nasr, verse 2]] in this connection; their wording is not written here. {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep53 00:10:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep53 00:11:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep53 00:11:30}
- The speaker names old resentment between the people of the desert and the people of the towns as another cause, the desert people resenting the comfort of the towns (needs source). {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep53 00:12:00}
- The speaker cites a verse, [[passage/quran-2-216|Surat al-Baqara, verse 216]], in this connection, and says that what the Muslims disliked in the apostasy had a side of good. He holds that the wars with the claimants, painful as they were, produced for the community an effect that nothing else would have produced (the speaker's view). {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep53 00:13:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep53 00:14:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep53 00:14:30}
- The speaker holds that the wars against the apostate tribes trained the Muslims before they met Persia and Rome, against whom they had earlier suffered real defeats, and that the military skill of [[person/khalid-ibn-al-walid|Khalid ibn al-Walid]] and the Companions' planning were formed in them (the speaker's view). {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep53 00:14:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep53 00:15:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep53 00:15:30}
- The speaker says the wars occupied the Muslims and kept them from being overwhelmed by grief after the Prophet's death, and united [[group/muhajirun|the Muhajirun]] and [[group/ansar|the Ansar]], the Banu Hashim and other clans of Quraysh. He sees this as part of God's wisdom in the trial (the speaker's view). {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep53 00:16:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep53 00:16:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep53 00:17:30}
- The speaker says [[person/umar-ibn-al-khattab|Umar ibn al-Khattab]] asked [[person/abu-bakr|Abu Bakr]] to leave those who withheld zakat, and that Abu Bakr answered that if they withheld even a tether they used to pay to the Prophet, he would fight them for it. The speaker gives no source and the wording is not reproduced here (needs source). {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep53 00:21:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep53 00:21:30}
- The speaker says Abu Bakr prepared eleven armies, the first under [[person/khalid-ibn-al-walid|Khalid ibn al-Walid]] to [[event/battle-of-buzakha|the battle of Buzakha]], where [[person/tulayha-ibn-khuwaylid|Tulayha ibn Khuwaylid]] was. By his figures Khalid had four thousand men and Tulayha seven thousand (needs source). The commander's name is garbled in the transcript and is written here in its known form. {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep53 00:22:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep53 00:23:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep53 00:23:30}
- The speaker says [[person/ikrima-ibn-abi-jahl|Ikrima ibn Abi Jahl]] led the second army toward [[place/al-yamama|Yamama]] but halted at a distance until Khalid had finished his first task. He says Abu Bakr wanted this reserve force to keep [[person/musaylima|Musaylima]] from moving out against Medina (the speaker's account); parts of this passage are garbled. {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep53 00:24:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep53 00:24:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep53 00:25:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep53 00:25:30}
- The speaker lists the other armies. The third, under [[person/amr-ibn-al-as|Amr ibn al-As]], he says went toward [[place/tabuk|Tabuk]] and [[place/dumat-al-jandal|Dumat al-Jandal]] in another direction, which Khalid had not completed. The fourth, under [[person/shurahbil-ibn-hasana|Shurahbil ibn Hasana]], was a reserve toward Yamama after about a week (his numbering here differs from the armies counted in the earlier part of the episode). The fifth, under [[person/khalid-ibn-said-ibn-al-as|Khalid ibn Sa'id ibn al-As]], went toward Syria. The sixth, under Tarif ibn Hajiz, went east of Medina and Mecca against [[group/hawazin|Hawazin]] and [[group/banu-sulaym|Banu Sulaym]]. The seventh, under [[person/al-ala-ibn-al-hadrami|al-Ala ibn al-Hadrami]], went to Bahrain. The eighth, under [[person/hudhayfa-ibn-mihsan|Hudhayfa ibn Mihsan]], went to [[place/oman|Oman]]. The ninth went to Oman and then to [[place/hadramawt|Hadramawt]], under a commander whose name is garbled. The tenth, under al-Muhajir ibn Abi Umayya, went to [[place/yemen|Yemen]] to finish off the remnants of al-Aswad al-Ansi's followers. The eleventh, under Suwayd ibn Muqarrin, went to the [[place/tihama|Tihama]] coast on the Red Sea as far as Bab al-Mandab. Several names and places are garbled and are read here from the clearer phrases (needs source for the figures and periods; names to be checked). {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep53 00:26:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep53 00:27:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep53 00:28:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep53 00:28:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep53 00:29:00}
- Reading the map, the speaker says the armies set out first from the centre and west of Arabia; Abu Bakr began with the places nearest Medina and widened outward step by step. [[event/battle-of-yamama|the battle of Yamama]] came last because it was the hardest battle, and the speaker says it will have an episode of its own (the speaker's view). {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep53 00:30:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep53 00:30:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep53 00:31:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep53 00:31:30}
- The speaker says [[person/tulayha-ibn-khuwaylid|Tulayha ibn Khuwaylid]] had opposed the Prophet on three occasions before his claim: the first is garbled in the transcript; the second was at the Trench, where he went out with [[group/banu-asad|Banu Asad]], his tribe; the third was at [[event/battle-of-khaybar|Khaybar]], where he volunteered with part of his people alongside the Jews against the Muslims. He says Tulayha claimed prophecy three or four days before the Prophet died (needs source). {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep53 00:32:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep53 00:32:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep53 00:33:00}
- The speaker says [[group/ghatafan|Ghatafan]] and [[group/tayy|Tayy]] had followed Tulayha. Khalid said he feared the moment was passing and that they had to attack; [[person/adi-ibn-hatim|Adi ibn Hatim]] asked to be let speak to the tribes in Tulayha's army, and went in. By the speaker's count two thousand came over and joined Khalid, bringing his army to six thousand against Tulayha's seven thousand (needs source). {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep53 00:34:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep53 00:34:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep53 00:35:00}
- The speaker says Khalid reminded the Muslims of the Prophet to lift their morale. He says [[person/uyayna-ibn-hisn|Uyayna ibn Hisn]] came with [[group/banu-fazara|Banu Fazara]] to help Tulayha, and describes him as a foolish man who was obeyed; his name is garbled in the transcript (the speaker's account). {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep53 00:35:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep53 00:35:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep53 00:36:00}
- The speaker says [[person/tulayha-ibn-khuwaylid|Tulayha ibn Khuwaylid]] fled to [[place/al-sham|Syria]] after his defeat and stayed there about a year. When news reached him that Arabia had returned to Islam, he came back and declared his Islam; [[person/abu-bakr|Abu Bakr]] accepted him reluctantly, the speaker says. In the caliphate of [[person/umar-ibn-al-khattab|Umar ibn al-Khattab]] he joined the campaign for [[place/iraq|Iraq]] and witnessed the battle of [[event/battle-of-nahawand|Nahawand]] (the speaker's account; some details garbled). {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep53 00:37:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep53 00:38:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep53 00:38:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep53 00:39:00}
- The speaker says Khalid captured [[person/uyayna-ibn-hisn|Uyayna ibn Hisn]] and sent him to Medina, where in the speaker's account the children called him an enemy of God. When he was brought before [[person/abu-bakr|Abu Bakr]] he declared his Islam, and Abu Bakr pardoned him; the speaker says he worshipped until his death (the speaker's account; needs source). {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep53 00:41:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep53 00:41:30}
- The speaker reflects on God's mercy toward a sinner who repents, as Tulayha did, and urges sinners not to despair. He says repentance has three conditions: regret for the sin, giving it up, and resolving not to return to it. He cites verses on repentance, [[passage/quran-9-104|Surat al-Tawba, verse 104]], without their wording being written here. The three conditions are his own list and have no source in the episode (needs source). {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep53 00:40:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep53 00:40:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep53 00:42:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep53 00:43:30}
- The speaker recalls that Khalid had killed [[event/ali-sent-to-banu-jadhima|Banu Jadhima]], as the previous episode told, and says Khalid learned from that error: when a man offered to speak to a tribe, he allowed it. He then swept the area around Buzakha for about three weeks, to some sixty miles around, and says [[group/banu-sulaym|Banu Sulaym]] returned to Islam and that Khalid defeated a woman named Salma who had gathered an army to fight the Muslims, all in a run of successive victories by the speaker's account (needs source). {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep53 00:44:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep53 00:45:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep53 00:45:30}
- The speaker says Abu Bakr sent Khalid against [[person/malik-ibn-nuwayra|Malik ibn Nuwayra]] with six thousand men, [[group/muhajirun|the Muhajirun]] and [[group/ansar|the Ansar]] among them. The Ansar objected that they had been told to wait for Abu Bakr's letter. Khalid answered that he was the commander and that the Caliph had ordered him as he was; he said he would go on with the Muhajirun, and the others could do as they pleased. The Ansar then said they would not let the chance pass and went with him. The dialogue is garbled in parts (the speaker's account). {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep53 00:45:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep53 00:46:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep53 00:46:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep53 00:47:00}
- The speaker describes [[person/malik-ibn-nuwayra|Malik ibn Nuwayra]] as a chief of [[group/banu-tamim|Banu Tamim]] with strong influence among them. He says Malik had withheld the zakat, then told his people there was no zakat on them and ordered them to disperse across the land; Khalid pursued them and took Malik captive (the speaker's account; garbled in parts). {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep53 00:47:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep53 00:47:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep53 00:48:00}
- The speaker sets out two accounts of the killing of the captives. In one, Khalid ordered them killed. In the other, he told the guards to hold their captives, a phrase that in the dialect of Kinana means to kill, which Khalid did not know. He says [[person/malik-ibn-nuwayra|Malik ibn Nuwayra]] was among those killed (two accounts, as the speaker gives them; needs source; the transcript once reads Malik ibn Wa'il, taken here to be Malik ibn Nuwayra). {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep53 00:48:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep53 00:49:00}
- The speaker says Umar was angry at the killing of Malik and asked Abu Bakr to dismiss Khalid. Abu Bakr said Khalid had interpreted and erred, and would not dismiss him, saying he could not sheathe a sword that God had drawn against the unbelievers (the speaker's account). {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep53 00:50:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep53 00:50:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep53 00:51:00}
- The speaker says Khalid married Malik's widow after his death, that Umar's anger grew, and that Abu Bakr sent for Khalid and rebuked him. The speaker holds that the marriage was lawful (the speaker's account; needs source; compare episode 54, which gives a different marriage). {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep53 00:51:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep53 00:52:00}

## Left out of this episode 53

Not written from episode 53: the opening at 00:00:00 to 00:00:30; the description of the map at 00:02:30 to 00:04:00, which is garbled; an unsourced explanation at 00:12:30 to 00:13:00; the audience comments at 00:18:00 to 00:19:30, which are outside the subject of the episode, and personal remarks with no source at 00:19:30 to 00:20:30; a general remark with no source at 00:26:30 to 00:27:00; a personal remark at 00:26:00 to 00:26:30; a repetition at 00:36:30 to 00:37:00; a personal comment from the audience at 00:44:00; and the speaker's closing and prayer at 00:52:30 to 00:53:00.

## Episode 54: the battle of Yamama: Musaylima and the Garden of Death, Habib ibn Zayd, the memorisers of the Qur'an, Abu Dujana and Zayd ibn al-Khattab, and the peace with Mujjaa, as the speaker and the audience tell it

:::perspectives
- **The speaker on zeal and reason (the speaker's view):** he calls young people to love the religion and the Prophet with reason and judgment, not with zeal without thought, and sees the story of Ikrima as an example of a zeal that seeks to atone for the past and loses its way. {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep54 00:03:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep54 00:06:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep54 00:06:30}
- **The speaker on what brings victory (the speaker's view):** he holds that victory comes not from courage and numbers alone but from preparing the hearts, remembering God and loving the Prophet. He takes Khalid's order to the army to worship and to recite the Qur'an before battle as proof, and says that faith is what sets the Muslims apart from their opponents in the battle. {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep54 00:14:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep54 00:15:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep54 00:18:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep54 00:33:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep54 00:34:00}
- **The speaker on the peace and bloodshed (the speaker's view):** he says Khalid was not bloodthirsty and that the religion is not a religion of blood, and sees Khalid's keeping of the agreement with Mujjaa as evidence of this. {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep54 00:50:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep54 00:50:30}
:::

- The speaker says the whole episode is about the battle of [[place/al-yamama|Yamama]] against [[person/musaylima|Musaylima]]. He says [[person/ikrima-ibn-abi-jahl|Ikrima ibn Abi Jahl]] was at the head of an army of about two thousand heading for [[place/al-yamama|Yamama]], that [[person/shurahbil-ibn-hasana|Shurahbil ibn Hasana]] followed behind Ikrima but ahead of Khalid, and that Khalid was coming from behind them. (The speaker counts Shurahbil's army as the third here; in episode 53 it was the fourth.) {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep54 00:00:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep54 00:01:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep54 00:02:00}
- The speaker says Ikrima suffered a heavy defeat at the hands of [[group/banu-hanifa|Banu Hanifa]]. Abu Bakr sent him word not to return, lest the people lose heart, and to head to [[place/oman|Oman]] and [[place/hadramawt|Hadramawt]]; Shurahbil was told not to attack until Abu Bakr's letter reached him (the speaker's account; the wording of the letter is garbled). He says it is said that Yamama was the battle in which the most Muslims fell as martyrs (needs source). {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep54 00:03:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep54 00:04:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep54 00:04:30}
- The speaker says [[person/musaylima|Musaylima]] claimed prophecy in the Prophet's lifetime, two or three days or a week before his death (his phrase is garbled; close to the timing the speaker gives for Tulayha in episode 53, three or four days), and that he was with the [[group/banu-hanifa|Banu Hanifa]] delegation in the year of delegations. The delegation entered the mosque to declare its Islam while he stayed outside; he then asked that authority be given to him after the Prophet, and the Prophet, holding something in his hand, said he would not give it to him even if he asked for this. The speaker also tells that the Prophet saw in a dream two gold bracelets on his hands, blew on them and they flew away, and interpreted them as two liars who would claim prophecy: [[person/tulayha-ibn-khuwaylid|Tulayha ibn Khuwaylid]] and [[person/musaylima|Musaylima]] (the speaker's account; needs source). {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep54 00:07:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep54 00:07:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep54 00:08:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep54 00:08:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep54 00:09:00}
- The speaker tells that [[person/musaylima|Musaylima]] wrote to the Prophet a letter that opened by claiming the title of messenger and proposed dividing the land between them. The Prophet replied with a letter addressing him as the liar, and the reply was carried to him by [[person/habib-ibn-zayd|Habib ibn Zayd]], the son of [[person/nusayba-bint-kab|Umm Umara]] (the speaker's account). {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep54 00:09:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep54 00:10:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep54 00:10:30}
- The speaker says [[person/musaylima|Musaylima]] asked [[person/habib-ibn-zayd|Habib ibn Zayd]] to testify that he was a messenger of God. Habib answered by affirming the Prophet's mission, then refused to testify for Musaylima; the transcript repeats his replies in a garbled form, so they are not written here. He says [[person/musaylima|Musaylima]] ordered his hands cut off, one after the other, until he was killed (the speaker's account). {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep54 00:11:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep54 00:11:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep54 00:12:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep54 00:12:30}
- The speaker gives the [[group/banu-hanifa|Banu Hanifa]] as a hundred thousand, of whom forty thousand were fighters, and Khalid's army as thirteen thousand, and says that by rational measures such a force could not do it (needs source). He gives twelve thousand for the Muslims elsewhere in the episode (see below). {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep54 00:13:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep54 00:13:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep54 00:14:00}
- The speaker says Khalid ordered the army that no one should shoot an arrow except while remembering God or in prostration (the speaker's account; needs source). The line-up, he says, was [[person/zayd-ibn-al-khattab|Zayd ibn al-Khattab]] on the right wing, [[person/abu-hudhayfa-ibn-utba|Abu Hudhayfa]] on the left, and Khalid at the centre. {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep54 00:14:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep54 00:15:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep54 00:16:00}
- The speaker says [[person/nusayba-bint-kab|Umm Umara]] went out with the army wanting to reach [[person/musaylima|Musaylima]], who had killed her son. Among those who went out, he names [[person/salim-mawla-abi-hudhayfa|Salim, mawla of Abu Hudhayfa]], [[person/abdullah-ibn-umar|Abdullah ibn Umar]], [[person/abu-dujana|Abu Dujana]], [[person/abd-al-rahman-ibn-abi-bakr|Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Bakr]], and [[person/wahshi-ibn-harb|Wahshi ibn Harb]], who had killed Hamza and, he says, wanted to atone for that through fighting (the speaker's account; the list is garbled in two places). {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep54 00:16:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep54 00:17:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep54 00:17:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep54 00:18:00}
- The speaker gives the Muslim force as twelve thousand, a figure that differs from the thirteen thousand he gave earlier in the episode (to be checked). He says the men were divided into groups each made up of people from different tribes rather than one tribe; the attack began, the Muslims were pushed back, and Musaylima's army reached Khalid's tent (the speaker's account; the text is garbled). {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep54 00:18:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep54 00:19:00}
- The speaker says [[person/mujjaa-ibn-murara|Mujjaa ibn Murara]], one of the leading commanders of [[group/banu-hanifa|Banu Hanifa]], was captured with his group, and that Khalid said: do not kill Mujjaa, keep him for me; he was kept in Khalid's tent. The rest of this account is garbled and is not written (to be checked). {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep54 00:19:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep54 00:20:00}
- The speaker says that the call for the men to be distinguished by their groups and tribes, "so that we know where we are attacked from", changed the course of the battle: the Ansar began to fight together and the Muhajirun together. The transcript does not make clear who gave the call (to be checked). He then says the Muslims called out the name of the Prophet and regrouped, and that Khalid called out one word, the Prophet's name, so the army turned, and the Ansar returned to their ranks (the speaker's account; the text is garbled). {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep54 00:21:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep54 00:22:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep54 00:22:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep54 00:23:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep54 00:23:30}
- The speaker tells, on the authority of [[person/abdullah-ibn-umar|Abdullah ibn Umar]], that he saw a man of the [[group/ansar|the Ansar]] whose right hand was paralysed, who fought with his left hand until he fell, then took up the sword in his left hand and pressed toward the Ansar banner. The speaker says the man said he feared that the Ansar would enter Paradise and he would not be with them. The man's name is not given in the transcript (the speaker's account; the names of some speakers are garbled; needs source). {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep54 00:24:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep54 00:24:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep54 00:25:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep54 00:25:30}
- The speaker says [[person/zayd-ibn-al-khattab|Zayd ibn al-Khattab]] called the people to stand firm and fight, and swore that he would not speak a word until God gave the Muslims victory or he met his Lord; he fell a martyr (the speaker's account). {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep54 00:26:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep54 00:26:30}
- The speaker describes the fighting growing fierce and the dead piling up on both sides, and says a place filled with blood was afterwards called the "ditch of blood" (needs source). He says [[person/ammar-ibn-yasir|Ammar ibn Yasir]] called on the people of the Qur'an after his ear had been cut off, in the account of one who saw him, and that [[person/salim-mawla-abi-hudhayfa|Salim, mawla of Abu Hudhayfa]] led about a thousand memorisers; by his estimate the army reached eleven thousand, with a thousand of them memorisers (to be checked). He also recalls that Ammar's parents, [[person/sumayya-bint-khayyat|Sumayya]] and [[person/yasir-ibn-amir|Yasir]], were martyred in Mecca. {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep54 00:27:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep54 00:27:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep54 00:28:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep54 00:28:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep54 00:29:00}
- The speaker says Khalid called for a single combat, and that [[person/musaylima|Musaylima]] came out warily; the account of the duel itself is garbled and is not written. He then says seven thousand fell at this stage, and that the defeat of the [[group/banu-hanifa|Banu Hanifa]] followed (needs source). {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep54 00:31:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep54 00:32:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep54 00:32:30}
- The speaker describes the garden in which the [[group/banu-hanifa|Banu Hanifa]] took shelter: a large orchard with a wall and a strong gate. He says some thirty thousand of Banu Hanifa went in and closed the gate, and that the Muslims circled it and found no way in (the speaker's account; needs source). {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep54 00:36:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep54 00:37:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep54 00:37:30}
- The speaker says [[person/anas-ibn-malik|Anas ibn Malik]] had a brother, al-Bara ibn Malik, and that the Prophet said of a dishevelled man whom God honours if he swears by Him; the speaker applies this to al-Bara and gives no source for the saying (needs source). He says al-Bara told the Muslims: lift me and throw me among them in the garden, and I will open the gate for you (the speaker's account; needs source). {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep54 00:38:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep54 00:38:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep54 00:39:00}
- The speaker describes al-Bara asking to be lifted on spears and thrown into the garden; he put on iron armour, fought until the gate was opened, and the Muslims entered (the speaker's account; needs source). The details of the fighting at the gate are not written, as the episode gives no source for them. {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep54 00:40:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep54 00:41:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep54 00:41:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep54 00:42:00}
- The speaker says the Muslims entered the garden, which was afterwards called the "Garden of Death", and that some seven thousand of Musaylima's army were killed inside it; he gives thirty thousand as the number who had gone in (the speaker's figures, not checked; to be reviewed). {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep54 00:43:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep54 00:43:30}
- The speaker says three people sought to kill [[person/musaylima|Musaylima]]: [[person/nusayba-bint-kab|Umm Umara]], who wanted revenge for her son; [[person/wahshi-ibn-harb|Wahshi ibn Harb]], who wanted to wipe out what he had done when he killed Hamza; and [[person/abu-dujana|Abu Dujana]] (the speaker's account). {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep54 00:43:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep54 00:44:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep54 00:44:30}
- The speaker says [[person/musaylima|Musaylima]] was killed by a black slave, who was [[person/wahshi-ibn-harb|Wahshi ibn Harb]], the same who had killed Hamza (the speaker's account; needs source). Among the martyrs he names [[person/zayd-ibn-al-khattab|Zayd ibn al-Khattab]], commander of the right wing, [[person/abu-hudhayfa-ibn-utba|Abu Hudhayfa]], commander of the left, and [[person/abu-dujana|Abu Dujana]]. He reports Wahshi's words that with this spear he killed the best of people while a polytheist, and the worst of people as a Muslim (needs source). He says [[person/nusayba-bint-kab|Umm Umara]] rejoiced that God had let her son's killer be killed. {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep54 00:46:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep54 00:46:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep54 00:47:00}
- The speaker says the Muslim dead came to about a thousand, a third of them Muhajirun and a third Ansar, and that about five hundred memorisers were martyred, which he says was the reason the Qur'an was gathered (the speaker's account; needs source; the figures are garbled in two places). At a later point he gives a different figure for the dead on the other side, which does not match the earlier figure (to be checked). {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep54 00:47:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep54 00:48:00}
- The speaker says [[person/mujjaa-ibn-murara|Mujjaa ibn Murara]] offered to negotiate a peace with the people of the forts. The terms, as he gives them, were the release of the captives and that Mujjaa should take a quarter of the treasures of the forts. He says the forts were found empty except for women. Khalid told Mujjaa that he had deceived him, and Mujjaa answered that he had no choice, since these were his own people; Khalid accepted the peace (the speaker's account; some wording is garbled). {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep54 00:48:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep54 00:49:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep54 00:49:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep54 00:50:00}
- The speaker says Mujjaa asked Khalid to marry him to his daughter, and Khalid did.
