Umar and Abu Bakr learned of it; Abu Bakr was angry and wrote to Khalid rebuking him, but did not dismiss him, because he was preparing him for a greater task, the conquest of Iraq and then Syria (the speaker's account; needs source; compare episode 53, which gives a different marriage, to Malik's widow). {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep54 00:50:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep54 00:51:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep54 00:51:30}

## Left out of this episode 54

Not written from episode 54: the speaker's recap of earlier episodes at 00:00:30 to 00:01:30; a garbled passage at 00:02:30; a garbled general remark at 00:05:00 to 00:05:30; an unsourced story about a later figure at 00:15:00 to 00:15:30; a garbled passage at 00:20:30 to 00:21:00; a repetition and a passage outside the subject at 00:30:00 to 00:31:00; audience comments at 00:33:00 to 00:33:30 and at 00:35:00 to 00:36:00; two passages at 00:39:30 and 00:40:30 outside the account; a garbled passage at 00:42:30 to 00:43:00; a dedication at the start of 00:44:00; a repetition at 00:45:00; and the speaker's closing at 00:52:00 to 00:53:00.

## Episode 57: Khalid ibn al-Walid in Syria: the four armies, the desert crossing and the spring, the battle of Yarmuk and the single command, Umar's removal of Khalid, the entry into Damascus and Khalid's death, as the speaker and the audience tell it

:::perspectives
- **The speaker on intention and help (the speaker's view):** he says that God's help comes in measure with the intention of the one who acts, and presents the army's crossing of the desert and its trust as carried by sincere purpose more than by numbers. {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep57 00:12:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep57 00:12:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep57 00:17:30}
- **The speaker on Umar's decision (the speaker's account):** he gives two reasons for Khalid's removal: fear of discord among the Muslims and the wish that the army not depend on one commander. The reasons are his own reading and are not checked against a source. {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep57 00:54:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep57 00:55:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep57 00:55:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep57 00:56:30}
:::

- The speaker opens the Syrian part of the Khalid series, after the Iraq campaign and the battle of [[place/al-yamama|Yamama]], which the earlier episodes have told. He asks viewers to follow the series in order, since each part rests on the one before. {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep57 00:00:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep57 00:01:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep57 00:02:00}
- The speaker says Abu Bakr sent four armies to Syria at once: one to Damascus under [[person/yazid-ibn-abi-sufyan|Yazid ibn Abi Sufyan]] (the transcript writes Zayd, flagged), one under [[person/shurahbil-ibn-hasana|Shurahbil ibn Hasana]], one to Palestine under [[person/amr-ibn-al-as|Amr ibn al-As]], and one to Homs under [[person/abu-ubayda-ibn-al-jarrah|Abu Ubayda ibn al-Jarrah]]. [[person/ikrima-ibn-abi-jahl|Ikrima ibn Abi Jahl]] followed with a small force to guard their rear. {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep57 00:02:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep57 00:02:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep57 00:03:30}
- The speaker gives the commanders' ages and forces. He calls the commander of the second army in his sixties, giving 65 in one line and 60 in another (flagged). He gives 6,000 each for the first two armies, 7,000 for Amr's and 5,000 for Abu Ubayda's, and about 2,000 with Ikrima. The total of about 26,000 is his and needs a source. {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep57 00:02:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep57 00:03:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep57 00:03:30}
- The speaker says Abu Bakr sent the four armies apart so that the Byzantines could not gather against one of them, and that each army on its own achieved little. He says the Byzantine forces were far larger than the Muslims'. {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep57 00:04:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep57 00:05:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep57 00:05:30}
- The speaker reads out a letter from Abu Bakr to Khalid. In his telling it appoints Khalid over the Muslim forces in Syria, tells him to return to Iraq once God grants victory in Syria, and warns him against self-admiration. The wording is not copied here. {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep57 00:07:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep57 00:08:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep57 00:08:30}
- The speaker tells of a dispute over which commanders would go with Khalid from Iraq, and names [[person/al-qaqa-ibn-amr|Qa'qa' ibn Amr]] and [[person/dirar-ibn-al-azwar|Dirar ibn al-Azwar]] (the transcript garbles Dirar's name). A saying that Qa'qa's voice in battle is worth a thousand men is given once as the Prophet's and once as Abu Bakr's; the attribution is unclear and flagged. {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep57 00:09:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep57 00:10:00}
- The speaker describes two routes to Syria: an easy one with water and pasture, which he gives as a month or more in one place and about fifteen days in another (flagged), and a harsh desert road with five days without water. He says Khalid asked the guide [[person/rafi-ibn-umayra|Rafi' ibn Umayra]], who said he had not travelled the desert road for thirty years and warned that it was hard, and that a man carrying much food and water could run out and die. The transcript gives Khalid's call for the quicker road for the people of Syria in one passage and his crossing of the hard road in another; the order is unclear here (flagged). {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep57 00:10:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep57 00:11:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep57 00:11:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep57 00:12:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep57 00:12:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep57 00:13:00}
- The speaker says the army had no water for five days, and that Khalid had about twenty camels kept thirsty and then used the water in them: one was slaughtered so the army could eat, and the water in its stomach given to the other camels. The sequence is garbled in the transcript; the details are the speaker's account and are not checked. {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep57 00:13:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep57 00:14:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep57 00:14:30}
- The speaker says the water would not last beyond three days and gives the army as ten thousand (needs source). After exhaustion set in, Khalid ordered the army to keep silent for a whole day and to say only a short formula of trust in God; the formula is not written here. {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep57 00:15:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep57 00:15:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep57 00:16:00}
- On the fifth day Khalid asked Rafi' ibn Umayra where the spring was. Rafi' said he had come there thirty years earlier as a child with his father and knew the water lay between two palm trees. The speaker says Qa'qa' prayed, two palm trees came into view, and the army dug and found water. {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep57 00:16:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep57 00:16:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep57 00:17:00}
- The speaker says Khalid reached the army before [[person/abu-ubayda-ibn-al-jarrah|Abu Ubayda]], the senior of the four commanders. Khalid told him that had Abu Bakr not put him over Abu Ubayda he would never have taken command, and Abu Ubayda answered that Khalid knew war far better than he did. {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep57 00:18:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep57 00:18:30}
- The speaker calls [[event/battle-of-yarmuk|Yarmuk]] the decisive battle for the Byzantine state in Syria: a Byzantine defeat there would end their rule in the region, and a Muslim defeat would have let the Byzantines advance as far as Medina, he says. {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep57 00:19:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep57 00:19:30}
- The speaker gives the Byzantine host as 240,000 and the Muslim army, once the four armies had joined, as 36,000; he gives no source for these. Elsewhere he gives 42,000 as the Byzantine force at Yarmuk, which conflicts with the first figure (flagged). He places Yarmuk in the south-west of Syria. {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep57 00:20:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep57 00:20:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep57 00:22:00}
- The speaker dates the day to 13 Rajab, giving the year first as 15 and then as 13 AH (flagged). He says Khalid stood before the army and said the day was no place for pride or oppression and that deeds should be for God alone. He proposed that the four commanders take turns, and took the command himself on the first day. {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep57 00:23:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep57 00:23:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep57 00:24:00}
- The speaker lists the arrangement: [[person/amr-ibn-al-as|Amr ibn al-As]] and [[person/shurahbil-ibn-hasana|Shurahbil ibn Hasana]] on the right wing, [[person/yazid-ibn-abi-sufyan|Yazid ibn Abi Sufyan]] on the left, [[person/abu-ubayda-ibn-al-jarrah|Abu Ubayda]] in the centre, and the cavalry under [[person/al-qaqa-ibn-amr|Qa'qa' ibn Amr]] and Dirar ibn al-Azwar. The transcript garbles some names and the order is flagged. {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep57 00:24:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep57 00:25:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep57 00:25:30}
- The speaker says Khalid divided the army into 36 units of a thousand, each under a companion, with those who had fought at Badr given the first place, and arranged so that the men would follow the companions. The numbers are the speaker's and need a source. {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep57 00:25:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep57 00:26:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep57 00:26:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep57 00:27:00}
- The speaker says [[person/al-miqdad-ibn-amr|Miqdad]] (the transcript's form of the name is garbled, flagged) recited aloud a chapter of the Qur'an that he names as al-Anfal, and that Khalid placed a preacher in each unit to rouse the men toward the Hereafter. The verses are not quoted here. {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep57 00:27:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep57 00:28:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep57 00:28:30}
- The speaker says that before the battle a letter from Umar reached Khalid, saying that Abu Bakr had died, removing Khalid and appointing Abu Ubayda. Khalid folded the letter, answered with a formula of obedience, and laughed, the speaker says. The battle had not yet begun. The dates he gives for the battle and for Abu Bakr's death are not checked here. {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep57 00:30:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep57 00:31:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep57 00:31:30}
- The speaker says that at night Khalid went to Abu Ubayda, greeted him as a soldier greets his commander, and offered to serve under him. Abu Ubayda took the command and answered with the formula of obedience, which the speaker presents as proof of Khalid's sincerity. {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep57 00:32:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep57 00:32:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep57 00:33:00}
- The speaker says the two armies faced each other, 240,000 against 36,000 as before. Khalid, now a soldier, came to Abu Ubayda with a plan: the Muslims should give way a little under the first charge, and keep the cavalry back until that charge had spent itself. The sentence about what Khalid fought for is garbled in the transcript and is not written here. {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep57 00:34:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep57 00:34:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep57 00:36:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep57 00:36:30}
- The speaker describes the Byzantine lines advancing with crosses, drums and a great mass of men under black banners, which he likens to clouds that hid the sun. Abu Ubayda appointed Khalid commander of the cavalry, and Khalid raised a black banner, which the speaker says was a gift from the Prophet (needs source; the sentence is garbled). The battle then began. {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep57 00:37:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep57 00:37:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep57 00:38:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep57 00:38:30}
- The speaker says a Byzantine commander named Mihan (the transcript's form) asked to speak with Khalid, and offered each soldier a thousand dinars and a turban if they went home, saying hunger and poverty had driven them out. Khalid's answer is garbled in the transcript and is not written here. {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep57 00:38:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep57 00:39:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep57 00:39:30}
- The speaker says Mihan told Khalid he had heard that a sword had come down from heaven to the Prophet and been given to Khalid, to kill whoever he met. Khalid denied it, saying he had once denied the Messenger, then believed, and that the Prophet prayed that he be a sword of God against the unbelievers. The speaker gives this in his own rendering. {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep57 00:40:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep57 00:41:00}
- The speaker says Mihan's companion, whose name the transcript garbles as Juja, asked what joining Islam requires. Khalid named the testimony of faith, the prayer and fighting alongside the Muslims. The speaker says the man converted, Khalid washed him in his tent, and he went into battle and was killed as a martyr (the speaker's account; needs source). {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep57 00:41:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep57 00:42:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep57 00:42:30}
- The speaker describes a Byzantine advance that drove the Muslims back, and the preachers rallying them. [[person/ikrima-ibn-abi-jahl|Ikrima ibn Abi Jahl]] called for men to pledge themselves to death. The speaker quotes him as saying he had fought the Messenger for years and would not flee now, and says about four hundred men swore to fight to the death (the figure needs a source). {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep57 00:43:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep57 00:44:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep57 00:44:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep57 00:45:00}
- The speaker says the four hundred fought and fell one after another. He tells of Ikrima's cousin, who gave his water to another wounded man, who passed it on, until it reached Ikrima, who had died of thirst. This is the speaker's account; it is not checked and needs a source. {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep57 00:45:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep57 00:46:00}
- The speaker says [[person/zubayr-ibn-al-awwam|al-Zubayr ibn al-Awwam]] broke into the Byzantine lines alone, passed through them and came out on the other side. He names al-Zubayr among the ten promised Paradise. {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep57 00:46:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep57 00:46:30}
- The speaker says the women of the army took tent poles and struck the men who turned to flee, to drive them back. This is the speaker's own account of the women's part. {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep57 00:46:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep57 00:47:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep57 00:47:30}
- The speaker says a masked cavalry rider fought in the midst of the Byzantines, and that Khalid asked who it was. The rider replied that she was [[person/khawla-bint-al-azwar|Khawla bint al-Azwar]], sister of Dirar, and the reason she gives is partly garbled in the transcript. {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep57 00:47:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep57 00:48:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep57 00:48:30}
- The speaker says Abu Sufyan returned to the fighting, calling for God's help, and that the Muslim line held. He says Abu Sufyan lost an eye in the fighting. The transcript does not make clear which Abu Sufyan is meant, the son of Harb or the son of al-Harith (flagged). {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep57 00:49:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep57 00:49:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep57 00:50:00}
- The speaker says Khalid saw the Byzantine lines pressed between the valley, the Yarmuk river and a lake, and opened a gap in the Muslim lines so that the enemy could leave the field. The Byzantines were driven out and Khalid pursued them. The speaker says more than seventy thousand Byzantines fell (needs source). {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep57 00:50:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep57 00:50:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep57 00:51:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep57 00:51:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep57 00:52:00}
- The speaker says the Muslims besieged Damascus, with Abu Ubayda on one side and Khalid on the other. Khalid and Qa'qa' went over the wall with ropes, broke a chain at the gate and entered. The people of Damascus asked Abu Ubayda for terms and he accepted a peace; the transcript reverses the compass points at one place (flagged). {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep57 00:52:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep57 00:52:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep57 00:53:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep57 00:53:30}
- The speaker says Khalid entered by force and Abu Ubayda by treaty. Abu Ubayda told Khalid to stop, and Khalid obeyed. The speaker says that had the fighting gone on, hundreds and thousands would have died, and presents the peaceful entry as God's wish to spare blood. {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep57 00:53:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep57 00:54:00}
- The speaker gives Umar's first reason for removing Khalid as fear of discord among the Muslims, who had begun to say they would not be defeated while Khalid led them. He cites a verse at this point, which is not quoted here. He says Umar wrote to the people that the removal was not for an accusation or a betrayal but out of fear of trouble for the Muslims, and gives Umar's second reason as a wish that the Muslims not depend on one commander. {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep57 00:54:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep57 00:54:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep57 00:55:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep57 00:55:30}
- The speaker says Khalid spent his last four years largely without fighting, in Homs, and that a plague in Syria took about forty of his children and grandchildren in one year (the speaker's figure, needs source). He gives Khalid's age at death as 56 and the year as 22 AH (needs source). He quotes Khalid's words on his deathbed: he had witnessed many battles, no part of his body was without a sword or spear wound, and he was dying in his bed like a camel. He says Umar wept and said that Khalid deserved command and that Abu Bakr knew men better than he did. {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep57 00:56:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep57 00:57:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep57 00:57:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep57 00:58:00}

## Left out of this episode 57

Not written from episode 57: the recap and the opening greetings at 00:00:00 to 00:01:30; passages outside the subject or with a present-day frame at 00:01:00 to 00:01:30, 00:05:30 to 00:07:30, 00:21:30 to 00:22:00, 00:29:30 to 00:30:30, 00:37:00 to 00:37:30 and 00:55:30 to 00:56:00; an advertisement at 00:33:30 to 00:34:00; garbled passages at 00:17:30 to 00:18:00 and 00:30:00 to 00:30:30; and the closing formula from 00:58:30.

## Episode 58: the martyrs of Uhud, first group: Abdullah ibn Haram and his son Jabir, Amr ibn al-Jamuh and his sons, Abdullah ibn Jahsh, Hanzala ibn Abi Amir, Anas ibn al-Nadr, and the burial of the paired martyrs, as the speaker and the audience tell it

:::perspectives
- **The speaker on gentle counsel (the speaker's view):** he says that the sons of Amr ibn al-Jamuh show how to call a father to God, with patience and mercy rather than harshness, and that the same gentleness is needed when a believer speaks to people in general, who must be taken by the hand gently. {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep58 00:19:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep58 00:19:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep58 00:21:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep58 00:21:30}
- **The speaker on the struggle with the self (the speaker's view):** answering an audience question about striving today, he says that the first degree of striving is against one's own desires, that learning and obedience come before any other effort, and that keeping a pledge to God is the measure of sincerity. {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep58 00:35:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep58 00:35:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep58 00:36:00}
:::

- The speaker says this episode takes the martyrs of Uhud together. There were seventy, and he will name about twenty, nine of them as the main subjects. He says the aim is to look at what moved them, not to urge anyone to seek death. {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep58 00:00:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep58 00:01:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep58 00:01:30}
- The speaker names the common motive as Paradise and begins with [[person/abdullah-ibn-amr-ibn-haram|Abdullah ibn Haram]], who, he says, had nine daughters. Jabir, his son, later says his father left seven daughters and debts; the number is flagged as a conflict inside the speaker's account. {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep58 00:02:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep58 00:02:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep58 00:05:00}
- When the lots were cast for the army, [[person/jabir-ibn-abdullah|Jabir]] wanted to go out with his father, and the lot fell to his father. Jabir wept. His father told him that had it been anything other than Paradise, he would have kept him at home. {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep58 00:03:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep58 00:03:30}
- Abdullah ibn Haram told his son that he expected to be the first of the martyrs that day. The speaker says he was indeed the first to fall in the battle, and that for this reason his name is placed first in the list of the martyrs. {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep58 00:03:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep58 00:04:00}
- After the battle Jabir came to the Prophet and asked to look at his father. The companions were reluctant, and the Prophet told them to let him look. The speaker says the body bore many wounds, that the Prophet told Jabir he might weep or not, and that angels were still shading the body with their wings. {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep58 00:04:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep58 00:04:30}
- The speaker tells, without naming a source in the transcript, that the Prophet told Jabir that God speaks to people only from behind a veil but spoke to his father face to face, and asked him for a wish. His father asked to return to the world to fight and be killed again, and was told that the dead do not return. He then asked that his state be told to the people; the speaker gives this account with no source named (needs source). {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep58 00:05:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep58 00:05:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep58 00:06:00}
- The speaker turns to the second martyr, [[person/amr-ibn-al-jamuh|Amr ibn al-Jamuh]]. He says Amr had worshipped an idol named Manat with great devotion, and kept a small idol in his house which he bowed to every morning. The speaker presents this as a long road from idolatry to faith. {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep58 00:06:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep58 00:07:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep58 00:07:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep58 00:08:00}
- The speaker tells how Amr's sons, who had secretly become Muslims, tried to persuade their father by taking the small idol out at night, throwing it into a pit, and later tying a dead dog to its neck and leaving it in a filthy place. Each time Amr washed the idol and went back to it, until he concluded that a thing that could not defend itself did not deserve worship and became a Muslim. The speaker gives this as his own account and it needs a source. {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep58 00:08:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep58 00:09:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep58 00:09:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep58 00:10:00}
- The speaker says Amr's Islam came three or four years before Uhud, and that the change was quick. He adds that the sons' patience with their father is a model for those who call others to God. {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep58 00:10:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep58 00:11:00}
- Amr was old and lame, and his sons tried to keep him from Uhud, since God had lifted fighting from him. He refused, and told them that they had kept him from Paradise at Badr and would not do so now. The Prophet told the sons that God had excused their father, but when Amr asked again, the Prophet allowed him to go out. {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep58 00:11:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep58 00:11:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep58 00:12:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep58 00:12:30}
- Amr went out toward Uhud on his lame leg, saying that he smelled the fragrance of Paradise. The speaker says he stood at Uhud facing Medina and prayed that God would not return him there. {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep58 00:13:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep58 00:13:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep58 00:14:30}
- The speaker reports a saying of the Prophet that he saw Amr ibn al-Jamuh entering Paradise on his lame leg (needs source). Amr's son Khallad fell with him in the same battle. {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep58 00:14:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep58 00:14:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep58 00:15:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep58 00:15:30}
- A rumour spread that the Prophet had been killed. Amr's wife asked about the Prophet first and was told only that her husband had fallen. She would not be satisfied until she saw the Prophet alive, and when she did she said that every calamity after him was small. {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep58 00:15:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep58 00:16:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep58 00:16:30}
- The Prophet stopped the burials until Abdullah ibn Haram and Amr ibn al-Jamuh were found. He had them buried together in one grave, because they had loved each other in this world. The speaker presents this as the Prophet's own act. {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep58 00:17:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep58 00:18:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep58 00:18:30}
- The speaker cites a verse at this point and links it to the example of Amr ibn al-Jamuh's change; the verse is linked, not quoted here. [[passage/quran-13-11|Verse]] {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep58 00:23:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep58 00:24:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep58 00:24:30}
- The speaker introduces the third martyr, [[person/abdullah-ibn-jahsh|Abdullah ibn Jahsh]]. He says Abdullah's mother was [[person/umayma-bint-abd-al-muttalib|Umayma bint Abd al-Muttalib]], a paternal aunt of the Prophet, so that Abdullah was the Prophet's cousin, and that he was the brother of the Prophet's wife Zaynab bint Jahsh. {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep58 00:25:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep58 00:25:30}
- The speaker says Abdullah ibn Jahsh was the first man to whom the Prophet gave a banner in a raid before Badr, and the first to whom a share of the booty was assigned (the speaker's claim; needs source). {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep58 00:26:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep58 00:26:30}
- The speaker tells of the prayers before the battle. [[person/abdullah-ibn-jahsh|Abdullah ibn Jahsh]] proposed to [[person/sad-ibn-muadh|Sa'd ibn Mu'adh]] that each pray while the other said Amen. Sa'd prayed first, asking to meet strong unbelievers and kill them, and Abdullah said Amen. Abdullah then prayed to meet a strong unbeliever who would kill him and cut off his nose and ears, so that God would ask him on the Day of Judgement why, and he would say it was for God. {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep58 00:27:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep58 00:27:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep58 00:28:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep58 00:28:30}
- Sa'd ibn Mu'adh says he saw Abdullah ibn Jahsh killed in the battle, with his nose and ears cut off, and that the prayer was fulfilled. The speaker presents this as Sa'd's own word (needs source). {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep58 00:30:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep58 00:30:30}
- The speaker tells of [[person/hanzala-ibn-abi-amir|Hanzala ibn Abi Amir]], who had married the night before the battle and went out at the call to fight before washing. The speaker says the Prophet saw angels washing him in a golden basin (his account of the saying; needs source), and that Hanzala's wife confirmed he had been with her that night. {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep58 00:31:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep58 00:32:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep58 00:32:30}
- The speaker introduces [[person/anas-ibn-al-nadr|Anas ibn al-Nadr]], whose name the transcript garbles (written here in its established form). He had missed Badr and wished to make up for it, and at Uhud he was outside Medina when the fighting began. {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep58 00:41:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep58 00:41:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep58 00:42:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep58 00:42:30}
- The speaker says that when some companions said the Prophet had been killed and turned back toward Medina, Anas asked them what they would do with life after him, and urged them to stand and die where he had died. {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep58 00:42:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep58 00:43:00}
- The speaker says Anas said he smelled Paradise beyond Uhud. When [[person/sad-ibn-muadh|Sa'd ibn Mu'adh]] asked where he was going, Anas answered that he was going to Paradise and swore by his Lord. The speaker says Sa'd tried to copy him and could not. {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep58 00:44:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep58 00:45:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep58 00:45:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep58 00:46:00}
- The speaker says that Anas was found dead beneath Uhud with eighty wounds (a figure from his account; needs source), and that he was recognised only when his sister knew him by a finger that had been cut. {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep58 00:47:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep58 00:47:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep58 00:48:30}
- The speaker says a verse of the Qur'an was revealed about Anas, and cites it at this point; the verse is linked here and not quoted (the claim about its revelation is the speaker's and needs a source). [[passage/quran-33-23|Verse]] {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep58 00:48:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep58 00:49:00}
- The speaker contrasts keeping a pledge at once with the postponement the devil suggests, saying tomorrow and later, and says scholars hold that the people of Hell feel no pain as sharp as the regret of the word 'later' they spoke in the world (the speaker's citation of scholars, needs source). {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep58 00:50:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep58 00:50:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep58 00:51:00}

## Left out of this episode 58

Not written from episode 58: the opening greetings and the programme's name at 00:00:00 to 00:00:30; audience comments and personal anecdotes at 00:22:00 to 00:22:30, 00:24:00 to 00:24:30, 00:33:30 to 00:34:30, 00:38:30 to 00:40:30 and 00:43:30 to 00:44:30; passages outside the account or with a present-day frame at 00:23:00 to 00:23:30, 00:29:00 to 00:29:30 and 00:46:30 to 00:47:00; garbled or repeated passages at 00:04:30 to 00:05:00, 00:09:00 to 00:09:30, 00:28:00 to 00:28:30 and 00:44:30 to 00:45:00; and the closing formula at 00:52:00.

## Episode 59: the martyrs of Uhud, second group: Sa'd ibn al-Rabi' and his last message, Yazid ibn al-Sakan and the ten Ansar youths, Mus'ab ibn Umayr, Hamza ibn Abd al-Muttalib and his killer Wahshi, and the burial and the remembrance of the martyrs, as the speaker and the audience tell it

:::perspectives
- **The speaker on sincere counsel (the speaker's view):** he holds that giving counsel is a duty even for someone who feels unworthy, that it is best given in private and with kindness, and that the saying he quotes, to convey even one verse, applies to everyone. He quotes that saying without a source in the transcript (needs source). {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep59 00:09:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep59 00:10:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep59 00:11:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep59 00:14:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep59 00:14:30}
- **The speaker on wealth and its test (the speaker's view):** he says wealth is not forbidden in itself, that companions such as Abu Bakr were rich and Uthman equipped an army from his own purse, and that the danger is luxury that turns a person from God. He reads Mus'ab's change as a lesson in patience. {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep59 00:19:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep59 00:19:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep59 00:39:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep59 00:40:00}
:::

- The speaker opens with praise for the Prophet and his companions, and goes on to the martyrs of Uhud, beginning with [[person/sad-ibn-al-rabi|Sa'd ibn al-Rabi']]. {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep59 00:00:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep59 00:00:30}
- The speaker says Sa'd, mortally wounded, said he had not died until he had killed five of the unbelievers, and sent word that he had found what he had been promised. The message reaches the Prophet through a companion, and the transcript's chain of messengers is unclear. {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep59 00:00:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep59 00:01:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep59 00:02:00}
- Sa'd sent word to the Ansar that they had no excuse before God if harm reached the Prophet while one of them still had eyes to blink. The speaker says this saying has lasted fourteen centuries. {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep59 00:02:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep59 00:03:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep59 00:03:30}
- The speaker says the Prophet praised Sa'd for giving counsel to God while alive and dead, and that the story of Sa'd's counsel is the first of the episode's lessons. {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep59 00:03:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep59 00:04:00}
- The speaker says that at Uhud, when the Muslims had scattered and the Prophet was left in the midst of the fighting, he asked who would push the enemy away from him, and Yazid ibn al-Sakan, a young man in his twenties, answered. {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep59 00:04:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep59 00:05:00}
- Yazid stood with ten young Ansar, who fought before the Prophet one after another. The speaker gives the ages of some of them as eighteen, twenty and twenty-two (his figures; needs source). {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep59 00:05:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep59 00:06:00}
- The speaker says the ten were killed one after another before the Prophet, and that Yazid was the last of them to fall. He describes Yazid still fighting after heavy wounds, with blood flowing, until he fell (the speaker's account). {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep59 00:06:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep59 00:07:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep59 00:07:30}
- When Yazid fell, the Prophet took his head onto his thigh and wiped the dust from his face, and said that Yazid had been faithful to his pledge. The speaker reports this as the Prophet's own words. {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep59 00:08:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep59 00:08:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep59 00:09:00}
- The speaker introduces [[person/musab-ibn-umayr|Mus'ab ibn Umayr]], who before Islam was the most elegant young man in Mecca, with fine perfumes and clothes. His mother withheld her support after he converted, confined him and treated him harshly until he managed to escape. {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep59 00:16:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep59 00:17:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep59 00:17:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep59 00:18:00}
- After his escape Mus'ab lived in poverty. The speaker says he wore rough clothing and lived a hard life until the battle of Uhud. {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep59 00:18:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep59 00:18:30}
- The Prophet gave Mus'ab the banner at Uhud. The speaker says an enemy struck his right hand, and he took the banner in his left; when that hand was also cut, he held the banner against his chest until he fell (the speaker's account, partly garbled). {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep59 00:20:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep59 00:20:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep59 00:21:00}
- The transcript names the man who killed Mus'ab as Ibn Qami'a, but that wording is garbled, so the name is flagged and not confirmed. The speaker says Mus'ab held the banner until he died, having given up everything for what he called the greater aim, Islam. {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep59 00:21:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep59 00:24:30}
- The speaker says Mus'ab's shroud was too short: when it covered his head, his feet showed, and when it covered his feet, his head showed. He says the Prophet stood over him and wept. {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep59 00:22:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep59 00:22:30}
- The speaker gives the Prophet's words over Mus'ab: that he had seen him in Mecca, that no youth there had finer clothes, and that he gave everything up for God and His Messenger. The speaker presents this as the Prophet's recollection (needs source). {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep59 00:23:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep59 00:23:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep59 00:24:00}
- The speaker says the ninth martyr is [[person/hamza|Hamza ibn Abd al-Muttalib]], the Prophet's uncle, and that the episode will tell only of his death, since his life needs one or two more episodes. {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep59 00:25:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep59 00:25:30}
- The speaker says Hamza led the army in the field at Uhud and walked among the ranks in a proud manner, and that the Prophet is reported to have said that God and His Messenger dislike that walk except when it is shown against the enemy (the speaker's report; needs source). {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep59 00:25:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep59 00:26:00}
- The speaker says Hamza killed five standard-bearers of the enemy that day (his figure; needs source), and that each time an enemy banner was taken up, another man took it and was killed. {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep59 00:27:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep59 00:27:30}
- The speaker says [[person/wahshi-ibn-harb|Wahshi ibn Harb]] went out with the Quraysh army to kill Hamza, having been promised his freedom by [[person/hind-bint-utba|Hind bint Utba]] and Jubayr ibn Mut'im if he did so (the speaker's account). {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep59 00:27:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep59 00:28:00}
- Wahshi, as the speaker gives his account after he became a Muslim, says he did not confront Hamza face to face. He hid behind a rock and waited, because he could not strike him except by ambush, and then threw his spear at close range, and Hamza fell. The details are Wahshi's own words as the speaker gives them, and the transcript is partly garbled. {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep59 00:28:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep59 00:29:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep59 00:30:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep59 00:31:00}
- The speaker says the Prophet wept over Hamza more than over any other martyr, and said that Hamza had no one to weep for him. The Ansar then sent their women to weep for Hamza, and when the Prophet woke and asked whether they were still weeping, they said yes, out of grief for Hamza. {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep59 00:33:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep59 00:34:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep59 00:34:30}
- The speaker lists the martyrs he has covered: [[person/abdullah-ibn-amr-ibn-haram|Abdullah ibn Haram]], [[person/amr-ibn-al-jamuh|Amr ibn al-Jamuh]], [[person/abdullah-ibn-jahsh|Abdullah ibn Jahsh]], [[person/hanzala-ibn-abi-amir|Hanzala ibn Abi Amir]], [[person/anas-ibn-al-nadr|Anas ibn al-Nadr]], [[person/sad-ibn-al-rabi|Sa'd ibn al-Rabi']], Yazid ibn al-Sakan, [[person/musab-ibn-umayr|Mus'ab ibn Umayr]] and [[person/hamza|Hamza]]. {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep59 00:35:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep59 00:35:30}
- The speaker says the Prophet had the martyrs buried in pairs, in one grave for each pair. He says [[person/abdullah-ibn-jahsh|Abdullah ibn Jahsh]] was buried together with Hamza (the transcript's wording at this point is partly garbled, flagged), and [[person/amr-ibn-al-jamuh|Amr ibn al-Jamuh]] with [[person/abdullah-ibn-amr-ibn-haram|Abdullah ibn Haram]], because they had loved each other. {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep59 00:35:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep59 00:36:00}
- The speaker tells of a companion's son, not named in the transcript, who said that about twenty years later a flood in Medina led the governor to call for graves to be moved. He went to his father's grave by its marker and found the body as it had been; the hand that was moved back under the cheek stopped the flow of blood from the wound. This is the speaker's account and needs a source. {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep59 00:36:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep59 00:36:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep59 00:37:00}
- The speaker reports a saying that the souls of the martyrs are in the crops of green birds in Paradise, that they eat of its fruits and rest in lamps of gold beneath the Throne, and that when they found the goodness of their food and drink they asked who would tell their brothers they were alive, and God said He would. The speaker cites a verse at this point; the verse is linked and not quoted here. The saying is given without a source (needs source). [[passage/quran-3-169|Verse]] {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep59 00:37:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep59 00:38:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep59 00:38:30}
- The speaker says he wanted to speak next about [[person/nusayba-bint-kab|Umm Umara Nusayba bint Ka'b]], a woman who stood out that day, but he first invites the audience's comments on each martyr, and the episode ends before her story. {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep59 00:39:00}

## Left out of this episode 59

Not written from episode 59: the audience's remarks and the speaker's questions at 00:09:30 to 00:10:00 beyond the point used above; a personal family example and audience remarks at 00:12:30 to 00:13:30; passages with a present-day frame at 00:20:00 to 00:20:30, 00:26:00 to 00:26:30 and 00:29:30 to 00:30:00; garbled passages at 00:23:30 to 00:24:00 (partly used), 00:36:30 to 00:37:00 and 00:40:00 to 00:40:30; an audience comment at 00:41:00 to 00:41:30; and the closing supplication and formula from 00:41:30 onward.

## Episode 60: Salman al-Farisi: the fire-keeper of Isfahan who became a Christian, the chain of teachers from Syria to Mosul to Nisibis to Amorium, the dying scholar's signs of the coming prophet, the betrayal and slavery, the palm trees between the two harra, the three tests at Quba, the mukataba of three hundred palms and forty uqiyya, the trench, and the amir of al-Mada'in, as the speaker and the audience tell it

- The speaker opens by hoping the companions' stories become practice, not just tales, then introduces [[person/salman-al-farisi|Salman al-Farisi]], originally from Isfahan in the middle of Persia, and frames the whole episode as the question of how much a person can give over years to reach the truth (his words). {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep60 00:00:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep60 00:01:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep60 00:01:30}
- Salman tells his own conversion story, says the speaker, first to the Prophet and later to Ibn Abbas: his father was the dihqan, the lord and chief of the village and its richest man, who loved him so much he kept him in the house like a servant girl for fear of harm (the speaker's narration of Salman's account). {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep60 00:02:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep60 00:02:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep60 00:03:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep60 00:03:30}
- He was devoted to Magianism until they made him custodian of the fire itself, keeper of the temple, while his father owned an estate; the speaker stresses the comfort and status Salman left behind (the speaker's narration). {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep60 00:04:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep60 00:04:30}
- One day, sent on an errand, he passed a church and heard the Christians praying; he liked their worship and stayed till evening, asked where the religion's origin was and was told Syria; he joined a caravan there and attached himself to the bishop's service — only to discover the man stole the charity he collected, hoarding seven chests of gold and silver which Salman saw buried under him when he died (the speaker's narration). {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep60 00:15:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep60 00:16:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep60 00:16:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep60 00:17:00}
- The next teacher, a righteous man, taught him until his own death approached; asked whom to go to, he said no one on earth remained on the truth except a man in [[place/mosul|Mosul]]. From Mosul the dying teacher sent him to Nisibis, and from Nisibis to a man in [[place/amorium|Amorium]] in the land of the Romans — each time serving, worshipping and learning for years until the teacher died (the speaker's narration; the years are his emphasis). {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep60 00:17:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep60 00:20:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep60 00:21:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep60 00:22:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep60 00:23:00}
- In Amorium he worked and acquired some cows and sheep; at the last teacher's death there was no one left to send him to, but the teacher told him the time of the final prophet had come: he would appear in the land of the Arabs, follow Abraham's creed, and emigrate to a land of palms between two harra (lava tracts); his signs — he eats gifts but not charity, and between his shoulders is the seal of prophethood (the speaker's narration). {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep60 00:23:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep60 00:24:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep60 00:24:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep60 00:25:00}
- Unable to reach Arabia alone, he paid Arab traders at Amorium his cows and sheep to carry him; on the road they betrayed and sold him as a slave to a Jewish man in [[place/wadi-al-qura|Wadi al-Qura]], between Syria and Medina; a cousin from Yathrib bought him and took him to his town — and entering it Salman saw the palms filling the place, walked out and found the two harra, and wept and trembled that he had arrived (the speaker's narration). {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep60 00:25:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep60 00:27:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep60 00:28:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep60 00:29:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep60 00:29:30}
- The Prophet migrated and reached [[place/quba|Quba]] while Salman was on top of a palm tree; his master's companion said "may God kill Banu Qayla — they are gathering at Quba around a man from Mecca who claims prophethood"; Salman trembled till he nearly fell, came down, was struck by his master and sent back to work, then took dates at evening to Quba (the speaker's narration). {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep60 00:32:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep60 00:32:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep60 00:33:00}
- He offered the dates as charity; the Prophet told his companions to eat but did not extend his own hand — sign one. Days later he brought dates as a gift; the Prophet ate and fed his companions — sign two. He followed the Prophet to a funeral at al-Baqi', trying to see the seal between his shoulders through the cloak; the Prophet understood, smiled and uncovered his back, and Salman saw the seal and fell on it kissing it and weeping (the speaker's narration; the seal's description at 00:35:00 is left in summary). {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep60 00:33:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep60 00:34:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep60 00:34:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep60 00:35:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep60 00:36:00}
- Salman could not attend Badr or Uhud because he was owned; the Prophet told him "write a mukataba, Salman"; his master set it at three hundred palm trees and forty uqiyya of gold — meant to defeat him. The Prophet told the companions "help your brother with palms", and they brought saplings till three hundred were gathered; the Prophet planted them with his own hands and not one died; then he gave Salman a gold nugget from one of his expeditions that weighed exactly forty uqiyya, and Salman was freed (the speaker's narration; the figures are the speaker's, needs_source). {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep60 00:43:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep60 00:43:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep60 00:44:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep60 00:44:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep60 00:45:00}
- The Prophet's first act after his freedom was to pair him in brotherhood with [[person/abu-al-darda|Abu al-Darda]]; then came the [[event/battle-of-the-trench|Trench]] — Salman proposed the Persian device of digging a ditch, since Medina could only be entered from the north, the other sides closed by the two harra and the heights (the speaker's narration). {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep60 00:45:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep60 00:45:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep60 00:46:00}
- While the companions could not break a rock in the trench, the Prophet struck it and a great spark flew, and he proclaimed "God is greatest — Persia has been conquered"; Salman the Persian heard it and believed (the speaker's narration; the exact wording is his). {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep60 00:46:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep60 00:47:00}
- In Umar's caliphate Salman marched with the conquering armies back to his homeland; entering [[place/al-madain|al-Mada'in]] he wept, remembering the Prophet's words at the rock; Umar appointed him amir of al-Mada'in — the boy who left as a lord's son returned as ruler after years (the speaker's narration). {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep60 00:47:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep60 00:48:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep60 00:48:30}
- At his first sermon in al-Mada'in the crowd waited for stories; he recited the whole of sura Yusuf and the people began leaving, disappointed it was "only the Qur'an"; when he finished he told them: you came to hear tales, and when the Qur'an was recited you turned away — staying for it was the first duty (the speaker's narration). {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep60 00:49:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep60 00:49:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep60 00:50:00}
- Salman married late; he sent Abu al-Darda to ask for a woman of Banu Layth, and her father answered: Salman I do not want — but you I want for my daughter; Abu al-Darda refused to propose over his brother's errand, returned embarrassed, and Salman smiled and quoted the verse of brethren on couches with no rancour between them — "that is me and you, Abu al-Darda" (the speaker's narration of the anecdote; needs_source). {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep60 00:50:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep60 00:51:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep60 00:51:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep60 00:52:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep60 00:52:30}
- He died in Uthman's caliphate, which the speaker dates to 36 AH; Uthman had removed him from the amirate of al-Mada'in and he returned to live in Medina near the Prophet's mosque (the speaker's date, needs_source). {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep60 00:53:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep60 00:53:30}
- The speaker's running exhortation through the episode is sacrifice for the truth: a boy of fourteen in the audience, asked for the lesson, says Salman strove until he reached it; the speaker repeats that reaching God after hardship tastes sweet, and that the road that seems harmful — slavery — may be God's way of carrying a person to his goal (his exhortation). {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep60 00:28:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep60 00:36:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep60 00:42:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep60 00:54:00}

## Left out of this episode 60

Not written from episode 60: the opening greeting and programme announcements at 00:00:00 to 00:01:00 in summary only; the "Madarat al-Ahdath" promo at 00:19:00 to 00:20:00; repetition loops at 00:14:00 to 00:15:00 and elsewhere; the description of the seal of prophethood at 00:35:00 kept in summary; garbled lines at 00:04:00 to 00:05:00 (his father's estate) and 00:09:30 to 00:14:30 (the Syria journey detail and the dishonest bishop's confrontation, used in summary only); exhortation passages at 00:26:00 to 00:27:00, 00:30:00 to 00:32:00 and 00:37:00 to 00:43:00 summarised; and the closing formula from 00:54:30.

## Episode 61: Fatima, the Prophet's youngest daughter: the daughters of the Prophet and the honouring of girls, her names and kunyas and her likeness to the Prophet, her childhood in the boycott and her care for her father, her marriage to Ali and the house beside the mosque, the servant and the tasbih, Abu Turab, the Prophet's death and her own death six months later, as the speaker and the audience tell it

- The episode opens with the programme's contest-winner announcements (left out) and the plan for the remaining episodes, then takes up the Prophet's eight children: seven by [[person/khadija|Khadija]] — al-Qasim, Abdullah and al-Tahir (or al-Tayyib, the speaker notes the disagreement), and four daughters, [[person/fatima|Fatima]], [[person/ruqayya-bint-muhammad|Ruqayya]], [[person/umm-kulthum-bint-muhammad|Umm Kulthum]] and [[person/zaynab-bint-muhammad|Zaynab]] — and Ibrahim by Maria the Copt; the boys all died young and the daughters lived (the speaker's narration). {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep61 00:02:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep61 00:03:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep61 00:04:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep61 00:04:30}
- The speaker spends the first minutes on the honouring of daughters: the Qur'an's description of the man's face darkening at the news of a girl, the Prophet's saying that whoever brings up three daughters with care earns Paradise (and the companions asked "even two?" — he said even two, and they felt he would have said one), attributed to Bukhari by the speaker (his narration; verse described not quoted). {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep61 00:05:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep61 00:06:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep61 00:06:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep61 00:07:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep61 00:07:30}
- Fatima was born five years before the Prophet's mission, in the year the Arabs rebuilt the Ka'ba, in the house where the Prophet had married Khadija; she became Muslim at about five — the youngest Muslim, says the speaker — at the moment the Prophet publicly called the family: "Banu Hashim, save yourselves from the Fire... Fatima bint Muhammad, save yourself from the Fire, for I own nothing for you before God" (the speaker's narration; the birth-year dating is his). {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep61 00:09:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep61 00:10:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep61 00:10:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep61 00:28:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep61 00:28:30}
- Her name is from al-fitam, weaning — weaned off faults and sins; her kunyas and titles as the audience names them: al-Zahra (for her whiteness touched with red, or because she was the zahra, the flower, of the Prophet's life), al-Batul (for a worship resembling Mary's, says the speaker), al-Tahira, Umm al-Hasan wal-Husayn, and Umm Abiha — "her father's mother" — for how she cared for him after Khadija's death (the speaker's and audience's list). {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep61 00:11:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep61 00:12:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep61 00:12:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep61 00:13:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep61 00:14:00}
- The speaker lists the marks of her standing: "Fatima is a part of me; whoever angers her has angered me" (he attributes to Bukhari), al-Tabarani's saying that the Prophet, Fatima, Hasan and Husayn will sit together on the day of judgement until the reckoning ends, and that on that day every prophet cries "myself, myself" while the Prophet says he asks not for himself but for Fatima his daughter (the speaker's narration of the hadiths; wording not transcribed, needs_source). {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep61 00:14:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep61 00:15:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep61 00:15:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep61 00:16:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep61 00:16:30}
- When she entered he would stand for her, take her hand and kiss it; coming back from a journey his last call was on her; Aisha said she saw no one more like the Prophet in manner and conduct, nor a more truthful person than Fatima; and in eighteen years of the Prophet's nine marriages not a word of gossip is reported from her (the speaker's narration of Aisha's testimony and his own remark). {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep61 00:16:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep61 00:17:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep61 00:17:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep61 00:21:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep61 00:21:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep61 00:22:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep61 00:23:00}
- Her suffering matched: her mother died when she was sixteen or ten by the speaker's two figures (he gives ten at one point and sixteen at another, flagged); she saw her father stoned and slandered; at seven she was the little girl who lifted the camel's offal off his back weeping while Quraysh watched, and he told her "do not weep, little daughter, God will aid your father"; she lived the three-year boycott in the ravine of Abu Talib from thirteen to sixteen eating leaves (the speaker's narration). {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep61 00:24:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep61 00:30:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep61 00:30:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep61 00:31:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep61 00:31:30}
- Two or three months after the boycott ended Khadija died; the sixteen-year-old said she did not know whether to grieve the separation or rejoice that Jibril had greeted Khadija and promised her a house of qasab in Paradise with no noise or toil (the speaker's narration). {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep61 00:32:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep61 00:33:00}
- After Khadija and Abu Talib died and abuse intensified, Fatima attached herself to her father, walking behind him wherever he went; she also saw her sister Ruqayya emigrate with Uthman (the speaker's narration). {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep61 00:33:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep61 00:34:00}
- Ali came to the Prophet to ask for Fatima and sat before him unable to speak; asked "have you come seeking Fatima?", he said yes; the Prophet provided her simple trousseau and held a wedding feast with the Ansar invited (the speaker's narration of the proposal scene). {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep61 00:36:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep61 00:38:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep61 00:38:30}
- The Prophet wanted her near: [[person/haritha-ibn-al-numan|Haritha ibn al-Nu'man]], a wealthy Ansari who owned the surrounding property, gave up his houses so she lived beside the Prophet's own rooms (the speaker's narration). {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep61 00:43:00}
- When housework and the handmill wore her hands, Ali sent her to ask the Prophet for a servant; she was too shy to ask; the Prophet came to them at night, sat between them, took their hands and said "shall I tell you of better than a servant? — when you go to your bed say subhan Allah thirty-three, al-hamdulillah thirty-three and Allahu akbar thirty-four" (the speaker's narration of the tasbih). {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep61 00:45:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep61 00:46:30}
- The speaker tells the house's life warmly: the laughter overheard — each claiming to be the elder, the Prophet settling that Ali was older by five years; the quarrel after which Ali slept angry in the mosque and the Prophet wiped the dust off him saying "rise, Abu Turab"; and the crisis when Ali considered marrying the daughter of Abu Jahl — the Prophet ascended the minbar and said he did not forbid the lawful, but the daughter of God's enemy could not share a house with the daughter of God's prophet, and if Ali wanted to marry her he should first divorce Fatima; Ali returned and asked her pardon and she forgave (the speaker's narration; the Abu Jahl episode is a contested report in the sources, flagged needs_source). {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep61 00:48:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep61 00:48:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep61 00:49:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep61 00:50:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep61 00:50:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep61 00:51:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep61 00:51:30}
- Their children as the speaker lists them: al-Hasan, al-Husayn, al-Muhsin who died before birth, and Umm Kulthum (his list; other children are not named in the episode, needs_source). Ali wanted to name the boys Harb; the Prophet suggested al-Hasan, then al-Husayn, then named the third al-Muhsin — and the speaker draws the lesson that war is not the root in Islam (his remark). {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep61 00:52:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep61 00:52:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep61 00:53:00}
- At the Prophet's final illness she came in weeping; he could not rise to kiss her, drew her close, whispered and she wept harder; whispered again and she laughed — she told Aisha afterward: the first time he said "I am dying tonight", and when he saw her tears he said she would be the first of his family to join him and the sayyida of the women of Paradise; and on the last day he told her, sweating, "no sorrow upon your father after today" (the speaker's narration of Aisha's account). {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep61 00:53:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep61 00:54:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep61 00:54:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep61 00:55:00}
- At the Prophet's death she stood saying only: "O father, he answered his Lord who called him; O father, the Garden of Firdaws is his shelter; O father, to Jibril we announce him"; and to Anas ibn Malik coming from the burial she said "were your souls pleased to pour earth on the Prophet's face?", and he looked at her with sorrow and she wept and went (the speaker's narration). {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep61 00:55:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep61 00:56:00}
- Her two instructions to Ali before she died: marry [[person/umama-bint-abi-al-as|Umama]], her sister's daughter, for she would be kindest to al-Hasan and al-Husayn; and bury her at night, well covered, for she was shy of people even in death (the speaker's narration). {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep61 00:56:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep61 00:57:00}
- She died at twenty-nine, six months after the Prophet, on a date the speaker gives as the thirteenth of Ramadan, and was buried at night in al-Baqi'; Ali wept and said the days had not wearied him as his two companions — Ahmad and Fatima — had in two successive months (the speaker's narration; the date and the wording are his, needs_source). {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep61 00:57:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep61 00:58:00}

## Left out of this episode 61

Not written from episode 61: the contest-winner names and addresses at 00:01:00 to 00:02:30; the series-plan remarks at 00:03:00 to 00:03:30; the audience's daughters'-order exchange at 00:04:00 to 00:05:00 in summary; repetition loops at 00:05:30, 00:40:00 to 00:41:00 and 00:49:30 (a long stalled segment); exhortation passages on women, hijab and the audience's remarks at 00:20:00 to 00:21:00, 00:33:30 to 00:36:30, 00:39:00 to 00:43:00 summarised; garbled lines at 00:34:00 and 00:47:00 to 00:48:00; and the closing formula from 00:58:30.

## Episode 62: a standalone episode on loving the Prophet: the hadith of loving him more than oneself, Umar's answer, the Pool and "my ummah, my ummah", the woman of Uhud and Abu Dajana, the journey to Ta'if, the last sermon, the death in Aisha's chamber and the companions' grief, and four practices for loving him, as the speaker tells it

- This is not a companion biography but a single-theme episode; the speaker asks whether the Prophet is truly the dearest person to each listener — dearer than children, money, self — and frames the whole lecture on the hadith "none of you believes until I am dearer to him than his family, his children, himself and his wealth", which he glosses as "no one's faith is complete" (the speaker's narration and gloss). {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep62 00:00:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep62 00:01:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep62 00:01:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep62 00:02:00}
- He tells the scene of the Prophet holding [[person/umar-ibn-al-khattab|Umar]]'s hand on a walk: Umar said "by God I love you, Messenger of God"; the Prophet asked "more than your son? — yes; more than your family? — yes; more than yourself? — no"; the Prophet answered "no, Umar — your faith is not complete until I am dearer to you than yourself"; Umar went out, reflected, returned and said "now you are dearer to me than myself", and the Prophet said "now, Umar" (the speaker's narration). {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep62 00:02:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep62 00:03:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep62 00:03:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep62 00:04:00}
- Abdullah ibn Umar, the teller, asked his father what he did in that moment; Umar said he asked himself whom he needed more — himself or the Messenger — and found he needed the Messenger more, because the Messenger could intercede for him while he could do nothing for the Messenger (the speaker's narration). {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep62 00:04:30}
- The speaker then paints the Prophet's love for his ummah at the Pool on the day of judgement: every prophet will cry "myself, myself" while this prophet calls "my ummah, my ummah"; he will recognise his own and give them to drink with his own hands, and when some are turned away he will say "they are of my ummah" and be told "you do not know what they did after you" (the speaker's narration of the hadith picture). {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep62 00:05:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep62 00:05:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep62 00:06:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep62 00:06:30}
- He takes the verse "and your Lord shall give you and you shall be satisfied" as the most reassuring verse, reading in it that the Prophet will not be content while one of his ummah remains in the Fire (the speaker's own reading; the verse is described, not written). {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep62 00:07:00}
- For the companions' love he tells the woman who lost father, husband and son or brother at Uhud — told three times of each death she answered "what of the Messenger of God?", and seeing him safe said "every calamity after you is small"; and Abu Dajana shielding the Prophet with his own back at Uhud till the arrows stuck in it (the speaker's narration; the woman's name is not given, needs_source). {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep62 00:07:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep62 00:08:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep62 00:08:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep62 00:09:00}
- The cost of his mission, to show how dear he was: Abu Talib and Khadija died in the same year — the outer shield and the inner comfort both removed at the height of the crisis, as though God were saying "you have no one but Me" (the speaker's reading). {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep62 00:17:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep62 00:17:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep62 00:18:00}
- Then the [[event/journey-to-taif|journey to Ta'if]], aged about fifty, on foot for what the speaker calls a hundred kilometres: the three leaders' replies (one mocked, one said he would not believe him hanging on the Ka'ba's cloth, one said if he is a true prophet he is too great to speak to and if a liar too low); the streets lined in two rows of stone-throwers; [[person/zayd-ibn-haritha|Zayd]] shielding him with his own body until the Prophet's feet ran with blood (the speaker's narration; the distance is his). {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep62 00:18:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep62 00:19:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep62 00:19:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep62 00:20:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep62 00:20:30}
- In the orchard refuge his prayer is quoted in part: "God, to You I complain of the weakness of my strength, the littleness of my means and my lowliness before men... if You are not angry with me I do not care"; the Angel of the Mountains offered to close the two mountains upon them, and he answered "no — perhaps God will bring out of their loins those who worship God alone" (the speaker's narration of the hadith; wording as he gives it). {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep62 00:23:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep62 00:23:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep62 00:24:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep62 00:24:30}
- The last days: after the farewell pilgrimage the verse "today I have completed your religion" was sent down and Abu Bakr wept, saying it was the Prophet's obituary; nine days before the death the last verse came down ("fear a day in which you return to God"); the Prophet visited the martyrs of Uhud and greeted them — "you are the forerunners and we, God willing, are following"; and when he said "I long for my brothers" he meant those who would believe without seeing him (the speaker's narration; verses described not quoted). {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep62 00:25:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep62 00:25:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep62 00:26:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep62 00:26:30}
- Three days before the end, in [[person/maymuna-bint-al-harith|Maymuna]]'s house, he gathered the wives and asked their leave to be nursed in [[person/aisha|Aisha]]'s room; [[person/ali-ibn-abi-talib|Ali]] and al-Fadl ibn al-Abbas carried him between them, his feet dragging (the speaker's narration). {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep62 00:27:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep62 00:27:30}
- From the chamber Aisha heard him repeating "there is no god but God — death has agonies"; when the mosque filled he asked to be carried, was poured seven waterskins to revive him, and gave the last sermon from the minbar: "your meeting with me is not this world — your meeting is at the Pool, and I see it from where I stand"; "it is not poverty I fear for you, but the world, that you compete for it as those before you did and it destroys you as it destroyed them"; "God, God, in the prayer"; "fear God concerning women"; and "a servant God gave the choice between this world and what is with Him chose what is with Him" — which only Abu Bakr understood, and he wept aloud, the first to break the silence of the Prophet's sermons, crying "we ransom you with our fathers, our mothers, our children, our wives, our wealth" (the speaker's narration). {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep62 00:28:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep62 00:28:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep62 00:29:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep62 00:29:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep62 00:30:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep62 00:30:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep62 00:31:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep62 00:31:30}
- The Prophet came down and defended Abu Bakr: "leave Abu Bakr — no one had a favour with me I did not repay except him; I could not repay him, so I left his repayment to God", and ordered every door into the mosque closed except Abu Bakr's; then came the last supplications and the last charge: "convey my peace to whoever follows me of my ummah until the day of judgement" (the speaker's narration). {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep62 00:31:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep62 00:32:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep62 00:32:30}
- Back in the chamber, [[person/abd-al-rahman-ibn-abi-bakr|Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Bakr]] held a siwak; the Prophet looked at it, Aisha understood, took it, softened it and gave it to him — and she counted it God's favour that the last thing to enter his mouth was from her saliva; Fatima entered, he could not rise, she wept at his two whispers and laughed at the second as told above (the speaker's narration of Aisha's account). {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep62 00:33:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep62 00:33:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep62 00:34:00}
