- He asked the others to leave, drew Aisha near, laid his head on her chest, fixed his eyes upward and said "rather the Highest Companion"; Jibril announced the Angel of Death at the door asking leave — he had asked leave of no one before — and the Angel offered the choice between remaining and joining God; he chose the Highest Companion three times; the Angel said at his head "out, soul of Muhammad ibn Abdullah, to God's mercy and pleasure and a Lord not wrathful"; his hand fell and his head grew heavy on Aisha's chest (the speaker's narration of the death account). {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep62 00:34:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep62 00:35:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep62 00:35:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep62 00:36:00}
- Aisha opened her door on the mosque crying "the Messenger of God is dead" and the mosque burst into weeping: Ali could not stand, Uthman sat dumbfounded, Umar raised his sword and swore to kill whoever said he had died, saying he had gone to his Lord as Moses had; Abu Bakr alone held firm — he entered, embraced the Prophet, kissed him and said "sweet in life and sweet in death", then went out: "whoever worshipped Muhammad, Muhammad has died; whoever worships God, God is alive and does not die" — and the sword fell from Umar's hand, who then went to find a place to weep alone (the speaker's narration). {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep62 00:36:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep62 00:36:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep62 00:37:00}
- At the burial Fatima asked "were your souls pleased to pour earth on the Prophet's face?" and stood announcing his death in her three phrases; the speaker closes with four practices for loving him: much salat upon him, visiting his city, following his sunna, and studying his sira (the speaker's closing exhortation). {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep62 00:37:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep62 00:38:00}

## Left out of this episode 62

Not written from episode 62: the opening greeting and frame at 00:00:00 in summary only; exhortation passages on imitation and celebrities at 00:21:00 to 00:23:00; repetition loops at 00:09:30 to 00:16:30 (audience exchanges and the Abu Dajana scene retold, used once), 00:23:30 (a stalled segment) and elsewhere; the speaker's present-day comparisons; and the closing formula at 00:38:00.

## Episode 63: a standalone episode on trust and certainty in God: the Yemen parable of how certainty grows, believing in the unseen, the creation-signs verses, the fire and the knife and the whale as servants of God, Moses's "no — my Lord is with me", the water from the rock and the child cast into the river, the dead raised by the dead, Umar's prayer for a share of certainty, the Prophet and Abu Bakr in the cave, Adi ibn Hatim's certainty, Abu al-Darda's unburned house, and the maid and the kite-bird, as the speaker tells it

- A thematic episode, not a companion biography. It opens on Ramadan night 28 with an exhortation to spend the last half-hour before the final breaking of the fast in worship — "the moment the workers collect their wages" — then states the subject: trust (thiqa) and certainty (yaqin) in God, the spirit of the whole series' theme of faith (the speaker's framing). {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep63 00:00:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep63 00:01:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep63 00:02:30}
- He distinguishes inherited trust — learnt at school that God is able — from lived certainty, through the Yemen parable: a man tells you of a country you never heard of (little trust), shows you a photograph (more), a documentary (more), buys you a ticket (more), and once you walk its streets a million people could not convince you it does not exist; certainty in God grows the same way, through worship, answered prayers and reflection on creation (the speaker's parable). {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep63 00:04:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep63 00:05:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep63 00:06:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep63 00:07:00}
- The opening of al-Baqara describes the righteous as those who believe in the unseen — trust before seeing — while other verses call on the heedless to look: the keys of the unseen are His alone, He knows what is in land and sea, and not a leaf falls without His knowledge (the speaker's narration; verses described, not written). {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep63 00:07:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep63 00:08:30}
- To teach that the laws of the world are God's servants, he strings together the scenes: the fire does not burn Abraham — asked at the end of his life for his finest days, Abraham says the days in the fire; the knife does not cut at the sacrifice and Ishmael says "press hard, father"; the whale is commanded not to digest Jonah and keeps him so he can glorify God, then is commanded to cast him on the shore — fire, knife and whale all servants of God, so why should you alone refuse (the speaker's narration and exhortation). {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep63 00:15:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep63 00:16:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep63 00:16:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep63 00:17:00}
- At the sea, with Pharaoh closing in and the people saying "we are overtaken", Moses answers "no — my Lord is with me and He will guide me"; the speaker notes that Moses did not know what would happen — that is what makes it certainty (the speaker's narration; the words are the hadith's). {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep63 00:18:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep63 00:19:00}
- The People of the Cave are his next proof that laws bend for believers: the sun inclines away from their cave at its rising and passing at its setting, the laws of the cosmos rearranged for a handful of young men (the speaker's narration; the verse described). {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep63 00:20:00}
- God brings the thing out of its opposite: during a drought, asked to pray for rain, Moses is told instead to strike the dry rock with his staff — the thing least likely to hold water — and twelve springs burst out for the twelve tribes, enough for seventy thousand (the speaker's narration; the figure is his, needs_source). {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep63 00:20:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep63 00:21:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep63 00:23:00}
- And rescue out of destruction: Pharaoh kills every newborn, so Moses's mother is inspired — not revelation, says the speaker, but an inner prompting — "if you fear for him, cast him into the river"; the river itself is God's servant, carries the chest and sets it down before Pharaoh's house, and Pharaoh's wife pleads "a comfort to my eye and yours — do not kill him" (the speaker's narration; the verses described). {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep63 00:23:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep63 00:24:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep63 00:25:00}
- He answers the objection that one should still go to the doctor: go, but know where the trust lies; people queue around the clock for a doctor they trust, yet do not give the Lord of the worlds the trust they give a man (his exhortation). {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep63 00:25:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep63 00:26:00}
- God raises the dead by the dead: in the story of the cow, a murdered man among the Children of Israel, the killer unknown, they are commanded to strike the corpse with a piece of the slaughtered cow and the dead man rises to name his killer — a lesson for a people who, says the speaker, only believed what they held in their hands (the speaker's narration; the verses described). {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep63 00:26:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep63 00:27:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep63 00:27:30}
- He returns to the mother whose child dies: had the boy lived he might have died with no one to pray for him; dying, he moves his mother to a lifetime of hajj, umra, charity and prayer that reaches him in his grave and carries both into Paradise — read the strange act as mercy, he says, and hold your trust (the speaker's narration and exhortation). {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep63 00:28:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep63 00:29:00}
- The Prophet's own certainty: Umar's oft-repeated prayer asks for "a share of Your awe that bars us from disobeying You, of Your obedience that brings us to Your Garden, and of certainty such that the calamities of this world grow light upon us"; and in the cave of Thawr, with the pursuers standing at the mouth, Abu Bakr says "if one of them but looks down at his feet he will see us", and the Prophet answers "Abu Bakr, what do you think of two whose third is God?" (the speaker's narration of the two reports). {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep63 00:29:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep63 00:30:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep63 00:30:30}
- Certainty that God will honour the religion: Adi ibn Hatim al-Ta'i, son of the famed generous chief, comes to Medina while the Muslims are weak and poor; the Prophet greets him "become Muslim, Adi, and be safe"; Adi says he has a religion; the Prophet answers "I know your religion better than you — are you not of the Rakusiyya? do you not take a quarter of your people's spoils?", then names what truly holds him back — "you say we are weak, poor, defeated" — and foretells the woman travelling alone from al-Hira to circle the House fearing none but God, the treasures of Kisra opened, and wealth till no one takes it; Adi testifies on the spot, and lived to see two of the three, awaiting the third as promised (the speaker's narration of the hadith). {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep63 00:31:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep63 00:32:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep63 00:32:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep63 00:33:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep63 00:34:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep63 00:34:30}
- Abu al-Darda's certainty: a man meets him on the road crying "your house is burning"; he answers "it is not burned"; the man swears it is and he repeats "it is not burned"; he returns to find every house burned except his, and explains: the Prophet taught us a prayer said morning and evening after which no harm befalls — he had said it and trusted the Prophet's word (the speaker's narration; the hadith is in Bukhari per the speaker, needs_source on the exact collection). {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep63 00:35:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep63 00:35:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep63 00:36:00}
- And the simplest certainty: a plain woman kept visiting Aisha and swearing "by Him who returned the lunch, by Him who returned the quilt"; asked, she told how she served a household, a kite-bird snatched the food she had made, she was accused of theft, beaten and taken to have her hand cut, and she called out "O succour of the beseeching, my hope and trust are in You that You will not lose me" — and the bird dropped the bundle back (the speaker's narration; the collection cited is his, needs_source). He closes: read the Qur'an much and worship much to grow certainty (his exhortation). {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep63 00:36:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep63 00:36:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep63 00:37:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep63 00:37:30}

## Left out of this episode 63

Not written from episode 63: the Ramadan-night exhortation and the last-half-hour image at 00:00:00 to 00:02:30 used in summary only; repetition loops throughout; the audience exchanges; the Yemen-parable elaboration at 00:04:30 to 00:07:30 summarised; the marriage/haram-wealth examples at 00:21:30 to 00:23:00 summarised; the "afraid woman" audience address at 00:18:30; heavily repeated filler lines flagged by the transcript; and the closing formula at 00:37:30.

## Episode 64: a standalone episode on God's love for His servants: the announcement to Jibril and the people of heaven, "whoever is hostile to a friend of Mine", drawing near through the nawafil, more merciful than a mother, the walking-and-hastening hadith, the heavens like a ring in the desert, the nightly descent, the names of mercy, Khadija's greeting, Ubayy weeping "did my Lord name me?", Abdullah ibn Haram addressed without a veil, and the practical signs that God loves you, as the speaker tells it

- A thematic episode built on reversing the usual direction: everyone teaches "love God", no one tells you how much God loves you; know it, says the speaker, and worship turns from routine and fear into love answering love — the root of the relationship is love, not dread (the speaker's framing). {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep64 00:00:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep64 00:01:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep64 00:01:30}
- First proof: the hadith that when God loves a servant He calls Jibril — "I love so-and-so, so love him" — Jibril calls out to the people of heaven "God loves so-and-so, so love him", they love him, and acceptance is then placed for him on earth; a person may hide his love for someone out of shyness, but God announces His by name before the whole universe (the speaker's narration of the hadith). {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep64 00:02:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep64 00:03:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep64 00:04:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep64 00:04:30}
- Second: the sacred hadith "whoever is hostile to a friend of Mine, I declare war on him"; the friends of God, per the verse he cites, are simply those who believe and have taqwa — not a remote rank; and the hadith continues: nothing draws a servant nearer to God than what He made obligatory, and the servant keeps drawing near with voluntary works until God loves him — then He becomes his hearing, his sight, his hand and his foot, and if he asks He gives and if he seeks refuge He shelters (the speaker's narration of the qudsi hadith; the verse described). {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep64 00:05:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep64 00:06:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep64 00:06:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep64 00:07:30}
- More merciful than parents: the Prophet saw a mother clutching her child in frantic tenderness and asked the companions "do you think this woman would throw her child into the fire?"; they said no; he said "God is more merciful to you than this mother to her child" — and Ali carried it further: were my judgment given to my father and mother I would be safe, for God is more merciful to me than they (the speaker's narration; Ali's remark as he reports it, needs_source). {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep64 00:08:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep64 00:08:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep64 00:09:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep64 00:10:30}
- The arithmetic of approach: "whoever draws near to Me a span, I draw near to him a cubit; whoever draws near a cubit, I draw near a fathom; whoever comes to Me walking, I come to him hastening" — the speaker dwells on the direction: the smaller, weaker party takes a step and the Lord hastens (the speaker's narration of the hadith, with his own note that no likeness is intended). {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep64 00:11:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep64 00:11:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep64 00:12:00}
- And the scale hadith — the first heaven in the second like a ring thrown in a desert, and so to the seventh, and the seventh to the Throne like a ring in a desert, and the Throne to the Kursi likewise, and the Kursi to God as nothing compared to His majesty — yet this Lord descends every night to the lowest heaven calling "who calls on Me that I may answer, who asks of Me that I may give, who seeks My forgiveness that I may forgive?" (the speaker's narration of both hadiths; the cosmic-scale wording as he gives it, needs_source). {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep64 00:12:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep64 00:12:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep64 00:13:30}
- He created your father with His two hands — the verse's rebuke to Iblis — breathed of His spirit into him, expelled your enemy Iblis from the Garden for refusing to prostrate to you, made the angels prostrate to him, prepared the Garden for you and set the angels to greet you there (the speaker's narration; verses described). {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep64 00:14:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep64 00:14:30}
- The counting of deeds is itself love: a good deed is written tenfold, up to seven hundredfold; a bad deed only as one; a coin of charity God takes in His right hand and rears for its giver as one rears a foal until it comes on the day of judgement like a mountain; and of fasting alone He says in the qudsi hadith "every deed of the son of Adam is his except fasting — it is Mine and I reward for it" (the speaker's narration of the hadiths). {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep64 00:15:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep64 00:15:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep64 00:16:00}
- He quotes at length the qudsi hadith "I and men and jinn are in a tremendous affair: I create and others are worshipped, I provide and others are thanked... the people of My remembrance are the people of My company; whoever wishes to sit with Me, let him remember Me... if they turn back to Me I am their beloved, and if they refuse I am their physician, I afflict them with trials to purify them of faults... whoever comes to Me repentant I meet from afar, and whoever turns away I call from near: where do you go — have you a lord besides Me?" (the speaker's narration; wording as he recites it, needs_source). {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep64 00:16:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep64 00:17:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep64 00:17:30}
- Every sura of the Qur'an opens "in the name of God, the Merciful, the Compassionate" — not "the Irresistible, the Avenger"; and in the most beautiful names, the names of power are many, the names of wrath only three by his count — al-Jabbar, al-Muntaqim, al-Qahhar — while the names of mercy overflow: al-Rahman, al-Rahim, al-Ghafur, al-Shakur, al-Latif, al-Sabur, al-Tawwab and al-Wadud, "the one who tenders affection to His servants"; written above the Throne is "My mercy precedes My wrath" (the speaker's narration; the name-list and the written sentence are his, needs_source). {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep64 00:17:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep64 00:18:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep64 00:18:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep64 00:19:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep64 00:19:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep64 00:20:00}
- What that love does to a person: Khadija, standing by the Prophet in her one great stance, receives Jibril descending from heaven solely to tell the Prophet "convey to Khadija God's greeting of peace — and give her the good news of a palace of qasab in the Garden, with no noise and no toil"; so that the earth might know of God's love for her, says the speaker (the speaker's narration). {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep64 00:20:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep64 00:20:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep64 00:21:00}
- And Ubayy ibn Ka'b: when sura al-Bayyina came down, the Prophet summoned him — "God has commanded me to recite it to you"; Ubayy wept and asked "did my Lord name me?"; told yes, he went on weeping "I am the one my Lord named" (the speaker's narration of the report). {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep64 00:21:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep64 00:21:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep64 00:22:00}
- And Abdullah ibn Haram, Jabir's father: father of nine daughters, he cast lots with his son over who would march to Uhud; martyred, he was told the glad news — the Prophet informed Jabir that God had spoken to no one except from behind a veil, but spoke to his father directly, saying "ask of Me, My servant"; he asked only to be sent back to be killed again in God's way for the sweetness of martyrdom he had tasted, and was told it was decreed they do not return (the speaker's narration of the hadith). {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep64 00:22:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep64 00:23:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep64 00:23:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep64 00:24:00}
- Even the gathering the listener sits in: when people gather to remember God the angels surround them and shade them with their wings from earth to heaven, and God says "bear witness, My angels, that I have forgiven them" (the speaker's narration of the hadith, applied to the audience). {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep64 00:24:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep64 00:25:00}
- To the objection "if He loves us, why are we afflicted?", he answers that affliction can itself be love: the servant who will not turn to God is shaken until he does, "your breaking is from love"; the dying child whose mother's lifetime of worship carries both to Paradise; "He does not afflict you except to cleanse you" — none of which lessens the grief, he notes, but places it (the speaker's argument and narration). {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep64 00:25:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep64 00:26:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep64 00:27:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep64 00:28:00}
- The practical signs that God loves you, as he lists them: first, being turned to religion at all — "God gives the world to whom He loves and whom He does not, but He gives religion only to whom He loves"; second, obedience made easy — a friend proposing a mosque, an umra ticket arriving unlooked-for; third, sin made hard — the youth who says "why can my friends do it and my father holds me back? — that is God loving you" (the speaker's narration and applications). {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep64 00:28:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep64 00:28:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep64 00:29:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep64 00:30:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep64 00:31:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep64 00:32:00}

## Left out of this episode 64

Not written from episode 64: the opening supplication at 00:00:00 in summary only; audience exchanges throughout; the "mother and the fire" elaboration at 00:08:30 to 00:10:30 summarised; the camel/mercy side-comment at 00:10:30; repetition loops at 00:17:00 and elsewhere; the stalled fill lines at 00:30:00 and 00:32:00 (long runs of repeated words in the transcript, flagged garbled); and the closing from 00:32:30.

## Episode 65: a standalone episode from the "school of imagination": al-Harith ibn Asad al-Muhasibi's circle that pictured the last day, the trumpet and the rising of the graves, the families who hold hands and the families who flee each other, the long standing, the sun brought near and the sweat, the seven under God's shade walked one by one, the prophets' "myself, myself" and the Prophet's "I am for it", and the reckoning beginning, as the speaker tells it

- A thematic episode, not a companion biography. It opens with two deaths the speaker heard of — a fifteen-year-old who prayed taraweeh and died at home, and a woman from the programme — as a reminder to ask for a good ending, then introduces its method: the "school of imagination" of al-Harith ibn Asad al-Muhasibi, a scholar of the third Hijri century who, watching Muslims grow absorbed in material life, gathered men and women weekly to picture scenes of the last day until, says the speaker, thousands returned to God; the method and the book al-Tawahhum are presented as the speaker reports them (needs_source). {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep65 00:00:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep65 00:01:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep65 00:01:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep65 00:02:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep65 00:03:00}
- The exercise begins with the trumpet: dust gathering into bone, flesh and blood returning, one blast reconstituting a person after millennia; graves splitting open and billions rising crying one word — "myself, myself"; the risen coming out barefoot and dust-covered, family members emerging side by side yet no one embracing, for "the day a man flees his brother, his mother, his father, his wife and his children" (the speaker's imagined scene on the hadiths and verses, described not written). {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep65 00:04:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep65 00:05:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep65 00:06:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep65 00:07:00}
- But the standing holds mercy as well as dread: the picture of a family still holding hands while everyone else scatters — a couple or friends who loved each other in God — against the verse that "the close friends that day will be enemies to each other, except the God-fearing"; his application: gather your household on obedience now so you come out of the graves together (the speaker's narration and exhortation). {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep65 00:07:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep65 00:08:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep65 00:09:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep65 00:10:00}
- The gathered crowds differ: some barefoot and unclothed as the Prophet described, some gathered on their faces — asked "do they walk on their faces?" he answered "He who made them walk on feet is able to make them walk on their faces"; the arrogant gathered the size of ants in the form of men, trampled, abasement covering them — the husband arrogant to his wife, the mistress to her servant; while others come ringed in light like the moon, their light running before them and at their right hands (the speaker's narration of the hadiths and verses). {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep65 00:15:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep65 00:16:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep65 00:17:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep65 00:18:00}
- Then the sun draws near and the sweat begins, each person to the measure of his deeds: to the ankles of some, the knees of some, the waist of some, and some bridled by sweat — a bit over the mouth so they cannot open it (the speaker's narration of the hadith, explaining the image). {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep65 00:18:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep65 00:19:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep65 00:20:00}
- While all stand thus, a caller announces the seven whom God shades in His shade the day there is no shade but His, and the speaker walks the categories as names called out one by one: a just ruler; a youth raised in the worship of God — the daughter who delayed her religion "till she is older" rebuking the mother who delayed her; two people who loved each other in God, meeting and parting upon it; a man whose heart is attached to the mosques; a man invited by a woman of rank and beauty who said "I fear God" (the speaker's narration of the hadith, with his own dramatised asides; the order is his). {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep65 00:20:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep65 00:21:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep65 00:22:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep65 00:23:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep65 00:24:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep65 00:25:30}
- Sixth, a man who remembered God in private and his eyes overflowed — "in private" meaning alone in your room or alone in a crowd with your heart on God; and seventh, deliberately held last because anyone can do it that night: a man who gives charity and conceals it until his left hand does not know what his right hand spent — leave the studio, find a poor man, give and hide it, he says, and you have secured the shade (the speaker's narration and application; the reordering is his own). {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep65 00:26:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep65 00:27:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep65 00:28:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep65 00:29:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep65 00:30:00}
- The standing stretches on till exhausted humanity — the same humanity, he notes, that said it needed no God — cries "where is our Lord to judge us, even into the Fire?"; they seek someone to intercede that the reckoning begin: to Adam — "myself, myself, my Lord is angry today with an anger the like of which He never had"; to Abraham — the same; to Moses — the same; to Jesus — the same; until they come to Muhammad, the seal of the prophets, who says "I am for it, I am for it" (the speaker's narration of the hadith, noting he is paraphrasing it plainly). {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep65 00:31:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep65 00:32:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep65 00:33:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep65 00:34:00}
- The Prophet prostrates beneath the Throne and praises God with a praise no one before him had been taught; it is said to him "raise your head — ask and you will be given, intercede and your intercession will be accepted"; he asks that the reckoning begin, and the reckoning begins for the honour of the Messenger — and the speaker closes with a long supplication for shade on that day, summarised only here (the speaker's narration and closing dua). {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep65 00:34:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep65 00:35:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep65 00:35:30}

## Left out of this episode 65

Not written from episode 65: the opening greeting and the two death announcements at 00:00:00 to 00:01:00 used only to set the frame; the dramatised dialogues with the audience throughout (a mother and daughter, a young man, each "stay standing" exchange) summarised in-line; the anecdote of the group he told the seven to at 00:30:30 to 00:31:30; the long closing supplication at 00:36:00 to 00:38:00 summarised in one clause; repetition loops and stalled lines flagged in the transcript; and the closing formula at 00:38:00.

## Episode 66: the school of imagination continued: the cistern is set up and the first meeting with the Prophet, those turned away "away, away", the clothing of the resurrected, Hell brought out on display with its seventy thousand reins, all the nations kneeling and the Prophet's "my ummah, my ummah", the three God does not look at, the six rules of the reckoning, and the proofs of God's love that close the episode, as the speaker and the audience tell it

- A thematic episode resuming last night's exercise: after the Prophet's intercession secures the start of the reckoning, three things happen before the account itself — the Prophet's cistern is set up, the resurrection-bare are clothed, and Hell is paraded (the speaker's framing of the hadiths). {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep66 00:02:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep66 00:02:30}
- The cistern: whiter than milk, sweeter than honey, its cups like the stars of the sky, the Prophet's minbar stands on it; he recognises his own by the traces of wudu' and calls "my ummah, my ummah" and gives them to drink with his own hand — a drink after which they never thirst again; and the second meeting imagined as joy on his face (the speaker's narration). {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep66 00:02:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep66 00:03:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep66 00:04:00}
- The reverse imagined too: one driven back by the angels while he cries "they are of my ummah" and is told "you do not know what they did after you", and he says "away, away — far, far"; the speaker names the remembered sins each might hear at that moment (the speaker's narration of the hadith and his dramatised asides). {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep66 00:05:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep66 00:05:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep66 00:06:00}
- The clothing: Abraham is dressed first, then the Prophet, then people each to the measure of his deeds — the hadith of the shirts, one to the thigh, one to the navel, and Umar ibn al-Khattab seen trailing his shirt; the speaker imagines the wait of the unclothed while others are dressed, and the woman whose covering in this world decides her delay (the speaker's narration of the hadith). {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep66 00:07:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep66 00:07:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep66 00:08:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep66 00:09:00}
- Then Hell is brought for display — not yet for punishment, says the speaker, but so the gathered know what awaits — drawn by seventy thousand reins, each rein held by seventy thousand angels, which he computes as nearly five billion angels; it sees them from afar and they hear its fury and moaning; its sparks thrown up like palaces (the speaker's narration of the hadiths and verses, described not written; the multiplication is his). {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep66 00:10:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep66 00:11:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep66 00:12:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep66 00:13:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep66 00:14:30}
- All the nations fall to their knees around it — "you will see every nation kneeling", which he notes is why the sura is named al-Jathiya; every prophet says "my Lord, safety", and only Muhammad says "my Lord, my ummah, my ummah" (the speaker's narration; the verses described). {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep66 00:15:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep66 00:16:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep66 00:17:00}
- Before the account he reads the hadith of the three God does not look at nor purify, and for them is a painful torment: the one insolent to his parents — the youth who raises his voice at his mother, the daughter who wrongs her family behind their backs, "righteousness is entering houses by their doors"; the woman who takes on men's ways (al-mutarajjila); and the dayyuth who sees indecency in his household and is not moved (the speaker's narration; the middle term glossed as the hadith's wording). {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep66 00:24:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep66 00:25:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep66 00:26:30}
- The reckoning itself is governed by six rules as he counts them, beginning with "no wronging today" — whoever does an atom's weight of good sees it and whoever does an atom's weight of evil sees it, not even the naqir on a date-stone wronged (the speaker's narration; the rest of the rules are taken in summary; the verses described). {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep66 00:28:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep66 00:29:00}
- He pauses mid-episode to urge reading on the hereafter — the only subject, he notes, given four sessions in the month — naming al-Muhasibi's Kitab al-Tawahhum, al-Ghazali's section on the standings of the day of judgement in the Revival's fourth quarter, and "the journey of eternity" books found in Mecca and Medina stalls (the speaker's recommendations; exact titles as he gives them, needs_source). {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep66 00:27:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep66 00:27:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep66 00:28:00}
- The second half returns to last night's proofs of God's love, now with the audience answering: affliction that cleanses till a believer walks the earth with no sin; the man whose prayer is answered despite himself; the contented heart as a sign; and Abu Hurayra's account — his mother who would not accept Islam and hurt him, the Prophet's prayer "God, guide Abu Hurayra's mother", her testimony behind the door, and the second prayer that God make him and his mother beloved to the believers and the believers beloved to them — "no believer heard of me that day without loving me", which he ties to "then acceptance is placed for him on earth" (the speaker's narration with guests' remarks). {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep66 00:50:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep66 00:52:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep66 00:52:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep66 00:53:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep66 00:54:00}
- The closing examples of love: Khadija's greeting by Jibril; Abu Bakr told through revelation "God is pleased with you — are you pleased with Him?"; Ubayy ibn Ka'b's "did my Lord name me?"; the servant God draws near on that day, covers with His light and asks "do you remember this sin?", who thinks himself lost until He says "I concealed it for you in the world and I forgive it today — enter My Garden"; and the call in Paradise "My servant, wish and desire" and "so-and-so, I am pleased with you — are you pleased with Me?" (the speaker's narration of the hadiths; the Abu Bakr wording as he gives it, needs_source). He ends with a long supplication for God's pleasure at the meeting, summarised only (the speaker's closing dua). {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep66 00:55:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep66 00:56:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep66 00:57:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep66 00:57:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep66 00:58:00}

## Left out of this episode 66

Not written from episode 66: the recap of episode 65 at 00:00:00 to 00:02:00 in summary only; the dramatised audience exchanges throughout; the hijab dramatisations at 00:06:00 to 00:09:30 summarised; the car-incident anecdote at 00:26:00; the remaining rules of the reckoning at 00:29:00 to 00:50:00 taken in summary (the transcript segment is repetitive and partly garbled); the guests' stories in full; the closing supplication at 00:58:30 to 01:00:00 summarised; and the sign-off at 01:00:00.

## Episode 68: a standalone episode on khushu' in the prayer: the man told "go back and pray, for you have not prayed", settling into each posture, the ablution that lets the sins drip away, facing the qibla with the heart too, what Allahu akbar means, the God who turns away when you turn away, the Fatiha dialogue "My servant praised Me", Umar ibn Abd al-Aziz pausing for the answer, bowing and prostration and the tashahhud, and the three ways people recite, as the speaker tells it

- A thematic episode opening with a Ramadan-day-12 check — is the early zeal still there, is the neck freed from the Fire yet — then taking up the question listeners ask most: how do I attain khushu' in the prayer; the speaker builds the "prescription" step by step through the prayer itself (the speaker's framing). {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep68 00:00:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep68 00:01:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep68 00:02:00}
- First, how hard it is: the man who entered the mosque and prayed quickly, greeted the Prophet and was told "go back and pray, for you have not prayed" — three times — until he said "by Him who sent you with the truth, I know no better than this, so teach me"; the Prophet taught him: rise, say the takbir, recite what is easy of the Qur'an, then bow until you are settled bowing, rise until you stand straight, prostrate until you are settled prostrating, sit until you are settled sitting — and so through the whole prayer (the speaker's narration of the hadith, dwelling on the word "settled" like particles settling in a shaken bottle). {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep68 00:02:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep68 00:03:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep68 00:04:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep68 00:04:30}
- Before the takbir, the wudu': the hadith that when a servant washes his face the sins leave with the water till they come out from under the eyelashes, and so the hands, the head and ears, and the feet till the sins come out from under the toenails — agree with yourself, he says, to recall this hadith at every ablution (the speaker's narration; "the hadith is sound" is his judgement). {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep68 00:30:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep68 00:31:00}
- Then the body faces the qibla and the heart must face it too — it is not right that the body looks toward the House while the heart turns its back (the speaker's exhortation). {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep68 00:31:30}
- The takbir: Allahu akbar means "I am entering Your presence — nothing is greater than You in my heart or my life, not my children, not my money"; the audience member who wept at the takbir because he found he could not honestly make God the greatest thing as he entered — his money and work were greater; and God chose this word for every transition, says the speaker, to rebuke the wandering heart (the speaker's narration and the guest's testimony). {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep68 00:32:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep68 00:33:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep68 00:33:30}
- You are in an audience with God; He faces you as long as you face Him, and the moment you turn away He turns away — "do you leave Me for something else? is there anything better than Me?"; a king would not tolerate such inattention, yet He only turns as you turn (the speaker's narration of the hadith's meaning). {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep68 00:34:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep68 00:35:00}
- Recite the Fatiha feeling each address — the praise, the mercy, the Master of the day of judgement, "You alone we worship", the plea for the straight path — for this prayer is a dialogue: the qudsi hadith that when the servant says "praise be to God, Lord of the worlds" God says "My servant praised Me", at "the Merciful, the Compassionate" He says "My servant lauded Me", at "Master of the day of judgement" "My servant glorified Me", and at "You alone we worship and You alone we ask for help" "this is between Me and My servant" (the speaker's narration of the qudsi hadith). {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep68 00:35:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep68 00:36:00}
- Which is why Umar ibn Abd al-Aziz would pause after each verse — "I enjoy my Lord's reply"; if your heart were present it too would rejoice in His answer, says the speaker (the speaker's narration; the report of Umar's pauses is his). {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep68 00:36:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep68 00:37:00}
- On the sura after the Fatiha he counts three kinds of people: one whose tongue recites while his heart wanders; one whose heart listens to its own tongue like listening to another person; and one whose heart receives first and hands the words to the tongue — the heart arriving at the verse before the tongue does, so that a hard verse finds him already braced (the speaker's typology). {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep68 00:37:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep68 00:38:00}
- Bowing: "glory to my Lord the Magnificent", feeling the greatness as you bend, saying it three times at least because once will not move a hard heart; rising: "God hears whoever praises Him — our Lord, to You is the praise", for straightening the back that walked bent like a creature of four legs deserves thanks (the speaker's commentary on the postures). {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep68 00:38:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep68 00:39:00}
- Prostration: the branch returning to its root, the face in the dust — you must feel your smallness, for if the breaking of the heart does not come you have not prayed, he says; and that is why the supplication in prostration is answered — the servant closest to his Lord while prostrating; two prostrations because you need to humble yourself twice; then the tashahhud — "greetings to God", blessings and good works to Him, peace upon the Prophet, peace upon ourselves and God's righteous servants, and the testimony raised with a finger as testimony is raised in courts (the speaker's commentary; "your dua is answered" and "closest while prostrating" are his narration of the hadiths). {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep68 00:39:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep68 00:40:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep68 00:40:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep68 00:41:00}
- He closes by calling the listeners to agree to practise khushu' for the thirteen days left of the month, having folded the "prescription" into the walk through the prayer itself (the speaker's closing exhortation). {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep68 00:41:00}

## Left out of this episode 68

Not written from episode 68: the Ramadan self-check exchange at 00:00:30 to 00:01:30 summarised; the mother-and-child-in-prayer aside at 00:04:30; the transcript segment 00:05:00 to 00:30:00 (audience exchanges, repetitions and further illustrations of settling and presence) taken in summary; the hadith-collections discussion in summary; and the closing formula at 00:41:00.

## Episode 69: a standalone episode on taqwa — the linguistic meaning of shielding oneself from God's anger, the simplest definition "that He finds you where He commanded and does not find you where He forbade", being mostly so counts, the honest merchant, the Prophet's parting counsel before his death, and what taqwa brings in this world and on the crossing of the Sirat, as the speaker tells it

- A thematic episode opening that this is the subject Ramadan cannot end without — the reason fasting itself was prescribed; a subject the speaker counts as mentioned in the Qur'an two hundred and fifty-eight times and tied to the qualities of the God-fearing in the Book's opening (the speaker's count, needs_source). {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep69 00:00:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep69 00:00:30}
- The word in language: waqa the thing, to shield — to put between yourself and it a barrier; so ittaqa Allah means guard yourself against God's anger with righteous work, as the hadith's "shield yourself from the Fire even with half a date" makes the morsel a barrier between you and it; and "He is worthy of taqwa and worthy of forgiveness" — worthy that He be feared, for His anger when angry is severe (the speaker's gloss of the linguistic meaning and the hadith). {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep69 00:01:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep69 00:01:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep69 00:02:30}
- The simplest definition to hold for life: that He finds you where He commanded you and does not find you where He forbade you — commanded dawn prayer, alms, the pilgrimage if able; forbade the forbidden look, the orphan's property, cheating at work; and no one does it one hundred percent, but whichever side outweighs your days decides it — seventy percent is enough to count you among the muttaqin, for God knows His servants (the speaker's formulation and arithmetic). {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep69 00:03:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep69 00:03:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep69 00:04:30}
- Among his illustrations: the merchant who does not win God's love except by three — taqwa, honesty in delivering goods, and truthfulness that never mislabels merchandise to sell it (the speaker's narration; the middle of the episode develops the applications and stories, summarised). {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep69 00:28:00}
- The Prophet's last counsel: a companion says the Prophet preached a sermon that made hearts tremble and eyes weep; they asked "is this a farewell sermon, Messenger of God?", he said yes; they said "counsel us", and he counselled one thing — taqwa of God — adding "whoever of you lives after me will see much differing" (the speaker's narration of the hadith). {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep69 00:28:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep69 00:29:00}
- What taqwa brings in this world, each tied to a verse as he lists them: God's company — "fear God; God is with the God-fearing"; His teaching; no fear nor grief for the one who fears and mends; expiation of misdeeds and a greater reward; never left stranded — "whoever fears God, He makes a way out for him and provides for him from where he does not expect"; and blessings opened on whole towns, not just individuals — "had the people of the towns believed and feared, We would have opened blessings from heaven and earth" (the speaker's list; the verses described, not written). {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep69 00:29:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep69 00:30:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep69 00:30:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep69 00:31:00}
- What taqwa brings on that day: the crossing of the Sirat — a bridge stretched over Hell whose width he puts at millions of kilometres, the bridge thinner than a hair and sharper than a sword, hooks and thorns upon it; "there is not one of you but will pass over it" — the speaker stresses it means crossing, not falling in — "then We save those who feared"; people cross at the blink of an eye, like lightning, like wind, crawling, or dragged on their faces (the speaker's narration of the hadiths and verses; his gloss of waridiha). {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep69 00:31:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep69 00:32:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep69 00:33:00}
- Then the angels' welcome: "those who feared their Lord are driven to the Garden in companies" until its gates are opened and its keepers greet them; being gathered as a delegation to the Merciful — "We gather the God-fearing to the Merciful as a delegation", like a guest met at the airport by great people; and "a Garden as wide as the heavens and the earth, prepared" — prepared, he notes, especially for the muttaqin (the speaker's narration; the verses described). {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep69 00:33:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep69 00:34:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep69 00:34:30}
- The closing charge, addressed one by one: the husband — fear God in your wife even if you divorce; the wife — do not anger your husband and bear with him; the son — be good to your father and mother; the youth — lower your gaze; the girl — keep your covering and do not soften your speech; traders and everyone — for "close friends that day are enemies to one another, except the God-fearing", so befriend the muttaqin and take them with you; he ends with the verse of fasting prescribed "so that you may fear" and the earthquake of the Hour, then a long supplication asking God to bring them out of Ramadan as muttaqin and to free them from the Fire that night (the speaker's exhortations; the verses described; the dua summarised). {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep69 00:35:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep69 00:36:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep69 00:37:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep69 00:37:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep69 00:38:00}

## Left out of this episode 69

Not written from episode 69: the segment 00:05:00 to 00:28:00 (further illustrations, audience exchanges and stories of taqwa among ordinary people) taken in summary; the 258-count application examples summarised; the repeated "He finds you where He commanded" refrain condensed; the closing supplication at 00:38:00 to 00:40:00 summarised; the sign-off at 00:40:00.

## Episode 70: a standalone episode on dua before the last ten nights — the man who asked "is our Lord near, so we whisper, or far, so we call out?", the only Qur'anic question answered without "say", no intermediary needed, the gap between prayer and answer and Satan's trick, answered prayers from Abu Hurayra's mother to Iblis himself, the four conditions — certainty, no haste, a broken humble heart, lawful food — and the etiquettes that make a prayer never turned down, as the speaker tells it

- A thematic episode preparing for the last ten nights of Ramadan: tomorrow's topic is the Night of Decree; today's is dua — its virtue, its conditions, its etiquette, and models of people whose prayers were answered, aiming to leave the listeners eager to keep asking (the speaker's framing). {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep70 00:00:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep70 00:01:00}
- The question: a man came to the Prophet asking "is our Lord far, so we call Him aloud, or near, so we whisper to Him?" — and the answer came not from the Prophet but from God Himself: "when My servants ask you about Me — I am near; I answer the call of the caller when he calls" (the speaker's narration of the hadith and the verse, described). {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep70 00:01:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep70 00:02:00}
- His observation: every question in the Qur'an is answered beginning "say" — they ask you about the sacred month, the spoils, the mountains — except this once; God dropped the "say" because dua needs no intermediary, not even the Messenger; call Him directly (the speaker's observation, presented as his count of the question-verses). {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep70 00:02:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep70 00:03:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep70 00:03:30}
- "I am near": nearness is something you feel while you call — the heart that senses His nearness has already had its prayer answered; and "I answer the call of the caller" is a promise, not a possibility, so call with insistence (the speaker's commentary). {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep70 00:03:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep70 00:04:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep70 00:04:30}
- Models of answered prayer: Abu Hurayra again — the Prophet's prayer that God endear him and his mother to the believers and the believers to them — "no believer heard of me without loving me" (the speaker's narration, repeated from an earlier night); and the scholars' argument — God answered the prayer of Iblis himself, "grant me respite till the day they are raised", and said "you are of the respited"; if He answered him, do not doubt yours (the speaker's narration; the scholars' point is his report). {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep70 00:28:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep70 00:29:00}
- Why answers feel rare: there is always a gap between the prayer and its answer so God can watch you; and the moment it is answered Satan's first task is to make you forget it came through your asking — because if you connected the two, your asking would grow, your trust in God would grow, your love of Him would grow; so the Prophet's way is the pattern: "good news — God has answered your prayer", then praise (the speaker's diagnosis and narration). {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep70 00:29:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep70 00:30:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep70 00:30:30}
- Four conditions for an answered prayer as he counts them: first, certainty — "call on God while you are certain of the answer", and never "if You will", for the servant is answered as long as he does not say "I asked and was not answered" (the speaker's narration of the hadiths). {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep70 00:31:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep70 00:31:30}
- Second, no haste — the one who says "I called and was not answered" and gives up is the one who loses, like a seed still under the soil you uproot just before it sprouts; a man told him he had made one prayer for ten years before God granted it in His own time (the speaker's narration of the hadith and the testimony). {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep70 00:31:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep70 00:32:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep70 00:32:30}
- Third, brokenness and khushu' — the more shattered the heart the nearer the answer; the speaker's image of the man clinging to a plank in a stormy sea, certain of drowning, calling "my Lord, my Lord"; Abdullah ibn Umar's sign — when the heart softens, the eye tears and the limbs tremble, "I say, it will be answered now" (the speaker's narration; the shipwreck parable is his, Ibn Umar's remark as he reports it). {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep70 00:33:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep70 00:34:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep70 00:34:30}
- Fourth, lawful food — "keep your food lawful and your prayer will be answered", and the hadith of the dust-covered traveller who stretches his hands to heaven crying "my Lord" while his food, drink, clothing and nourishment are all unlawful — "so how can he be answered?" (the speaker's narration of the hadiths). {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep70 00:35:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep70 00:35:30}
- The etiquettes: raised hands, beginning with praise of God and blessing on the Prophet, calling Him by His names and attributes, pressing and insisting — God loves those who persist in dua — and giving charity after the prayer, since charity shields the prayer from rejection; Ibn al-Qayyim's word that whoever keeps these four conditions and these manners never has a prayer turned back — "it cannot be" (the speaker's list and his citation of Ibn al-Qayyim). {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep70 00:35:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep70 00:36:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep70 00:36:30}
- And for those who cannot compose fine prayers: Mu'adh asked the Prophet what to say, saying "I do not know the polished dua"; the Prophet asked what he does say — "God, I ask You the Garden; God, save me from the Fire" — and the Prophet said "around these we and Mu'adh chant" (the speaker's narration of the hadith); then the call to make dua for the ummah and for al-Aqsa mosque in the coming ten nights, and a long closing supplication for forgiveness, acceptance, the Night of Decree, and leaving the month cleansed (the speaker's narration and closing dua, summarised). {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep70 00:36:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep70 00:37:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep70 00:40:00}

## Left out of this episode 70

Not written from episode 70: the segment 00:04:30 to 00:28:30 (further verses and stories on the virtue of dua and audience exchanges) taken in summary; repeated exhortations to pray for specific listeners' cases summarised; the closing supplication at 00:37:30 to 00:40:00 summarised; the sign-off.

## Episode 72: a standalone episode on companionship and love for God's sake — the sister who takes your hand to obey God together, Musa asking for a minister from his family, "sit with us that we may believe for an hour", the mortar that binds believers, Umar's "cling to a brother's warmth", the Prophet holding Mu'adh's hand and the Bedouin in the market, as the speaker tells it

- A thematic episode on the eve of the last days: tomorrow's two topics are how to stay firm after Ramadan and how to bid it farewell — tonight's is companionship; without a companion who pulls you toward God you will not hold on, says the speaker, for man is a social creature (the speaker's framing). {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep72 00:02:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep72 00:03:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep72 00:05:00}
- Even Musa, sent to Pharaoh, asked his Lord to expand his breast, ease his task and "make for me a minister from my family — Harun my brother, strengthen my back with him"; if a prophet needed a companion on God's path, so do we (the speaker's narration of the verse, described). {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep72 00:05:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep72 00:05:30}
- Salman al-Farisi would knock on his brother Abu al-Darda's door saying "sit with us that we may believe for an hour" — the speaker notes it became the companions' watchword (the speaker's narration of the report). {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep72 00:26:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep72 00:26:30}
- The reward of a visit for God's sake: to the one who goes to visit a brother God sends an angel behind him saying "you are blessed, your walking is blessed, and the Garden is yours" (the speaker's narration of the hadith). {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep72 00:25:30}
- Why such reward: love for God's sake works like the mortar between bricks — each believer a brick and the bond with God the cement that holds them firm; and Umar ibn al-Khattab's saying — whoever finds warmth of affection from a brother, let him cling to it with hand and teeth, for such finds are few (the speaker's analogy and narration of Umar's words). {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep72 00:26:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep72 00:27:00}
- The Prophet himself loved for God's sake: taking Mu'adh ibn Jabal's hand he said "by God I love you, Mu'adh — do not forget to say at the end of every prayer: God, help me to remember You, thank You and worship You well" (the speaker's narration of the hadith). {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep72 00:27:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep72 00:28:00}
- And Abdullah ibn Abbas — the Prophet would open his arms to him, gather him to his chest and pray that God teach him the interpretation; love in this religion is always tied to blessing (the speaker's narration). {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep72 00:28:30}
- And the Prophet would not leave anyone unembraced: he came upon Zahir, the rough Bedouin trader, standing in the market and hugged him from behind; Zahir said afterwards "nothing gladdened me like my skin touching the Prophet's skin"; then the Prophet raised his hands in the market and called "who will buy this slave?" — Zahir answered "you would find me worthless" and the Prophet said "but to God you are not worthless" (the speaker's narration of the hadith; the Zahir wording as he gives it). {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep72 00:29:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep72 00:30:00}
- The charge: before Ramadan ends, find a companion in God — a sister in God for the women, a brother for the men — and take each other's hands toward obedience, for without this you will not last; then the long closing supplication for firmness after Ramadan, including prayers for the people of Palestine and al-Aqsa mosque (the speaker's exhortation and closing dua, summarised). {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep72 00:30:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep72 00:31:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep72 00:37:00}

## Left out of this episode 72

Not written from episode 72: the broadcast scheduling details for the post-Ramadan season at 00:00:30 to 00:02:30 (Iqraa channel times and the plan to continue into the conquests, Amr ibn al-As, the rightly-guided caliphs and the Prophet's wives — left out as programme housekeeping, not content of the series record); the segment 00:05:30 to 00:25:30 (further examples and audience exchanges on companionship) taken in summary; the full closing supplication at 00:31:30 to 00:39:00 summarised; the sign-off.

## Episode 73: a standalone episode on zeal for Islam — the youth who keeps relapsing, praying and fasting are not yet belonging, the man who came running from the far end of the city, Abu Bakr who did not sleep to dream, Umar's "when would I sleep?", al-Hasan's scene of Islam complaining on the day of judgement, "do not disgrace the Muslims" at al-Muthanna's battle, Uqba at the ocean, and "employ us, do not replace us", as the speaker tells it

- A thematic episode opening with the young man who draws near to God and falls again and again until he thinks there is no use; the speaker answers the missing meaning is zeal — gheera for Islam — and asks: do you belong to Islam? praying and fasting alone are not belonging; belonging is that Islam is the dearest thing in you, that your heart burns for it as it does for your family (the speaker's framing and definitions). {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep73 00:00:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep73 00:01:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep73 00:04:00}
- The first model: sura Ya-Sin's man who "came running from the farthest part of the city" — the village had three prophets already, yet one man felt the religion was his concern too, and the Qur'an notes he came from the farthest edge to show how far his love carried him (the speaker's narration of the verse, described). {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep73 00:05:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep73 00:06:00}
- The second model: Abu Bakr — "I do not sleep so that I may dream; I am on the road and have not yet arrived", against people who dream while healthy and walking; and Umar ibn al-Khattab — "when would I sleep? if I sleep at night I waste my Lord's right, and if I sleep by day I waste my subjects' right" (the speaker's narration of their sayings). {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep73 00:24:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep73 00:25:00}
- Al-Hasan al-Basri's imagined scene: on the day of judgement Islam itself comes, and God asks each person — this one says "my Lord, he forsook me", that one "my Lord, he aided me" — a mother who raised her children but abandoned those around her finds the flood takes her children too; until Islam takes Umar by the hand and says "my Lord, I was a stranger until this man took me in" — and the speaker asks each listener: will it say your name, "I was a stranger in this factory, this company, until so-and-so brought me here"? (the speaker's narration of al-Hasan's picture). {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep73 00:25:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep73 00:26:30}
- Why is our passion cold? — the speaker's stinging aside: a people who weep when their team wins or loses but feel nothing when they hear "Muhammad died leaving daughters" as a jibe — he insists he is not calling for violence but for love: mend the person next to you, and Islam returns well (the speaker's exhortation). {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep73 00:26:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep73 00:27:30}
- Al-Muthanna ibn Haritha's cry at his battle against the Persians: the tribe of Bakr on the right wing hung back and the Persians began winning through their gap, until al-Muthanna shouted "do not disgrace the Muslims!" — and they turned like lions; the speaker turns the cry on the audience: do not disgrace the Muslims with your bad manners, your loud voices, your neglected appearance — the first step to guiding people is being an example, and the second is loving people (the speaker's narration of the battle and the application). {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep73 00:28:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep73 00:29:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep73 00:30:00}
- Uqba ibn Nafi at the Atlantic after the conquest of Africa: "O sea, by God, if I knew there was land beyond you I would cross you to make it worship God" — the speaker notes he was speaking of the Americas without knowing they were there; and the Yamama fighter's "I will not die while Islam is not mighty" (the speaker's narration of the reports). {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep73 00:32:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep73 00:33:00}
- The practical turn: let a quarter of the passion spent on football matches and serials be spent for Islam; be the best at your work so people say "religious and successful"; Ibn al-Qayyim's word that the highest of works is calling to God because it is the station of the prophets; and the chain of reward — guide one person and every good they and their guided do lands in your scale after your death; the closing supplication includes "employ us, do not replace us" and prayers for Palestine and al-Aqsa (the speaker's exhortations, the Ibn al-Qayyim citation, and the closing dua, summarised). {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep73 00:31:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep73 00:34:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep73 00:35:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep73 00:36:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep73 00:38:00}

## Left out of this episode 73

Not written from episode 73: the segment 00:06:30 to 00:24:00 (further stories of zeal, audience exchanges and the dying-companion scene) taken in summary; the long football-and-serial aside partly summarised; the football fan story at 00:31:30 to 00:32:30 summarised; the full closing supplication summarised; the sign-off at 00:39:00.

## Episode 74: a standalone episode on refinement — etiquette is from our religion, not foreign values; answering the mother's call and Jurayj's lesson; the best food for your family; removing harm from the path as a branch of faith; the angels harmed by what harms people; asking permission before entering, three times, not at the door's face; Jabir's "it is I" that the Prophet disliked; waiting to be seated; leaving after the meal; no man leads prayer in another's house; visiting the sick briefly; and the neighbour's air, water and light, as the speaker tells it

- A thematic episode on the last Ramadan days: the topic people least expect — etiquette — and the speaker insists it is not outside the religion: refinement in dealing with people is a part of manners, and those who think piety means gloom and hardness have it backwards; the whole episode is small concrete examples (the speaker's framing). {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep74 00:00:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep74 00:01:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep74 00:02:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep74 00:03:00}
- With the parents — not dutifulness itself but its refinement: the mother calls and you are absorbed; the story of the worshipper whose mother called him while he prayed and he said "my Lord, my mother or my prayer?" and stayed praying three days — until her prayer against him brought the ordeal of the woman's accusation; a lesson that immersion in worship is no excuse to ignore her call (the speaker's narration of the Jurayj story as he gives it). {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep74 00:03:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep74 00:04:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep74 00:05:00}
- More refinements at home: the man who gives his wife and children the best of his food, drink and clothes before himself; and the companion on his deathbed who could not pronounce the shahada — a sign, says the speaker, of unfinished business with his mother (the speaker's narration; the second story's ending he leaves as a warning). {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep74 00:05:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep74 00:06:00}
- In the street: faith is seventy-odd branches, the highest the testimony and the lowest removing harm from the path — so the paper you pick up off the street is a piece of faith, and the Prophet fourteen hundred years ago counted it charity in a desert environment where paths hardly mattered (the speaker's narration of the hadiths). {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep74 00:24:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep74 00:25:30}
- The master hadith of this whole etiquette: "the angels are harmed by what harms the children of Adam" — so whatever offends people in street or home offends the angels; the eater of onion or garlic keeps away from the mosque, and by the same reasoning the speaker extends it to the cigarette's smell — his inference, not a ruling, he notes (the speaker's narration of the hadith and his own deduction, flagged as his reasoning). {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep74 00:26:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep74 00:27:30}
- Entering houses: "do not enter houses other than your own until you take leave" — tasta'nisu, ask till the household is ready; and if told "go back", go back without hurt, "that is purer for you"; do not stand facing the door but to its right or left; permission is asked three times, with a pause between each, for someone inside may be praying or occupied (the speaker's narration of the verse and hadiths, described). {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep74 00:28:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep74 00:30:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep74 00:30:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep74 00:31:30}
- And answer with your name, not "it is I": Jabir came to the Prophet and knocked; "who is it?" — "me"; the Prophet answered "me, me" as if he disliked it — teach people your name, says the speaker, after fourteen hundred years (the speaker's narration of the hadith). {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep74 00:32:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep74 00:32:30}
- As a guest: do not take a seat until shown where; do not treat your host's patient waiting as permission for your phone call — "what is taken by shyness is forbidden", his leave was only courtesy; when a companion invited the Prophet to a meal and an extra man tagged along, the Prophet told the host "a man followed us — if you wish, feed him", teaching both host and follower; and "when you are fed, disperse" — do not overstay (the speaker's narration of the hadiths and the verse). {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep74 00:33:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep74 00:34:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep74 00:34:30}
- Two more: no man leads the prayer in another man's house — the owner leads unless he yields; and visiting the sick — the Prophet's way is the shortened visit and the bright face, not the long sitting that wears the patient out, as his own visitors once wore him until a maid had to drive them off (the speaker's narration of the hadiths and the anecdote). {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep74 00:35:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep74 00:36:30}
- With neighbours: if they smell your cooking, send them some; and do not block their air, water or light — fourteen hundred years before modern building codes, says the speaker; he closes by addressing the religious themselves: do not let people taste piety as gloom and heaviness — the Prophet never chose between two things but the easier, so long as it was not a sin (the speaker's narration and closing charge). {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep74 00:37:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep74 00:37:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep74 00:38:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep74 00:38:30}

## Left out of this episode 74

Not written from episode 74: the segment 00:06:30 to 00:24:00 (further etiquette examples — gatherings, greetings, household courtesies — and audience exchanges) taken in summary; repeated examples condensed; the closing formula at 00:38:30 to 00:39:00.

## Episode 75: a standalone episode on death — remember often the destroyer of pleasures, "you are days", death exposes the world, the sermon at Damascus on those who amassed and built and hoped, how the angel takes the soul, the funeral that says "hasten me", the grave that asks "what did you prepare for me?", Zayn al-Abidin's poem on his own dying, and Rabi' ibn Haytham's grave by his bed, as the speaker tells it

- A thematic episode: after Paradise and the standing comes the stage everyone fears — death; the speaker's aim is not to terrify but to ready the listener for that standing before God (the speaker's framing). {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep75 00:00:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep75 00:01:30}
- The Prophet's counsel: "remember often the destroyer of pleasures" — death is what demolished every fortune, horsemanship and amusement; and the speaker's formula from the elders: you are days, each breath that leaves is a part of you gone; ask the old, the meaning is plain to them (the speaker's narration of the hadith and his gloss). {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep75 00:01:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep75 00:03:30}
- Death exposes the world: no gathering of youth without a grave among them now; he recalls the Alexandria quarter of al-Muntazah where a king lived in luxury — where is the kingdom now? and the sermon at Damascus: "people, those before you amassed much, built buildings and hoped far — their gathering became ruins, their buildings graves, their hopes delusion" (the speaker's narration of the report). {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep75 00:04:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep75 00:06:00}
- In a hundred years not one soul now on the face of the earth remains — the obituary pages already carry names of the young; then the imagined scene: the angel of death standing over you while ten pounds of unlawful money sits beside you and you cannot speak — "until death comes to one of them he says: my Lord, send me back, that I may work righteousness in what I left" — and the answer is no (the speaker's narration of the verse, described). {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep75 00:06:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep75 00:22:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep75 00:22:30}
