- How the angel draws the soul: Umar asks Ubayy ibn Ka'b — for the corrupt servant like a thorny branch thrust into a fleece and torn out; for the believer like a drop slipping from the mouth of a waterskin; Amr ibn al-As questioned on his deathbed "how do you feel it?"; and Umar ibn Abd al-Aziz dying reciting "that abode of the hereafter We make for those who seek no haughtiness on earth nor corruption — and the outcome is for the God-fearing" (the speaker's narration of the reports). {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep75 00:23:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep75 00:25:00}
- The funeral: the believer's bier says "hasten me, hasten me" — Sa'd ibn Mu'adh's body was heavy yet the bearers found it light, and the Prophet told them others than you were carrying it — while the other's wailing is heard by everything in heaven and earth except the two heavy ones, man and jinn (the speaker's narration of the hadiths). {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep75 00:25:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep75 00:27:00}
- The grave speaks: "the grave is either a garden of the gardens of Paradise or a pit of the pits of the Fire"; and the call — "son of Adam, I am the house of loneliness, the house of darkness, the house of desolation, the house of worms; this is what I prepared for you — what did you prepare for me?" — answered by your fasting, prayer, alms and good character, or by your trespasses, and the caller from before God: "My servant spoke truth — spread for him from Paradise", or "he lied — spread for him from the Fire" (the speaker's narration of the hadiths). {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep75 00:27:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep75 00:29:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep75 00:30:00}
- The bitterness: "every soul shall taste death" — death's stupor, of which the dying Prophet said wiping the sweat "there is indeed a stupor to death"; and death like the traveller longing for his family — you are going to them; Zayn al-Abidin's poem imagining his own dying — "the stranger is not the stranger of Syria or Yemen; the stranger is the stranger of the grave and the shroud", recited at length (the speaker's narration and the poem he quotes). {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep75 00:30:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep75 00:31:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep75 00:32:00}
- Rabi' ibn Haytham kept a dug grave beside his house: he would lie in it and rehearse "my Lord, send me back" — then rise saying "He has returned you, Rabi'; He gave you the chance — work before you go and cannot return" (the speaker's narration of the report). {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep75 00:35:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep75 00:36:00}
- The correction at the close: he is not asking anyone to sit at home in gloom till death comes — the world in your hand, not in your heart; dress well, go out, succeed, provided prayer stands first; the grave is a garden for the believer, and only the sinner should fear — though even he, if he repents now, wins (the speaker's closing balance). {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep75 00:36:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep75 00:37:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep75 00:38:00}

## Left out of this episode 75

Not written from episode 75: the obituary-pages dramatisation at 00:03:00 summarised; the segment 00:07:30 to 00:20:30 (further stories of the dead and audience exchanges) taken in summary; the full poem of Zayn al-Abidin at 00:32:00 to 00:35:00 quoted by the speaker is described, not reproduced; the closing formula at 00:38:30.

## Episode 76: a special standalone episode on Palestine and al-Aqsa, broadcast while the wounds were bleeding — the woman's reply "then there is no calamity", the value of the blessed land, the prophets buried and killed there, seven centuries under tyrants as requital, the Prophet leading the prophets in prayer so "whose house is it?", fifteen thousand martyrs for this soil, Saladin who could not smile, the song the conquerors sang, the wahn hadith, and the speaker's answer: mend ten around you, donate, boycott, pray, as he tells it

- A special episode — the speaker explains the regular companions' biographies are set aside this night because the ummah's wounds are bleeding in Palestine and al-Aqsa; he opens with the woman who asked a man his calamity three times — did Islam's enemies overrun Muslim lands? was the commander of the faithful killed? was a sanctity of the Muslims violated? — and on hearing no three times said "then there is no calamity"; today, he says, there is (the speaker's narration of the report and his framing). {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep76 00:00:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep76 00:01:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep76 00:02:00}
- His three questions for the episode: what is this land's worth, whose land is it, and its history from Adam until now — and the goal that every heart own this land as the Muslims' own (the speaker's outline). {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep76 00:03:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep76 00:04:00}
- The worth: the Qur'an never names this land without "blessed" or "holy" — the land We blessed for Abraham, the holy land God wrote for you, "the farthest mosque around which We blessed" — and he stresses "around it" so no one thinks the blessing stops at the building; the fig and the olive he reads as the oath to this very soil; and the prophets' nearness — Abraham, Isaac, Jacob, Joseph born or living there, Zachariah, John, Jesus, and Muhammad carried there by night (the speaker's narration of the verses, described; the fig-and-olive identification is his gloss). {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep76 00:05:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep76 00:05:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep76 00:06:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep76 00:07:00}
- The history as he tells it: God sent prophets again and again — Zachariah sawn apart, John slain for a dancing-woman, Jesus nearly killed — "they kill the prophets without right" was not rhetoric, he says; and seven centuries of tyrants' rule from sixty-four years before Christ until Umar were requital for the killing of prophets (the speaker's narration; the dating and requital framing are his). {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep76 00:41:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep76 00:42:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep76 00:42:30}
- Why the Prophet did not conquer it himself: God willed that the ummah after him should take it — "this land you Muslims are responsible for, not Muhammad alone"; yet He honoured the Prophet with the night journey — ascension could only begin from there — and the wall where he tethered al-Buraq, renamed by others to efface the Prophet's trace (the speaker's narration and reasoning). {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep76 00:43:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep76 00:44:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep76 00:45:00}
- The night of the isra': the mosque filled with hundreds of thousands of God's prophets from Adam to Jesus come down to receive him, and he led them all in prayer — and the homeowner prays as imam, says the speaker, so whose house is it? (the speaker's narration of the hadith and his inference). {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep76 00:45:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep76 00:46:30}
- The conquest: the one spot in all the conquests where Abu Bakr sent four armies — under Amr ibn al-As, Abu Ubayda ibn al-Jarrah, Shurahbil ibn Hasana and Khalid ibn al-Walid; the speaker counts fifteen thousand Muslim martyrs for this land, five hundred of them companions, out of nine thousand in all the conquests — the highest price paid anywhere (the speaker's figures, needs_source). {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep76 00:47:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep76 00:47:30}
- Umar's entry: he came from Medina for this city alone; the Jews recognised him — "the one described in the Torah: a tall frame and a patched robe"; he would not pray inside the Church of the Resurrection lest a later people say "here Umar prayed" and build a mosque over it; then he gathered the armies on the Golan field and Bilal, who had sworn not to call the adhan after the Prophet, called it again — "this is a day that gladdens the Messenger of God" (the speaker's narration of the reports). {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep76 00:48:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep76 00:49:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep76 00:50:00}
- The long rule: thirteen hundred years with the land in Muslim hands — broken only by some eighty years of the Crusaders — because the Muslims were well; and Saladin's restoration: a whole generation revived for God, his refusal to smile while his brothers were besieged — "I am ashamed before God that He should see me laughing" — his reading of "there has come to you a messenger from among yourselves, grievous to him is your suffering, anxious over you, with the believers kind and merciful" as his last words (the speaker's narration of the history and the reports, the years as he counts them). {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep76 00:50:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep76 00:52:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep76 00:53:30}
- The later loss: the British entering Jerusalem announcing "now the crusades are over" and singing their song "Muhammad died leaving daughters" — an insult, he says, not to women but to the whole ummah; and the Prophet's warning of nations summoning one another against you as diners are summoned to a dish — not from your fewness, for you are many, but the foam of the torrent — with wahn, love of this world and hatred of death, thrown into your hearts (the speaker's narration of the reports and the hadith). {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep76 00:54:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep76 00:54:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep76 00:55:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep76 00:56:00}
- His answer — not demonstrations alone, which he fears vent the energy and leave nothing: every Muslim mends the ten nearest to him and returns them to God; prepare the young; give money and blood for your brothers there; boycott whatever product helps kill them; make dua for them every night; "this is the only solution — return faith to the ummah and the land returns" (the speaker's prescriptions, all in his voice). He closes with a long supplication for the people of Palestine and al-Aqsa (the speaker's closing dua, summarised). {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep76 00:56:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep76 00:57:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep76 00:58:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep76 00:58:30}

## Left out of this episode 76

Not written from episode 76: the segment 00:07:30 to 00:40:30 (the detailed chronology from Adam through Solomon's temple, further prophets, and audience exchanges) taken in summary; repeated exhortations condensed; the full closing supplication summarised; the sign-off.

## Episode 78: a standalone episode on Paradise — the race the Bedouin's camel won and "God raises nothing of this world but He lowers it", the locked gate opened only for Muhammad, the gate's width like Mecca to Syria, the first entry-faces like the full moon, "who will smell Paradise?", the price of a metre, the man who threw away his dates at Uhud, the women of this world recreated more beautiful than the hur, "be in this world a stranger", the homesickness poem of Eden's gardens, and the greatest bliss of all — the sight of God's face, as the speaker tells it

- A thematic episode: everyone in this world wants happiness, and nothing complete exists here — the race in which the companions held their mounts back until a poor Bedouin's camel beat the Prophet's, and the Prophet said "God wrote: He raises nothing of this world without lowering it" — youth is followed by weakness, money by money's troubles, every delight by its weariness; only Paradise holds whole happiness (the speaker's narration of the hadith and his list). {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep78 00:00:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep78 00:02:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep78 00:02:30}
- Imagine you crossed the Sirat: before you the gate of Paradise, locked; mankind searches for an opener, the prophets cannot, until Muhammad comes; the gatekeeper asks who and is told "God commanded me to open for none but you" — and it opens (the speaker's narration of the hadith). {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep78 00:04:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep78 00:05:00}
- The gate's leaf: the gap of its opening like the distance between Mecca and Syria — and that is only the doorway's crack (the speaker's narration of the hadith). {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep78 00:05:30}
- The first to enter: faces shining like the moon on its fourteenth night — no relieving themselves, their combs of gold, their sweat musk that renews and changes (the speaker's narration of the hadith). {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep78 00:06:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep78 00:07:00}
- The price: "behold, God's merchandise is dear — God's merchandise is Paradise"; a metre of Paradise for two rak'as; the man at Uhud who heard the call, looked at the dates in his hand — "between me and Paradise only these few dates?" — threw them down, fought and fell a martyr; and the companion asking "who will smell Paradise for us?" answered "Paradise, by God, is light glittering, a swaying fragrant plant, a built palace, a beautiful wife" (the speaker's narration of the hadiths and the Uhud story). {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep78 00:20:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep78 00:21:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep78 00:22:00}
- Its fragrance reaches five hundred years of travel away — which is why the companions could say, going into battle, "I smell Paradise from behind this mountain"; and their question to a new Muslim — "what was your father's land?" — because the first father Adam entered Paradise before he ever descended to earth: that was our first homeland, which is why "be in this world as a stranger or a passer-by" is no pessimism but homesickness, like the verse "dwell in the gardens of Eden — our first abodes are there" (the speaker's narration of the hadiths, the report and the poetry). {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep78 00:27:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep78 00:28:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep78 00:29:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep78 00:30:00}
- The loves of Paradise: the women of this world recreated — "We created them anew" — more radiant than the hur, made virgins, loving, of one age; a wife's beauty lighting her palace until her husband is dazed by it; and love there refined, against the unreal loves of films that ruined the young (the speaker's narration of the verse and reports; the comparative beauty claim is his reading, needs_source). {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep78 00:24:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep78 00:25:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep78 00:26:30}
- New pleasures God keeps scattering on its people — and above all the looking at God's face: the callers announce "today is the day of more" — not that they asked for palaces, but they agree on one thing: "show us Your face that we may look at You"; the veils are lifted and they see Him, a bliss greater than every bliss since creation (the speaker's narration of the hadith and the verse "for those who do good is more"). {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep78 00:31:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep78 00:32:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep78 00:35:30}
- And God speaks to each by name — "so-and-so, I am pleased with you; are you pleased with Me?" — the meaning, he says, of "God is pleased with them and they with Him"; then "do you remember that sin?... I have forgiven you"; then "wish, My servant — you will not wish a thing but I give it you", and God reminds him of wishes he himself forgot (the speaker's narration of the reports; the by-name address as he gives it). {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep78 00:36:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep78 00:37:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep78 00:37:30}
- He closes on the question "who is a lover of Paradise?" — a lover who rises in the depth of night to pray the dawn in the mosque (the speaker's closing exhortation and brief supplication, summarised). {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep78 00:38:00}

## Left out of this episode 78

Not written from episode 78: the segment 00:07:30 to 00:20:00 (the rivers, palaces, fruits and audience exchanges) taken in summary; the film-and-serial aside partly summarised; the closing formula.

## Episode 79: the finale, a standalone episode on the eleven stations of purification — only the pure enter Paradise, four cleansings in this world (repentance, asking forgiveness, good deeds that erase bad ones, affliction), three in the grave (the funeral prayer, the grave's terrors, gifts of deeds from the living — the Egyptian who made hajj for Ibn Hazm), and four on the day of judgement (its horrors, standing exposed before God, the Prophet's intercession, God's own pardon), and the warning that whoever reaches the Fire after eleven cleansings is the worst of people, as the speaker tells it

- The series' final episode opens where last night's ended — "no one enters Paradise but the pure, only": "peace upon you — you are pure, so enter it to abide"; tibtum means made pure, nothing of filth left in you; a speck of disobedience remaining and you slip off the Sirat (the speaker's narration of the verse and his gloss). {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep79 00:00:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep79 00:02:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep79 00:02:30}
- But God in His mercy set eleven stations of purification between you and the gate — four in this world, three in the grave, four on the day of judgement (the speaker's enumeration). {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep79 00:03:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep79 00:04:30}
- In this world, the first: repentance — its four conditions he recaps (leaving the sin, regretting it, resolving not to return, restoring people's rights except backbiting) — and a sincere, comprehensive repentance, not one thing left aside; the second, asking forgiveness — not the same as repentance: repentance covers the sins you know you did, istighfar the ones you forgot, "the Messenger of God would ask forgiveness a hundred times a day", and "whoever keeps to istighfar God gives him a way out of every trouble, relief from every grief and provision from where he does not expect" (the speaker's narration of the hadiths). {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep79 00:05:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep79 00:07:00}
- The third, good deeds that erase bad ones — "follow a bad deed with a good one and it erases it"; and the fourth, affliction — the trials God sends to cleanse (the speaker's list; the fourth station as he names it). {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep79 00:19:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep79 00:20:00}
- In the grave, three: the funeral prayer of the believers over you — so live among people who will pray it; the grave's terrors — its darkness and its squeeze; and gifts of deeds from the living to the dead — hajj, umra, charity and dua reach the deceased in his grave, a point he says the four imams agreed on, each with clear sound hadiths (the speaker's narration and his citation of the consensus). {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep79 00:20:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep79 00:21:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep79 00:22:00}
- His proof-story: an Egyptian living in Saudi Arabia told him "this year I am not doing hajj for myself — I am doing it for Ibn Hazm al-Andalusi"; how dear a man must be to God, he marvels, that a hajj is still being sent to him centuries on; and his own sight in the Sacred Mosque — a dead man carried in on the crowd's crush with only the imam to pray over him, until one more man caught up (the speaker's anecdotes). {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep79 00:23:00} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep79 00:24:30}
- On the day of judgement, four more if the first seven were not enough: its horrors — the sun brought down, the heavens stripped, the mountains carded wool, the seas bursting into flame, the graves pouring out (the speaker's narration of the verses, described); the standing exposed before God — "what deluded you about Me? did you think My meeting a light thing? you beautified yourself for people and brought Me the ugly" — a standing that itself burns the sins off, as the saying goes that some will wish the Fire over the presentation (the speaker's narration of the reports and his dramatisation). {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep79 00:26:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep79 00:27:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep79 00:28:30}
- Third of that day, the Prophet's intercession — after the prophets, the angels, the believers and the children have all interceded, God's beloved Muhammad remains; and fourth and last, God's own pardon — a mercy so wide, says the speaker, that even Iblis hopes it might reach him (the speaker's narration of the hadiths; the Iblis remark is his). {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep79 00:29:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep79 00:30:00}
- Whoever still falls to the Fire after eleven stations: the worst of people, says the speaker — not the sinner who slips and aches and breaks before God, but the one for whom God was never first, fifteen, twenty, forty years; those whose filth remains get cleansed in the Fire like gold in the flame until every impurity is out, then they come out pure and hear "peace upon you — you are pure" — but late, far too late (the speaker's narration and the gold analogy). {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep79 00:31:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep79 00:34:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep79 00:35:00}
- The finale's point: of the eleven stations only three are in your hands tonight — repentance, asking forgiveness, and good deeds that erase; Ramadan is the chance; he closes the series urging them to hold to the three till they die pure (the speaker's closing charge). {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep79 00:36:30} {cite:assabile-amr-khaled wa-nal9a-al-aheba/ep79 00:37:30}
